title: Lamborghini for Sale in Miami: 2026 Complete Buyer's Guide
excerpt: Looking for a Lamborghini in Miami? This 2026 guide covers every model — Revuelto, Urus, Huracán Tecnica — plus CPO options, dealers, pricing, and negotiation tips.
content:
Miami and Lamborghini share a natural kinship. The city's year-round sunshine, its culture of spectacular wealth, its love of design and excess — these qualities make Miami not just one of the largest Lamborghini markets in the United States, but one of the most important in the world. If you're looking for a Lamborghini in Miami, you're in the right place. This guide covers everything from current models to certified pre-owned options, local dealers, real-world pricing, and the negotiation strategies that actually work when buying a bull.

Current Lamborghini Models Available in Miami (2026)

Lamborghini Revuelto — The Flagship V12 Hybrid

The Revuelto is the spiritual successor to the Aventador and the most powerful production Lamborghini ever built. Introduced in 2023, it pairs a naturally aspirated 6.5-liter V12 — a Lamborghini signature since the Miura — with three electric motors for a combined 1,015 hp.

SpecificationRevuelto
Engine6.5L V12 + 3 electric motors
Combined Power1,015 hp
0–60 mph2.5 seconds
Top Speed217 mph (350 km/h)
Transmission8-speed DCT
Base MSRP~$517,000
Typical Miami Transaction Price$550,000–$650,000+
Miami Availability6–18 month wait list; occasional dealer stock

The Revuelto represents a watershed moment for Lamborghini: the end of purely combustion V12 power and the beginning of the hybrid era. For enthusiasts, this is somewhat bittersweet — the V12 alone sounds extraordinary, but the electric motors complicate the emotional purity slightly. Objectively, the Revuelto is the fastest, most capable Lamborghini ever built, and demand far exceeds supply in every global market.

Who should buy it: The Revuelto is for buyers who want the ultimate Lamborghini statement — the most powerful model, the flagship V12, and the latest technology. Budget $600,000+ fully loaded, and expect to wait.

Lamborghini Urus S — The Super SUV

The Urus redefined what a Lamborghini could be — and, many argue, what an SUV could be. The Urus S, updated for 2023, is powered by a 4.0-liter twin-turbocharged V8 producing 657 hp. It's simultaneously practical enough to carry four adults and their luggage and fast enough to embarrass most sports cars.

SpecificationUrus S
Engine4.0L twin-turbo V8
Power657 hp
Torque627 lb-ft
0–60 mph3.5 seconds
Top Speed189 mph (305 km/h)
Seating4–5
Base MSRP~$233,000
Typical Miami Transaction Price$260,000–$350,000
Miami AvailabilityGood; in-stock at most dealers

In Miami, the Urus is by far Lamborghini's best-selling model — accounting for approximately 60% of local sales. The practical-luxury positioning resonates particularly well in a city where school runs and yacht trips are part of the same lifestyle. The Urus SE, a plug-in hybrid variant with 800 hp, began deliveries in 2024 and adds even more performance alongside electric-only range.

Who should buy it: Anyone who wants Lamborghini ownership combined with genuine daily usability. The Urus is the most practical entry into the brand and, statistically, the one most likely to be in inventory at your local dealer.

Lamborghini Huracán Tecnica — The Driver's Lamborghini

The Huracán Tecnica occupies a special place in the lineup: it's the most driver-focused street Huracán, positioned between the EVO and the extreme STO. Rear-wheel drive only, with a 631 hp naturally aspirated V10 and a character that rewards driver involvement above all else.

SpecificationHuracán Tecnica
Engine5.2L naturally aspirated V10
Power631 hp
0–60 mph3.2 seconds
Top Speed202 mph (325 km/h)
DriveRear-wheel drive
Base MSRP~$246,000
Typical Miami Transaction Price$265,000–$310,000
Miami AvailabilityGood; approaching end of Huracán production cycle

The Huracán line is approaching the end of its production run, making the Tecnica potentially the last naturally aspirated V10 Lamborghini in series production. This "end of an era" significance is contributing to strong market interest and, for many purists, makes it the most compelling current Lamborghini buy.

Who should buy it: Driving purists who prize engagement over outright power. The naturally aspirated V10's sound and response character cannot be replicated by any hybrid or turbocharged engine. Buy one before they're gone.

Certified Pre-Owned (CPO) Lamborghinis in Miami

Lamborghini's Certified Pre-Owned program — branded "Lamborghini Approved" — provides a structured way to purchase used examples with factory backing. Key features of the program:

  • Eligibility: Lamborghinis up to 7 years old with under 62,000 miles
  • Inspection: 172-point factory inspection process performed by certified technicians
  • Warranty: 12-month/unlimited mileage warranty extension (renewable)
  • Roadside assistance: Included as part of the program
  • Financing: Special rate financing available through Lamborghini Financial Services

CPO Lamborghinis typically carry a 5-10% premium over non-certified examples, but that premium buys significant peace of mind. For a $250,000+ purchase, having factory warranty coverage is substantial insurance.

Typical CPO Pricing in Miami (2026)

Model / YearTypical CPO Price Range
Huracán EVO (2019–2022)$195,000–$245,000
Huracán Tecnica (2022–2024)$220,000–$275,000
Huracán STO (2021–2024)$295,000–$380,000
Urus (2019–2022)$175,000–$230,000
Urus S (2023–2024)$215,000–$270,000
Aventador S (2017–2020)$320,000–$450,000
Aventador SVJ (2019–2022)$650,000–$950,000

Miami's Lamborghini Dealers

The Collection — Coral Gables

Located at 200 Bird Road in Coral Gables, The Collection is one of the largest and most prestigious luxury and exotic car dealerships in the United States. Lamborghini is one of their anchor brands, and their inventory depth is typically the strongest in the Miami market. The Collection's clientele includes many of Miami's wealthiest families, and the buying experience reflects that — professional, unhurried, and thorough.

The Collection also handles CPO certification and maintains a substantial service department with factory-trained Lamborghini technicians. They are the recommended first stop for buyers considering a new Revuelto, Urus, or Huracán.

Prestige Imports — North Miami Beach

Prestige Imports at 280 NE 167th Street has been one of South Florida's landmark exotic car dealers for decades. Their Lamborghini center is one of the highest-volume Lamborghini retailers in the country, regularly appearing in the manufacturer's top 10 dealers nationally.

Prestige is particularly strong on pre-owned inventory — they maintain an extensive selection of used Lamborghinis at any given time, often spanning multiple model years and variants. For buyers seeking specific colors, options, or models that aren't available at other dealers, Prestige's inventory breadth makes them a natural second stop.

Lamborghini Broward — Davie

Located at 6195 SW 18th Street in Davie (Broward County), Lamborghini Broward serves the Fort Lauderdale-West Palm Beach corridor but is within easy reach for Miami buyers. Their inventory is typically smaller than The Collection or Prestige but often includes allocation units for models with long wait lists at the larger dealers.

Worth contacting when the other dealers report extended wait times — allocation policies mean different dealers sometimes have different delivery timelines for the same model.

The Buying Process: What to Expect

New Lamborghini Purchase

Buying a new Lamborghini in 2026 involves navigating a market where demand for most models exceeds supply. Here's what to expect:

  1. Configuration — Work with the dealer's brand specialist to specify your car via Lamborghini's Ad Personam customization program. Choices include exterior color (standard and Ad Personam options), interior material and color, wheel design, and numerous performance and comfort options
  2. Order placement — The dealer submits your order to Lamborghini headquarters; allocation is managed centrally based on dealer volume and customer priority
  3. Wait time — For the Revuelto, expect 12-18 months. For the Urus S, 3-9 months is more typical. The Huracán Tecnica is increasingly available from stock as the model approaches end of production
  4. Delivery deposit — Typically 10-15% of MSRP, paid at order placement
  5. Final payment — On delivery; financing arranged through Lamborghini Financial Services or your own bank

Pre-Owned Purchase

The pre-owned process is more straightforward but requires due diligence:

  1. Carfax and service records review — Non-negotiable; a complete service history from authorized dealers is strongly preferred
  2. Pre-purchase inspection (PPI) — Have an independent Lamborghini-specialist technician inspect the car, particularly if buying from a private party
  3. Title verification — Ensure clean title with no liens; use a title search service for private purchases
  4. Test drive — Request a test drive on a mix of highway and city roads; listen for unusual sounds from the engine, transmission, and suspension

Negotiation Tips for Miami Lamborghini Buyers

Lamborghinis are not heavily negotiated in the way that mainstream vehicles are, but there are strategies that create value:

  • New cars: don't negotiate on price, negotiate on allocation — In a seller's market for the Revuelto, asking for a price discount rarely works. Instead, focus on getting earlier delivery, better allocation priority, or included options
  • Pre-owned: everything is negotiable — Dealers have more flexibility on used inventory, particularly if a car has been sitting for more than 60 days. Research comparable sales on Bring a Trailer and duPont REGISTRY before making an offer
  • CPO premium is negotiable — The CPO certification premium (typically $10,000–$25,000 above market) can often be reduced, particularly for cars approaching the program's age or mileage limits
  • Trade-in leverage — If you have a trade-in, get an independent appraisal from a separate dealer before accepting the selling dealer's offer. Trade-in value is a common area where dealers recoup flexibility on sale price
  • Year-end timing — The final quarter of the calendar year often brings more dealer flexibility as they manage inventory and quota targets. December and January can be advantageous for pre-owned purchases
  • Build relationships — Miami's Lamborghini community is tight-knit. Dealers reward repeat customers and referrals with allocation priority and better service. If you're a first-time buyer, buying a CPO Urus before ordering a Revuelto is a recognized pathway to priority treatment

Total Cost of Lamborghini Ownership in Miami

Cost CategoryUrus SHuracán TecnicaRevuelto
Annual service$3,000–$8,000$4,000–$10,000$8,000–$18,000
Insurance (annual)$8,000–$20,000$12,000–$28,000$20,000–$45,000
Tires (replacement set)$3,000–$5,000$4,000–$7,000$6,000–$12,000
Storage / detailing$2,000–$8,000$2,000–$8,000$3,000–$10,000
Total annual running costs~$16,000–$41,000~$22,000–$53,000~$37,000–$85,000

These figures don't include depreciation (or appreciation, depending on the model and market conditions) or financing costs. Insurance is a particularly significant variable in Miami, where rates are higher than in most other major U.S. cities due to accident frequency, theft rates, and repair costs.

Final Advice for Miami Lamborghini Buyers

Miami is one of the best cities in the world to own a Lamborghini. The climate is perfect for open-air driving, the roads (particularly the MacArthur and Venetian causeways) provide genuine spectacle, and the social context — where a Lamborghini is noticed and appreciated rather than provoking resentment — makes every drive an event.

For new buyers: start with a test drive at both The Collection and Prestige Imports. Compare the buying experiences, the inventory, and the personalities of the brand specialists. The relationship you form with your dealer matters over time, particularly as you consider future purchases or trades. Choose the one that treats you best.

For the market as a whole: Lamborghini ownership in Miami has never been more accessible (relatively speaking) or more supported. The brand's dealer network, service infrastructure, and community of local owners creates an ecosystem that makes the ownership experience genuinely rewarding. Welcome to the herd.

title: The Collection Miami: Inside South Florida's Premier Exotic Car Dealer
excerpt: The Collection in Coral Gables is Miami's definitive destination for Ferrari, Porsche, McLaren, Koenigsegg, and Bugatti. Here's everything you need to know.
content:
When South Florida's wealthiest buyers want a Ferrari, Porsche, McLaren, Koenigsegg, or Bugatti, they don't browse the internet — they drive to Coral Gables. The Collection has been the region's undisputed benchmark for exotic car retail since 1986, and four decades of operation have only deepened its position at the top of the Miami luxury automotive market.

This isn't a dealer that happens to sell exotic cars. It's a curated experience built around the world's most extraordinary machines, staffed by people who genuinely live and breathe this world. Here's the full story of who they are, what they offer, and why buyers from across the United States — and the world — choose The Collection.

History: Four Decades of Excellence in Coral Gables

The Collection was founded in 1986 by Irma and Marc Auerbach, opening its doors in Coral Gables at a time when Miami was still finding its footing as a global luxury market. The timing proved prescient. As Miami's real estate boom transformed the city through the late 1990s and 2000s, the clientele for $300,000 sports cars grew with it.

Unlike multi-brand mega-dealers that treat exotic brands as prestige props in otherwise conventional operations, The Collection built its identity around exclusivity and depth. Their Coral Gables campus on Bird Road grew to encompass multiple dedicated showrooms, each tuned to a specific brand's personality and aesthetic expectations.

Today, The Collection operates one of the highest-volume exotic dealership groups in the United States, with a reputation that routinely draws buyers from New York, Los Angeles, Texas, and internationally. Being based in Miami — one of the world's premier destinations for ultra-high-net-worth individuals — hasn't hurt.

The Brands: What You'll Find at The Collection

The Collection holds franchises for some of the most exclusive marques on the planet. Here's a breakdown of what each brand brings to their Coral Gables home:

Ferrari Miami

Ferrari is the emotional core of The Collection's identity. The Coral Gables Ferrari showroom holds a coveted authorized dealer status, allowing them to sell both new-production Ferraris and Ferrari Approved certified pre-owned vehicles. Their allocation of limited models — including the Roma Spider, SF90 Stradale, 812 Competizione, and various Icona and Special Series cars — draws serious collectors who understand that allocation relationships are everything in the Ferrari world.

The service center handles everything from scheduled maintenance to full restoration work, with factory-trained technicians and a parts inventory that few outside of Maranello can match.

Porsche Coral Gables

The Collection's Porsche operation is one of the most comprehensive in South Florida. The full model lineup — 911, Taycan, Cayenne, Macan, Panamera, and the 718 variants — is always represented, with the sports car side given special attention. Their Porsche Exclusive Manufaktur and Porsche Tequipment relationships mean bespoke ordering is genuinely available, not just on paper.

McLaren Miami

The Collection is South Florida's authorized McLaren retailer, handling the full range from the entry GT and Artura through the Super Series and Track variants. With McLaren's recent expansion into electrification and their ongoing development of new platform architecture, The Collection team is positioned to guide buyers through one of the most technically complex lineups in the supercar segment.

Koenigsegg South Florida

Koenigsegg's presence in Miami runs through The Collection, making them one of a small handful of authorized Koenigsegg dealers globally. The Swedish manufacturer produces fewer than 100 cars per year across all models, meaning The Collection doesn't keep Jesko Absoluts or CC850s in stock — but they do maintain the client relationships and allocation access that allow serious buyers to engage with the brand. If you're pursuing a Koenigsegg in the Southeast US, The Collection is your starting point.

Bugatti South Florida

Bugatti's dealer network is among the most exclusive in the world. The Collection's Bugatti authorization connects Miami buyers to the Chiron Super Sport, Tourbillon, and whatever Molsheim produces next. Like Koenigsegg, Bugatti vehicles are typically ordered rather than stocked — The Collection facilitates the bespoke configuration process and manages delivery logistics for clients in the Southeast.

The Coral Gables Campus

The Collection's main campus sits in the heart of Coral Gables, Miami's most elegant municipality and home to some of the highest residential property values in Florida. The location is deliberate: Coral Gables clients arrive expecting a certain level of discretion and refinement, and The Collection delivers.

LocationAddressBrands
The Collection Main Campus250 Giralda Ave, Coral Gables, FL 33134Ferrari, Koenigsegg, Bugatti
The Collection PorscheCoral Gables CampusPorsche full lineup
The Collection McLarenCoral Gables / Miami areaMcLaren full lineup

The showrooms themselves are architectural statements. Floor-to-ceiling glass, track lighting calibrated for automotive color rendering, and enough square footage to let each car breathe without visual clutter. Unlike many exotic dealers that cram every available square foot with inventory, The Collection edits its floor displays carefully.

The Buying Experience

Buying at The Collection is different from buying at a conventional dealership in ways that matter to the clientele. High-pressure sales tactics are absent — not because they've been trained away, but because the client base won't tolerate them. A buyer comparing a $400,000 Ferrari against a $420,000 McLaren doesn't need a closer; they need information, patience, and access.

The Collection's sales team is structured around long-term client relationships rather than single transactions. Many clients have purchased five, ten, or more vehicles over the years. The staff turnover that plagues conventional dealerships is notably absent here — advisors who've been with the dealer for a decade or more aren't unusual.

Key aspects of The Collection buying experience:

  • Dedicated sales advisors with brand-specific expertise
  • Factory ordering with full bespoke configuration support
  • Ferrari Approved and brand-certified pre-owned inventory
  • Financing through manufacturer captive lenders and private banking relationships
  • Consignment and trade-in services for existing exotic vehicles
  • Concierge delivery coordination for out-of-state and international clients

Service Center: Where the Relationship Continues

The purchase is only the beginning. For exotic car owners, the service relationship is as important as the buying experience — and The Collection's service operation is a significant part of their competitive advantage.

Their service center employs factory-certified master technicians for each brand, with proprietary diagnostic equipment and genuine OEM parts. For Ferrari and Porsche in particular, the depth of service capability matters enormously: a Ferrari that misses a scheduled service window can face warranty implications and resale value impact.

The Collection also offers:

  • Scheduled maintenance and warranty service for all brands
  • Performance work and track preparation
  • Collision repair through authorized body shop relationships
  • Storage solutions for seasonal vehicles
  • Detailing and paint protection film installation

Why The Collection Dominates Miami's Exotic Market

Miami has other exotic car dealers. Braman Motors holds significant luxury franchises. Multiple independent exotic dealers operate throughout the metro area. So why does The Collection consistently attract the most serious buyers?

The answer is allocation. In a world where the most desirable cars — limited Ferrari series, Koenigsegg models, Bugatti configurations — are rationed by manufacturers based on relationship history and purchase volume, The Collection's four decades of transaction history gives them priority that newer operations simply can't match. A collector who wants a Ferrari Daytona SP3 doesn't just walk in and order one. They need a dealer with enough standing to secure an allocation — and The Collection is that dealer in South Florida.

Beyond allocation, their reputation for discretion and genuine client service has created a self-reinforcing cycle. High-profile clients — athletes, entertainment figures, real estate developers, finance professionals — choose The Collection partly because other high-profile clients choose The Collection. The social proof is real and valuable.

Events and Community

The Collection hosts and participates in events throughout the year that reinforce their position in Miami's automotive community. New model unveilings, brand-exclusive client dinners, driving experiences, and participation in larger events like the Concours d'Elegance at the Biltmore keep the dealership connected to the culture rather than operating as a pure retail operation.

Their involvement with Ferrari's client motorsport programs — track days, driving experiences at circuits like Homestead-Miami Speedway — gives clients experiences that go beyond ownership into genuine performance.

Visiting The Collection

Whether you're ready to buy, exploring options, or simply want to see some of the world's finest automobiles in person, The Collection in Coral Gables is worth the visit. The showroom is open during regular business hours, and the staff is accustomed to enthusiasts who arrive without buying intent — though they're equally prepared when you do.

For buyers pursuing specific allocations, factory orders, or pre-owned inventory, the best approach is to reach out directly to a brand-specific advisor rather than walking in cold. The most desirable vehicles never make it to the showroom floor — they're spoken for before they arrive.

In South Florida's exotic car market, The Collection isn't just a dealer. It's the standard against which all others are measured.

title: Aston Martin in Miami: Dealers, Events & the Culture of Britain's Most Beautiful Cars
excerpt: Aston Martin Miami blends British elegance with South Florida glamour. From the DB12 to the DBX707, here's the complete guide to buying, leasing, and the culture around the brand.
content:
There's a particular kind of person who chooses an Aston Martin over a Ferrari or Lamborghini. They want speed, yes — but they also want a car that carries itself with restraint. A car that whispers rather than shouts. A car that a British secret agent might drive. In Miami, where ostentation is rarely punished and often rewarded, Aston Martin's restrained elegance has found a surprisingly devoted audience.

The brand's Miami presence has grown significantly over the past decade, driven by new model releases that have broadened Aston Martin's appeal beyond its traditional grand tourer niche into SUVs, ultra-performance variants, and F1-derived hypercars. Here's everything you need to know about Aston Martin in Miami.

Aston Martin Miami: The Dealership

Aston Martin's South Florida presence is anchored by Aston Martin Miami, the authorized dealer serving the Greater Miami, Broward, and Palm Beach markets. Located in the heart of Miami's luxury automotive corridor, the dealership represents the full current model lineup and handles both new car sales and Aston Martin Certified Pre-Owned inventory.

Unlike some exotic dealers where Aston Martin is a secondary brand, this is a brand-dedicated operation. The showroom design follows Aston Martin's global visual identity — dark tones, dramatic lighting, a spare elegance that mirrors the cars themselves. Staff are brand specialists rather than generalists, a distinction that matters when you're deciding between a DB12 grand tourer and a Vantage roadster.

The service operation is factory authorized, employing technicians trained by Aston Martin Works (the brand's official service and restoration division). This matters for warranty compliance, but also for the increasingly complex electronics and AMG-sourced powertrain components that underpin modern Aston Martin vehicles.

The Current Lineup: Models Available in Miami

Aston Martin's current model range is the most diverse in the brand's history, spanning grand tourers, sports cars, a high-performance SUV, and a mid-engine hypercar. Here's what Miami buyers are considering:

DB12: The Grand Tourer Reinvented

The DB12 is Aston Martin's current flagship grand tourer and arguably the most important car in the lineup. Powered by a 671-horsepower twin-turbocharged 4.0-liter V8 sourced from AMG, it reaches 60 mph in 3.5 seconds while maintaining the long-distance luxury that DB-series Astons have always delivered.

SpecDB12
Engine4.0L Twin-Turbo V8 (AMG-sourced)
Power671 hp
0-60 mph3.5 seconds
Top Speed202 mph
Starting Price~$245,000

In Miami's market, the DB12 competes directly with the Ferrari Roma, Bentley Continental GT, and Porsche 911 Turbo S. It wins on visual distinction and the emotional weight of the Aston Martin nameplate.

Vantage: The Sports Car

The current Vantage represents a sharper, more focused take on the Aston Martin formula. Available as coupe and roadster, it uses the same AMG V8 in a 665-hp tune and sits lower, wider, and more aggressively than the DB12. The Vantage is the car for buyers who want genuine sports car credentials without sacrificing the Aston Martin character.

Miami's driving environment — long stretches of US-1, the MacArthur Causeway, Alligator Alley on weekend blasts to Naples — suits the Vantage well. It's not a track car, but it rewards spirited driving in a way that grand tourers never quite do.

DBX707: The Supercar SUV

The DBX707 is Aston Martin's answer to a question nobody knew they needed answered: what if the world's fastest SUV was also genuinely beautiful? Powered by a 707-horsepower version of the AMG V8, it reaches 60 mph in 3.1 seconds and tops out at 193 mph — numbers that embarrass most dedicated sports cars.

In Miami, the DBX707 is arguably Aston Martin's most relevant model. The city's car culture prizes practicality alongside performance, and an SUV that can carry golf clubs, a family, and still destroy a Lamborghini Urus off the line is exactly the kind of value proposition that resonates here. It also sits at a useful price point: starting around $240,000, it's expensive but accessible relative to the V12-powered Vantage or the DBS series.

Vanquish and DBS: The Flagship GT

For buyers who want Aston Martin's most powerful expression in a conventional body style, the DBS and upcoming Vanquish represent the pinnacle of the brand's non-hypercar lineup. These cars carry V12 heritage and price tags that reflect it — typically $340,000 and above.

Miami Events: Where Aston Martin Shows Up

Aston Martin's presence in Miami extends beyond the dealership into the city's broader luxury events calendar:

Art Basel Miami Beach

Aston Martin has maintained a presence at Art Basel Miami Beach for several years, typically through activations in the Design Miami fair or branded spaces in Wynwood and the Design District. The brand's intersection of performance and aesthetics resonates with the art world audience, and Art Basel week's concentration of ultra-high-net-worth individuals represents fertile ground for brand engagement.

Festivals of Speed

The annual Festivals of Speed events at Palazzo Versace (now the EAST Miami Hotel area) and Aventura regularly feature Aston Martin as a featured marque. These events draw serious collectors and enthusiasts who appreciate the brand's motorsport heritage alongside its design lineage.

Dealer Events and Private Previews

Aston Martin Miami hosts private client events around major model launches and special editions. These typically take place at the dealership or at selected venues in Coral Gables and Coconut Grove. If you're on the dealer's client list, invitations arrive via email and sometimes personal calls.

Celebrity Sightings: Aston Martin in Miami's Culture

Aston Martin has always attracted a specific type of high-profile owner — one who values understatement over spectacle. In Miami, where Ferrari and Lamborghini ownership is almost the default for wealthy car enthusiasts, an Aston Martin stands out precisely because it doesn't try to. Notable figures in Miami's sports, entertainment, and finance communities have been associated with various Aston Martin models over the years, drawn by the brand's combination of British heritage, genuine performance, and design language that hasn't needed to shout in seven decades.

Leasing vs. Buying: What Makes Sense in Miami

Aston Martin vehicles can be acquired through purchase, financing, or lease. For Miami buyers, the choice involves several local-market considerations:

The Case for Leasing

Aston Martin has accelerated its model cycle significantly in recent years, driven by the shift to AMG powertrains and increasing competition in the ultra-luxury segment. For buyers who want to stay current with the model lineup, leasing offers a way to drive a new Aston Martin every 3 years without managing residual value risk.

  • Typical lease terms: 36-48 months, 10,000-15,000 miles/year
  • Strong residual values protect monthly payments
  • No exposure to exotic car depreciation curves
  • Florida's no-sales-tax-on-leases structure benefits some buyers

The Case for Buying

Aston Martins have historically been poor long-term investments — with the notable exception of limited-production special series that tend to appreciate. For buyers who will use the car heavily, plan to modify it, or simply prefer ownership psychology, purchase makes more sense.

  • No mileage restrictions for road trip enthusiasts
  • Freedom to modify (aftermarket exhaust, wheel upgrades)
  • Certain special editions (One-77, Valkyrie, limited DBS Superleggera variants) have investment upside
  • Financing available through Aston Martin Financial Services and third-party lenders

Aston Martin Ownership in Miami: Practical Considerations

Insurance: Exotic car insurance for an Aston Martin in South Florida typically runs $3,000-$8,000 annually depending on the model, driver profile, and coverage level. Hagerty, Chubb, and AIG are common choices among Miami Aston Martin owners.

Service intervals: Modern Aston Martins require annual service or every 10,000 miles, whichever comes first. Service at an authorized dealer runs $800-$1,500 for routine maintenance, more for brake service, tire replacements, or major intervals.

Climate considerations: Miami's heat and humidity are harder on exotic cars than most owners expect. Proper storage (climate-controlled if possible), regular coolant system checks, and attention to rubber seals and gaskets are important for South Florida ownership.

Is Aston Martin Right for You?

Among the options in the $200,000-$350,000 sports car segment, Aston Martin occupies a specific emotional and aesthetic territory. If you want the car that turns heads at The Biltmore on a Sunday morning, earns respect from serious automotive enthusiasts, and delivers a driving experience with genuine character rather than synthetic perfection — an Aston Martin is hard to beat in Miami's market.

The dealer relationship matters significantly with this brand. Aston Martin Miami's team is equipped to guide buyers through configuration choices, secure allocation on limited models, and provide the ownership support that justifies the premium. Start there.

  • Leasing an Aston Martin in Miami: Complete Guide for 2026
  • Best Convertibles for Miami in 2026: The Ultimate Drop-Top Living Guide

title: Koenigsegg for Sale: How to Buy the World's Most Exclusive Hypercar
excerpt: Fewer than 100 Koenigseggs are built each year. Here's how to get one — models, pricing, the allocation process, Miami dealers, and what ownership actually costs.
content:
You don't simply walk into a dealership and buy a Koenigsegg. The Swedish manufacturer, founded by Christian von Koenigsegg in 1994, produces fewer than 100 cars per year across its entire global operation — making them rarer than Bugatti, rarer than Pagani, and available to a smaller group of clients than almost any other automobile on earth.

If you're searching "Koenigsegg for sale," you're either a serious collector ready to engage with a genuinely complex acquisition process, or you're doing research. Either way, this guide covers everything: the models, production numbers, pricing, how allocation works, Miami's role in the Koenigsegg ecosystem, and what ongoing ownership actually costs.

The Models: What Koenigsegg Currently Produces

Koenigsegg's current lineup is simultaneously small in number and enormous in scope. The brand occupies the absolute apex of production hypercar performance, with powertrain technology and aerodynamic solutions that regularly appear years ahead of the broader industry.

Jesko: The 1,600-Horsepower Track and Road Weapon

Named after Christian von Koenigsegg's father, Jesko Åke von Koenigsegg, the Jesko comes in two variants that represent the clearest expression of the brand's current technical philosophy:

VariantPowerFocusProductionEst. Price
Jesko1,600 hp (E85)Road/track balance125 units total~$3.0M USD
Jesko Absolut1,600 hpTop speed record attempt125 units total~$3.0M USD

The Jesko Absolut is designed to exceed 300 mph — a figure that, if achieved in official testing, would make it the fastest production car in history. The 9-speed Light Speed Transmission (LST) can engage any gear from any gear without sequential shifting, representing a fundamental reimagining of transmission design.

All 125 Jesko units were sold before the car was formally announced at the 2019 Geneva Motor Show. If you want a Jesko, you're looking at the pre-owned market — and prices have increased significantly from original sticker.

Gemera: The Four-Seat Hypercar

The Gemera may be the most technically audacious production car ever announced. A four-seat, four-door hypercar with a 2.0-liter three-cylinder "Tiny Friendly Giant" (TFG) engine paired with three electric motors for a combined output of 1,700 horsepower. Zero emissions range for urban driving. 1,700 horsepower available at any moment. Four actual adults comfortably seated.

SpecGemera
Combined Output1,700 hp
0-60 mph1.9 seconds
Top Speed250+ mph
Seating4 adults
Production300 units
Est. Price~$1.7M USD

Production units are currently in client delivery. At 300 units, the Gemera is actually the highest-volume model in Koenigsegg history — though that's relative to the brand's standards, not the industry's.

CC850: The Anniversary Edition

Released in 2022 to celebrate 50 years of Koenigsegg, the CC850 is a tribute to the original CC8S that launched the brand in 2002. It combines a 1,385-horsepower twin-supercharged V8 with an extraordinary transmission innovation: a dual-clutch automatic that can also operate as a traditional 6-speed manual. The driver can choose their experience in real time.

SpecCC850
Engine5.0L Twin-Supercharged V8
Power1,385 hp (E85) / 1,185 hp (98 RON)
TransmissionKoenigsegg Light Speed Transmission (manual/DCT)
Production50 units
Est. Price~$4.0M USD

With only 50 units, the CC850 is among the most exclusive production cars ever built. All were allocated to existing Koenigsegg clients before public announcement.

Regera: The Hybrid Flagship (Previous Generation)

The Regera, now out of production but appearing regularly on the pre-owned market, remains one of the most technically impressive cars ever built. Its hybrid system — a combustion engine driving the rear axle through a hydraulic coupling, combined with three electric motors — produces over 1,500 horsepower with absolutely no conventional transmission. The car accelerates from 0 to 250 mph in 20 seconds.

Pre-owned Regeras trade between $3.5M and $5M+ depending on specification and provenance.

Production Numbers: Why Koenigsegg Is Truly Scarce

Understanding Koenigsegg's scale is essential for understanding the acquisition process. This is not artificial scarcity — it's the genuine output of a Ängelholm, Sweden factory that employs roughly 600 people and builds each car largely by hand over several months.

  • Annual global production: Approximately 50-100 cars across all models
  • Comparison: Ferrari builds ~13,000 cars/year; Lamborghini builds ~10,000+
  • Worldwide authorized dealers: Approximately 25 globally
  • US authorized dealers: Fewer than 10

When demand for any given model consistently exceeds supply by factors of 10:1 or more, the economics of acquisition change fundamentally. Koenigsegg doesn't sell cars at sticker price to anonymous buyers. They sell to known collectors whose relationship with the brand justifies the allocation of a car that hundreds of others want.

How to Get a Koenigsegg Allocation

The allocation process is the most important concept for anyone seriously pursuing a new Koenigsegg. Here's how it works in practice:

Step 1: Establish a Relationship with an Authorized Dealer

In the United States, Koenigsegg allocation flows through a small network of authorized dealers. In South Florida, The Collection in Coral Gables holds the regional Koenigsegg authorization and serves as the primary access point for Southeast US buyers.

Establishing a relationship means visiting the dealer, expressing serious intent, and — critically — demonstrating purchase history with luxury and exotic vehicles. A first-time exotic car buyer pursuing a Jesko allocation is not going to be successful. A collector with a Ferrari, McLaren, and Pagani in the garage who has worked with The Collection for several years is a different conversation.

Step 2: Register Your Interest for Specific Models

When Koenigsegg announces a new model or opens production slots, the factory works with dealers to fill allocations from their existing client lists. Registering interest means a formal conversation with the dealer, often accompanied by a refundable deposit to demonstrate seriousness.

Step 3: Configuration and Factory Interaction

If you receive an allocation, the specification process begins. Koenigsegg offers extensive personalization — paint colors, interior materials, carbon fiber trim options, and performance specifications that can be tuned to the client's preference. Some buyers fly to Ängelholm to visit the factory during their car's build, which Koenigsegg actively encourages.

Step 4: Delivery

New Koenigsegg deliveries can include the option of personal delivery at the factory, a driving experience in Sweden, and factory handover ceremony. For US buyers, vehicles are then transported to the authorized dealer for domestic delivery.

The Pre-Owned Market: Finding a Koenigsegg for Sale Today

Given that most new Koenigsegg models are sold before public announcement, the pre-owned market is the realistic path for many buyers. Key sources:

Authorized Dealer Pre-Owned Programs

The Collection and other authorized Koenigsegg dealers occasionally have pre-owned inventory, either from trade-ins or client consignments. These offer the best combination of vetting and transaction support.

Specialist Exotic Brokers

Miami's exotic car broker community includes several operators who specialize in ultra-rare hypercars. Firms like RK Motors, duPont Registry (based in St. Petersburg, FL), and specialist brokers operating out of Miami's Design District can source Koenigsegg vehicles through international networks.

Online Marketplaces

duPont Registry, Exotic Car Trader, and occasionally Cars & Bids or Bring a Trailer list Koenigsegg vehicles. Pricing on the pre-owned market ranges widely:

  • Agera RS: $5M-$10M+ depending on specification
  • Regera: $3.5M-$5.5M
  • Jesko (if/when available): $4M-$6M+
  • CC850: likely $5M+ given 50-unit production

Maintenance and Ownership Costs

Owning a Koenigsegg involves costs and considerations that differ significantly from even other exotic cars:

ExpenseEstimated Annual CostNotes
Annual Service$15,000-$40,000+Factory-recommended service at authorized dealer
Tires$5,000-$15,000/setCustom Michelin or Pirelli fitments
Insurance$25,000-$60,000/yearSpecialty exotic insurers: Chubb, AIG, Hagerty
Storage$3,000-$10,000/yearClimate-controlled, security-monitored preferred
Transport$2,000-$8,000 per moveEnclosed transport for shows, service, events

Koenigsegg vehicles require service by factory-trained technicians. In the US, this means your car may occasionally need to travel to an authorized service center rather than being serviced locally. The factory in Ängelholm also handles major service work, which some clients use as an opportunity to visit Sweden.

Is a Koenigsegg the Right Hypercar?

At this level of the market, the rational analysis matters less than the emotional and philosophical alignment with the brand. Koenigsegg's appeal is specific: they are the world's most technically ambitious manufacturer, operating outside the constraints of public markets, legacy structures, or brand management by committee. Christian von Koenigsegg personally oversees engineering decisions that would be delegated five layers down at any conventional automaker.

If that narrative resonates — if you want the car that represents the absolute frontier of what's mechanically possible, built by people who genuinely believe they can outperform anyone — then Koenigsegg is the answer. The scarcity is real, the acquisition process is demanding, and the ownership experience is unlike anything else in the automotive world.

Start with The Collection in Coral Gables. Tell them what you're looking for. Be patient and prepared to demonstrate your seriousness. The world's most exclusive hypercar is worth the effort.

title: Miami Car Meets & Events Calendar 2026: The Complete Guide
excerpt: From Cars & Coffee Aventura to Art Basel supercars, here's the definitive 2026 guide to every major car meet, show, and automotive event in Miami.
content:
Miami's car culture is year-round, sun-soaked, and genuinely world-class. With a concentration of exotic and luxury vehicles that rivals Los Angeles and New York, the city's automotive event scene has evolved from informal weekend gatherings into a calendar of major shows, curated meets, and events that draw participants and spectators from across the country.

Whether you drive a Ferrari F40 or a clean E46 M3, whether you're a concours collector or a JDM enthusiast, Miami has an event for you. Here's the complete 2026 guide to car meets, shows, and automotive events in the Miami area — organized by event type and month.

Monthly Recurring Events: The Backbone of Miami's Car Culture

Cars & Coffee Aventura

Cars & Coffee Aventura is arguably the premier recurring automotive event in South Florida. Held on the first Saturday of every month at the Aventura Mall (19501 Biscayne Blvd), the event draws 200-500 vehicles ranging from stock daily drivers to seven-figure exotics, with attendance varying by weather and season.

DetailInfo
FrequencyFirst Saturday of every month
Time7:00 AM – 10:00 AM
LocationAventura Mall, 19501 Biscayne Blvd, Aventura
EntryFree (participants and spectators)
What to ExpectExotics, classics, JDM, muscle, coffee vendors

The Aventura location is perfect — the mall's large parking area accommodates the event without disrupting regular traffic, and the Biscayne Boulevard corridor is itself a showcase for the drive in. Arrive before 7:30 AM if you want a good spot; the prime real estate fills up fast, and the most notable cars tend to leave by 9:00 AM as the South Florida heat becomes a consideration.

What to bring: Camera, walking shoes, sunscreen. Coffee is available from food trucks. There's no judging or competition — this is a come-as-you-are gathering built around shared enthusiasm.

Cars & Coffee Brickell

The Brickell edition runs on irregular Saturdays (check @cncbrickell on Instagram for dates) and draws a younger, more urban crowd reflecting the neighborhood's demographic. Locations rotate through the Brickell area, sometimes at the Miami Worldcenter adjacent lots or near Brickell City Centre.

DetailInfo
FrequencyMonthly (verify dates via Instagram)
Time7:00 AM – 10:00 AM
LocationRotating Brickell venues
VibeModern exotics, tuned cars, Wynwood-adjacent culture

Supercar Saturdays Florida

Supercar Saturdays Florida (SSF) has been one of South Florida's most consistent automotive events for over a decade. Founded as a premium gathering for supercar and exotic car owners, SSF events run monthly and attract a curated mix of Ferraris, Lamborghinis, McLarens, Porsches, and occasionally rarer machinery from manufacturers like Koenigsegg, Pagani, and Bugatti.

DetailInfo
FrequencyMonthly
TimeTypically 8:00 AM – 11:00 AM
LocationRotating South Florida venues (check superfcarsaturdays.com)
EntryFree for spectators; participant registration for some events
HighlightConsistently high-end inventory; organized by enthusiasts for enthusiasts

SSF's curation distinguishes it from general Cars & Coffee events. The organizers actively shape the vehicle mix, which results in a higher average car quality and a tighter community feel. If you want to see multiple Ferraris, Lamborghinis, and occasionally a Pagani or two in one place without the chaos of larger public events, SSF is your event.

Annual Events: The Marquee Calendar

Festivals of Speed (January & October)

The Festivals of Speed is South Florida's most prestigious automotive lifestyle event series, running twice annually (typically January and October) at the Pebble Beach-adjacent grounds at the Boca Raton Resort & Club and occasionally Miami venues.

2026 EventEstimated DatesLocation
Festivals of Speed – WinterJanuary 2026Boca Raton Resort & Club / Miami area
Festivals of Speed – FallOctober 2026TBD (check festivalsofspeed.com)

The Festivals of Speed events combine a curated automobile display — think Italian exotics, classic American muscle, and contemporary hypercars — with a luxury lifestyle marketplace, watches, aviation, and fine dining. Tickets run $50-$150 for general admission, with VIP packages available. The car quality is consistently spectacular; it's one of the few events where you'll reliably see Bugattis, Koenigseggs, and original Ferrari GTOs sharing a lawn.

Art Basel Miami Beach (December)

Art Basel, held annually the first week of December at the Miami Beach Convention Center, isn't a car show — but for automotive collectors, it's one of the most important weeks of the year. The concentration of ultra-high-net-worth collectors, the presence of every major luxury and exotic brand activation, and the generally elevated atmosphere make Art Basel week a de facto automotive event.

What happens at Art Basel for car people:

  • Major brands (Ferrari, Lamborghini, Porsche, Rolls-Royce) run activations in the Design District and Wynwood
  • Dealer events and private preview dinners for clients
  • Informal displays of collector cars throughout South Beach and the Design District
  • Car auctions (sometimes Gooding & Company or RM Sotheby's run satellite sales)
  • Notable vehicles arrived by their owners from New York, LA, and internationally

In 2026, Art Basel Miami Beach is scheduled for December 3-7. The surrounding week (December 1-8) sees the broader "Basel week" art and luxury ecosystem activate across the metro area. If you own something worth showing, keep it out of the garage this week.

Miami Concours (Spring)

The Miami Concours, typically held in March or April, is the area's premier formal concours d'elegance-style event. Unlike the casual car meets, the Concours features judged competition across categories — pre-war classics, post-war European, American muscle, Italian GT, and contemporary hypercars — with awards for preservation, restoration quality, and overall best-in-show.

Venues have included the grounds of the Biltmore Hotel in Coral Gables, which provides the appropriate architectural backdrop for concours-caliber machinery. Entry is juried — submitting a vehicle for consideration requires an application and acceptance isn't guaranteed.

The Best Drives: Where Miami Car Culture Happens on the Road

Beyond organized events, Miami's car culture plays out on specific roads and routes that enthusiasts return to regularly:

The MacArthur Causeway (US-41)

The causeway connecting downtown Miami to Miami Beach, with the bay on both sides and the skyline as backdrop, is Miami's most photogenic automotive corridor. On Friday and Saturday evenings, the causeway becomes an informal showcase as exotic car owners cruise between the mainland and South Beach.

Alligator Alley (I-75 toward Naples)

For owners who want to actually use their cars, the I-75 stretch from Miami to Naples through the Everglades offers long, straight, low-traffic sections that demonstrate what a 600-horsepower sports car was built for. This is where Sunday morning drives go when they get serious.

Brickell to Coconut Grove via Bayshore Drive

The stretch of Bayshore Drive and South Bayshore Drive connecting Brickell to Coconut Grove is one of the few genuinely scenic urban drives in Miami — waterfront views, canopy roads, and good sightlines that let you actually see the car in motion.

Tips for Attending Miami Car Events

Arrive early. Every Miami car event worth attending fills up quickly. For C&C Aventura, 7:00 AM arrival is ideal. By 8:30 AM, parking spaces are full and the early crowd is beginning to leave.

Check social media for updates. Miami's car event scene runs substantially on Instagram. Follow @cncaventura, @superfcarsaturdays, @festivalsofspeed, and local enthusiast accounts for schedule changes, location updates, and last-minute additions.

Respect the culture. Miami's car events have worked hard to maintain good relationships with venue managers and local authorities. Burnouts in parking lots, aggressive driving on departure, and disrespecting businesses that host events are the fastest way to get events cancelled. The community self-polices this effectively.

Engage the community. The best part of Miami's car events isn't the cars — it's the community. Owners are generally happy to talk about their cars. Ask questions, share knowledge, and don't be afraid to introduce yourself. The Miami car community, despite its reputation for exclusivity, is genuinely welcoming to enthusiasts who approach with genuine interest.

Finding More Events

The Miami automotive event calendar is more dynamic than any single article can capture. For comprehensive, up-to-date listings:

  • Cars & Coffee Aventura — @cncaventura
  • Festivals of Speed — festivalsofspeed.com
  • Art Basel — artbasel.com/miami-beach (December)

Miami's car culture is one of the city's genuine treasures — an organic community built around shared enthusiasm that cuts across the social and economic stratification that defines so much of Miami life. Whether you park a $4 million Koenigsegg or a $40,000 Civic Type R, if you love cars, you belong at these events.

title: Best Rolling Tool Chests & Garage Cabinets for Car Enthusiasts in Miami (2026)
excerpt: Your Miami garage deserves better than a pile of tools on a folding table. These rolling tool chests and cabinets keep everything organized, mobile, and ready for your next weekend wrench session.
content:
Here's a truth most car enthusiasts learn the hard way: the limiting factor in your home garage isn't skill or ambition — it's organization. You can have $5,000 worth of Snap-on wrenches, but if they're scattered across three milk crates and a cardboard box, you'll spend more time hunting for a 10mm socket than actually turning bolts.

In Miami especially, garage organization matters more than you'd think. The humidity corrodes unprotected tools fast, so having enclosed drawers with felt liners isn't a luxury — it's preservation. And if you're working in a two-car garage with an exotic that needs to stay pristine, a rolling cabinet that moves where you need it (and tucks away when you don't) is the difference between a functional workspace and a frustrating one.

We evaluated the best rolling tool chests and garage storage cabinets available on Amazon, focusing on build quality, drawer capacity, mobility, and value for the serious home mechanic.

Quick Comparison

ProductDrawersMaterialPrice RangeBest For
Milwaukee Heavy Duty Tool Chest Combo16Steel$800–$1,000Serious home mechanics who want pro-grade quality
DEWALT ToughSystem 2.0 Rolling Tool BoxModularStructural Foam$180–$250Mobile mechanics who need portability
Sunex Premium Full Drawer Service Cart8Steel$350–$500Track-side or driveway detailing stations
CRAFTSMAN 2000 Series Rolling Tool Cabinet5Steel$250–$350Best value for a full-size rolling cabinet
Goplus 6-Drawer Rolling Tool Chest6Steel$150–$220Budget-friendly starter chest

1. Milwaukee Heavy Duty Tool Storage Combo — The Professional Standard

If you've ever walked into a professional shop and admired those red steel cabinets with the buttery-smooth drawers, this is the home version. Milwaukee's Heavy Duty combo pairs a top chest with a rolling cabinet for 16 total drawers of organized storage. The 100-lb rated drawer slides are the real star — they glide like they're on ball bearings (because they are) and hold serious weight without sagging.

At roughly $800–$1,000, this isn't impulse-buy territory. But consider what it replaces: years of accumulated random toolboxes, bags, and "I'll organize it later" piles. The power strip built into the cabinet back is a nice touch for Miami garage sessions where you're running a DA polisher and a shop light simultaneously.

Why it works in Miami: The powder-coated steel construction resists the humidity that turns cheaper cabinets into rust factories. The keyed locking system also matters if your garage doubles as a common area in a condo building.

👉 Check price on Amazon

2. DEWALT ToughSystem 2.0 Rolling Tool Box — Maximum Portability

Not everyone has a dedicated garage bay. If you're working in a Miami condo parking spot, a friend's driveway, or mobile detailing at car meets, you need storage that moves. The DEWALT ToughSystem 2.0 is a modular system: a rolling base connects to stackable boxes, drawers, and organizers that click together with metal latches.

The IP65 water resistance rating is genuinely useful in Miami, where an afternoon thunderstorm can appear in 15 minutes. Your tools stay dry even if you get caught out. The telescoping metal handle and oversized wheels roll smoothly across uneven garage floors and driveways.

Best use case: The car enthusiast who works on their car at the track, at friends' garages, or anywhere that isn't a permanent shop. Also excellent as a supplementary system alongside a stationary cabinet.

👉 Check price on Amazon

3. Sunex Premium Full Drawer Service Cart — The Rolling Workstation

Service carts are different from tool chests. They're lower, wider, and designed to roll right up to whatever you're working on — which is exactly what you want when you're detailing an engine bay or doing brake work in the driveway. The Sunex 8057 (their premium full-drawer model) has 8 drawers with liner mats included, a tool-tray top, and 450-lb capacity casters.

What makes this a Miami garage essential is the work surface. That top tray becomes your staging area for fasteners, chemicals, microfiber towels — whatever the current job demands. Roll it next to the car, work, roll it back. No more walking back and forth to a wall-mounted cabinet.

Pro tip: Pair this with a full-size stationary chest. Use the Sunex cart for your most-used tools (the 20% of tools you reach for 80% of the time) and keep the rest in the main cabinet.

👉 Check price on Amazon

4. CRAFTSMAN 2000 Series Rolling Tool Cabinet — Best Value Full-Size

CRAFTSMAN won't win any luxury awards, but their 2000 Series rolling cabinet is the best bang-for-buck in full-size garage storage. Five deep drawers with ball-bearing slides, a keyed lock, and a solid powder-coat finish for around $250–$350. That's less than half the price of the Milwaukee combo, and for a home enthusiast who isn't wrenching daily, it's genuinely all you need.

The 26-inch width fits comfortably in single-car garages and the 900-lb total capacity means you can load it up without worry. Drawer depth accommodates larger tools like torque wrenches and breaker bars without jamming.

The catch: The drawer slides aren't as smooth as Milwaukee or Snap-on, and the lock mechanism feels a bit toyish. But for the price? No complaints.

👉 Check price on Amazon

5. Goplus 6-Drawer Rolling Tool Chest — Budget Starter

If you're just getting into working on your own car and don't want to drop $500+ on storage, the Goplus 6-drawer chest is a legitimate starting point. At $150–$220, it gives you a top chest and bottom cabinet with casters. The steel is thinner than premium brands and the drawers don't have the satisfying weighted feel of a CRAFTSMAN or Milwaukee, but everything functions.

This is the "gateway drug" tool chest. You'll use it for two years, outgrow it, upgrade to something better, and either keep the Goplus for overflow storage or sell it on Facebook Marketplace (where garage equipment moves fast in Miami).

👉 Check price on Amazon

What to Look For in a Garage Tool Chest

Drawer Slides Matter Most

Ball-bearing slides vs. friction slides is the single biggest quality differentiator. Ball-bearing slides are smooth, durable, and support more weight. Friction slides work but they'll stick, especially in Miami humidity. Every pick above uses ball-bearing slides.

Rust Protection

Miami's salt air is murder on bare steel. Look for powder-coated finishes (not just paint) and consider adding silica gel packets to drawers if your garage isn't climate-controlled. Drawer liners aren't just for organization — they prevent tools from sweating against bare steel and creating rust spots.

Caster Quality

If you're rolling a loaded cabinet across a garage floor, cheap casters make it a wrestling match. Look for 5-inch or larger wheels with at least two locking casters. Polyurethane wheels are quieter and smoother on epoxy or concrete than hard rubber.

Lock It Up

In Miami, where garage break-ins happen (especially in multi-unit buildings), a keyed lock isn't paranoia — it's insurance. Every full-size cabinet on this list includes locking mechanisms. If yours doesn't, add a hasp lock to the top drawer.

The Bottom Line

A good tool chest is a multiplier — it makes every garage session faster, more organized, and more enjoyable. The Milwaukee combo is the endgame purchase for serious home mechanics. The CRAFTSMAN 2000 Series is the sweet spot of price and quality. And the DEWALT ToughSystem is unmatched for portability. Pick the one that matches how and where you work, and you'll wonder how you ever functioned without it.

title: Best Portable Power Stations for Car Detailing & Garage Use in Miami (2026)
excerpt: Whether you're running a DA polisher in a driveway without outlets or keeping your garage tools powered during a Miami hurricane, a portable power station is the most underrated car enthusiast investment.
content:
Here's a scenario every Miami car enthusiast has faced: you want to polish, buff, or detail your car outside — maybe the light is better, maybe the garage is packed, maybe you're at a car meet — and there's no outlet within 100 feet. Extension cords get sketchy past 50 feet (voltage drop kills motor tools), and generators are loud, heavy, and smell like an old lawnmower.

Portable power stations solve this quietly. They're essentially giant lithium batteries with AC outlets, USB ports, and DC outputs built in. Charge them overnight from a wall outlet (or from solar panels, if you're feeling Miami-eco), and they'll run a polisher, shop vacuum, work lights, phone chargers, and a Bluetooth speaker simultaneously for hours.

They're also hurricane insurance. Miami gets at least one serious storm threat per season, and when the power goes out for 2–5 days (it happens), a good power station keeps your phone charged, your fridge running, and your sanity intact. That alone justifies the investment.

Quick Comparison

1. EcoFlow DELTA Pro — The Garage Powerhouse

If you want to run a full detailing setup — DA polisher (800W), shop vacuum (1,200W), LED work lights, and charge your phone — the DELTA Pro handles all of it simultaneously without breaking a sweat. The 3,600Wh capacity and 3,600W output mean you can genuinely run power tools for an entire afternoon detailing session on a single charge.

It's also the best hurricane prep in this roundup. With the optional Smart Generator or extra battery (sold separately), you can keep a refrigerator running for 2+ days during a power outage. In Miami, where FPL outages after storms can stretch for days, that's not hypothetical — it's annual planning.

The catch is weight (99 lbs) and price. This isn't something you casually toss in a trunk. It lives in your garage and rolls out on the included wheels when needed.

Miami use case: Permanent garage power backup that doubles as a portable detailing station. If your condo doesn't have outlets in the parking area (common in Brickell and Downtown high-rises), this solves the problem permanently.

👉 Check price on Amazon

2. Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 — The Sweet Spot

For most car enthusiasts, the Jackery 1000 v2 is the right answer. It has enough capacity (1,070Wh) to run a DA polisher for 60–90 minutes continuously, powers USB-C fast charging for phones and laptops, and weighs only 22 lbs — light enough to carry with one hand.

The LiFePO4 battery chemistry is the upgrade over the original Explorer 1000. It's rated for 4,000+ charge cycles (roughly 10 years of regular use), handles Miami heat better than standard lithium-ion, and charges from 0–80% in under 2 hours via wall outlet.

This is also the unit you throw in the car for track days at Homestead. Run a tire pressure gauge, inflate tires with an electric pump, charge walkie-talkies, and keep phones topped up all day.

Why it wins: The power-to-weight ratio is unmatched. You get genuine tool-running capability without needing a hand truck to move it.

👉 Check price on Amazon

3. Anker Solix C300 DC — The Ultralight Companion

At 7.7 lbs, the Anker C300 DC is barely heavier than a laptop. It won't run a polisher or shop vac, but it will keep phones, tablets, dash cams, and USB-powered accessories running all day at car meets, shows, or outdoor events. The 300W output can handle a small work light or soldering iron for minor electrical jobs.

Think of this as the complement to your main power station, not a replacement. Keep it in the trunk permanently as an emergency backup and daily convenience unit. It charges from a car's 12V outlet while you drive, so it's always ready.

Best for: Car meet regulars, mobile phone photography/videography at shows, and as an emergency phone charger during Miami hurricane season.

👉 Check price on Amazon

4. Goal Zero Yeti 1500X — The Premium Pick

Goal Zero pioneered the portable power station category, and the Yeti 1500X shows their experience. The build quality is noticeably above competitors — the aluminum housing feels like it belongs in a professional setting, the display is clear and informative, and the output ports are intelligently arranged (not crammed together like some competitors).

At 1,516Wh and 2,000W output, it sits between the Jackery 1000 v2 and the EcoFlow DELTA Pro in capability. It'll run a polisher, charge tools, and handle a partial home backup during outages. The modular expansion system lets you add extra batteries later if your needs grow.

Why pay the premium: Build quality, customer support, and a brand that's been doing this longer than anyone. If you buy tools based on durability rather than spec sheets, this is your station.

👉 Check price on Amazon

5. BLUETTI AC200P — Best Mid-Range Heavy Duty

The BLUETTI AC200P gives you 2,000Wh of capacity and 2,000W of output at a price point that significantly undercuts the EcoFlow DELTA Pro and Goal Zero Yeti. If you need serious power for extended detailing sessions or garage backup but don't want to spend $2,000+, this is the practical choice.

The 60-lb weight means it's not ultra-portable, but it's manageable — think of it as a semi-permanent garage fixture that occasionally travels. It has 17 output ports including a wireless charging pad on top, which is genuinely convenient during garage sessions.

Miami value play: For the price of the EcoFlow DELTA Pro, you could buy the BLUETTI AC200P AND a smaller backup unit. If budget matters, that's a smarter split than one premium unit.

Power Station Sizing for Common Detailing Tools

ToolWattageRuntime on 1,000Wh StationRuntime on 2,000Wh Station

Runtimes are approximate. Actual performance depends on inverter efficiency (typically 85–90%) and tool power draw variation.

What to Consider Before Buying

AC Output Wattage vs. Capacity

These are different numbers that get confused constantly. Output wattage (measured in watts) determines what tools you can run simultaneously. Capacity (measured in watt-hours) determines how long you can run them. A 2,000W / 1,000Wh station can run a 1,000W tool — but only for about an hour. A 1,500W / 3,000Wh station can't run a 2,000W tool at all, but it can run a 1,000W tool for three hours.

Battery Chemistry

LiFePO4 (lithium iron phosphate) is the newer standard and better for Miami's heat. It handles high temperatures without degradation, lasts 3–5x longer than standard lithium-ion (measured in charge cycles), and is safer. The Jackery 1000 v2 and newer models use LiFePO4. Older units may use standard lithium-ion — they still work but won't last as long in Florida heat.

Charging Speed

Fast charging (0–80% in 1–2 hours) is a genuine convenience. If you forgot to charge overnight and have a morning detail appointment, fast charging saves the day. EcoFlow and Jackery lead here; Goal Zero is slower.

The Bottom Line

A portable power station is one of those purchases that seems like a luxury until you use it — then it becomes indispensable. For Miami car enthusiasts, the dual-purpose value (detailing power + hurricane backup) makes the ROI obvious. The Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 is the best all-around pick for most people. The EcoFlow DELTA Pro is the answer if budget isn't a constraint and you want garage-grade power anywhere.

title: Best Garage Floor Coatings & Epoxy Kits for Miami Car Enthusiasts (2026)
excerpt: A clean, coated garage floor isn't just cosmetic — in Miami's humidity, it protects against moisture damage, makes spills easy to clean, and turns your parking spot into a proper showroom for your car.
content:
Walk into any serious car enthusiast's garage and look down. Chances are the floor isn't bare concrete — it's a polished, coated surface that looks like it belongs in a dealership showroom. That's not vanity. A properly coated garage floor is one of the highest-ROI upgrades you can make to your home workspace, especially in Miami where humidity, moisture intrusion, and salt air conspire to turn bare concrete into a crumbling, stained mess.

A good epoxy or polyurea coating does four things: it seals the concrete against moisture migration (critical in Miami where water literally pushes up through slabs during rainy season), it makes oil and chemical spills wipe up in seconds instead of permanently staining, it reflects overhead lighting to brighten the space, and yes — it makes your garage look incredible.

Here's the truth about DIY garage floor coatings: the preparation is 80% of the job. The actual coating application is straightforward. If you're willing to spend a weekend on surface prep (grinding, cleaning, etching), any of these products will give you professional-looking results.

Quick Comparison

ProductTypeCoveragePrice RangeBest For
Rust-Oleum RockSolid Garage Floor CoatingPolycuramineUp to 500 sq ft$250–$350Best overall — professional results, one-coat application
Rust-Oleum EpoxyShield KitEpoxyUp to 500 sq ft$120–$180Best value — proven formula at a great price
Colored Epoxies Clear Epoxy ResinEpoxy ResinVaries$150–$300Custom color mixing and creative finishes
BEHR Premium Epoxy Floor PaintEpoxy AcrylicUp to 500 sq ft$180–$250Easiest application for DIY beginners
Rust Bullet DuraGrade ConcretePolyurethaneVaries$300–$500Maximum durability and chemical resistance

1. Rust-Oleum RockSolid Garage Floor Coating — Best Overall

RockSolid uses polycuramine rather than traditional epoxy, and the difference is significant. Polycuramine is 20x stronger than epoxy by Rust-Oleum's testing, cures faster (24 hours to foot traffic vs. 72+ for standard epoxy), and doesn't yellow with UV exposure. In Miami, where garage doors are open half the day letting in direct sun, UV resistance isn't optional.

The kit includes everything: coating, decorative chips, etching solution, and application tools. One coat covers up to 500 square feet — a standard two-car garage. The finished look is a high-gloss, showroom-quality surface that makes even a basic garage look like a concours prep bay.

Application tip: Miami's humidity can interfere with curing. Check that the concrete moisture level is below 4 lbs per 1,000 sq ft before applying (cheap moisture test kits are available). Apply in the morning when humidity is lowest, and keep the garage closed during curing.

👉 Check price on Amazon

2. Rust-Oleum EpoxyShield Garage Floor Kit — Best Value

The EpoxyShield has been the go-to DIY garage floor coating for over a decade, and for good reason: it works, it's affordable, and the results look great. At $120–$180 for a full garage kit, it's less than half the price of professional installation and less than the RockSolid while still delivering a solid, attractive finish.

The two-part epoxy formula mixes easily and applies with a standard roller. The kit includes decorative paint chips that you broadcast into the wet coating — they hide minor imperfections in the concrete and add visual depth. Expect about 72 hours before you can drive on it, which means planning your application for a long weekend.

Honest take: The EpoxyShield isn't as durable as the RockSolid or professional polyurea coatings. In a Miami garage where you're driving on it daily with hot tires, you might see wear in high-traffic areas after 3–5 years. But at this price, recoating every few years is still cheaper than a single professional application.

👉 Check price on Amazon

3. Colored Epoxies Clear Epoxy Resin Coating — For Custom Finishes

If you want something beyond solid gray or tan, Colored Epoxies gives you the ability to create truly custom floors. Their clear epoxy can be tinted to any color, layered over metallic pigments for that liquid-metal look you see in high-end showrooms, or applied clear over stained concrete for a natural but protected finish.

This is more of a "project" product than a kit-in-a-box. You'll need to calculate coverage, buy pigments separately, and follow a more involved application process. But the results can be stunning — think the kind of metallic, swirling floors you see at exotic car dealers in the Design District.

Best for: The enthusiast who wants their garage floor to be as much of a statement as the car parked on it. Pair with color-matched walls and good lighting and you've built a proper car cave.

👉 Check price on Amazon

4. BEHR Premium Epoxy Concrete & Garage Floor Paint — Easiest DIY

BEHR's one-part epoxy is as close to "paint your garage floor" as it gets. No mixing ratios, no pot life to worry about, no two-component chemistry that panics first-timers. Open the can, stir, roll it on. It's an acrylic-epoxy hybrid that doesn't match the hardness of true two-part systems, but the ease of application is a genuine advantage.

For condos and townhomes in Miami where you might need to coat a single-car garage or parking spot, the simplicity is the selling point. You can reasonably start and finish in a single Saturday. The satin finish hides minor imperfections better than high-gloss options.

Durability note: This is the least durable option on the list. Expect 2–3 years in a daily-use garage before you see wear. Think of it as a maintenance item (recoat periodically) rather than a permanent solution.

👉 Check price on Amazon

5. Rust Bullet DuraGrade Concrete — Maximum Durability

Rust Bullet DuraGrade is polyurethane-based rather than epoxy, which gives it superior chemical resistance and impact durability. This is the product for the garage where you're actually working on cars — where brake fluid gets spilled, jack stands get dragged, and oil drips are a regular occurrence. It handles all of it without staining or peeling.

The application is more involved (multiple thin coats rather than one thick coat), and the price per square foot is the highest on this list. But the finished product is essentially industrial-grade floor protection. Professional shops in Hialeah and Opa-locka use similar polyurethane systems for exactly these reasons.

Miami advantage: DuraGrade tolerates moisture in concrete better than most epoxies, which matters enormously in South Florida where slab moisture is a chronic issue. If previous epoxy coatings have peeled off your garage floor, moisture was likely the culprit — and DuraGrade is the solution.

👉 Check price on Amazon

Miami-Specific Floor Coating Considerations

The Moisture Problem

South Florida's water table is high. Very high. Moisture migrates upward through concrete slabs constantly, and in rainy season (June–October), it intensifies. This hydrostatic pressure is the #1 reason garage floor coatings fail in Miami — the water pushes up from below and delaminates the coating.

The fix: Test for moisture before applying any coating. Tape a 2x2-foot piece of plastic sheeting to the bare concrete, seal the edges, and wait 24 hours. If moisture collects underneath, you need a moisture-mitigating primer before your topcoat. Rust-Oleum and Ghostshield both make concrete sealers designed for this.

Hot Tire Pickup

When you drive in Miami, your tires get hot. When you park on a freshly coated floor, hot tires can soften cheaper coatings and literally peel them up when you drive away. This is called "hot tire pickup" and it's the most common complaint about budget garage floor products in Florida.

The RockSolid polycuramine and Rust Bullet DuraGrade both resist hot tire pickup. Standard epoxies (including the EpoxyShield) can be vulnerable — a clear topcoat helps significantly.

UV Exposure

If your garage faces south or west (common in Miami), direct sunlight will yellow standard epoxies within a year. Polycuramine (RockSolid) and polyurethane (Rust Bullet) are UV-stable. If using standard epoxy, apply a UV-resistant clear topcoat.

Surface Prep Checklist

StepWhat to DoTime RequiredWhy It Matters
1. CleanDegrease entire floor with TSP or concrete degreaser2–3 hoursCoating won't bond to oil or grease
2. RepairFill cracks and divots with concrete patching compound1–2 hours + dry timeCoating follows the surface — cracks telegraph through
3. Etch/GrindAcid etch (muriatic acid) or diamond grind the surface3–4 hoursCreates mechanical bond profile for coating adhesion
4. Moisture TestPlastic sheet test or calcium chloride test24 hoursDetects hydrostatic pressure that causes delamination
5. DryAllow 24–48 hours of dry time after etching24–48 hoursSurface must be completely dry for coating adhesion

The Bottom Line

A coated garage floor transforms your space from utilitarian parking to proper car storage. In Miami's humid, salt-air environment, it's also functional protection for your concrete. The Rust-Oleum RockSolid is our top pick for the best combination of durability, looks, and DIY-friendliness. The EpoxyShield kit is the smart budget choice. And if your floor has persistent moisture issues (common in South Florida), the Rust Bullet DuraGrade's tolerance for imperfect conditions makes it worth the premium.

Whichever you choose: don't skip the prep work. A $300 coating on properly prepared concrete will outlast a $500 coating on concrete that wasn't cleaned and etched. The weekend you spend on prep is the weekend that makes the next 5–10 years look effortless.

title: How Miami Became the Hypercar Capital of America
excerpt: From tax advantages to year-round driving weather, here's why more hypercars per capita call Miami home than any other U.S. city — and what it means for the market in 2026.
content:
Drive down Collins Avenue on any given Saturday and you'll see more seven-figure machinery than most cities witness in a year. A Bugatti Chiron idles at a red light next to a Pagani Huayra. A Koenigsegg Jesko rolls out of a Bal Harbour valet. This isn't a concours — it's just Miami being Miami.

But Miami's status as America's undisputed hypercar capital didn't happen by accident. It's the result of a perfect storm of economics, demographics, climate, and culture that's been building for over a decade. Here's how it happened — and why it's accelerating in 2026.

The Tax Advantage That Started It All

Florida has no state income tax. That single fact has been the gravitational pull drawing wealthy car collectors from New York, California, and Illinois for years. When you're saving millions annually in state taxes, dropping million on a Pagani Utopia feels less like a splurge and more like a rounding error.

But it goes deeper than income tax. Florida's vehicle registration and titling process is relatively straightforward compared to states like California, which imposes additional smog requirements and luxury taxes. For hypercar owners who frequently buy, sell, and trade vehicles, Miami's regulatory environment is remarkably friction-free.

Year-Round Driving Weather

Most hypercar owners in northern states garage their machines from November through April. That's half the year where a million car sits under a cover, depreciating and collecting dust. In Miami, there's no winter storage season. You can drive a Rimac Nevera on Christmas Day with the windows down.

This year-round usability fundamentally changes the ownership calculus. A hypercar in Miami isn't just a garage queen or investment vehicle — it's actual transportation. And when you can actually use a car, the emotional justification for buying one gets much easier.

The Dealer and Service Ecosystem

Miami now has one of the densest networks of exotic and hypercar dealers in the world. The numbers tell the story:

Dealer / GalleryLocationSpecialtyNotable Inventory
The CollectionCoral GablesFerrari, Porsche, Maserati, Aston MartinSouth Florida's largest multi-brand luxury dealer
