The MC20 Coupe weighs just 3,306 pounds — lighter than a Porsche 911 Turbo S and dramatically lighter than its Italian competition. Combined with a carbon-fiber monocoque tub, double-wishbone suspension at all four corners, and a mid-engine layout, it delivers a driving experience that punches well above its price class.

Where to Find a Maserati MC20 for Sale in Miami

Miami has several reliable channels for sourcing an MC20:

Authorized Maserati Dealers

  • Maserati of Central Florida — One of the highest-volume Maserati dealers in the Southeast, regularly stocking new and certified pre-owned MC20s.
  • The Collection (Coral Gables) — Miami's premier multi-brand luxury dealer carries Maserati alongside Ferrari and Alfa Romeo. Their pre-owned inventory often includes MC20 coupes and Cielos.
  • Rick Case Maserati (Fort Lauderdale) — Just north of Miami, frequently has MC20 allocation and trade-ins.

Independent Exotic Dealers

  • Prestige Imports (North Miami Beach) — Carries a rotating selection of pre-owned exotics including MC20s.
  • The Barn Miami — Known for curated exotic inventory at competitive prices.
  • iLusso — Online-first exotic dealer with a large MC20 selection and delivery to Miami.

Private Sales & Auction Platforms

  • Bring a Trailer — MC20s are starting to appear regularly, often selling below dealer retail.
  • Cars & Bids — Another strong auction platform for modern exotics.
  • DuPont Registry — The traditional luxury car marketplace, always listing MC20 inventory from Florida sellers.

MC20 vs. the Competition: How It Stacks Up in Miami

The MC20 competes in an interesting space — priced below the core Ferrari and Lamborghini lineup but delivering comparable or superior performance.

CarPower0–60WeightMiami Price Range
Maserati MC20621 hp2.9s3,306 lbs$175K–$270K
Ferrari F8 Tributo710 hp2.9s3,164 lbs$280K–$350K
Lamborghini Huracán EVO631 hp2.9s3,351 lbs$230K–$310K
McLaren Artura671 hp3.0s3,303 lbs$225K–$280K
Porsche 911 GT3502 hp3.2s3,164 lbs$220K–$280K

The MC20 offers arguably the best value proposition in this group. It matches or beats the 0–60 times of cars costing $100,000+ more, and its exclusivity factor in Miami is high — you'll see ten Huracáns for every MC20 on the streets of South Beach.

Maserati MC20 Buyer's Checklist for Miami

Before you pull the trigger on an MC20, here's what to watch for:

Pre-Purchase Inspection

  • Nettuno engine health: The pre-chamber combustion system is advanced technology. Have an independent specialist check for any turbo or oil consumption issues on higher-mileage examples.
  • Suspension alignment: Miami's roads are notoriously rough. Check for signs of pothole damage to the double-wishbone front suspension.
  • Paint and body: Florida sun is brutal on Italian paint. Look for fading, especially on darker colors, and ensure any PPF (paint protection film) coverage is documented.

Ownership Costs

  • Insurance: Expect $3,500–$6,000/year in Miami depending on driving record and coverage levels. Surprisingly reasonable for a supercar.
  • Maintenance: Annual service runs $1,500–$2,500 at authorized dealers. Major service (every 3 years or 30,000 miles) can reach $5,000–$8,000.
  • Tires: Budget $2,000–$3,000 for a set of Bridgestone Potenza replacements.
  • Depreciation: Early MC20s have stabilized on the secondary market, suggesting the worst depreciation has passed.

Miami-Specific Considerations

  • Salt air: If you're near the coast, undercarriage and brake component corrosion is a real concern. Ceramic coating for the underbody is a worthwhile investment.
  • Heat management: The MC20 handles heat well, but ensure the AC system is fully functional — mid-engine cars with small cabins get hot in Miami summers.
  • Ride height: The MC20 has a nose-lift system. Make sure it works — Miami's parking garages and restaurant valet ramps will test your ground clearance daily.

Should You Buy the MC20 Folgore Instead?

The MC20 Folgore is Maserati's all-electric version, and it deserves serious consideration for Miami buyers. With 740 horsepower from three electric motors, all-wheel drive, and a 2.8-second 0–60 time, it's the fastest MC20 variant. The tri-motor setup gives it a torque-vectoring capability that transforms the handling character.

However, the Folgore weighs nearly 4,500 pounds — over 1,100 pounds more than the coupe — and its range sits around 250 miles. For Miami daily driving, the range is more than adequate. The weight penalty shows up mainly on track days. If you're prioritizing street driving and want the lowest running costs, the Folgore is compelling. If you want the purest driving experience, the V6 coupe remains the choice.

The Bottom Line on Buying a Maserati MC20 in Miami

The Maserati MC20 for sale market in Miami is hitting a sweet spot in 2026. Early coupes are available below $200,000 — supercar performance for the price of a well-equipped Porsche 911 Turbo. The Cielo offers drop-top thrills perfectly suited to Miami's climate, and the Folgore brings cutting-edge EV technology to the mid-engine formula.

With fewer than 5,000 MC20s produced globally through 2024, it remains a genuinely rare sight even in Miami's supercar-saturated streets. For buyers who want something special without the Ferrari or Lamborghini price of entry — and who appreciate engineering over badge snobbery — the MC20 is one of the smartest exotic car purchases you can make in 2026.

title: Porsche 911 GT3 for Sale in Miami: 2026 Pricing, Specs & Buyer's Guide
excerpt: The Porsche 911 GT3 is the purist's sports car — a naturally aspirated, high-revving masterpiece. Miami's market has strong inventory across generations. Here's your complete guide to buying one.
content:
Few cars command the reverence of the Porsche 911 GT3. With its naturally aspirated flat-six screaming to 9,000 RPM, race-derived suspension, and a driving experience that borders on religious, the GT3 has been the benchmark track-day sports car for over two decades. If you're looking for a Porsche 911 GT3 for sale in Miami, you're shopping in one of the deepest and most active Porsche markets in the United States.

South Florida's Porsche culture is enormous — from weekend meetups at Supercar Saturdays to track days at Homestead-Miami Speedway. Here's everything you need to know about buying a GT3 in Miami in 2026.

Porsche 911 GT3 Pricing in Miami: 2026 Market Overview

The Porsche 911 GT3 price varies significantly by generation. The current 992-generation GT3 still commands premiums, while earlier generations have become increasingly accessible. Here's the Miami market breakdown:

GenerationYearsPowerMiami Market PriceMSRP When New
991.1 GT32014–2016475 hp, 3.8L$130,000–$175,000$131,000–$143,000
991.2 GT32018–2019500 hp, 4.0L$165,000–$220,000$144,000–$161,000
992 GT32022–2024502 hp, 4.0L$210,000–$280,000$162,000–$180,000
992 GT3 Touring2022–2024502 hp, 4.0L$225,000–$295,000$163,000–$181,000
992.2 GT3 (facelift)2025–present510 hp, 4.0L$250,000–$320,000+$195,000+

The 991.2 generation remains the sweet spot for many buyers: it introduced the larger 4.0-liter engine, offered a manual transmission option, and can be found under $200,000 for well-maintained examples. The 992 GT3 trades above MSRP at virtually every Miami dealer — a testament to demand that shows no sign of cooling.

Porsche 911 GT3 Specs: What Makes It Special

The GT3 isn't just a faster 911 — it's a fundamentally different machine from the standard Carrera. Understanding the engineering is key to appreciating what you're buying.

Spec992 GT3 (2022–2024)992.2 GT3 (2025+)
Engine4.0L Flat-6 NA4.0L Flat-6 NA
Power502 hp @ 8,400 RPM510 hp @ 8,500 RPM
Torque346 lb-ft @ 6,100 RPM348 lb-ft @ 6,250 RPM
Redline9,000 RPM9,000 RPM
0–60 mph3.2 sec (PDK) / 3.7 sec (MT)3.1 sec (PDK) / 3.6 sec (MT)
Top Speed197 mph199 mph
Weight3,164 lbs (PDK)3,186 lbs (PDK)
Transmission7-speed PDK / 6-speed MT7-speed PDK / 6-speed MT

The defining characteristic is the engine: a naturally aspirated 4.0-liter flat-six derived from the 911 RSR race car. No turbos, no hybrid assistance — just pure mechanical fury that rewards every RPM you wring out of it. The fact that Porsche continues to build a naturally aspirated, 9,000-RPM engine in 2026 makes the GT3 an increasingly rare breed.

Manual vs. PDK: Which Porsche 911 GT3 Should You Buy?

This is the great GT3 debate, and it's especially relevant in Miami where your driving will split between street and track.

Choose the 6-Speed Manual If:

  • You prioritize driving engagement over lap times
  • You want the best long-term value (manual GT3s consistently hold premiums)
  • Most of your driving is on scenic routes like A1A or the Keys
  • You appreciate the mechanical connection of heel-toe downshifts

Choose the 7-Speed PDK If:

  • Track days at Homestead-Miami are a priority — the PDK is roughly 0.5 seconds faster per lap
  • You'll deal with heavy Miami traffic regularly (I-95, Brickell, the Beach)
  • You want launch control and the fastest possible acceleration
  • You plan to do time-attack or competitive events

In the Miami market, manual GT3s command a $15,000–$30,000 premium over equivalent PDK models. For investment purposes, the manual is the clear winner. For pure track performance, the PDK is objectively faster.

Where to Find a Porsche 911 GT3 for Sale in Miami

Miami's Porsche market is one of the largest in the country, with multiple authorized dealers and a massive independent exotic car network.

Authorized Porsche Dealers

  • The Collection (Coral Gables) — One of Florida's top-volume Porsche dealers, frequently has GT3 allocation and pre-owned inventory.
  • Porsche Miami — The city's flagship dealer on Biscayne Boulevard. Strong new allocation and a curated Porsche Approved pre-owned selection.
  • Porsche Fort Lauderdale — Just north, regularly carries GT3 and GT3 Touring inventory.
  • Champion Porsche (Pompano Beach) — The world's number one Porsche dealer by volume. If a GT3 exists, Champion probably has one.

Independent Specialists

  • Prestige Imports (North Miami Beach) — Large exotic inventory, often with GT3s at competitive pricing.
  • iLusso — Online-focused dealer with nationwide delivery and a significant GT3 selection.
  • Exotic Cars of Houston — Frequently ships to Miami buyers; known for transparent pricing.

Private Sales & Auctions

  • Bring a Trailer — The dominant platform for GT3 sales. Excellent price transparency through completed auction data.
  • Rennlist Forums — The Porsche enthusiast community marketplace. Knowledgeable sellers, detailed histories.
  • PCarMarket — Porsche-only auction site with a curated, enthusiast-focused audience.

Porsche 911 GT3 Buyer's Checklist for Miami

The GT3 is generally bulletproof, but there are specific things to inspect — especially in South Florida's climate.

Pre-Purchase Essentials

  • IMS bearing (991.1 only): The 991.1 GT3 uses a different engine architecture than the standard 991, but verify service history. The 4.0L in 991.2+ has no IMS concern.
  • Rear main seal: Some 991-generation GT3s developed minor rear main seal weeps. Check for oil residue around the bell housing.
  • Clutch life (manual models): A GT3 clutch replacement runs $4,000–$6,000 installed. Ask for clutch wear percentage via PIWIS diagnostic data.
  • Track use history: Not a deal-breaker, but heavily tracked GT3s may need brake rotors, pads, and potentially wheel bearings sooner. Request maintenance records.

Ownership Costs in Miami

  • Insurance: $3,000–$5,500/year depending on coverage, driver profile, and whether you add track-day coverage.
  • Annual service: $800–$1,500 at independent Porsche specialists; $1,200–$2,200 at the dealer.
  • Tires: $1,800–$2,800 per set for Michelin Pilot Sport Cup 2s. Miami's hot pavement accelerates rear tire wear — expect to replace rears every 8,000–12,000 miles.
  • Brakes: PCCB ceramic brakes are standard on the 992 GT3. If they need replacement, budget $15,000–$20,000. Iron rotors (available as a delete option) cost $3,000–$5,000 per axle.

Miami-Specific Tips

  • Paint protection film is essential: Florida's highways are littered with debris and road grit. A full front PPF wrap ($2,500–$4,000) will save thousands in paint correction.
  • Choose your color wisely: Darker colors suffer more in Miami's UV exposure. Guards Red, Shark Blue, and lighter PTS colors hold up better than black or dark grey.
  • Rear wing vs. Touring: The GT3's swan-neck rear wing draws attention everywhere in Miami. If you prefer a subtler look — or want to avoid valet "adjustments" — the Touring's retractable spoiler is the stealth option.
  • Homestead-Miami Speedway: One of the biggest advantages of GT3 ownership in Miami is having a world-class track 45 minutes from Brickell. Multiple track-day organizations (PCA, Chin Motorsports, PBOC) run events year-round.

GT3 vs. GT3 Touring vs. GT3 RS: Which One for Miami?

Porsche offers three GT3 flavors, and each has a different personality:

ModelWingManual Available?Best ForMiami Price Premium
GT3Fixed swan-neckYesTrack + street balanceBaseline
GT3 TouringRetractable spoilerYesStreet-focused elegance+$10K–$25K
GT3 RSMassive DRS wingNo (PDK only)Maximum track performance+$100K–$200K

For most Miami buyers, the standard GT3 with a manual transmission is the Goldilocks choice — enough downforce for spirited track use, comfortable enough for daily driving, and the manual adds a layer of engagement that makes every drive on A1A feel special. The Touring is perfect if you want the GT3 experience without the visual drama. The GT3 RS is a dedicated track weapon that happens to be street-legal — brilliant at Homestead, but its aggressive suspension and DRS wing make it a serious commitment for daily Miami driving.

The Bottom Line on Buying a Porsche 911 GT3 in Miami

The Porsche 911 GT3 for sale market in Miami is robust, diverse, and — for the 991 generation — increasingly accessible. Whether you're after a $140,000 991.1 entry point or a $300,000+ 992.2 with all the options, Miami's dealer network and enthusiast community make it one of the best cities in America to buy and own a GT3.

The 911 GT3 is more than a sports car — it's a statement about what matters to you as a driver. In a city full of turbocharged SUVs and flashy badges, the GT3's naturally aspirated flat-six and single-minded focus on driving purity make it something genuinely special. Miami's track access, year-round driving weather, and thriving Porsche community are just the icing on the cake.

title: Mercedes-AMG GT for Sale in Miami: 2026 Pricing, Specs & Buyer's Guide
excerpt: The Mercedes-AMG GT is a front-engine grand tourer with supercar performance. Miami's market has strong inventory from the original two-door to the all-new 2024+ four-door. Here's your complete buying guide.
content:
The Mercedes-AMG GT is Stuttgart's answer to every grand tourer that ever existed — a handcrafted twin-turbo V8 wrapped in some of the most dramatic bodywork Mercedes has ever produced. Whether you're looking at the original two-door coupe and roadster (C190) or the completely reimagined 2024+ four-door (X290), finding a Mercedes-AMG GT for sale in Miami puts you in one of the country's deepest luxury car markets.

Miami's combination of oceanside boulevards, see-and-be-seen culture, and year-round driving weather makes it the natural habitat for the AMG GT. Here's everything you need to know about buying one in 2026.

Mercedes-AMG GT Price Guide: What Miami Dealers Are Charging in 2026

The Mercedes-AMG GT price spans a wide range depending on generation, body style, and trim level. The original C190 generation (2016–2024) has depreciated into genuinely compelling territory, while the new X290-based car commands full sticker and beyond. Here's the current Miami market:

ModelYearsPowerMiami Market PriceMSRP When New

AMG GT S (C190)2016–2020515 hp, 4.0L V8 TT$85,000–$120,000$130,000–$137,000

The sweet spot for value buyers is the C190 AMG GT S — you get the handcrafted 4.0-liter twin-turbo V8, the dramatic long-hood proportions, and supercar-rivaling performance for under $100,000. Meanwhile, the GT R and especially the limited GT R Pro and Black Series have become serious collector pieces, with values climbing steadily in Miami's enthusiast market.

Mercedes-AMG GT Specs: Engineering Breakdown

At the heart of every AMG GT is the M178 (original) or M177 (new generation) handcrafted twin-turbo V8 — each engine signed by a single AMG technician in Affalterbach. Understanding the two generations is critical when shopping.

Original Generation (C190, 2016–2024)

  • Layout: Front-mid engine, rear-wheel drive, rear-mounted transaxle
  • Engine: 4.0L twin-turbo V8 (M178), "hot inside V" turbo placement
  • Transmission: AMG SPEEDSHIFT 7-speed dual-clutch
  • Chassis: Aluminum spaceframe, double wishbone front/multilink rear
  • Body Styles: Coupe, Roadster

New Generation (X290, 2024–present)

  • Layout: Front-mid engine, all-wheel drive (AMG Performance 4MATIC+), rear-axle steering
  • Engine: 4.0L twin-turbo V8 (M177) + 48V mild hybrid (GT 55) or plug-in hybrid (GT 63)
  • Transmission: AMG SPEEDSHIFT MCT 9-speed
  • Chassis: AMG Active Ride Control with active anti-roll stabilization
  • Body Style: Two-door coupe only (for now)

The original C190 is the purer, more analog experience — rear-wheel drive, lighter, and with that incredible long-hood silhouette that recalls the 300 SL. The new X290 is the more technologically advanced car, with AWD, active aero, rear-axle steering, and a sophistication level that puts it squarely against the Porsche 911 Turbo S and Aston Martin Vantage.

Mercedes-AMG GT for Sale in Miami: Where to Shop

Miami's Mercedes dealer network is extensive, and the independent exotic market fills in every gap. Here's where to look for an AMG GT for sale in South Florida.

Authorized Mercedes-AMG Dealers

  • Mercedes-Benz of Miami — Flagship dealer on Biscayne, consistent AMG GT inventory including new-gen allocations.
  • Mercedes-Benz of Coral Gables — Strong pre-owned AMG selection, competitive pricing on C190 models.
  • Mercedes-Benz of Fort Lauderdale — Large CPO inventory, often carries GT S and GT C models at below-market pricing.
  • The Collection (Coral Gables) — Multi-brand luxury dealer with deep AMG expertise and trade-in inventory.

Independent Exotic Dealers

  • Prestige Imports (North Miami Beach) — Consistently stocks AMG GT variants alongside their Lamborghini and Bentley inventory.
  • Exotics Auto Gallery — Specializes in high-performance Germans, frequently has GT R and Black Series listings.
  • HGreg Lux (Pompano Beach) — High-volume luxury dealer with competitive pricing and a wide AMG selection.

Private Sales & Auctions

  • Bring a Trailer — Excellent for C190 GT, GT S, and GT R models with detailed histories and transparent pricing.
  • Cars & Bids — Doug DeMuro's platform regularly features AMG GTs with strong buyer engagement.
  • MBWorld Forums — The Mercedes enthusiast community marketplace for private-party deals.

Mercedes-AMG GT Ownership Costs in Miami

The AMG GT is a handcrafted grand tourer, and ownership costs reflect that pedigree. Here's what to budget beyond the purchase price.

Brakes (pads/rotors)$2,500–$4,000 per axle$3,000–$5,000 per axle (carbon ceramic opt.)
Registration (FL)$400–$800$500–$1,000

Common Maintenance Items to Watch

  • Transmission fluid (C190): The dual-clutch transaxle requires fluid changes every 20,000 miles. Budget $600–$900 at an independent shop.
  • Engine mounts: The C190's front-mid engine placement puts stress on mounts, especially in Miami's stop-and-go heat. Inspect at 40,000+ miles.
  • Air suspension (GT C/GT R): The adaptive suspension uses air struts that can develop leaks after 50,000–60,000 miles. Replacement runs $1,500–$2,500 per corner.
  • Turbo actuators: Early C190 models (2016–2017) had occasional wastegate actuator issues. Verify they've been addressed or replaced under the extended TSB.

AMG GT vs. the Competition: How It Stacks Up in Miami

The AMG GT occupies a unique position — more exotic than a Porsche 911, more comfortable than a McLaren, and with a presence that rivals anything from Italy. Here's how it compares to the cars you'll cross-shop in Miami.

ModelPower0–60 mphMiami Price RangeBest For
AMG GT S (C190)515 hp3.7 sec$85K–$120KValue + drama
Porsche 911 Turbo S (992)640 hp2.6 sec$210K–$260KAll-weather speed
Aston Martin Vantage (2025)656 hp3.4 sec$175K–$210KBritish grand touring
Maserati MC20621 hp3.0 sec$195K–$240KItalian mid-engine exotic
AMG GT 63 (X290)577 hp3.1 sec$195K–$230KTech-forward GT

The C190 AMG GT S is arguably the best performance value on this list — nothing else delivers a handcrafted V8, exotic proportions, and that level of street presence for under $100,000. For buyers with a bigger budget, the new-gen GT 63 trades the old car's raw character for cutting-edge technology and all-weather capability.

Miami-Specific Tips for AMG GT Buyers

  • The C190 Roadster is a Miami icon: If you're considering a C190, the Roadster version was practically designed for Ocean Drive. The soft top operates in under 11 seconds and works at speeds up to 30 mph — perfect for the cruise.
  • Color matters: AMG Solarbeam Yellow, Brilliant Blue Magno, and designo Diamond White are the head-turners in Miami. Darker matte finishes (Selenite Grey Magno) look stunning but require meticulous maintenance in Florida's UV and salt air.
  • The Black Series is an investment: Only 1,700 units were produced worldwide. Miami has a disproportionate concentration of them, and values have been climbing 10–15% annually. If you can find one under $600,000, it's likely to appreciate.
  • PPF is mandatory: Florida highway debris and Miami's construction zones will pepper the AMG GT's long hood. Budget $3,000–$5,000 for full front-end paint protection film immediately after purchase.
  • Skip the carbon ceramic brakes on the C190 (unless tracking): For street driving in Miami, the standard iron brakes are more than adequate and dramatically cheaper to service. Carbon ceramics make sense for GT R owners who track at Homestead.

The Bottom Line on Buying a Mercedes-AMG GT in Miami

The Mercedes-AMG GT for sale market in Miami is one of the strongest in the nation, spanning sub-$80,000 early C190 coupes to seven-figure Black Series collectibles. Few cars offer this combination of handcrafted AMG engineering, head-turning design, and genuine grand touring capability.

For value seekers, the C190 AMG GT S between 2018 and 2020 is the standout — depreciation has done the heavy lifting, and you're left with a car that looks, sounds, and drives like something twice its price. For those wanting the latest technology, the X290-generation GT 63 is a quantum leap in chassis dynamics and refinement. Either way, you're getting one of the most characterful grand tourers money can buy, in a city that appreciates exactly that kind of thing.

title: Porsche Cayenne Turbo for Sale in Miami: 2026 Pricing, Specs & Buyer's Guide
excerpt: The Porsche Cayenne Turbo is the performance SUV that started it all — and Miami is its natural habitat. Here's your complete guide to buying one in 2026, from pricing to ownership costs.
content:
The Porsche Cayenne Turbo is the SUV that proved performance and practicality aren't mutually exclusive — and two decades later, it remains the benchmark that every competitor chases. If you're searching for a Porsche Cayenne Turbo for sale in Miami, you're shopping in one of the model's strongest markets in the entire United States.

Miami's unique cocktail of highway cruising, school runs, weekend getaways to the Keys, and the occasional blast down an empty stretch of Alligator Alley makes the Cayenne Turbo the quintessential South Florida daily driver. Here's everything you need to know about buying one in 2026.

Porsche Cayenne Turbo Pricing in Miami: 2026 Market Overview

The Porsche Cayenne Turbo price varies dramatically by generation, with the first-generation now offering remarkable value and the current third-generation still commanding strong premiums. Here's what the Miami market looks like:

GenerationYearsPowerMiami Market PriceMSRP When New
Cayenne Turbo (955/957)2003–2010450–500 hp, 4.5L/4.8L V8 TT$15,000–$35,000$89,000–$107,000
Cayenne Turbo (92A)2011–2018500–520 hp, 4.8L V8 TT$35,000–$65,000$110,000–$130,000
Cayenne Turbo (9YA)2019–2023541 hp, 4.0L V8 TT$75,000–$110,000$128,000–$145,000
Cayenne Turbo E-Hybrid (9YA facelift)2024–present729 hp, 4.0L V8 TT + electric$145,000–$175,000$155,000–$170,000
Cayenne Turbo GT (9YA)2022–present631–739 hp$160,000–$220,000$182,000–$200,000

The current sweet spot is the 9YA Cayenne Turbo (2019–2023) — Porsche's brilliant 4.0-liter twin-turbo V8 produces 541 horsepower, the interior is thoroughly modern with dual screens, and prices have settled into the $80,000–$100,000 range for well-equipped examples with reasonable mileage. That's a staggering amount of SUV for the money.

Porsche Cayenne Turbo Specs: What Makes It Special

The Cayenne Turbo isn't just a fast SUV — it's an engineering showcase that Porsche uses to demonstrate what's possible when you apply sports car thinking to a five-passenger hauler.

SpecCayenne Turbo (9YA, 2019–2023)Cayenne Turbo E-Hybrid (2024+)Cayenne Turbo GT (2022+)
Engine4.0L Twin-Turbo V84.0L TT V8 + Electric Motor4.0L TT V8 (+ E-Hybrid in 2024+)
Power541 hp729 hp631 hp / 739 hp (E-Hybrid)
Torque567 lb-ft700 lb-ft626 lb-ft / 700 lb-ft
0–60 mph3.7 sec3.4 sec3.1 sec / 3.2 sec
Top Speed177 mph183 mph186 mph / 183 mph
Weight4,850 lbs5,530 lbs4,950 lbs / 5,540 lbs
Transmission8-speed Tiptronic8-speed Tiptronic8-speed Tiptronic
DriveAWD (PTM)AWD (PTM)AWD (PTM)

The defining achievement of the Cayenne Turbo is how it disguises its 4,850+ pound curb weight. Porsche's three-chamber air suspension, rear-axle steering, active anti-roll bars (PDCC), and torque-vectoring rear differential work in concert to make this SUV change direction like something half its weight. It's the reason the Cayenne Turbo GT holds a Nürburgring SUV lap record that embarrasses most sports cars.

Where to Find a Porsche Cayenne Turbo for Sale in Miami

The Cayenne is Porsche's best-selling model, so inventory is strong across Miami's dealer network. Here's where to start your search.

Authorized Porsche Dealers

  • Champion Porsche (Pompano Beach) — The world's largest Porsche dealer by volume. Their pre-owned Cayenne Turbo inventory is typically 10–20 units deep at any given time.
  • The Collection (Coral Gables) — One of Florida's premier luxury dealers with excellent Porsche Approved CPO inventory and financing options.
  • Porsche Miami — The city's flagship store on Biscayne Boulevard. Strong new allocation for the Turbo E-Hybrid and quality pre-owned.
  • Braman Porsche (West Palm Beach) — Worth the drive north for their aggressive pricing and extensive Cayenne selection.

Independent Dealers

  • HGreg Lux (Pompano Beach) — High-volume luxury dealer that frequently prices Cayenne Turbos below market average.
  • Prestige Imports (North Miami Beach) — Mixed exotic inventory often includes well-spec'd Cayenne Turbos as trade-ins.
  • AutoNation — Multiple South Florida locations with a solid Porsche CPO pipeline and competitive financing.

Private Sales & Online Platforms

  • Bring a Trailer — Increasingly popular for Cayenne Turbo sales, especially well-optioned and low-mileage examples.
  • Rennlist Forums — The Porsche enthusiast marketplace where knowledgeable owners sell to knowledgeable buyers.
  • Porsche Finder — Porsche's official CPO search tool aggregates inventory across all US dealers.

Porsche Cayenne Turbo: Key Options and Packages to Look For

Porsche's options list is legendary (and legendarily expensive). When shopping for a used Cayenne Turbo, these options significantly impact both driving experience and resale value in Miami.

Must-Have Options

  • Sport Chrono Package: Adds launch control, the Sport Response button, and a dashboard stopwatch. A $1,300 option new that adds $3,000–$5,000 to resale.
  • PDCC (Porsche Dynamic Chassis Control): Active anti-roll bars that transform the Cayenne's handling. Non-negotiable for the enthusiast buyer.
  • Rear-axle steering: Tightens the turning circle for Miami parking garages and sharpens high-speed stability. A $1,700 option new that's worth every penny.
  • Panoramic sunroof: Standard on some trims, optional on others. Hugely desirable in Miami's market.

Nice-to-Have Options

  • Lightweight Sport Package (Turbo GT only): Carbon fiber roof, titanium exhaust, carbon-ceramic brakes, and Alcantara interior. Adds significant collector value.
  • Air suspension with PASM: Standard on the Turbo but verify — it's the foundation of the car's dual personality.
  • Burmester 3D sound system: A $6,000+ option that makes the cabin a concert hall. Very sought-after in resale.
  • Night Vision Assist: Useful for dark Florida backroads and wildlife detection.

Porsche Cayenne Turbo Ownership Costs in Miami

The Cayenne Turbo is a Porsche, which means ownership costs are premium but manageable if you plan ahead. Florida's lack of state income tax helps offset some of the maintenance budget.

Cost Category9YA (2019–2023)92A (2011–2018)955/957 (2003–2010)
Insurance$2,200–$4,000/yr$1,500–$3,000/yr$1,000–$2,000/yr
Scheduled Service$800–$1,500/yr$1,000–$2,000/yr$1,500–$3,000/yr
Tires$1,200–$2,000/set$1,000–$1,600/set$800–$1,400/set
Brakes (pads + rotors)$2,000–$3,500/axle$1,500–$2,800/axle$1,200–$2,200/axle
Carbon Ceramic Brakes (if equipped)$12,000–$18,000/set$10,000–$15,000/setN/A standard

Generation-Specific Issues to Inspect

First Generation (955/957, 2003–2010)

  • Coolant pipes: The plastic coolant pipes behind the intake manifold are a known failure point. Replacement with aluminum aftermarket pipes is a $1,500–$2,500 job and should be done preventatively.
  • Transfer case: Can develop leaks or whining after 80,000+ miles. Listen for noise during low-speed turns.
  • Air suspension: Struts typically need replacement around 80,000–100,000 miles — $1,000–$1,500 per corner.

Second Generation (92A, 2011–2018)

  • Timing chain guides: The 4.8L V8 can develop timing chain guide wear at high mileage. Listen for rattle on cold start.
  • Adaptive air suspension: More reliable than the first gen but still an aging wear item. Budget for replacement after 70,000 miles.
  • Turbo coolant lines: Can seep coolant at the turbo fittings. Inspect for staining during pre-purchase inspection.

Third Generation (9YA, 2019–present)

  • Generally very reliable: The 9YA Cayenne Turbo has been remarkably trouble-free. Most issues are minor electronic glitches resolved through software updates.
  • PCM screen delamination: Some early 2019–2020 models experienced touch screen issues. Verify or confirm replacement under warranty.
  • Brake dust: The iron brake package produces heavy brake dust — especially noticeable on light-colored wheels in Miami's rain. Consider upgrading pads to a low-dust compound.

Why the Cayenne Turbo Is the Perfect Miami SUV

Miami has no shortage of performance SUVs — the Urus, the DBX, the G 63, the BMW XM. But the Cayenne Turbo has carved out a unique position that makes it arguably the most logical choice for South Florida life.

Practical Performance

  • Towing capacity: 7,716 lbs — enough to tow a boat to the marina, a track car to Homestead, or a loaded trailer to a weekend house in the Keys.
  • Cargo space: 27.2 cu ft behind the rear seats, 60.3 cu ft with seats folded. Practical enough for Costco runs and golf bags.
  • Five real seats: Unlike the Urus's somewhat cramped rear, the Cayenne offers genuine adult space in the second row.

Miami-Specific Advantages

  • Hurricane season capability: AWD, air suspension that can raise ground clearance, and the ability to navigate flooded streets give the Cayenne a practical edge that two-door exotics simply don't have.
  • Valet-friendly: The Cayenne Turbo is fast and luxurious without the anxiety-inducing low ride height of a supercar. You can hand the keys to a South Beach valet without wincing.
  • Year-round comfort: Ventilated seats, quad-zone climate control, and excellent NVH make the Cayenne a sanctuary in Miami's summer heat.
  • Fuel economy: The 9YA Cayenne Turbo delivers 15 city / 19 highway MPG — not great, but significantly better than a Urus (12/16) or G 63 (14/17). The Turbo E-Hybrid adds 25+ miles of electric-only range for local errands.

Cayenne Turbo vs. Cayenne Turbo GT: Which One for Miami?

The Turbo GT represents the ultimate expression of the Cayenne, but is the premium worth it for Miami driving?

FeatureCayenne TurboCayenne Turbo GT
Power541 hp631–739 hp
0–60 mph3.7 sec3.1 sec
SuspensionAdaptive air (PASM)Stiffer springs, retuned PDCC
ExhaustSport exhaust (opt.)Titanium sport exhaust (std.)
Seats18-way adaptive sportFull bucket seats (lightweight)
Ride ComfortExcellentFirm — feels every road imperfection
Miami Price$75K–$110K (used)$160K–$220K (used)

For most Miami buyers, the standard Cayenne Turbo is the smarter choice. Its adaptive suspension handles Miami's often-rough road surfaces with grace, the power is more than sufficient for any real-world scenario, and the price difference funds a lot of options, maintenance, or a second car. The Turbo GT makes sense if you're a track enthusiast who'll regularly use Homestead-Miami Speedway and wants the bragging rights of a Nürburgring-record SUV in the school carpool lane.

The Bottom Line on Buying a Porsche Cayenne Turbo in Miami

The Porsche Cayenne Turbo for sale market in Miami is one of the healthiest luxury SUV segments in the country. Whether you're after a sub-$40,000 second-generation bargain or a $170,000 new Turbo E-Hybrid with 729 horsepower, South Florida's dealer network has you covered.

What makes the Cayenne Turbo special in Miami isn't just its speed — it's the completeness of the package. This is a vehicle that can blast through a track day at Homestead, haul the family to Key West for the weekend, survive hurricane season, and still look like a million bucks in the Design District parking garage. No other performance SUV in this price range delivers that breadth of capability with Porsche's engineering precision.

In a city that demands both performance and practicality from its vehicles, the Cayenne Turbo isn't just a good choice — it's the obvious one.

title: Best Car Paint Protection Kits for Miami's Salt Air & UV in 2026
excerpt: Between Miami's relentless UV, salt-laden ocean air, and road debris on I-95, your exotic car's paint doesn't stand a chance unprotected. Here are the best complete paint protection kits — PPF, ceramic coatings, and combo systems — to keep your investment looking showroom-fresh.
content:
If you own an exotic or luxury car in Miami, paint protection isn't optional — it's survival. The combination of year-round UV bombardment, salt-laden coastal air, limestone dust from endless construction, and the occasional rock chip from I-95 creates a hostile environment for automotive paint that would make a Colorado garage queen weep.

We've tested and researched the best car paint protection kits available in 2026 — from full PPF (paint protection film) systems to ceramic coating bundles to hybrid combo kits that give you the best of both worlds. Every product here was evaluated with Miami's specific challenges in mind: heat resistance, UV stability, hydrophobic performance in tropical downpours, and salt-air durability.

Why Miami Is Uniquely Brutal on Car Paint

Before dropping $200+ on protection products, it helps to understand what you're protecting against:

  • UV Index: Miami averages a UV index of 10-12 in summer — "extreme" on the EPA scale. That's enough to fade unprotected clear coat in under 18 months.
  • Salt air: Within 5 miles of the coast (so basically all of Miami-Dade), airborne salt accelerates oxidation and can pit unprotected paint.
  • Hard water spots: Miami's water is notoriously mineral-heavy. Sprinkler overspray on your car creates etched spots that bond to clear coat within hours in the heat.
  • Construction debris: Limestone dust from Miami's perpetual construction boom settles on surfaces and, when wet, becomes mildly alkaline — enough to damage wax and cheap sealants.
  • Love bugs: Twice a year, these acid-filled insects splatter across every South Florida vehicle and etch paint within 24 hours if not removed.

Best Complete Paint Protection Film (PPF) Kits

PPF is the gold standard for physical protection — a self-healing thermoplastic urethane film that absorbs rock chips, scratches, and environmental contamination. These kits are designed for DIY or professional installation.

XPEL Ultimate Plus PPF Kit

FeatureDetails
CoverageFull front end (hood, fenders, bumper, mirrors)
Film thickness8.5 mil
Self-healingYes — heat-activated
UV resistance10-year warranty against yellowing
Price range$80–$150 (partial kit) / $300–$600 (full front)

XPEL is the industry benchmark, and for good reason. Their Ultimate Plus film has the best self-healing properties on the market — light scratches from car washes and fingernails literally disappear when exposed to heat (which, in Miami, means they heal themselves just sitting in your driveway). The film is optically clear, won't yellow even after years of UV exposure, and has the best edge-seal adhesion of any PPF we've tested.

Miami-specific note: XPEL's hydrophobic top coat sheds water and prevents hard water spot etching — a massive advantage here. The pre-cut kits for popular vehicles (Porsche 911, Lamborghini Urus, Mercedes G-Class) fit precisely and reduce installation time.

Check XPEL Ultimate Plus PPF kits on Amazon →

3M Scotchgard Pro Series PPF Kit

FeatureDetails
CoverageFull front end or custom panels
Film thickness8 mil
Self-healingYes
UV resistance7-year warranty
Price range$60–$120 (partial) / $250–$500 (full front)

3M practically invented PPF, and their Scotchgard Pro Series remains a top-tier choice. It's slightly thinner than XPEL Ultimate Plus but offers excellent clarity and self-healing performance. The main advantage is availability — 3M film and pre-cut kits are widely stocked, and most professional installers in Miami carry it as their primary option.

Check 3M Scotchgard Pro PPF kits on Amazon →

SunTek Ultra PPF

SunTek's Ultra film is the value pick — slightly less expensive than XPEL and 3M but with competitive self-healing and clarity. It's a great choice for protecting daily drivers or for covering additional panels beyond the front end without breaking the budget. The 10-year warranty gives confidence for long-term Miami ownership.

Check SunTek Ultra PPF on Amazon →

Best Ceramic Coating Kits for DIY Application

Ceramic coatings create a semi-permanent chemical bond with your paint that provides UV protection, hydrophobic water beading, and chemical resistance. They don't prevent rock chips like PPF, but they're the best defense against UV fade, water spots, and environmental contamination.

CarPro CQuartz UK 3.0 Kit

FeatureDetails
Durability2+ years
Hardness9H
UV protectionExcellent — blocks UV-A and UV-B
Water contact angle110°+
Kit includes30ml coating, applicator, microfiber towels
Price$65–$80

CQuartz UK 3.0 is the enthusiast community's go-to DIY ceramic coating, and it earned that reputation. The application is more forgiving than most professional-grade coatings — you have a longer working time before it flashes, which matters enormously when you're applying in Miami's heat. The UV protection is outstanding, and the hydrophobic performance means rain and sprinkler water bead off instead of sitting and etching.

Check CarPro CQuartz UK 3.0 on Amazon →

Gtechniq Crystal Serum Light Kit

FeatureDetails
Durability3–5 years
Hardness9H
UV protectionSuperior — dual-layer system
Water contact angle115°+
Kit includes30ml coating, applicator pad, prep spray
Price$80–$110

Gtechniq is the choice of most high-end detailers in Miami, and Crystal Serum Light brings their professional-grade chemistry to a DIY-friendly format. The dual-layer structure (flexible base layer, hard top layer) is specifically designed to resist cracking in extreme temperature cycles — something that matters when your car's paint surface hits 180°F in a Miami parking lot.

Pro tip: Apply this coating in an air-conditioned garage, ideally early morning. Miami humidity above 70% can cause hazing during cure. If you don't have a garage, many Miami self-service detailing bays offer covered, shaded stalls.

Check Gtechniq Crystal Serum Light on Amazon →

Adam's Polishes UV Ceramic Paint Coating Kit

Adam's has built a loyal following for their complete kits that include everything from surface prep spray to the ceramic coating itself. Their UV Ceramic Paint Coating Kit is the most beginner-friendly option — color-coded application steps, clear video instructions, and a forgiving flash time. Durability is 2-3 years with proper maintenance. At $50–$70, it's the best entry point for first-time ceramic coating users.

Check Adam's UV Ceramic Coating Kit on Amazon →

Best PPF + Ceramic Hybrid Combo Kits

The smart play for Miami exotic car owners is combining PPF on high-impact areas with ceramic coating everywhere else. These combo approaches give you physical chip protection where you need it and chemical/UV protection everywhere.

The Recommended Miami Stack

Protection ZoneProductWhy
Hood, front bumper, fenders, mirrorsXPEL Ultimate Plus PPFRock chips from I-95, construction debris
Rocker panels & rear bumperXPEL or 3M PPF partial coverageRoad debris, parking lot dings
All remaining painted surfacesGtechniq Crystal Serum LightUV, salt, water spots, bird droppings
Wheels & calipersCarPro CQuartz DluxBrake dust repellent, salt protection
GlassGtechniq G1 ClearVisionRain visibility, easier bug removal

Total cost for DIY combo kit: $400–$700 in materials (PPF + ceramic coating + wheel coating + glass coating). Professional installation of this same stack in Miami runs $3,000–$6,000 depending on the vehicle, so the DIY savings are substantial if you have the patience and a climate-controlled workspace.

Nexgen Ceramic Spray + PPF Maintenance Bundle

For owners who already have PPF installed and want an easy maintenance layer, Nexgen's ceramic spray provides a quick-apply hydrophobic boost that's safe on PPF, painted surfaces, and glass. It's not a replacement for a full ceramic coating, but it's perfect for maintaining protection between annual detail sessions. The bundle includes spray sealant, detailer, and microfiber towels.

Check Nexgen Ceramic Spray Bundle on Amazon →

Application Tips for Miami's Climate

Applying paint protection products in South Florida requires adjusting standard procedures for heat and humidity:

  • Temperature: Apply ceramic coatings between 60°F–80°F. In Miami, this means early morning (before 9 AM) or in an air-conditioned garage. Panel temperature above 90°F causes premature flashing and streaking.
  • Humidity: Keep humidity below 70% during ceramic coating cure. A dehumidifier in your garage is a worthwhile $200 investment that pays for itself on the first coating job.
  • PPF installation: Use a slip solution with slightly more soap in hot weather — the film becomes more pliable and stretchy in heat, which helps with complex curves but makes repositioning trickier.
  • Cure time: Add 25-50% to manufacturer-recommended cure times in Miami's humidity. If the label says "24 hours before water exposure," give it 36 hours.
  • Surface prep: Miami's hard water means your pre-coating wash should include a water spot remover step. Iron remover is also critical — brake dust and rail dust embed in paint faster in humid, salt-air environments.

What Protection Do Miami's Top Detailers Use?

We talked to several South Florida detailing shops that specialize in exotics. The consensus:

  • Most popular PPF: XPEL Ultimate Plus (used by roughly 70% of Miami's high-end shops)
  • Most popular professional ceramic: Gtechniq Crystal Serum Ultra (the pro-only version of Crystal Serum Light)
  • Most popular DIY ceramic: CarPro CQuartz UK 3.0
  • Most common protection package: Full front PPF + full body ceramic coating — typically $4,000–$7,000 installed for a supercar

Maintenance Schedule for Miami-Protected Cars

TaskFrequencyProduct
Rinseless washWeeklyOptimum No Rinse or CarPro Ech2O
Full contact washBi-weeklypH-neutral shampoo (avoid dish soap)
Ceramic boost sprayMonthlyCarPro Reload or Gtechniq C2v3
Iron/contamination removalQuarterlyCarPro Iron X
Full coating inspectionAnnuallyWater bead test — recoat if beading drops below 90°

The Bottom Line

In Miami, paint protection is an investment, not an expense. A $500 DIY PPF + ceramic coating setup can prevent thousands in paint correction, clear coat failure, and depreciation on your exotic car. The sun, salt, and construction debris aren't going anywhere — but with the right protection stack, your paint can look showroom-fresh years after you drove it off the lot.

For the best value, start with XPEL Ultimate Plus on the front end and CarPro CQuartz UK 3.0 on everything else. If you want maximum durability, upgrade the ceramic to Gtechniq Crystal Serum Light. And regardless of what you choose, get a dehumidifier for your garage — your coating jobs will thank you.

title: Best Cordless Polishers & Detailing Machines for Exotic Cars in Miami (2026)
excerpt: Cordless polishers have finally caught up to their corded counterparts — and for Miami exotic car owners, the freedom to polish anywhere without extension cords is a game-changer. Here are the best cordless machines worth your money.
content:
For years, cordless polishers were a joke — underpowered, short battery life, inconsistent speed. That's no longer the case. In 2026, the latest generation of cordless polishers and detailing machines deliver legitimate professional-grade performance with the freedom to work anywhere: your garage, a parking garage, your driveway, or even a marina dock next to your boat.

For Miami exotic car owners specifically, cordless polishers solve a real problem. Many South Florida homes and condos have garages without convenient outlet placement. Condo parking garages rarely have accessible power. And if your car lives in a storage facility or you detail at car shows, dragging extension cords across a parking lot isn't just inconvenient — it's a trip hazard and a liability.

We evaluated the best cordless polishers available in 2026 based on power output, battery life, ergonomics, and — critically — whether they're safe for exotic car clear coats that are often softer and thinner than mainstream vehicles.

Why Cordless Polishers Matter for Exotic Cars

  • No cord drag across paint: A power cord dragging across a Lamborghini's hood creates micro-scratches. Cordless eliminates this entirely.
  • Better control: Without fighting a cord, you can maintain consistent pressure and angle — critical on curved exotic body panels.
  • Portability: Polish at car shows, storage units, or wherever your car lives. No outlet hunting.
  • Quieter operation: Most cordless models run 10-15 dB quieter than corded equivalents. Your neighbors in Coral Gables will appreciate this at 7 AM.

Best Cordless Dual-Action Polishers

Dual-action (DA) polishers are the safest choice for exotic cars. The random orbital motion makes it virtually impossible to burn through clear coat — even on soft Italian and British paints that are notoriously thin.

Rupes HLR 15 iBrid Nano (Long Neck)

SpecDetails
TypeDual-action (random orbital)
Orbit15mm (aggressive for cordless)
Pad size3-inch / 5-inch (interchangeable neck)
Battery10.8V Li-ion, ~45 min runtime
Weight1.85 lbs (with battery)
Speed range2,000–5,500 OPM
Price$280–$350 (kit with batteries)

The Rupes iBrid is the gold standard of cordless polishing, and the HLR 15 with the long-neck attachment is the configuration every exotic car detailer in Miami reaches for. The 15mm orbit provides genuine cutting ability — enough to remove light swirls and water spot etching without needing a corded machine. The interchangeable neck system lets you switch between 3-inch (for tight areas around badges, vents, and body lines) and 5-inch (for flat panels) in seconds.

Why it's perfect for exotics: The lightweight design and compact size let you polish inside wheel wells, around side mirrors, and in the tight gaps of cars like the McLaren 720S or Ferrari 296 GTB where a full-size polisher can't physically reach. The variable speed control gives you precision on soft Ferrari Rosso Corsa paint that a heavy corded machine can't match.

Battery tip: Buy the kit with two batteries. In Miami's heat, battery performance degrades about 15% — having a spare means you can complete an entire car without waiting to recharge.

Check Rupes HLR 15 iBrid Nano on Amazon →

Milwaukee M12 Variable Speed Polisher/Sander Kit

SpecDetails
TypeDual-action / random orbital
Pad size3-inch
BatteryM12 platform (12V), ~30 min runtime
Weight2.1 lbs
Speed range2,500–14,000 OPM
Price$130–$180 (kit with battery & charger)

If you're already in the Milwaukee M12 ecosystem (and many Miami homeowners are), this polisher is a no-brainer addition. It shares batteries with Milwaukee's massive tool lineup — drills, impacts, lights — so you may already own compatible batteries. The 3-inch pad is sized for spot corrections and detail work rather than full-panel polishing, making it ideal as a supplementary tool.

Best use case: Quick swirl removal on a single panel, spot polishing before a car show, or maintaining a ceramic coating's gloss between professional details. It won't replace a full-size polisher for complete paint correction, but for 90% of maintenance polishing on exotic cars, it's more than enough.

Check Milwaukee M12 Polisher Kit on Amazon →

Flex PXE 80 Cordless Polisher

SpecDetails
TypeDual-action (random orbital + forced rotation)
Orbit8mm, 12mm, or 15mm (interchangeable)
Pad size3-inch
Battery10.8V Li-ion, ~40 min runtime
Weight1.76 lbs
Speed range1,800–4,500 OPM
Price$250–$320 (kit)

The Flex PXE 80 is Rupes' main competitor in the cordless space, and it has one significant advantage: interchangeable orbit drives. You can swap between 8mm (fine finishing), 12mm (all-purpose), and 15mm (aggressive cutting) orbits to match the task. This versatility means one machine handles everything from final-stage jeweling on a Rolls-Royce's piano black trim to removing heavy swirls from a Porsche's guards red paint.

Miami detail shop favorite: Several South Florida mobile detailers carry the PXE 80 as their primary cordless machine because the orbit swap system means they bring one tool instead of three. The forced-rotation mode provides consistent cutting power even at low speeds — something that matters when you're working carefully around carbon fiber trim pieces.

Check Flex PXE 80 Cordless Polisher on Amazon →

Best Cordless Full-Size Polishers (5-inch+)

If you need full-panel coverage and don't want the compromise of a 3-inch pad, these larger cordless options deliver near-corded performance.

TORQ BUF505X 20V Cordless Random Orbital Polisher

SpecDetails
TypeDual-action (random orbital)
Pad size5-inch / 6-inch
Battery20V / 4.0Ah Li-ion, ~50 min runtime
Weight4.5 lbs (with battery)
Speed range1,500–6,800 OPM
Price$180–$230 (kit with battery & charger)

Chemical Guys' TORQ BUF505X is the first cordless polisher that genuinely competes with mid-range corded machines on power and runtime. The 20V / 4.0Ah battery delivers nearly an hour of runtime — enough to polish an entire sedan or handle two to three panels on a supercar before needing a swap. The 5/6-inch pad covers full panels quickly, and the random orbital action is safe on all paint types.

Value proposition: At $180–$230, this is less than the Rupes or Flex by a significant margin while delivering comparable performance for DIY enthusiasts. It lacks the precision of the smaller machines for tight spots, but for flat-panel polishing — hoods, roofs, doors, trunk lids — it's the best cordless value available.

Check TORQ BUF505X Cordless Polisher on Amazon →

Dewalt DCM849 20V MAX XR Cordless Polisher

SpecDetails
TypeDual-action (variable speed)
Pad size5-inch / 6-inch
Battery20V MAX XR (compatible with all Dewalt 20V), ~45 min runtime
Weight5.2 lbs (with battery)
Speed range2,400–5,600 OPM
Price$200–$280 (tool only) / $300–$380 (kit)

Dewalt's entry into cordless polishing was worth the wait. The DCM849 uses the ubiquitous 20V MAX battery platform — meaning if you own any Dewalt cordless tools, you already have compatible batteries. Build quality is tank-like (this is Dewalt, after all), and the electronic speed control maintains consistent OPM under load, which prevents the bogging that cheaper cordless polishers suffer from on large panels.

For the Miami homeowner: If you've got a Dewalt drill, impact, and circular saw in the garage already, adding the DCM849 is a no-brainer. One battery platform, one charger, and you're polishing without buying into a new ecosystem. The 5Ah batteries give the best runtime — spring for those over the 2Ah compact cells.

Check Dewalt DCM849 Cordless Polisher on Amazon →

Best Polishing Compound & Pad Kits to Pair With

A polisher is only as good as the compounds and pads you run on it. These kits are specifically suited for exotic car paints:

Rupes D-A Fine Polishing System Kit

Matched to the iBrid Nano, this kit includes Rupes' proprietary D-A Fine compound and color-coded foam pads. The compound is formulated for soft European paints — it cuts light defects without the aggressive abrasives that can haze Ferrari or Aston Martin clear coats. At $60–$85, it's the complete companion to the iBrid Nano.

Check Rupes D-A Fine Polishing Kit on Amazon →

Meguiar's Microfiber Correction System

Meguiar's Microfiber Correction System uses microfiber cutting discs paired with their D300 compound for one-step correction — cut and finish in a single pass. It's faster than traditional foam pad + compound combinations and produces excellent results on harder German and American paints (Porsche, Corvette, AMG). At $40–$55 for the complete kit, it's the best value in polishing consumables.

Check Meguiar's Microfiber Correction System on Amazon →

Cordless vs. Corded: When Each Makes Sense

ScenarioBest ChoiceWhy
Full paint correction (heavy defects)CordedSustained power over 2-4 hours, no battery swaps
Maintenance polishing (light swirls)CordlessQuick, convenient, no setup time
Tight areas (mirrors, bumpers, vents)Cordless 3-inchCompact size, no cord interference
Mobile / on-location detailingCordlessNo power source needed
Condo/apartment garageCordlessLimited outlets, cord management issues
Home garage with powerEither (cordless for convenience)Personal preference

For most Miami exotic car owners doing maintenance polishing — removing light swirls between professional details, prepping for car shows, or maintaining a ceramic coating's gloss — a cordless polisher is all you need. Save the corded machine for annual or bi-annual full paint corrections.

Polishing Tips for Miami's Climate

  • Never polish in direct sunlight. Miami's UV heats panels to 160°F+ in minutes. Hot panels cause compound to dry instantly, creating marring instead of correction. Always work in shade or a garage.
  • Work early morning or evening. Panel temperature should be below 100°F for optimal compound performance. In Miami, that means before 9 AM or after 6 PM if working outdoors.
  • Use less compound than you think. Miami's heat makes compounds work faster. Start with a pea-sized amount and add only if needed. Over-application creates buildup that's harder to remove in humidity.
  • Keep your pads clean. Salt air and humidity cause compound residue to cake faster. Use a pad brush every 2-3 sections, and swap to a fresh pad more frequently than you would in a dry climate.
  • IPA wipe-down after polishing. Before applying sealant or ceramic coating, use isopropyl alcohol (50/50 with distilled water) to remove all compound oils. Miami's humidity can trap oils under sealant, causing clouding.

Complete Cordless Polishing Setup Under $500

Here's the kit we'd build for a Miami exotic car owner who wants to handle maintenance polishing at home:

ItemPrice
TORQ BUF505X 20V Cordless Polisher Kit$200
Rupes D-A Fine Polishing Kit (compound + pads)$70
Extra 20V 4.0Ah battery$60
Chemical Guys microfiber towels (12-pack)$25
IPA spray bottle + distilled water$15
LED swirl finder light$30
Pad brush / cleaning tool$12

Total: ~$412 — less than a single professional polishing session at most Miami detailing shops, and you'll use it dozens of times.

The Bottom Line

Cordless polishers have crossed the threshold from "novelty" to "necessity" for Miami exotic car owners. The Rupes HLR 15 iBrid Nano is the best overall if budget isn't the primary concern — it's the machine professional detailers trust on million-dollar cars. The TORQ BUF505X offers the best value for full-size cordless polishing. And the Milwaukee M12 or Dewalt DCM849 make sense if you're already invested in those battery platforms.

Whatever you choose, the freedom to polish without cords — no tripping hazards, no dragging across paint, no hunting for outlets in your condo garage — makes the investment worthwhile. Your exotic car's paint will thank you, and so will the resale value when it's time to upgrade.

title: Ferrari 296 GTB for Sale in Miami: 2026 Pricing, Specs & Buyer's Guide
excerpt: The Ferrari 296 GTB is Ferrari's plug-in hybrid V6 supercar — and Miami dealers have them. Here's what to know about pricing, specs, and where to find a 296 GTB for sale in South Florida.
content:
The Ferrari 296 GTB rewrote the rules when it launched. A V6 in a Ferrari? Heresy — until you drive it. The 296 GTB's twin-turbo V6 paired with an electric motor produces 819 horsepower, and it's one of the most exciting Ferraris to come out of Maranello in a decade. If you're looking for a Ferrari 296 GTB for sale in Miami, here's everything you need to know about pricing, specs, and where to find one.

Ferrari 296 GTB Specs & Performance

At the heart of the 296 GTB sits a 2.9-liter twin-turbo V6 — Ferrari's first road-going V6 since the Dino — supplemented by a single electric motor mounted between the engine and the 8-speed dual-clutch transmission. Together, they produce 819 hp and 546 lb-ft of torque.

SpecFerrari 296 GTB296 GTB Assetto Fiorano
Engine2.9L Twin-Turbo V6 + Electric Motor2.9L Twin-Turbo V6 + Electric Motor
Total Power819 hp819 hp
Torque546 lb-ft546 lb-ft
0-60 mph2.9 seconds2.9 seconds
Top Speed205 mph205 mph
Electric Range~16 miles~16 miles
Weight3,395 lbs3,296 lbs (Assetto Fiorano)
Transmission8-Speed DCT8-Speed DCT

The Assetto Fiorano package shaves nearly 100 pounds by adding carbon fiber and Multimatic dampers (the same technology used in the GT3 racing car). It also adds a fixed rear wing and aggressive front splitter. For Miami, where straight-line speed and canyon carving through the Keys are the main use cases, the standard 296 GTB is more than enough — but the Assetto Fiorano is the one collectors want.

Ferrari 296 GTB Pricing in Miami

Here's what you should expect to pay for a Ferrari 296 GTB for sale in the Miami market as of 2026:

Model / ConditionPrice RangeNotes
New 296 GTB (MSRP)$345,000 – $370,000Base before options; options easily add $50K+
New 296 GTB Assetto Fiorano$380,000 – $420,000Limited allocation; dealer markups common
New 296 GTS (Spider)$375,000 – $410,000Convertible version; highly sought in Miami
Used 296 GTB (2023-2024)$310,000 – $360,000Low-mile examples; depreciation has been minimal
Used 296 GTB Assetto Fiorano$370,000 – $430,000Often trading at or above MSRP

Ferrari's allocation system means you typically need a purchase history with an authorized dealer to get a new 296 GTB at MSRP. Miami's two authorized Ferrari dealers — Ferrari of Fort Lauderdale and The Collection in Coral Gables — both handle allocations, but expect a wait. The pre-owned market is your fastest path to ownership.

Where to Find a Ferrari 296 GTB for Sale in Miami

Authorized Ferrari Dealers

  • The Collection (Coral Gables) — South Florida's largest luxury dealer group. They handle new Ferrari allocations and typically have pre-owned 296 GTBs in stock. Located at 200 Bird Road, Coral Gables.
  • Ferrari of Fort Lauderdale — The other authorized dealer serving the Miami metro. About 30 minutes north on I-95, they often have both new allocations and certified pre-owned inventory.

Independent Exotic Dealers

  • Prestige Imports (North Miami Beach) — While primarily a Lamborghini dealer, their pre-owned showroom regularly stocks Ferraris including 296 GTBs.
  • RMC Miami — Trusted independent dealer on NW 36th Street with a rotating inventory of late-model exotics.
  • Curated Miami — Boutique dealer in Wynwood specializing in low-mile, well-specced exotics.
  • South Motors Exotics — Part of the South Motors group in Homestead, they frequently list recent Ferraris at competitive prices.

Online Marketplaces

  • DuPont Registry — The go-to for high-end exotics. Filter by Miami or South Florida for local listings.
  • Bring a Trailer — Auction format with detailed inspections. 296 GTBs appear regularly and often sell below dealer ask.
  • Cars.com / Autotrader — Cast a wider net; filter to 200-mile radius from Miami for shipping convenience.

Ferrari 296 GTB vs. the Competition in Miami

If you're cross-shopping the 296 GTB, here's how it stacks up against the alternatives you'll see on the streets of Brickell and Bal Harbour:

ModelPower0-60Base PriceMiami Factor
Ferrari 296 GTB819 hp2.9s$345KElectric-only mode for Ocean Drive cruising
McLaren 750S740 hp2.7s$318KRaw track performance; less exclusivity
Lamborghini Huracán Tecnica631 hp3.0s$305KV10 sound; attention magnet
Porsche 911 GT3 RS518 hp3.0s$241KTrack weapon; more understated
Maserati MC20621 hp2.9s$217KValue play; less dealer drama

The 296 GTB's killer feature for Miami? eDrive mode. You can cruise up to 16 miles on pure electric power at speeds up to 84 mph. That means silent cruising through South Beach, Coconut Grove, or your gated community — then unleashing 819 horsepower when you hit an open stretch of highway. No other Ferrari offers that duality.

What to Watch Out For When Buying

  • Options matter enormously. A well-optioned 296 GTB can cost $50,000-$80,000 more than a stripped one. Carbon fiber wheels, racing seats, Assetto Fiorano pack, paint-to-sample colors — check the original window sticker carefully.
  • Allocation markups. Some dealers are still charging over MSRP for new allocations. Don't overpay — the pre-owned market is normalizing, and patience saves money.
  • Hybrid system maintenance. The 296 GTB's electric motor and battery add complexity. Make sure any used example has full Ferrari service history. The 7-year maintenance program (included new) is a significant value.
  • Miami salt air. Any Ferrari stored outdoors in South Florida is exposed to salt air corrosion. Check for bubbling around trim, under the hood, and on brake components. A covered garage is non-negotiable.
  • Insurance. Expect to pay $5,000-$10,000+ annually for full coverage in Miami, depending on your driving record and where you live. Get quotes before you buy.

Is the Ferrari 296 GTB a Good Buy in 2026?

The 296 GTB represents Ferrari's future — hybrid power delivering more performance than the outgoing F8 Tributo while being more livable daily. Values have held strong because it's genuinely one of the best driver's cars Ferrari has ever made. For Miami buyers, the electric cruising mode, stunning design, and Ferrari badge make it a near-perfect fit. Just be patient with the buying process, avoid dealer markup traps, and always get a pre-purchase inspection on any pre-owned example.

title: Lamborghini Revuelto for Sale in Miami: 2026 Pricing, Specs & Buyer's Guide

If you're looking for a Lamborghini Revuelto for sale in Miami, you're in the right place — but be prepared for a wait and a serious price tag.

The key number: that V12 revs to 9,500 rpm. In an era of turbocharging, this is the last naturally aspirated V12 Lamborghini will ever make. The sound alone is worth the price of entry — imagine that screaming through the MacArthur Causeway tunnel at full tilt.

Lamborghini Revuelto Pricing in Miami

Where to Find a Lamborghini Revuelto for Sale in Miami

Authorized Lamborghini Dealers

Located on NE 163rd Street, they handle new Revuelto allocations and are the first stop for serious buyers. Their Ad Personam studio lets you configure custom specs for future allocation slots.

Lamborghini Revuelto vs. the Competition

At the $600K+ price point, the Revuelto competes with a rarefied group. Here's how it compares to what you'll see in Miami's most exclusive garages:

Aston Martin Valhalla998 hp2.5s$800KMid-engine; limited production
Porsche 918 Spyder (Used)887 hp2.5s$1.5M+Appreciating classic; collector piece

The Revuelto's trump card in Miami? Presence. Nothing else on the road commands attention like a Lamborghini — and the Revuelto's angular, aggressive design is peak Sant'Agata. The scissor doors, the massive rear diffuser, and the Y-shaped headlights make it unmistakable from any angle. In a city where your car is your calling card, the Revuelto is the loudest introduction money can buy.

What to Watch Out For When Buying a Revuelto

  • Dealer markups are real. Some authorized dealers are adding $100K-$300K over MSRP. If you're buying new, negotiate hard or be willing to wait for the secondary market to cool.
  • Ad Personam options add up fast. Lamborghini's customization program lets you go wild — custom paint, interior materials, stitching, exposed carbon fiber — but a fully loaded Revuelto can approach $800K before markups. Review the build sheet carefully on any pre-owned example to understand what you're paying for.
  • Hybrid complexity. The Revuelto's triple-motor setup is new technology. Ensure any pre-owned example has complete Lamborghini service records. The high-voltage battery pack and electric motors add maintenance considerations that didn't exist with the Aventador.
  • Ground clearance. The Revuelto sits low — very low. Miami's speed bumps, parking garage ramps, and uneven streets in areas like Coral Gables and Little Havana are a real hazard. The front-axle lift system (standard equipment) is essential and should be used liberally.
  • Insurance costs. A Revuelto in Miami will cost $8,000-$20,000+ annually to insure depending on your profile. High-value exotic insurance from Hagerty or Chubb is worth exploring for cars in this price range.
  • Salt air exposure. Like any exotic in South Florida, the Revuelto needs protection from salt air. Paint protection film, ceramic coating, and covered storage are non-negotiable for preserving the finish.

Is the Lamborghini Revuelto Worth It in 2026?

If you want the last naturally aspirated V12 Lamborghini will ever produce, the answer is unequivocally yes — but only at or near MSRP. Paying $300K over sticker on a car that will eventually be available closer to list price is a gamble. The smart play: put your name on the list at Prestige Imports or Lamborghini Broward, configure your dream spec, and wait. If you can't wait, the secondary market has options — just make sure you're paying for the spec and condition, not just the hype.

For Miami, there's no better flagship. The Revuelto is designed for exactly this kind of city: loud, dramatic, impossibly fast, and built to be seen. It's the Aventador's successor, and it earns that title.

title: Porsche Taycan for Sale in Miami: 2026 Pricing, Specs & Buyer's Guide
excerpt: The Porsche Taycan is the electric sports car rewriting the rules in Miami. Here's your complete guide to finding a Porsche Taycan for sale, what each model costs, and where to buy one in South Florida.
content:
The Porsche Taycan has done something no other electric car has managed in Miami: it earned respect from the supercar crowd. In a city powered by V8 rumbles and twin-turbo screams, the Taycan carved out its lane with brutal acceleration, genuine driving dynamics, and a design that looks right at home on Collins Avenue. If you're looking for a Porsche Taycan for sale in Miami, the market in 2026 is stacked with options — from base models under $100K to the fire-breathing Turbo GT at nearly $250K.

Porsche Taycan 2026 Model Lineup & Specs

Porsche offers the Taycan in a dizzying number of configurations. Here's the full 2026 lineup and what each model brings to the table:

ModelPower (hp)0-60 mphRange (est.)Base MSRP
Taycan4024.8s~270 mi$92,900
Taycan 4S5373.7s~260 mi$110,300
Taycan GTS5903.5s~250 mi$136,700
Taycan Turbo6703.2s~245 mi$161,500
Taycan Turbo S7502.6s~240 mi$197,400
Taycan Turbo GT1,0192.1s~215 mi$240,000
Taycan Sport Turismo (wagon)402–1,0194.8–2.1s~250–270 mi$94,900+

The headline: the Turbo GT with the Weissach package is the fastest production Porsche ever built, clocking a Nürburgring lap faster than the 918 Spyder. It produces over 1,000 horsepower on launch control — in a four-door sedan. For Miami, where straight-line speed rules the causeways, that number speaks for itself.

Porsche Taycan Pricing in the Miami Market

Here's what Porsche Taycan pricing actually looks like in South Florida as of April 2026:

Model / ConditionPrice RangeNotes
New Taycan (base)$92,900 – $105,000Configured with typical options
New Taycan 4S$110,000 – $130,000Most popular Miami configuration
New Taycan GTS$136,000 – $160,000The enthusiast's sweet spot
New Taycan Turbo / Turbo S$161,000 – $220,000Fully loaded Turbo S approaches $220K
New Taycan Turbo GT$240,000 – $280,000Weissach package adds ~$30K
Used 2023-2024 Taycan$55,000 – $75,000Strong depreciation = great value
Used 2023-2024 Taycan 4S/GTS$70,000 – $100,000Best bang-for-buck in the lineup
Used 2023-2024 Turbo/Turbo S$95,000 – $145,000Significant savings over new

The used market is where the Taycan gets interesting. The 2023-2024 models depreciated significantly — some base Taycans have lost 40% of their sticker price in two years. For buyers who don't need the absolute latest tech, a certified pre-owned Taycan 4S around $80K is arguably the best performance-per-dollar deal in Miami right now.

Where to Find a Porsche Taycan for Sale in Miami

Authorized Porsche Dealers

  • The Collection Porsche (Coral Gables) — South Florida's flagship Porsche dealer on Bird Road. Massive inventory of new and CPO Taycans. Their showroom usually has 15-25 Taycans in stock at any given time, making it the easiest place to compare trims in person.
  • Braman Porsche (West Palm Beach) — Worth the drive north if The Collection doesn't have your spec. They're one of the highest-volume Porsche dealers in the Southeast and frequently have Turbo GT allocations.
  • Porsche Fort Lauderdale — Another authorized option between Miami and Palm Beach with solid CPO inventory.

Independent & Specialty Dealers

  • Champion Porsche (Pompano Beach) — The world's largest Porsche dealer by volume. Their pre-owned selection is enormous and they often have hard-to-find Taycan specs.
  • iLusso (Miami) — Consignment dealer that occasionally lists higher-spec Turbo S and Turbo GT models at competitive prices.
  • CarMax / Carvana — Don't overlook these for base and 4S models. The online platforms often have competitively priced Taycans with return policies that give buyers peace of mind.

Online Marketplaces

  • Bring a Trailer — Taycans sell regularly on BaT. The auction format sometimes yields below-market pricing, especially for base and 4S models.
  • Cars & Bids — Doug DeMuro's platform has become a solid Taycan marketplace.
  • Autotrader / Cars.com — Filter to the Miami-Fort Lauderdale metro area for the widest selection of dealer-listed inventory.

Porsche Taycan for Sale: New vs. Used in Miami

The new-vs-used calculus on the Taycan is more interesting than most exotics because of how rapidly early models depreciated. Here's the honest breakdown:

FactorBuy New (2026)Buy Used (2023-2024)
Price$93K – $280K$55K – $145K
Battery / RangeLatest chemistry, longest range~5-10% degradation typical
TechnologyLatest infotainment, ADASOlder software (updatable via OTA)
WarrantyFull 4-year / 50K milesRemaining or CPO extension available
Depreciation RiskExpect 30-40% loss in 3 yearsAlready absorbed the big hit
AvailabilityOrder or dealer stockPlentiful in South Florida

Our recommendation: unless you specifically want the Turbo GT or the 2026 model-year updates, a CPO 2024 Taycan GTS is the move. You get 590 horsepower, the sport suspension, GTS-specific tuning, and Porsche's CPO warranty — for roughly the price of a new base model.

Owning a Porsche Taycan in Miami: What to Know

  • Charging infrastructure is solid. Miami-Dade has over 800 public Level 2 chargers and a growing network of DC fast chargers. The Taycan supports up to 270 kW charging, which means a 5-80% fill in about 22 minutes at a compatible station. Porsche's own Electrify America partnership gives Taycan owners 3 years of free 30-minute charging sessions.
  • Range anxiety is a non-issue for daily driving. Most Miami commutes are under 40 miles round-trip. Even the base Taycan's 270-mile range covers a week of typical driving without charging. The only scenario where range matters: a spontaneous Miami-to-Orlando road trip.
  • Insurance runs $2,500 – $6,000 annually. That's significantly less than a comparable gas-powered Porsche 911 Turbo, thanks to lower repair frequency and the Taycan's excellent safety ratings.
  • Miami heat and EV range. Running AC in 95°F heat does reduce range by roughly 10-15%. Plan accordingly for summer road trips, but for daily use, it's barely noticeable.
  • Condo charging. Florida law (FL Statute 718.113) gives condo owners the right to install EV chargers in their parking spaces at their own expense. Most new luxury towers in Brickell and Sunny Isles come with chargers pre-installed.
  • Salt air considerations. The Taycan's aluminum and composite body panels resist corrosion better than steel, but the brake rotors (if you don't opt for PCCB ceramics) will need attention. Regular washing and an annual ceramic coating refresh are smart moves in the salt air.

Porsche Taycan vs. the Competition in Miami

ModelPower0-60RangeBase PriceMiami Factor
Porsche Taycan GTS590 hp3.5s~250 mi$137KBest driver's EV, period
Tesla Model S Plaid1,020 hp1.9s~350 mi$90KFaster, cheaper, less exclusive
BMW i5 M60593 hp3.7s~256 mi$86KPractical, comfortable, less exciting
Mercedes EQS 580536 hp4.1s~350 mi$106KRange king, luxury-first approach
Lucid Air Grand Touring819 hp3.0s~500 mi$139KBest range; less dealer support in FL

The Tesla is faster and cheaper. The Mercedes has more range. But neither drives like a Porsche. The Taycan's steering feel, chassis balance, and braking precision are in a different league — it drives like a 911 that happens to be electric. For Miami buyers who value the driving experience over spec-sheet numbers, the Taycan wins convincingly.

Is the Porsche Taycan Worth Buying in 2026?

Absolutely — especially at used prices. The Porsche Taycan for sale market in Miami has never been more favorable to buyers. New models offer cutting-edge performance, while used examples represent staggering value for what you get. Whether you're replacing a gas-powered 911, adding an EV to your garage, or making the jump from Tesla, the Taycan delivers something no other electric car in this price range can: it makes you want to take the long way home.

Start at The Collection in Coral Gables, browse the CPO inventory online, or hit Bring a Trailer for auction deals. The hardest part isn't finding a Taycan in Miami — it's choosing which one.
