title: Lamborghini Huracán for Sale in Miami: 2026 Pricing, Specs & Buyer's Guide
excerpt: The Lamborghini Huracán is the best-selling Lambo ever — and Miami is the best place to buy one. Here's your complete guide to finding a Lamborghini Huracán for sale, what each variant costs, and how to buy smart.
content:
The Lamborghini Huracán is the most successful Lamborghini ever produced. Over its decade-long run from 2014 to 2024, Lamborghini built more than 20,000 units — and a disproportionate number of them ended up in South Florida. If you're searching for a Lamborghini Huracán for sale in Miami, the market in 2026 is in a sweet spot: production has ended, prices have settled from their pandemic peaks, and the sheer volume of cars means there's a Huracán for nearly every budget from $160K to $500K+.

Lamborghini Huracán Variants & Specs

The Huracán went through more variants than any Lamborghini before it. Understanding the lineup is essential for finding the right one:

VariantYearsPower (hp)0-60DrivetrainKey Feature
LP 610-42014-20196102.9sAWDOriginal; most balanced
LP 580-22016-20195803.4sRWDPurist's choice; tail-happy
Performante2017-20196402.9sAWDALA aero; Nürburgring record
EVO2019-20226402.9sAWDUpdated tech, LDVI system
EVO RWD2020-20226103.3sRWDBest driver engagement
EVO Spyder2019-20226403.1sAWDDrop-top; Miami's favorite
STO2021-20236403.0sRWDTrack weapon; rear-wheel steer
Tecnica2022-20246403.2sRWDBetween EVO RWD and STO
Sterrato2023-20246103.4sAWDOff-road Huracán; lifted, rally-inspired

Every Huracán shares the same naturally aspirated 5.2-liter V10 — one of the greatest engines ever fitted to a production car. It revs to 8,500 rpm and produces a sound that's become the literal soundtrack of Miami Beach. No turbo lag, no hybrid assistance, just ten cylinders of mechanical fury. With Lamborghini moving to V8 hybrids for the Huracán's successor (the Temerario), these V10 models are the end of an era.

Lamborghini Huracán Pricing in Miami (2026)

The Lamborghini Huracán price range in South Florida varies enormously depending on variant, year, mileage, and spec. Here's the realistic market:

VariantPrice Range (Miami 2026)Notes
LP 610-4 Coupe (2014-2017)$160,000 – $200,000Best entry point; high-mile examples under $170K
LP 610-4 Spyder (2016-2018)$185,000 – $230,000Convertible premium; Miami tax
LP 580-2 RWD (2016-2019)$155,000 – $190,000Lowest entry; enthusiast favorite
Performante Coupe$250,000 – $320,000Appreciating; collector interest growing
Performante Spyder$280,000 – $350,000Rare; only ~1,200 built worldwide
EVO Coupe (AWD)$220,000 – $275,000Best all-arounder for daily driving
EVO Spyder (AWD)$250,000 – $310,000The quintessential Miami Lambo
EVO RWD$200,000 – $250,000Underrated; most fun per dollar
STO$300,000 – $400,000Track-focused; low production numbers
Tecnica$280,000 – $350,000Final-year RWD; excellent spec
Sterrato$300,000 – $380,000Only ~1,500 built; novelty collector piece

The value play in 2026: an EVO RWD Coupe around $210K. You get the updated LDVI electronics, the full 640 hp in a lighter rear-drive package, and it sits at a price point below the AWD EVO — despite being the better driver's car. For maximum Miami flex, the EVO Spyder in a loud color (Verde Mantis, Arancio Borealis) commands instant attention and holds value better than conservative specs.

Where to Find a Lamborghini Huracán for Sale in Miami

Authorized Lamborghini Dealers

  • Prestige Imports (North Miami Beach) — South Florida's original Lamborghini dealer. They consistently have 10-20+ pre-owned Huracáns in inventory ranging from early LP 610-4s to late Tecnicas. Their service department knows these cars inside and out, which matters for pre-purchase inspections.
  • Lamborghini Broward (Fort Lauderdale) — The newer authorized dealer serving the Broward market. Solid selection of CPO Huracáns with Lamborghini's certified pre-owned warranty.

Independent Exotic Dealers

  • RMC Miami — One of the best-curated exotic inventories in South Florida. They cherry-pick low-mile, well-specced Huracáns and stand behind what they sell.
  • Curated Miami (Wynwood) — Boutique dealer specializing in interesting specs. If you want a Huracán with a story — rare color, special edition, celebrity provenance — check here first.
  • iLusso — High-volume consignment dealer with competitive pricing. They typically have 5-10 Huracáns listed at any time.
  • The Collection (Coral Gables) — While primarily a Porsche/Ferrari/Aston Martin dealer, their pre-owned department frequently has Huracáns taken in on trade.

Online & Auction Platforms

  • Bring a Trailer — Huracáns are among the most actively traded exotics on BaT. Recent results: LP 610-4s selling in the $165K-$195K range, Performantes reaching $300K+. The auction format often beats dealer pricing.
  • Cars & Bids — Good for sub-$250K Huracáns. The enthusiast audience tends to pay fair prices without the dealer markup.
  • DuPont Registry — The legacy platform still has strong Lamborghini inventory. Filter to Florida for local options.
  • Autotrader / Cars.com — Cast the widest net. The Miami-Fort Lauderdale metro typically has 40-60 Huracáns listed across these platforms.

Lamborghini Huracán: Which Variant to Buy in Miami

With so many versions available, here's how to match the right Huracán to your use case:

If You Want...Buy ThisWhy
Best value entryLP 580-2 RWDCheapest Huracán; most engaging to drive
Daily driver + weekend toyEVO AWD CoupeMost refined; LDVI makes it easy to live with
Maximum Miami presenceEVO SpyderOpen-top V10 on Ocean Drive = peak Miami
Track days at HomesteadSTOPurpose-built; rear-steer, fixed aero, stripped interior
Future collectiblePerformante / SterratoLimited production; both gaining collector interest
Best all-around pickTecnicaFinal evolution; RWD fun with refined electronics

What to Watch Out For When Buying a Huracán

  • Rental car history is rampant in Miami. The Huracán is the #1 exotic rental car in South Florida. Many ex-rental units enter the private market with suspiciously low miles but hard lives. Check the VIN history through Carfax and AutoCheck, inspect for curbed wheels and interior wear, and ask for complete service records. If the car was registered to an LLC with "rental" or "exotic" in the name, proceed with extreme caution.
  • The E-Gear / dual-clutch transmission is robust but not invincible. Early LP 610-4 models occasionally show clutch wear if driven aggressively from day one. A pre-purchase inspection should include a clutch wear reading from the Lamborghini diagnostic tool. Replacement costs $8,000-$15,000.
  • Carbon ceramic brakes are expensive. Most Huracáns come with carbon ceramic rotors (CCB). Replacement cost: $15,000-$25,000 for a full set. Check rotor thickness during inspection — if they're near minimum spec, factor that into your offer.
  • Paint protection is critical. The Huracán's front end is rock-chip-prone. Look for existing PPF (paint protection film) coverage. If it doesn't have it, budget $3,000-$6,000 for a quality installation in Miami.
  • Insurance in Miami runs $5,000-$15,000 annually. Rates vary wildly based on your age, driving record, and coverage level. Get quotes before you buy — some carriers won't insure drivers under 25 on a Huracán at all.
  • Maintenance isn't cheap, but it's predictable. Annual service runs $1,500-$3,000 at an authorized dealer. The major service (every 2 years or 12,000 miles) including timing belt inspection and fluid changes runs $4,000-$6,000. Budget accordingly, and never skip the scheduled maintenance on a V10.

Lamborghini Huracán vs. the Competition

ModelPower0-60Price Range (Used)Miami Factor
Lamborghini Huracán EVO640 hp2.9s$220K – $275KV10 sound; maximum street presence
Ferrari F8 Tributo710 hp2.9s$250K – $310KMore power, more refined, less drama
McLaren 720S710 hp2.8s$180K – $240KFastest of the group; biggest depreciation
Porsche 911 GT3502 hp3.2s$210K – $280KBest track car; less flashy
Aston Martin Vantage656 hp3.4s$155K – $200KUnderrated; gorgeous design

The Huracán's advantage in Miami is simple: nothing else sounds like it, and nothing else looks like it. The McLaren 720S is objectively faster and currently cheaper — but it doesn't turn heads the way a Lamborghini does. In a city where your car is your introduction, that matters more than lap times.

Is the Lamborghini Huracán a Good Buy in 2026?

The Huracán is entering the phase of its lifecycle where it transitions from depreciating used car to appreciating modern classic. The naturally aspirated V10 is dead — Lamborghini's Temerario replacement uses a twin-turbo V8 with hybrid assist. That makes every Huracán the last of its kind: the final mass-produced, naturally aspirated V10 supercar.

Prices have stabilized after the post-pandemic correction, and the Miami market has enough inventory to keep values competitive. If you buy a clean, well-documented Huracán now — especially a Performante, STO, or Sterrato — you're likely buying at or near the floor. The LP 610-4 and EVO models may still drift down slightly, but the spread between them and the special editions will continue to widen.

For a city that practically invented supercar culture, the Lamborghini Huracán for sale in Miami is the defining modern exotic. Start at Prestige Imports, browse Bring a Trailer, and go hear that V10 in person. Some things you just have to experience to understand.

title: Best Car Storage Bags & Cocoons for Miami Hurricane Season 2026
excerpt: Hurricane season is coming, and your exotic car needs more than a standard cover. These inflatable car capsules and storage cocoons protect against flooding, humidity, and debris — essential for any Miami collector.
content:
Miami's hurricane season runs from June through November, and if you're storing an exotic car — or even a well-loved daily driver — in a garage that's anywhere near sea level (so, basically all of Miami), you need to think about protection beyond a basic car cover. Flooding, humidity spikes, wind-driven debris, and power outages that kill your garage dehumidifier can turn a $300,000 car into an insurance claim overnight.

Car storage bags and inflatable cocoons are the answer. These sealed, climate-controlled enclosures sit on your garage floor and create a protective bubble around your vehicle — keeping out moisture, mold, rodents, and in some cases, several inches of floodwater. They're not cheap, but compared to the cost of water damage on a Ferrari or Lamborghini, they're the best insurance policy you'll never file a claim on.

Here are the best options for Miami exotic car owners heading into the 2026 hurricane season.

Best Car Storage Bags & Cocoons: Our Top Picks

ProductPrice RangeTypeFlood ProtectionBest For
CarCapsule Showcase$350–$500Inflatable bubbleNo (open bottom)Dust, humidity, and mold prevention
CarCapsule Signature Series$500–$700Inflatable bubble w/ fanPartial (raised floor mat)Long-term storage with active airflow
Carcoon Indoor$600–$900Sealed cocoon w/ air managementPartialPremium humidity control, European engineering
PermaBag by Intercept$250–$400Sealed vapor-barrier bagYes (fully sealed)Flood zones, budget-friendly full seal
Zerust Car Capsule$300–$450Corrosion-inhibiting bagYes (zippered seal)Salt-air corrosion prevention
Flood Guard Auto Bag$200–$350Heavy-duty flood bagYes (designed for flooding)Flood-prone garages, emergency prep

CarCapsule Showcase & Signature Series

The CarCapsule is the name most collectors know, and for good reason. The Showcase model is a clear PVC bubble that inflates around your car using a small continuous fan. It creates positive air pressure inside the capsule, which means outside air (and moisture) can't get in — the same principle used in hospital clean rooms.

  • Showcase ($350–$500): Clear bubble, continuous-flow fan, fits cars up to 18 feet. Great for display garages where you want to show off the car while protecting it. The fan runs 24/7 on minimal electricity.
  • Signature Series ($500–$700): Adds a raised floor mat and more robust fan system. The floor mat creates a buffer zone between your car and the garage floor — critical in Miami where a few inches of water intrusion during a storm can reach your undercarriage.

Miami-specific note: The CarCapsule is excellent for humidity and mold prevention, but it's not a flood barrier. If your garage takes on significant water (6+ inches), the open-bottom design means water gets in. For true flood protection, pair it with a raised platform or go with a sealed bag instead.

→ Check CarCapsule Signature Series on Amazon

Carcoon Indoor

The Carcoon is the European alternative to CarCapsule, and it's arguably better engineered for tropical climates. Made in the UK (where they know a thing or two about damp), the Carcoon uses a patented airflow system that not only maintains positive pressure but actively circulates and filters the air inside.

  • Available in multiple sizes to fit everything from a Porsche 911 to a Rolls-Royce Cullinan
  • Built-in charcoal filters remove moisture and odors
  • Clear panels for visibility, reinforced seams for durability
  • Runs on standard 110V — power draw is minimal (about 15 watts)

The Carcoon's air management is genuinely superior to the CarCapsule's basic fan system. In Miami's 80%+ humidity environment, that filtration and active dehumidification makes a real difference for long-term storage. If you're storing a car for 3+ months during hurricane season, this is the upgrade worth making.

→ Check Carcoon Indoor on Amazon

PermaBag by Intercept Technology

If your primary concern is flood protection — and in Miami, it should be — the PermaBag takes a fundamentally different approach. Instead of an inflatable bubble, it's a heavy-duty, fully sealed vapor-barrier bag that wraps around your car and zips shut. No fan, no electricity, no moving parts.

  • Made from Intercept Technology's reactive copper-particle film that actively neutralizes corrosion-causing gases
  • Fully sealed zipper closure — rated to keep out water, dust, and pests
  • No power required, making it ideal for hurricane scenarios where you lose electricity
  • Reusable for multiple seasons

Why it matters for Miami: During Hurricane Irma in 2017, countless Miami garages flooded with 6–18 inches of saltwater. Cars in standard covers or even on low-rise lifts suffered catastrophic damage. A fully sealed PermaBag could have saved many of them. It's not glamorous, but it works when the power goes out and the water comes in.

→ Check PermaBag on Amazon

Zerust Car Capsule

The Zerust Car Capsule is specifically designed for corrosion prevention — which makes it uniquely relevant to Miami's salt-air environment. Zerust's parent company (Northern Technologies International) specializes in industrial corrosion-inhibiting products, and their car capsule integrates VCI (Vapor Corrosion Inhibitor) technology into the bag material.

  • Zippered closure creates a sealed environment
  • VCI molecules continuously release inside the bag, forming a protective layer on all metal surfaces
  • Protects against rust, tarnish, and oxidation — even on brake rotors, exhaust components, and suspension parts
  • No power needed; VCI protection lasts up to 5 years

For Miami collectors with beachfront or waterfront properties — where salt air penetrates even closed garages — the Zerust adds a layer of chemical corrosion protection that no other car bag offers. Pair it with a good dehumidifier for the ultimate storage setup.

→ Check Zerust Car Capsule on Amazon

How to Choose: Inflatable Bubble vs. Sealed Bag

These two product types serve different purposes, and Miami collectors may actually want both:

FeatureInflatable Bubble (CarCapsule, Carcoon)Sealed Bag (PermaBag, Zerust)
Humidity controlExcellent (active airflow)Good (passive seal)
Flood protectionMinimalExcellent
Requires powerYes (24/7)No
Display friendlyYes (clear panels)No (opaque)
Corrosion preventionIndirect (dry air)Direct (VCI technology)
Setup time15–30 minutes10–20 minutes
Price range$350–$900$200–$450
Best forYear-round storage, show garagesHurricane prep, flood zones

Our recommendation for Miami: Use an inflatable bubble (CarCapsule or Carcoon) for everyday storage September through May. When a named storm is approaching, slip the car into a sealed PermaBag or Zerust capsule. The sealed bag doesn't need power, so when your garage loses electricity during a Cat 3 hurricane, your car is still protected.

Additional Hurricane Prep for Your Garage

A storage bag alone isn't a complete hurricane plan. Here's the full checklist Miami exotic car owners should follow:

  • Elevate the car: If you have a car lift, raise it to maximum height before the storm. Even 4 feet of elevation can mean the difference between dry and destroyed. QuickJack portable lifts work great for this.
  • Disconnect the battery: Use a Battery Tender to top off the charge, then disconnect. Power surges when electricity returns can damage vehicle electronics.
  • Fill the gas tank: A full tank prevents moisture condensation inside the fuel system during extended storage.
  • Document everything: Take dated photos of the car's condition, VIN, and storage setup for insurance purposes before the storm.
  • Check your insurance: Standard comprehensive auto insurance covers flood damage, but verify your policy covers the full agreed value of a modified or exotic vehicle.

Where Miami Collectors Store Their Cars During Hurricane Season

Not everyone has a garage above the flood plain. These are the options Miami exotic car owners use:

  • Enclosed transport to higher ground: Some collectors ship their most valuable cars to storage facilities in Central or North Florida before peak season. Cost: $1,000–$2,000 per car each way.
  • Climate-controlled storage facilities: Companies like Vault Motorsports and Classic Car Storage offer insured, hurricane-rated storage in reinforced facilities. Cost: $500–$1,500/month per vehicle.
  • Home garage with full prep: The most common approach. Lift + sealed bag + disconnected battery + full insurance. Total cost for supplies: $500–$1,500 one-time.

The Bottom Line

Miami hurricane season isn't a matter of if, it's a matter of when. The $200–$800 you spend on a quality car storage bag or cocoon is the cheapest insurance you'll ever buy for a six-figure vehicle. Whether you go with a CarCapsule for year-round humidity protection or a PermaBag for emergency flood defense, having the right storage system ready before the first tropical depression forms is the move.

Don't wait until there's a named storm in the Gulf. Order now, test the setup in your garage, and know exactly how long it takes to deploy. When the 2026 season hits, you'll be the collector whose car survives while others are filing claims.

title: Best Paint Chip Repair & Touch-Up Kits for Exotic Cars in Miami (2026)
excerpt: I-95 rock chips, parking lot dings, and Miami's unforgiving sun conspire against your exotic car's paint. These professional-grade touch-up systems fix the damage before it spreads — without a $5,000 body shop bill.
content:
If you drive an exotic car in Miami — or really, if you drive any car on I-95 — you know rock chips are inevitable. That stretch of highway between Brickell and Fort Lauderdale is basically a rock chip gauntlet: construction debris, loose aggregate from endless road work, and the occasional rogue pebble launched by a dump truck that clearly doesn't care about your Rosso Corsa paint.

A single rock chip on a Ferrari, Lamborghini, or Porsche isn't just a cosmetic annoyance — it's exposed bare metal that will rust and spread if left untreated, especially in Miami's salt-air, high-humidity environment. And body shop quotes for professional paint repair on exotic cars? $800–$5,000+ per panel depending on the color and brand.

The smart move is a professional-grade paint touch-up kit that lets you repair chips at home, stopping the damage before it becomes a four-figure problem. Here are the best options for 2026.

Best Paint Chip Repair Kits: Our Top Picks

ProductPrice RangeSkill LevelBest ForColor Match Quality
Dr. ColorChip$50–$70BeginnerSmall to medium rock chipsExcellent (OEM codes)
TouchUpDirect$20–$60BeginnerBudget-friendly, wide color databaseVery Good
Langka Paint Chip Repair$15–$30BeginnerCompanion product for any touch-up paintN/A (works with any paint)
ERA Paints$30–$50IntermediateSpray can touch-up for larger areasGood (OEM matched)
Chipex$40–$60BeginnerEuropean cars, precision applicationExcellent
OEM Dealer Touch-Up Kits$30–$80IntermediatePerfect color match for specific brandsPerfect (factory paint)

Dr. ColorChip: The Gold Standard

Dr. ColorChip is the kit most detailers and car enthusiasts recommend, and for good reason: it uses a proprietary paint-and-blending-solution system that makes chip repair nearly foolproof. You apply the color-matched paint to the chip, let it dry, then wipe away the excess with the SealAct blending solution. What's left is a clean, flush repair that's virtually invisible from more than a foot away.

  • Color matching: Uses OEM paint codes. For exotics, you'll find your paint code on the door jamb sticker or in the owner's manual. Dr. ColorChip covers Ferrari, Lamborghini, Porsche, McLaren, Aston Martin, and virtually every other manufacturer.
  • What's in the kit: Paint, SealAct solution, microfiber cloths, applicators, and detailed instructions. The Standard kit handles about 50 small chips.
  • Difficulty: Truly beginner-friendly. The SealAct solution is the secret — it dissolves excess paint without affecting the repaired area, so you literally can't mess it up. Apply paint, wipe off excess. Done.

Miami tip: If your car has a multi-stage paint (common on tri-coat whites, metallic silvers, and pearl finishes), order the multi-stage version. Standard single-stage kits won't match the depth and shimmer of Ferrari's Bianco Avus or Porsche's Chalk.

→ Check Dr. ColorChip Kits on Amazon

TouchUpDirect: Best Budget Option

TouchUpDirect offers the widest color database in the industry and ships exact-match paint in multiple formats: brush-in-cap bottles, paint pens, and spray cans. For exotic car owners who want to keep a touch-up pen in the glovebox for quick on-the-spot repairs, this is the way to go.

  • Paint pen format: Perfect for emergency repairs. See a fresh chip after parking at Bal Harbour? Fix it in 60 seconds before the bare metal starts oxidizing.
  • Spray can format: For larger areas of damage — like a gravel road mishap or a particularly aggressive stretch of construction zone. Pair with the included primer and clear coat for a durable repair.
  • Price advantage: A basic brush kit starts around $20 — roughly half the cost of Dr. ColorChip. Quality is slightly lower on color accuracy for complex metallics, but for solid colors, it's excellent.

→ Check TouchUpDirect on Amazon

Langka Paint Chip Repair: The Secret Weapon

Langka isn't a paint — it's a blending solution that works with any touch-up paint (OEM, aftermarket, or dealer-supplied). The concept is similar to Dr. ColorChip's SealAct: you apply your touch-up paint to the chip, let it dry slightly, then use Langka to dissolve and level the excess.

  • Why it matters: The biggest problem with DIY touch-up paint isn't the color match — it's the blob of paint that sits above the surface and looks worse than the chip. Langka eliminates that problem entirely.
  • Pair it with OEM paint: Buy your exact-match paint from your dealer (Ferrari, Porsche, and Lamborghini all sell touch-up bottles), then use Langka to level and blend. This gives you a factory-perfect color with a professional-grade finish.
  • Kit includes: Blob Eliminator solution, microfiber cloths, and application guide. One bottle handles hundreds of chips.

Pro combo: OEM dealer touch-up paint ($30–$50) + Langka Blob Eliminator ($15) = the best possible repair at the lowest cost. This is what many high-end detailers in Miami actually use.

→ Check Langka Blob Eliminator on Amazon

Chipex: Best for European Exotics

Chipex is a UK-based company that's built its reputation on European car paint matching. If you're driving a Porsche, McLaren, Aston Martin, or Bentley, Chipex's color formulas are often more accurate than American alternatives for complex European paint finishes.

  • Three-step system: Paint, blend, polish. Simple enough for anyone, and the results are consistently excellent on metallic and pearl finishes.
  • European paint expertise: Chipex specifically calibrates for the multi-layer paint systems used by European manufacturers. German and Italian paint processes differ from American ones, and Chipex accounts for this.
  • Durability: Chipex repairs are designed to withstand car washes and polishing. Once cured, the repair is permanent and UV-stable — important for Miami's intense sunlight.

→ Check Chipex on Amazon

When DIY Isn't Enough: Professional Paint Repair Options

Touch-up kits are perfect for small chips and minor dings. But some damage requires professional attention:

Damage TypeDIY Touch-Up?Professional Repair Cost (Miami)
Small rock chips (< 3mm)Yes — perfect for kits$50–$150 per chip
Medium chips with bare metalYes — use primer first$150–$400 per chip
Long scratches (through clear coat)Partial — can improve appearance$300–$1,000 per panel
Deep scratches (through paint to metal)No — temporary fix only$800–$2,500 per panel
Large area damage (keying, scraping)No$1,500–$5,000+ per panel

For deep damage on exotic cars, always consult a body shop that specializes in your brand. Ferrari and Lamborghini paints require specific base coat, mid-coat, and clear coat layers that generic body shops often get wrong. In Miami, shops like Ferrari of Miami's body center, Prestige Collision Center, and Exotic Car Body Works have the factory paint systems and spray booth calibrations to match these finishes correctly.

How to Apply Touch-Up Paint Like a Pro

Even the best kit produces mediocre results if applied incorrectly. Here's the method professional detailers use:

Step 1: Clean the Area

Wash the damaged area thoroughly. Use clay bar treatment to remove embedded contaminants around the chip. Any dirt or wax in the chip will prevent paint adhesion.

Step 2: Treat Rust (If Present)

Miami's salt air means even fresh chips can start rusting within days. If you see any orange discoloration in the chip, dab it with a toothpick dipped in rust converter (available at any auto parts store). Let it dry completely before applying paint.

Step 3: Apply Paint in Thin Layers

Use a fine-tipped applicator or toothpick — never the brush that comes in most OEM bottles (too thick). Apply a tiny amount of paint, let it dry for 10 minutes, then add another thin layer. Two to three thin layers beats one thick glob every time.

Step 4: Level and Blend

Once the paint is dry (24 hours for best results), use your leveling solution (Dr. ColorChip SealAct, Langka, or Chipex blend) to remove excess paint above the surface. This is the step that separates amateur repairs from invisible ones.

Step 5: Protect

After leveling, apply a ceramic coating or paint sealant over the repaired area. This protects the fresh paint from UV degradation and provides the same hydrophobic properties as the rest of the car's surface.

Preventing Paint Chips in Miami: The Proactive Approach

The best chip repair is the one you never have to do. Here's how Miami exotic car owners minimize paint damage:

  • Paint Protection Film (PPF): Full-front PPF (hood, fenders, bumper, mirrors) is the single best investment for any car driven on I-95. Quality film from XPEL, SunTek, or 3M runs $2,000–$5,000 for the front end and absorbs rock impacts without damaging paint. XPEL PPF kits are available for DIY installation on many vehicles.
  • Increase following distance: Most rock chips come from the car directly ahead of you. On I-95 construction zones, drop back to 4+ car lengths. Yes, someone will merge into the gap. Let them.
  • Avoid construction zones when possible: Take the Turnpike instead of I-95 through the Golden Glades interchange. That stretch is chip central due to permanent construction.
  • Ceramic coating: While it won't prevent chips, a ceramic coating makes the surrounding paint harder and more resistant to minor scratching from debris that doesn't fully chip.

Which Kit Should You Buy?

Here's the quick decision tree:

  • First time doing touch-up, want foolproof results? → Dr. ColorChip
  • Want a paint pen for the glovebox? → TouchUpDirect paint pen
  • Already have OEM paint, need a leveling solution? → Langka Blob Eliminator
  • European exotic with complex metallic paint? → Chipex
  • Want the maximum quality at any price? → OEM dealer paint + Langka + ceramic coating touch-up

The Bottom Line

Every mile you drive in Miami puts your paint at risk. Between I-95's construction zones, the Palmetto's mystery debris, and parking lots where people open doors like they're trying to escape a sinking ship, your exotic car will get chips. The question is whether you fix them for $50 with a kit and 30 minutes of your time, or let them rust and spread until you're facing a $3,000 body shop bill.

Keep a Dr. ColorChip kit in your garage, a TouchUpDirect pen in your glovebox, and inspect your front end after every highway drive. In Miami's salt air, even 48 hours of exposed bare metal can start the corrosion process. Act fast, repair clean, and protect the repair with ceramic coating. Your paint — and your resale value — will thank you.

title: Porsche 911 Turbo S for Sale in Miami: 2026 Pricing, Specs & Buyer's Guide
excerpt: The Porsche 911 Turbo S is the ultimate all-weather supercar — 640 hp, AWD, and a 2.6-second 0-60. Miami's market is loaded with options. Here's your complete buyer's guide.
content:
The Porsche 911 Turbo S has been the stealth supercar king for decades. While Lamborghinis and Ferraris grab the attention at Bal Harbour valet stands, the Turbo S quietly obliterates everything on the road — 640 horsepower, all-wheel drive, and a 2.6-second 0-60 time that makes million-dollar hypercars nervous. If you're looking for a Porsche 911 Turbo S for sale in Miami, you're shopping in one of the most active Porsche markets in the country.

Miami is Porsche's largest U.S. market by volume. Between The Collection in Coral Gables, Champion Porsche in Pompano Beach, and Braman Porsche in West Palm, the dealer pipeline is deep — and the private resale market is even deeper. Here's everything you need to know about buying a 911 Turbo S in South Florida in 2026.

Porsche 911 Turbo S Pricing in Miami: 2026 Market Overview

The Porsche 911 Turbo S price depends heavily on generation, mileage, and whether you're buying the coupe or cabriolet. Miami tends to command a slight premium over national averages due to demand, but the selection is unmatched. Here's what you'll find:

GenerationYearsPowerMiami Market PriceMSRP When New
991.1 Turbo S2014–2016580 hp, 3.8L twin-turbo$120,000–$155,000$182,000–$199,000
991.2 Turbo S2017–2019580 hp, 3.8L twin-turbo$140,000–$185,000$189,000–$207,000
992 Turbo S2021–2025640 hp, 3.7L twin-turbo$210,000–$280,000$231,000–$253,000
992 Turbo S Cabriolet2021–2025640 hp, 3.7L twin-turbo$225,000–$300,000$245,000–$267,000

Key takeaway: The 991.1 Turbo S represents absurd value — you get 90% of the modern car's performance for roughly half the price. The 992 holds strong due to demand, but we're starting to see some depreciation on early 2021 models.

What Makes the Porsche 911 Turbo S Special

Every generation of the 911 Turbo S has been about the same idea: take the already-brilliant 911 platform and make it faster than things that cost three times as much. The current 992 generation takes this to an absurd level.

992 Turbo S Key Specs

SpecDetail
Engine3.7L twin-turbocharged flat-six
Horsepower640 hp @ 6,750 RPM
Torque590 lb-ft @ 2,500–4,000 RPM
0-60 MPH2.6 seconds
Quarter Mile10.5 seconds @ 134 mph
Top Speed205 mph
DrivetrainAWD with rear-biased torque split
Transmission8-speed PDK dual-clutch
Curb Weight3,636 lbs

That 2.6-second 0-60 makes the Turbo S faster to 60 than a McLaren 720S, Lamborghini Huracán STO, and Ferrari SF90 — all in a car you can daily drive in the rain without a second thought. That's the magic of the Turbo S: it does everything, and does it better than most purpose-built machines.

Where to Find a Porsche 911 Turbo S for Sale in Miami

Miami's Porsche ecosystem is massive. Here are the best sources:

Authorized Porsche Dealers

  • The Collection – Coral Gables: Miami's premier luxury dealer. Strong CPO Turbo S inventory with full Porsche backing.
  • Champion Porsche – Pompano Beach: The world's largest Porsche dealer by volume. If a Turbo S exists in South Florida, Champion probably has it.
  • Braman Porsche – West Palm Beach: Excellent for buyers in northern Miami-Dade and Broward looking to avoid the downtown markup.

Exotic & Independent Dealers

  • Prestige Imports – North Miami Beach: Lamborghini dealer that frequently stocks high-spec Turbo S models.
  • iLusso – Coral Gables: Specializes in curated exotic inventory with detailed condition reports.
  • Exotic Cars of Houston (Miami consignments): Often has rare specs like PTS (Paint to Sample) cars.

Online & Auction Platforms

  • Bring a Trailer (BaT): The go-to for well-documented examples. Miami sellers are active.
  • Cars & Bids: Doug DeMuro's platform — tends to attract enthusiast-owned cars.
  • DuPont Registry: The classic high-end listing site. Heavy Miami presence.
  • Autotrader / Cars.com: Don't sleep on mainstream platforms for dealer inventory.

Porsche 911 Turbo S Buyer's Checklist for Miami

The Turbo S is a remarkably reliable supercar, but there are things to watch for — especially in Miami's climate.

Pre-Purchase Must-Dos

  • Check the Carfax and Porsche history report: Porsche dealers can pull detailed records including every service visit. Miami cars often have minor collision damage from parking in Brickell — make sure it's disclosed.
  • Inspect for salt/corrosion: Coastal humidity and salt air are the Turbo S's only real enemy. Check underbody, wheel wells, and brake components for surface corrosion.
  • PDK service history: The PDK transmission is bulletproof but requires fluid changes every 40,000 miles or 4 years. Skipping this is expensive.
  • Tire condition: Turbo S tires are $1,800–$2,500 for a set (Pirelli P Zero or Michelin Pilot Sport). Budget accordingly.
  • Ceramic brakes (PCCB): Most Turbo S models come with ceramic composite brakes. They last 80,000+ miles but cost $15,000–$20,000 to replace. Check rotor thickness.

Miami-Specific Considerations

  • Paint protection: Miami's UV exposure is brutal. Check whether the car has PPF (paint protection film) — if not, budget $5,000–$8,000 for full-body coverage.
  • Interior condition: Leather bakes in South Florida sun. Look for cracking, fading, or deformation on the dashboard and seats.
  • Flood history: Miami floods. Period. Always check for water damage signs: musty smell, water lines in the trunk, corroded electronics.
  • Hurricane storage: Ask the seller how the car was stored during hurricane season. A Turbo S that spent a night in a flooding garage is not the same car.

Porsche 911 Turbo S: Cost of Ownership in Miami

The Turbo S is surprisingly affordable to own relative to Italian and British exotics — but it's still a $200K+ car. Here's what to budget:

ExpenseAnnual Cost (Estimated)
Insurance (Miami, clean record)$4,500–$8,000
Scheduled Maintenance$1,500–$3,000
Tires (every 15K–20K miles)$1,800–$2,500/set
Ceramic Brake Pads (when needed)$3,000–$4,500
Registration & Taxes (FL)$2,500–$4,500
PPF / Ceramic Coating$1,000–$2,000 (maintenance)

Total estimated annual cost: $11,000–$24,000 depending on mileage and brake needs. That's roughly half what a comparable Ferrari or Lamborghini costs to maintain — and you get a car that starts every single time.

Porsche 911 Turbo S vs. the Competition

In Miami, the Turbo S competes with some heavy hitters. Here's how it stacks up:

CarPower0-60Price Range (Miami)Annual Maintenance
Porsche 911 Turbo S640 hp2.6s$210K–$280K$8K–$15K
McLaren 720S710 hp2.7s$180K–$250K$12K–$25K
Ferrari F8 Tributo710 hp2.9s$260K–$320K$15K–$30K
Lamborghini Huracán EVO631 hp2.9s$220K–$280K$12K–$22K
Aston Martin DBS715 hp3.4s$200K–$270K$10K–$20K

The Turbo S wins on reliability, AWD usability (critical for Miami's summer downpours), and running costs. It loses on drama — nobody's pulling out their phone to film a Porsche at LIV. But most Turbo S owners are past the point of needing validation.

Is Now the Right Time to Buy a Porsche 911 Turbo S in Miami?

Honestly? Yes. The 992 Turbo S market has cooled from its pandemic-era highs, when dealers were charging $50K+ markups. You can now find lightly used 2022 models at or slightly below original MSRP. The 991.2 generation is in a sweet spot where it's depreciated enough to be accessible but new enough to feel modern.

The incoming 992.2 generation (expected late 2026) will likely feature a hybrid powertrain, which could push demand for the pure twin-turbo models higher. If you want a "last of the analog" Turbo S, the window is narrowing.

Bottom Line

The Porsche 911 Turbo S is the thinking person's supercar — and Miami is the best place in America to buy one. Whether you're looking for a screaming-deal 991 or a spec'd-out 992 with Chalk Metallic paint and a full leather interior, the inventory is here. Do your homework on condition and maintenance history, budget for PPF and good insurance, and you'll have a car that will embarrass everything at the next Cars & Coffee while still getting you to the office on Monday.

Start your search at Champion Porsche for volume, Bring a Trailer for unique specs, and The Collection for the white-glove CPO experience. Your future Turbo S is already somewhere in South Florida — go find it.

title: Bugatti for Sale: Where to Find One in Miami & What You'll Actually Pay (2026)
excerpt: Bugatti ownership is the apex of the automotive world — seven-figure price tags, waitlists measured in years, and a Miami scene that's home to more Bugattis per capita than almost anywhere. Here's the real buyer's guide.
content:
There is no car on Earth that commands attention like a Bugatti. Not a Ferrari, not a Lamborghini, not even a Pagani. When a Bugatti rolls down Ocean Drive, traffic stops. Phones come out. People who don't know a carburetor from a crankshaft still know they're looking at something impossibly rare and expensive. If you're searching for a Bugatti for sale, Miami is one of the few cities in the world where that search is actually realistic.

South Florida has quietly become one of the densest Bugatti markets globally. The combination of no state income tax, year-round driving weather, and a concentration of ultra-high-net-worth buyers means Bugattis actually change hands here with relative regularity. "Relative" being the key word — we're still talking about a car with total global production measured in hundreds, not thousands.

Bugatti Models & Pricing: What's Actually Available in 2026

When you're shopping for a Bugatti for sale, you're looking at a handful of models — each with wildly different price points and availability. Here's the full breakdown:

ModelProduction YearsUnits BuiltPower2026 Market Price
Veyron 16.42005–20112521,001 hp, W16$1.2M–$1.8M

Chiron Sport2019–2022~601,479 hp, W16$3.2M–$4.2M

Reality check: If you're looking to enter Bugatti ownership for the "lowest" price, the first-generation Veyron 16.4 coupe is your entry point at around $1.2–1.5 million. That's a car that has actually depreciated from its $1.7M MSRP — one of the few bargains in the Bugatti universe.

Where to Find a Bugatti for Sale in Miami

You won't find a Bugatti on Autotrader (well, maybe). Here's where the real deals happen:

Authorized & Semi-Official Channels

  • Braman Motorcars – West Palm Beach: The closest thing Miami has to a Bugatti dealer relationship. High-net-worth clients often consign here.
  • Prestige Imports – North Miami Beach: Lamborghini Miami's home, but regularly handles Bugatti consignments and trades. One of the most connected exotic dealers in Florida.
  • The Collection – Coral Gables: Moves hypercars at this level through their private client network. You may need to ask specifically — not everything hits the website.

Specialist Hypercar Dealers

  • Curated – Miami: Hypercar-focused dealer with deep Bugatti connections. They've moved multiple Chirons and Veyrons through South Florida.
  • Miller Motorcars – Greenwich, CT (ships to Miami): East Coast Bugatti authority that frequently sells to Florida collectors.
  • Al Ain Class Motors (Dubai → Miami consignments): The Middle East-to-Miami pipeline is real. Some of the most unique Bugatti specs come through this channel.

Auction Houses

  • RM Sotheby's: The premier Bugatti auction house. Their Amelia Island and Miami sales regularly feature Bugattis.
  • Bonhams / Gooding & Company: Less frequent but occasionally offer exceptional examples.
  • Bring a Trailer: Yes, seriously. BaT has sold Veyrons. The buyer pool at this level is smaller, but the platform's transparency is unmatched.

Bugatti Chiron: The Most Attainable Modern Bugatti

If any Bugatti can be called "attainable" — and that word is doing heavy lifting here — it's the Chiron. With 500 units produced in the standard spec, it's the highest-volume modern Bugatti, and 2026 is actually an interesting time to buy one.

Chiron Key Specs

SpecDetail
Engine8.0L quad-turbocharged W16
Horsepower1,479 hp
Torque1,180 lb-ft
0-60 MPH2.4 seconds
Top Speed261 mph (limited to 261; SS did 304)
DrivetrainAWD
Transmission7-speed dual-clutch
Curb Weight4,400 lbs

Production ended in 2022, and with the new Tourbillon (V16 hybrid) arriving in 2026, the W16-powered Chiron is now a "last of its kind" car. Expect values to firm up over the next few years as collectors recognize the Chiron as the final expression of the quad-turbo W16 era.

Bugatti Veyron: The Entry-Level Bugatti

The Veyron started it all — the car that proved a 1,000-horsepower, 250-mph production car was possible. In 2026, the base Veyron has settled into what might be the most fascinating price bracket in the exotic car world.

At $1.2–1.8 million, you're paying less than a new Ferrari SF90 XX Stradale for a car with a quad-turbo W16, 1,001 horsepower, and the kind of engineering that made the entire automotive industry collectively lose its mind in 2005. The catch? Maintenance.

The Real Cost of Bugatti Ownership in Miami

If the purchase price doesn't faze you, the ownership costs might raise an eyebrow. Bugatti ownership is not for the faint of wallet:

ExpenseVeyron (Annual)Chiron (Annual)
Insurance$30,000–$50,000$40,000–$80,000
Scheduled Service$20,000–$35,000$15,000–$25,000
Tires (every 2,500 miles)$25,000–$35,000/set$12,000–$18,000/set
Wheel Replacement (recommended with tires)$50,000–$70,000/setN/A (standard change)
Storage (climate-controlled, Miami)$6,000–$15,000$6,000–$15,000
Registration & Taxes (FL)$12,000–$20,000$25,000–$40,000

The infamous Veyron tire/wheel bill: The original Veyron's specially developed Michelin PAX tires are bonded to the wheels, meaning you replace both together. At around $25,000–$35,000 per set of tires and $50,000–$70,000 for wheels, the Veyron's reputation for insane running costs is well-earned. The Chiron uses more conventional (but still bespoke) tires that are significantly cheaper to replace.

Bugatti Buying Tips for Miami Collectors

Due Diligence Essentials

  • Service history is everything: A Bugatti without complete factory service records is worth significantly less. Bugatti's authorized service network is tiny — most U.S. work goes through Bugatti Beverly Hills or Miller Motorcars.
  • Provenance matters: One-owner, low-mileage, documented cars command premiums of 20-30% over equivalent examples with murky histories.
  • Spec sheet drives value: Special colors, exposed carbon fiber, unique interior combinations — these details can swing the price by hundreds of thousands of dollars.
  • Beware of "Dubai specials": Cars imported from the Middle East may have undisclosed desert sand damage, extreme heat cycling, or incomplete service histories. Always verify with Bugatti's factory records.

Miami-Specific Factors

  • Humidity and corrosion: Even cars stored indoors face Miami's humidity. Insist on climate-controlled storage history and check for any signs of moisture damage in electronics.
  • Flood risk: Miami Beach, Brickell, and Aventura flood regularly. Run a thorough flood check on any South Florida-based Bugatti.
  • Importation paperwork: Many Bugattis in Miami were imported from Europe or the Middle East. Ensure all DOT/EPA compliance paperwork and customs clearance is clean.
  • Photography tax: You will be stopped for photos everywhere you go. Budget extra time for every errand. This is not a joke.

Bugatti Tourbillon: The Future Is Already Spoken For

Bugatti's next chapter is the Tourbillon — a naturally aspirated 8.3L V16 paired with three electric motors for a combined 1,775 horsepower. MSRP is approximately $4 million, and all 250 units allocated for production are already spoken for. If you want one, the secondary market is your only option, and early allocation flips are already rumored at $6–8 million.

The Tourbillon's arrival makes the W16-era cars (Veyron, Chiron, and derivatives) feel like the end of an era — which they are. For collectors, that makes right now a strategic time to acquire a Chiron or limited variant before the market reprices them as the last of the W16 lineage.

Bottom Line

Shopping for a Bugatti for sale in Miami is one of the most rarefied automotive experiences on the planet. The inventory exists — South Florida moves more hypercars than virtually any other U.S. market — but the process is nothing like buying a normal car. Expect to work through private networks, specialized dealers, and auction houses. Budget not just for the car, but for the ecosystem around it: insurance, storage, service, and tires that cost more than most people's daily drivers.

If you're entering at the Veyron level, you're getting a genuine piece of automotive history for the price of a nice house. If you're chasing a Chiron Pur Sport or Divo, you're in investment-grade territory where the car is as much an asset as a machine. Either way, Miami is where the cars are — and where the buyers are. Start with RM Sotheby's for auction opportunities, Prestige Imports for local consignments, and your own network for off-market deals. At this level, the best Bugattis never hit a public listing.

content:
Pagani for Sale: How to Buy One in Miami & What They Actually Cost (2026)

Finding a Pagani for sale is nothing like shopping for a normal car — or even a normal supercar. Horacio Pagani's atelier in Modena produces roughly 40–50 cars per year, making every model rarer than most limited-edition watches. Miami happens to be one of the best cities in the world to find one, thanks to a concentration of ultra-high-net-worth collectors and a handful of dealers who specialize in seven-figure exotics.

This guide breaks down every Pagani model you're likely to encounter on the resale market, realistic 2026 pricing, where to look in South Florida, and the hidden costs that come with owning a hand-built Italian hypercar.

Every Pagani Model for Sale in 2026 — Pricing Overview

Pagani's lineup is small but each model commands wildly different prices depending on spec, mileage, and provenance. Here's what the market looks like right now:

If you see a Pagani for sale below these ranges, scrutinize the listing carefully — accident history, grey-market imports, or title issues are the usual culprits for below-market pricing.

Where to Find a Pagani for Sale in Miami

Miami's exotic car ecosystem is one of the best in the world for sourcing ultra-rare machines. Here are the primary channels for finding a Pagani for sale in South Florida:

Authorized & Specialist Dealers

  • Prestige Imports (North Miami Beach) — One of the few U.S. dealers with direct Pagani allocation. They handle new Utopia deliveries and occasionally list pre-owned Huayras.
  • The Collection (Coral Gables) — While primarily a Ferrari/Maserati dealer, their exotic consignment wing occasionally handles Pagani trades.
  • iLusso (Aventura) — Specializes in ultra-high-end consignments and has listed Paganis multiple times.

Private Sales & Brokers

Most Pagani transactions at this price point happen through private brokers who connect buyers and sellers discreetly. Miami-based brokers like Curated and Collecting Cars have facilitated multiple Pagani deals in South Florida. Expect broker fees of 2–5% on top of the sale price.

Online Marketplaces

  • Bring a Trailer (BaT) — Paganis have sold here, though rarely. When they do, the auctions draw massive attention.
  • duPont Registry — The traditional classifieds platform for seven-figure cars. Usually has 3–8 Paganis listed nationally.
  • James Edition — European-heavy marketplace with global Pagani inventory, some Miami-based.

Pagani Utopia — The Current-Production Model for Sale

The Pagani Utopia is the newest model and the one most likely to appear in dealer allocations. With a starting MSRP of $2.95 million, the Utopia is Pagani's vision of a pure, driver-focused hypercar — lighter than the Huayra, with a 852-hp twin-turbo V12 built by Mercedes-AMG, and a 7-speed manual or automated manual transmission.

Allocation spots for the Utopia were sold out before the car debuted publicly. On the secondary market, expect to pay $3.8 million to $5 million+ depending on specification. Cars with exposed carbon bodies, special liveries, or unique interior commissions command premiums north of $5M.

Pagani Huayra for Sale — The Most Attainable Option

The Pagani Huayra (2012–2018 coupe) represents the most "accessible" entry point into Pagani ownership, if you can call $2.8 million accessible. The Huayra's AMG-sourced 6.0L twin-turbo V12 produces 730 hp and remains one of the most dramatic-sounding engines ever fitted to a road car.

Key things to check when evaluating a Huayra for sale:

  • Service history — Must be maintained by a Pagani-authorized service center. The nearest is Prestige Imports in North Miami Beach.
  • Clutch condition — The single-clutch automated manual is the Huayra's weak point. Replacement costs $30K–$50K.
  • Carbon fiber condition — Pagani's carbo-titanium weave is stunning but expensive to repair. Any crack or delamination is a five-figure fix.
  • Provenance — Paganis with documented celebrity or notable collector ownership can command 20–30% premiums.

Pagani Zonda for Sale — The Collector's Grail

The original Pagani Zonda has crossed firmly into collectible territory. Prices have been climbing steadily since 2020, with special editions like the Zonda Cinque, Zonda R, and various one-offs commanding prices well into eight figures at auction.

A "standard" Zonda F or Zonda S in good condition typically trades between $2.5 million and $4 million. The Zonda Cinque (5 coupes, 5 roadsters) has traded above $6 million, and true one-off commissions have fetched $7M+ at RM Sotheby's and Gooding & Company auctions.

True Cost of Pagani Ownership in Miami

The purchase price is just the beginning. Here's what ongoing Pagani ownership actually costs in South Florida:

ExpenseAnnual Estimated Cost
Insurance (agreed value)$25,000–$60,000
Annual service$5,000–$15,000
Storage (climate-controlled)$6,000–$18,000
Tires (Pirelli P Zero)$4,000–$6,000 per set
Florida registration & taxesVaries (no state income tax, ~6% sales tax on purchase)
DepreciationLikely appreciation for most models

The good news: most Pagani models are appreciating assets. Unlike most supercars that lose value the moment you drive them off the lot, Paganis have historically gained 5–15% annually on the secondary market, making them one of the few cars that function as both toys and investments.

Financing a Pagani Purchase

Traditional auto lenders won't touch a Pagani. You'll need specialty lenders who handle exotic and collector vehicles:

  • Woodside Credit — Popular among Miami collectors, offers terms on vehicles up to $10M+
  • Premier Financial Services — Lease and loan options for exotics, with Pagani experience
  • Private banking — If you're buying a Pagani, your private banker at JPM, UBS, or Goldman can likely structure a collateralized loan

Typical terms: 20–30% down, 3–7 year terms, rates around 6–8% for well-qualified borrowers. Many Pagani buyers pay cash or use portfolio-backed lending.

Import & Title Considerations for Pagani in Florida

Some Paganis on the market are grey-market imports — particularly Zondas that were never officially federalized for the U.S. These cars may carry "Show or Display" exemptions that limit driving to 2,500 miles per year. Before purchasing any Pagani for sale, confirm:

  • Whether the car has a clean U.S. title or is on Show or Display exemption
  • EPA and DOT compliance documentation
  • Whether the VIN matches Pagani's production records (your dealer can verify with the factory)

Should You Buy a Pagani in Miami?

If you have the means, Miami is arguably the best city in America to own a Pagani. No state income tax, year-round driving weather, a robust service and storage infrastructure, and a community of fellow collectors who actually drive their cars. The city's car culture doesn't just tolerate seven-figure hypercars — it celebrates them.

Whether you're eyeing a Pagani Utopia allocation, hunting for a clean Huayra, or dreaming about a Zonda for your collection, the South Florida market offers more access to these ultra-rare machines than almost anywhere outside of Monaco or Dubai.

title: Ferrari 812 for Sale in Miami: 2026 Pricing, Specs & Buyer's Guide
excerpt: The Ferrari 812 Superfast and 812 Competizione represent the last of Ferrari's naturally aspirated V12 front-engine grand tourers. Here's what they cost in Miami, where to find one, and what every buyer needs to know in 2026.
content:
Ferrari 812 for Sale in Miami: 2026 Pricing, Specs & Buyer's Guide

The Ferrari 812 family holds a special place in automotive history — it's the last front-mounted, naturally aspirated V12 Ferrari will ever build. With the 12Cilindri now taking over as the turbocharged successor, the 812 Superfast, GTS, and Competizione have become instant modern classics. If you're searching for a Ferrari 812 for sale in Miami, the window to buy at reasonable prices is closing fast.

This guide covers every 812 variant, realistic 2026 market pricing, where to shop in South Florida, and the ownership costs you should expect.

Ferrari 812 Model Lineup — Specs & 2026 Pricing

Ferrari produced four variants of the 812 platform. Each shares the legendary 6.5-liter naturally aspirated V12 but in different states of tune:

ModelYearsPower0-60 mphOriginal MSRP2026 Market Price
812 Superfast2018–2022789 hp2.8s$340,000$290K–$370K
812 GTS2020–2022789 hp2.9s$365,000$370K–$460K
812 Competizione2021–2022819 hp2.8s$600,000$750K–$1.1M
812 Competizione A2022819 hp2.8s$650,000+$1M–$1.5M+

The 812 Superfast represents the best value in the lineup — a sub-3-second V12 Ferrari for under $300K is remarkable given what this car is. The Competizione variants, limited to 999 coupes and 599 Aperta models, are already deep in collector territory.

Why the Ferrari 812 for Sale Market Is Heating Up

Three factors are driving 812 values upward in 2026:

  1. Last naturally aspirated V12 — Ferrari's 12Cilindri uses a twin-turbo V12. The 812's 8,500-rpm screaming NA engine is unrepeatable. Collectors know this.
  2. Production has ended — No more 812s will ever be built. Supply is fixed, and attrition (accidents, exports) only shrinks it.
  3. The sound — Nothing in Ferrari's current lineup sounds like the 812. That emotional factor translates directly into resale value.

Early 812 Superfasts with higher mileage have found a floor around $280K–$290K. Low-mile examples with desirable specs (Rosso Corsa, racing stripes, carbon fiber options) are pushing past $370K. The trajectory is clear: these are going up, not down.

Where to Find a Ferrari 812 for Sale in Miami

Authorized Ferrari Dealers

  • The Collection (Coral Gables) — Miami's authorized Ferrari dealer regularly stocks pre-owned 812s. Buying here gets you Ferrari Approved certification and a factory-backed warranty extension.
  • Ferrari of Fort Lauderdale — Broward County's authorized dealer, about 30 minutes north. Similar inventory and certification program.

Independent Exotic Dealers

  • Prestige Imports (North Miami Beach) — High-volume exotic dealer that frequently lists 812 Superfasts and GTS models.
  • South Beach Exotics / iLusso — Consignment-focused dealers in the Aventura/Miami Beach area.
  • RMC Miami (Wynwood) — Boutique dealer specializing in spec'd-out exotics, often with unique 812 configurations.

Online & Auction Platforms

  • Bring a Trailer — Multiple 812s sell here monthly. Transparent bidding with full photo documentation.
  • Cars & Bids — Doug DeMuro's platform has become a go-to for modern exotics in this price range.
  • duPont Registry — Usually 20–40 812s listed nationally at any given time.
  • RM Sotheby's / Gooding — For Competizione variants, the major auction houses are where the best examples trade.

Ferrari 812 Superfast for Sale — The Smart Buy

The 812 Superfast is the volume model and offers the most accessible entry into V12 Ferrari ownership. With 789 hp from that glorious 6.5-liter engine, rear-wheel drive, and a 7-speed dual-clutch gearbox, it's one of the most visceral driving experiences money can buy.

When shopping for a 812 Superfast for sale, prioritize these specs:

  • Carbon fiber racing seats — A $5K option new that adds $15K+ to resale
  • Front lift system — Essential for Miami's aggressive speed bumps and driveway transitions
  • Apple CarPlay — Retrofitted on many early cars; a must-have for daily usability
  • Atelier / Tailor Made spec — Custom-ordered cars with unique color combinations command 10–20% premiums

Avoid: high-mileage examples (20K+ miles) unless significantly discounted, cars with aftermarket exhaust (potential warranty issues), and any 812 without documented Ferrari service history.

Ferrari 812 GTS for Sale — The Open-Top V12

The 812 GTS is the retractable hardtop version of the Superfast, and it's become the more desirable variant for Miami buyers for obvious reasons — year-round top-down weather and a V12 soundtrack with nothing between you and the sky.

GTS models command a $80K–$100K premium over equivalent Superfast coupes. This gap has been widening throughout 2025–2026 as collectors recognize the GTS as the more special car. Production numbers were lower than the coupe, adding to scarcity.

Ferrari 812 Competizione for Sale — The Collector's Choice

The 812 Competizione is the track-focused, limited-production masterpiece of the 812 family. Ferrari bumped output to 819 hp, added a new 9,500-rpm redline (the highest of any road-going Ferrari V12 ever), and stripped 38 kg through carbon fiber bodywork and a redesigned exhaust.

With only 999 coupes and 599 Aperta (targa) models built, the Competizione is already firmly a collector car. Prices have risen from MSRP of ~$600K to $750K–$1.1M for coupes and $1M–$1.5M+ for the Aperta. Allocation went exclusively to existing Ferrari clients, meaning most examples have impeccable provenance.

Cost of Owning a Ferrari 812 in Miami

ExpenseAnnual Estimated Cost
Insurance$5,000–$12,000 (depending on driving record & value)
Annual service (7-year included on newer cars)$0–$3,500
Major service (post-warranty)$3,000–$8,000
Tires (Pirelli P Zero or Michelin PS4S)$2,000–$3,500 per set
Brakes (carbon ceramic replacement)$12,000–$18,000 (every 30K–50K miles)
Storage (climate-controlled, optional)$3,000–$12,000
Florida sales tax (at purchase)~6% of sale price

One major advantage of the 812 over mid-engine Ferraris: the front-engine layout makes routine maintenance significantly easier and cheaper. Engine-out services — the bane of 488 and F8 ownership — aren't necessary on the 812.

Ferrari 812 vs. the New 12Cilindri — Should You Wait?

Ferrari's successor to the 812, the 12Cilindri, packs a twin-turbo 6.5L V12 with 820 hp. It's faster on paper, more refined, and packed with the latest tech. So why buy an 812 instead?

  • The engine character — The 812's naturally aspirated V12 revs to 8,500 rpm (9,500 in the Competizione) with a linear, screaming powerband. The 12Cilindri's turbo V12 is powerful but different in character.
  • Investment potential — The 812 is a "last of its kind" car. The 12Cilindri, however good, is the first of a new generation and will depreciate initially.
  • Immediate availability — You can buy a 812 today. The 12Cilindri has a multi-year waitlist for new allocations.

For drivers who prioritize raw emotion and future collectibility, the 812 is the clear choice. For those wanting the latest technology and don't mind waiting, the 12Cilindri is the future.

Pre-Purchase Inspection Checklist for Ferrari 812

Before buying any Ferrari 812 for sale, ensure:

  • Full Ferrari service history — Gaps in dealer service records hurt resale significantly
  • Paint meter check — Verify original paint on all panels; repainted 812s lose 10–15% value
  • Suspension check — The magnetorheological dampers are expensive to replace ($4K–$8K per corner)
  • Recall status — Several 812 recalls issued for fuel system and airbag components; ensure all completed
  • Tire date codes — Flat-spotted tires from long storage are common on low-mile examples
  • PPI by Ferrari-authorized shop — Budget $500–$1,000 for a thorough pre-purchase inspection at The Collection or Ferrari of Fort Lauderdale

Bottom Line: Is the Ferrari 812 Worth It in 2026?

The Ferrari 812 for sale market in Miami offers one of the most compelling propositions in the exotic car world right now. You're getting the last naturally aspirated V12 Ferrari ever made, in a city built for driving it year-round, at prices that — for the Superfast at least — are still within reach for serious enthusiasts.

The Superfast under $300K is the value play. The GTS is the Miami-perfect open-top V12. And the Competizione is a future seven-figure collector car you can still buy in the low seven figures today. Whichever variant you choose, you're buying a piece of Ferrari history that's only going to become more significant with time.

title: Best Touchless Car Drying Blowers & Forced Air Dryers for Exotic Cars in Miami
excerpt: Towel-drying a $300K paint job is a gamble. These forced-air car dryers eliminate swirl risk entirely — and they're built for Miami's year-round wash schedule.
content:
Here's a truth that every Miami exotic car owner learns the hard way: towels cause swirl marks. Even the softest, most expensive microfiber towel drags microscopic debris across your paint with every pass. On a $3,000 Grigio Telesto Ferrari paint job or a $15,000 custom Lamborghini wrap, that's an expensive lesson.

The solution is forced-air drying — using powerful, filtered blowers to push water off your car's surface without ever touching the paint. Professional detailers in Miami have been using these for years. Now the home-use options are good enough (and affordable enough) that there's no excuse to towel-dry an exotic car ever again.

We tested and researched the best touchless car drying blowers on the market, with a focus on what works for Miami's year-round washing reality: frequent washes, high humidity, and the salt-air residue that makes drying even more critical.

Why Touchless Drying Matters More in Miami

Miami's environment is uniquely punishing for car paint:

  • Salt air deposits: Even if you never drive on the beach, airborne salt settles on your car daily. When you towel-dry, those salt crystals become micro-abrasives dragging across your clear coat.
  • Frequent washing: Most Miami exotic owners wash weekly or more. That's 50+ towel-drying sessions per year — each one adding micro-scratches that compound into visible swirl marks.
  • Hard water spots: Miami's municipal water is notoriously mineral-heavy. If water beads dry in the sun (which takes about 90 seconds in July), they etch into clear coat. Forced air removes every drop before evaporation.
  • Year-round UV: Swirl marks that might be invisible in Seattle become glaringly obvious under Miami's intense sun, especially on dark-colored cars.

Best Touchless Car Drying Blowers — Our Picks

The BigBoi BlowR PRO is what most professional Miami detailers reach for. Dual brushless motors deliver enough force to blow water out of every crevice — side mirrors, door handles, badges, fuel door, wheel lug holes — in about 5 minutes flat on a full-size sedan. The HEPA filter is the key feature: it ensures you're blowing clean, filtered air onto your paint, not garage dust and pollen.

For Miami owners washing in their garage or driveway, the BlowR PRO handles everything from a Porsche 911 to a Rolls-Royce Cullinan without breaking a sweat. The variable speed control lets you dial it down for delicate areas like convertible top seams.

Who it's for: The value-conscious enthusiast who wants serious performance without the premium brand tax.

Comparison: All Five Blowers Side by Side

SGCB Pro$130–$180200 MPH6.8 lbsNoBest value, warm air option
Adam's Air Cannon$200–$280250 MPH7.2 lbsYesAll-rounder, quality build

How to Dry an Exotic Car with a Blower — The Right Technique

Having a great blower is step one. Using it correctly is step two. Here's the technique Miami's best detailers use:

  1. Start from the top down: Begin at the roof and work your way down. Water flows downward — don't fight gravity.
  2. Keep the nozzle 6-12 inches from the surface: Too close and you risk pushing water into crevices instead of off the car. Too far and you lose effectiveness.
  3. Use a sweeping motion: Move the blower in long, overlapping passes rather than focusing on one spot. This pushes water sheets off efficiently.
  4. Hit the trap zones: After the main panels, focus on: side mirror housings, door handle recesses, fuel door, trunk/hood seams, badge lettering, wheel lug holes, and window trim channels. These are where water hides and drips down onto dry panels five minutes later.
  5. Finish with wheel centers and brake calipers: Blow water out of wheel spokes, lug nut recesses, and around brake calipers. This prevents brake dust from forming water-spot rings.

Blower vs. Drying Towel vs. Drying Aid: Cost Over Time

MethodInitial CostAnnual Cost (52 washes)Swirl RiskTime per Dry
Premium microfiber towels$30–$60$100–$200 (replacement)Moderate15–20 min
Drying aid + towel$50–$80$150–$250Low-moderate12–18 min
Forced air blower$100–$500$0 (electricity only)Zero5–10 min

The math is clear: a blower pays for itself within the first year through saved towel costs alone — and that's before factoring in the paint correction you won't need because you eliminated towel-induced swirl marks. A single-stage paint correction on a Ferrari or Lamborghini in Miami runs $800–$1,500. One avoided correction pays for the best blower on this list three times over.

Pro Tips for Miami Blower Users

  • Blow before the sun hits: Wash and dry early morning or in shade. If the sun hits wet panels before you finish blowing, you'll get water spots anyway. Miami's morning hours (before 9 AM) are ideal.
  • Pair with a ceramic coating: A hydrophobic ceramic coating makes water bead up and sheet off faster, which means the blower works even more efficiently. It's the ultimate Miami combo.
  • Clean your filter monthly: In Miami's pollen-heavy spring and dusty dry season, blower filters clog faster. A dirty filter reduces airflow and can push debris onto your paint — defeating the whole purpose.
  • Store indoors: Miami's humidity can corrode internal motor components over time. Keep your blower inside, not in a non-climate-controlled garage.
  • Use the warm air setting in humidity: On 90%+ humidity days (so, most of summer), the warm air setting helps evaporate residual moisture that cool air alone can't remove.

Our Recommendation

For most Miami exotic car owners, the BigBoi BlowR PRO is the best investment. The dual motors, HEPA filter, and manageable weight make it the complete package for weekly home washing. If you're on a tighter budget, the SGCB Pro delivers remarkable value — and the warm air feature is genuinely useful in Miami's humidity.

Whatever you choose, switching from towel drying to forced air is one of the highest-ROI upgrades you can make for your car's paint. Your clear coat will thank you — and your detailer's paint correction bill will drop to zero.

title: Best Garage Storage Systems & Tool Carts for Miami Car Enthusiasts (2026)
excerpt: Your Miami garage deserves better than a pile of microfiber towels on a folding table. These tool carts, wall systems, and storage solutions turn a parking spot into a proper workshop.
content:
Every Miami car enthusiast eventually hits the same wall: you've got $50,000 worth of car in your garage and $50 worth of organization holding everything together. Bottles of ceramic coating balanced on a washing machine. A $400 polisher sitting on the concrete floor collecting dust. Microfiber towels stuffed in a plastic bin that also holds dog treats.

If you've invested in the car and the products, it's time to invest in where you keep them. A properly organized garage isn't just about aesthetics — it protects your tools, speeds up your workflow, and honestly makes the whole car care ritual more enjoyable. Here are the best garage storage systems and tool carts for Miami car enthusiasts, from weekend detailers to full-blown home garage builds.

Why Garage Storage Matters More in Miami

Miami's climate creates specific challenges that most garage organization guides ignore:

  • Humidity: Year-round 60-80%+ humidity means metal tools rust, chemical products degrade faster, and microfiber towels develop mildew if stored improperly. Sealed, climate-aware storage isn't optional here.
  • Heat: Garage temperatures in Miami can exceed 110°F in summer. Some chemicals (spray waxes, certain coatings) have storage temperature limits. Ventilated, shaded storage extends product life.
  • Insects and pests: Open bins and unsealed containers attract everything from palmetto bugs to lizards. Enclosed cabinets with gaskets are worth the premium.
  • Salt air corrosion: Even inland Miami garages get salt air infiltration. Stainless steel or powder-coated storage outlasts raw steel significantly.

title: How to Detail Your Exotic Car in Your Miami Driveway: A Step-by-Step Guide
excerpt: You don't need a $200 detail appointment to keep your exotic looking showroom-fresh. Here's the exact process Miami's best detailers use — adapted for your driveway.
content:
Professional detailing in Miami runs $150-$500 per session for exotic cars. If you're doing it every two weeks — and in Miami's climate, you should be — that's $4,000-$13,000 a year. Or you could do it yourself, get better results (because nobody cares about your car more than you), and spend a fraction of the cost on products that last months.

Here's the exact step-by-step process to detail your exotic car in your Miami driveway. We'll cover timing, products, technique, and the Miami-specific adjustments that most generic detailing guides miss.

Before You Start: Miami-Specific Rules

  • Time it right: Never detail in direct sun. In Miami, that means early morning (before 9 AM) or late afternoon (after 5 PM). Products flash-dry in the midday heat and leave streaks and residue.
  • Work in sections: Even in the shade, Miami's humidity and heat mean products dry faster. Wash, clay, and coat one panel at a time.
  • Use filtered water if possible: Miami tap water is hard. It leaves mineral deposits (water spots) that etch into clear coat. A deionized water filter attachment ($50-$80) eliminates this problem entirely.
  • Park on concrete, not grass: Florida grass = fire ants. You don't want to discover them while you're lying on the ground cleaning wheel wells.

Step 1: Pre-Rinse and Foam Cannon (10 minutes)

Start by rinsing the entire car with a pressure washer to blast off loose dirt, sand, and salt. Then load your Chemical Guys TORQ Foam Cannon with Chemical Guys Citrus Wash & Gloss and blanket the car in thick foam. Let it dwell for 3-5 minutes.

This step is non-negotiable in Miami. Salt crystals and sand sit on your paint — if you skip the foam pre-soak and go straight to hand washing, you're grinding those particles into your clear coat.

Shop Chemical Guys Foam Cannon + Citrus Wash →

Step 2: Two-Bucket Hand Wash (15 minutes)

Use two buckets: one with soap solution, one with clean rinse water. Both should have grit guards at the bottom. Dip your Chemical Guys Chenille Wash Mitt in the soap bucket, wash one panel, then rinse the mitt in the clean bucket before reloading with soap.

Work top-down (roof → hood/trunk → upper sides → lower sides → bumpers). The lower panels are always dirtiest — you don't want to drag that grime up to the hood.

Pro tip: Use a separate mitt and bucket for wheels. Brake dust is metallic and will scratch paint if transferred.

Shop Chemical Guys Wash Mitt →

Step 3: Iron Removal (5 minutes)

After washing, spray the entire car with Chemical Guys Decon Pro Iron Remover. You'll see purple/red spots appear — that's the product reacting with embedded iron particles. Let it sit for 2-3 minutes, then rinse thoroughly. This step removes contamination that washing alone can't touch.

In Miami, iron contamination comes from brake dust (I-95 stop-and-go), construction debris (cranes on every block downtown), and Metrorail rail dust if you park anywhere near the tracks.

Shop Chemical Guys Decon Pro →

Step 4: Clay Bar Treatment (20 minutes)

Tear off a small piece of Chemical Guys Heavy Duty Clay Bar, flatten it, and spray the panel with clay lubricant. Glide the clay back and forth with light pressure. You'll feel it grabbing contaminants at first, then the surface becomes silky smooth. Fold the clay to expose a fresh surface every few passes.

Do this quarterly at minimum. Miami's airborne contaminants are relentless — your paint accumulates more embedded particles in one month here than three months in most other cities.

Shop Chemical Guys Clay Bar Kit →

Step 5: Dry — Properly (10 minutes)

Never let a car air-dry in Miami. The hard water and humidity guarantee water spots. Use a large, plush microfiber drying towel or a dedicated car blower/dryer. Pat dry, don't drag — dragging creates micro-scratches on freshly cleaned paint.

Pro tip: Blow out water trapped in mirrors, door handles, emblems, and panel gaps first. This water drips out later and creates runs through your freshly applied coating.

Step 6: Polish (Optional — 30 minutes)

If your paint has swirl marks, oxidation, or light scratches, this is when you correct them. Use a dual-action polisher (Chemical Guys TORQ 15DA is excellent) with a medium-cut polish. Work one panel at a time, 3-4 passes, medium speed and pressure.

Skip this step if your paint is in good condition — polishing removes a microscopic layer of clear coat, so only do it when needed.

Shop Chemical Guys TORQ Polisher →

Step 7: Ceramic Coating or Sealant (20 minutes)

This is the protection layer — the most important step for Miami cars. You have two options:

  • Quick option: Chemical Guys HydroSlick Ceramic Coating Hyperwax — spray on, spread with a microfiber, buff off. Takes 10 minutes. Lasts 2-4 weeks. Do it every wash.
  • Long-lasting option: Chemical Guys JetSeal — apply a thin layer, let it haze, buff off. Lasts 6-12 months. Reapply twice a year.

In Miami, ceramic/sealant protection isn't cosmetic — it's structural. UV rays degrade unprotected clear coat measurably within weeks. Salt air accelerates that. A proper sealant layer is the single most important thing you can do for your paint.

Shop Chemical Guys HydroSlick →

Step 8: Interior (20 minutes)

While the exterior coating cures, move inside:

  • Vacuum all carpets, mats, and seat crevices. Miami's sand gets everywhere.
  • Leather: Clean with Chemical Guys Leather Cleaner, then condition with Chemical Guys Leather Conditioner. The heat in a parked Miami car is brutal on leather — conditioning every 2-4 weeks prevents cracking.
  • Dashboard and trim: Spray Chemical Guys InnerClean on a microfiber and wipe all surfaces. The UV blockers in this product prevent the cracked, faded dashes that plague every 3+ year old Florida car.
  • Glass: Clean inside glass last — it collects outgassing film from the dash in Miami's heat.

Shop Chemical Guys Leather & Interior Kit →

Step 9: Trim and Tires (10 minutes)

Apply Chemical Guys VRP Dressing to all exterior black trim, rubber seals, and tire sidewalls. Use an applicator pad for even coverage. VRP gives a deep, natural-looking finish without the greasy, sling-off mess of cheap tire shine.

Check your tires for dry rot while you're down there — Miami's heat accelerates rubber degradation, and Florida has some of the highest tire blowout rates in the country.

Shop Chemical Guys VRP →

Step 10: Final Inspection (5 minutes)

Walk around the car in good light. Check for:

  • Missed water spots (especially on glass and chrome)
  • Streaks from product that dried too fast
  • Trim dressing on paint (wipe off immediately)
  • Any areas the sealant/coating missed

Total Time: About 2 Hours

That's for a full detail. Weekly maintenance washes (Steps 1-2 and 5 only) take 30 minutes. The quarterly deep clean (all steps) takes the full two hours but keeps your exotic looking showroom-fresh year-round.

Annual cost (bi-weekly)$200-$300$5,200-$13,000
Annual savings$5,000-$12,700

The math is clear. Invest in the right products, spend two hours on a Saturday morning, and your exotic will look better than 90% of the cars at any Miami car meet.
