title: How Miami's Salt Air Is Destroying Your Car — And How to Stop It
excerpt: Living near the ocean in Miami means your car is under constant chemical attack. Here's the science behind salt air corrosion and the products that actually prevent it.
content:
You moved to Miami for the ocean views. Your car didn't sign up for that. If you live or park within 5 miles of the coast — which in Miami-Dade, is basically everywhere — your vehicle is under constant assault from airborne salt particles, and the damage is happening faster than you think.

The Science: What Salt Air Actually Does to Your Car

Ocean air carries microscopic salt crystals that deposit on every surface of your vehicle. When combined with Miami's humidity (averaging 73% year-round), these crystals form a saline solution on your paint, metal, and rubber. This triggers electrochemical corrosion — essentially, your car is slowly rusting from the outside in.

The damage isn't just cosmetic:

  • Clear coat degradation: Salt crystals create micro-abrasions and chemical etching in clear coat within weeks of exposure
  • Metal corrosion: Brake components, suspension bolts, exhaust systems, and undercarriage metal corrode 5-10x faster near the coast
  • Rubber deterioration: Salt accelerates rubber dry rot in seals, tires, and hoses
  • Electrical connections: Salt deposits on electrical connectors cause resistance and intermittent failures
  • Chrome pitting: Exhaust tips, trim pieces, and wheels develop permanent pitting if salt isn't removed regularly

How Close Is Too Close?

Studies show that salt air concentration drops significantly after 1 mile from the coast and is minimal after 5 miles. Here's the bad news for Miami car owners:

Distance from CoastSalt Corrosion RiskMiami Areas
Under 1 mileSevereMiami Beach, Key Biscayne, Brickell waterfront, Sunny Isles
1-3 milesHighDowntown, Wynwood, Coconut Grove, Coral Gables east
3-5 milesModerateLittle Havana, Doral east, Aventura
5+ milesLowWestchester, Kendall, Hialeah, Homestead

If you live on the beach and park outside, your car is in the severe zone. Even a covered garage in Miami Beach still exposes your car to salt air every time you drive.

The Defense Plan: Products That Actually Work

Layer 1: Wash Off the Salt — Weekly

The single most important thing you can do is wash your car every week. Salt accumulates daily, and every day it sits on your paint, it's doing damage. Use a pH-neutral car wash soap — Chemical Guys Citrus Wash & Gloss is ideal because the citrus formula actively dissolves salt deposits rather than just rinsing over them.

Pay special attention to:

  • Wheel wells and undercarriage (where salt builds up most)
  • Door jambs and trunk hinges (salt collects in crevices)
  • Around emblems and trim pieces (salt hides in gaps)

Shop Chemical Guys Citrus Wash & Gloss →

Layer 2: Decontaminate — Monthly

Washing removes surface salt, but embedded particles need more aggressive treatment. Once a month, use Chemical Guys Decon Pro Iron Remover to chemically dissolve metallic contaminants, followed by a Chemical Guys Clay Bar treatment to physically pull out everything else.

This combo removes contaminants that washing alone misses — the stuff that's already bonded to your clear coat and is actively degrading it.

Shop Chemical Guys Decon Pro + Clay Bar →

Layer 3: Seal the Paint — Quarterly

A bare paint surface absorbs salt and UV damage with no resistance. A sealed surface repels both. Your options:

  • Best budget option: Chemical Guys JetSeal — synthetic sealant that lasts 6-12 months and provides genuine UV + salt barrier. Apply once a quarter for maximum protection.
  • Best weekly option: Chemical Guys HydroSlick Ceramic Coating Hyperwax — spray-on ceramic protection you apply after every wash. The hydrophobic layer repels salt water on contact.
  • Best permanent option: Professional ceramic coating (Ceramic Pro, Gtechniq, or similar) — $1,200-$3,000 but lasts 2-5 years. Worth it for cars parked near the coast daily.

Shop Chemical Guys JetSeal →

Layer 4: Protect the Trim and Rubber

Salt doesn't just attack paint — it destroys every exterior surface. Chemical Guys VRP Dressing creates a protective barrier on vinyl, rubber, and plastic trim. Apply it to:

  • Tire sidewalls
  • Black plastic trim (bumpers, mirrors, fender flares)
  • Rubber door seals and window gaskets
  • Wiper blades

Without protection, black trim turns chalky grey within 6 months in Miami. Rubber seals crack and leak. Wiper blades deteriorate and streak. VRP prevents all of it.

Shop Chemical Guys VRP →

Layer 5: Protect the Undercarriage

This is the most overlooked area. Your undercarriage is exposed to more salt spray than any other part of the car — every puddle you drive through in Miami contains dissolved salt. Options:

  • DIY: Spray undercarriage with a rust inhibitor like Fluid Film or CRC Marine every 6 months
  • Professional: Get an undercoating treatment ($200-$400/year) — worth it for cars you plan to keep long-term
  • Weekly: Use an undercarriage attachment on your pressure washer during weekly washes to blast salt deposits off

Layer 6: Protect the Interior

Salt air gets inside your car too — through the HVAC system, open windows, and every time you open a door. It settles on leather, plastics, and electronics. Use Chemical Guys InnerClean Interior Detailer weekly on all interior surfaces. Its UV and contamination protection prevents the accelerated interior degradation that's unique to coastal Florida cars.

For leather specifically, Chemical Guys Leather Conditioner monthly creates a barrier that prevents salt and humidity from drying out and cracking your seats.

Shop Chemical Guys Interior Care →

The Real Cost of Ignoring Salt Air

Damage TypeTimeline (Unprotected)Repair Cost
Clear coat failure2-3 years$3,000-$8,000 (full respray)
Brake caliper corrosion1-2 years$500-$2,000
Trim fading/chalking6-12 months$500-$1,500 (replacement)
Rubber seal failure2-3 years$300-$800
Electrical connector corrosion3-5 years$200-$2,000 (diagnosis + repair)
Undercarriage rust3-5 years$1,000-$5,000+

Total potential damage: $5,500-$19,300. Total annual prevention cost with the right products: $200-$400. The math speaks for itself.

The Miami Salt Air Defense Checklist

  • ☐ Weekly: Full wash with salt-dissolving soap + undercarriage rinse
  • ☐ Bi-weekly: Interior wipe-down with UV-protective cleaner
  • ☐ Monthly: Iron decontamination + clay bar + leather conditioning + trim dressing
  • ☐ Quarterly: Sealant or ceramic coating reapplication
  • ☐ Bi-annually: Undercarriage rust inhibitor treatment
  • ☐ Annually: Full paint condition assessment + professional detail

Your car didn't choose to live near the ocean. You did. The least you can do is protect it.

  • Price transparency: Auction format reveals true market value. No dealer markup games.
  • Vehicle History Reports: Integrated Carfax/AutoCheck on most listings
  • Buyer Protection: eBay's Money Back Guarantee covers vehicles up to $100,000
  • Buy It Now: Skip the auction and buy at a fixed price when you find the right car

Best Exotic Car Categories on eBay Motors

Ferraris Under $200K

The sweet spot on eBay Motors. You'll find F430s, 458 Italias, California Ts, and early Romas listed by private sellers and small dealers nationwide. Private sellers especially price competitively because they're avoiding dealer consignment fees (typically 5-10%).

Browse Ferraris on eBay Motors →

Lamborghini Huracáns

The Huracán is Miami's unofficial city car. Used examples from 2015-2020 have dropped significantly as the Temerario approaches. eBay regularly has Huracáns listed $10-30K below local Miami dealer prices because sellers in less exotic-friendly markets (think Ohio, Minnesota) can't move them as easily.

Browse Lamborghini Huracáns on eBay Motors →

Porsche 911 (991/992)

The 911 is the most liquid exotic on the market — which means eBay has huge inventory. Turbo S models, GT3s, and GTS variants all trade actively. The auction format is particularly good for 911s because the market is well-established and buyers know exactly what fair value is.

Browse Porsche 911s on eBay Motors →

McLarens (Best Value Play)

McLarens depreciate harder than any other exotic brand. A 570S that stickered at $200K+ can be found on eBay for $120-140K. The 720S is following the same curve. If you want the most supercar for your money, McLarens on eBay Motors are where the deals are.

Browse McLarens on eBay Motors →

The Miami Buyer's Advantage

Living in Miami gives you a unique edge when buying on eBay Motors:

  • No state income tax: Florida's tax-friendly environment means lower total cost of ownership
  • Shipping hub: Miami's port and logistics infrastructure means shipping a car from anywhere in the US is fast and affordable ($500-$1,200 enclosed transport from most cities)
  • Huge service network: Once the car arrives, you have access to Ferrari, Lamborghini, Porsche, and McLaren authorized service right in Miami-Dade
  • Strong resale market: If you decide to sell, Miami's local demand for exotics means you'll get more than sellers in smaller markets

How to Buy Safely on eBay Motors

1. Check the Seller

Look for sellers with 98%+ positive feedback and a history of vehicle sales. Power sellers and dealers with eBay storefronts are generally safer. Avoid first-time sellers listing a $150K car — the risk/reward isn't worth it.

2. Get a Pre-Purchase Inspection

Never buy an exotic sight-unseen without a PPI. Services like Lemon Squad and SGS will send an inspector to the car's location for $200-$350. They'll check mechanical condition, body panel gaps (accident indicator), paint depth, and electronics. Non-negotiable for any car over $50K.

3. Verify the VIN

Run the VIN through Carfax, AutoCheck, and the NICB (National Insurance Crime Bureau) stolen vehicle database. For Ferraris specifically, also check the Ferrari Classiche registry for service history.

4. Understand the Auction

  • Reserve auctions: The seller sets a minimum price. If bidding doesn't reach it, the car doesn't sell. You can message the seller to ask what the reserve is.
  • No reserve: The car sells to the highest bidder regardless of price. This is where the best deals happen — but also where emotional bidding can burn you.
  • Buy It Now: Fixed price, no waiting. Usually priced slightly above auction market value but the convenience is worth it.

5. Arrange Transport

Use enclosed transport only for exotics. Open carriers expose the car to road debris and weather. Reliable enclosed carriers for Florida delivery:

  • Intercity Lines — specializes in exotic and classic car transport
  • Passport Transport — white-glove enclosed service
  • uShip — marketplace for carriers, get competing quotes

eBay Motors vs. Other Platforms

PlatformBest ForPrice LevelBuyer Protection
eBay MotorsBest deals, widest selectionBelow marketStrong (Money Back Guarantee)
Bring a TrailerEnthusiast cars, curatedAt/above marketLimited
Cars & BidsModern enthusiast carsAt marketLimited
DuPont RegistryUltra-luxury, new inventoryAbove marketNone (dealer listings)
Local dealersSee before buyingAbove marketDealer warranty

Current Deals Worth Watching

eBay Motors inventory changes daily, but these categories consistently offer the best value for Miami buyers:

  • 2015-2018 Lamborghini Huracán LP 610-4: $150-180K — down from $260K+ new
  • 2017-2020 Ferrari 488 GTB: $220-260K — the last naturally-aspirated-feeling turbo V8
  • 2018-2021 McLaren 720S: $160-200K — arguably the best performance per dollar in any exotic
  • 2019-2022 Porsche 911 Turbo S (992): $180-210K — the all-weather supercar

Browse all exotic cars on eBay Motors →

After the Purchase: Get It Miami-Ready

Once your eBay find arrives in Miami, get it properly protected for the climate. Salt air, UV, and humidity will start working on it immediately. At minimum:

  • Full paint correction and ceramic coating
  • PPF (paint protection film) on high-impact areas
  • Interior leather conditioning
  • Undercarriage rust inhibitor treatment

Welcome to Miami. Your car's going to love it here — if you take care of it.

title: Best Deals on Exotic Car Wheels & Tires: eBay vs. Local Miami Shops
excerpt: Replacing wheels or tires on an exotic in Miami? eBay often beats local shops by 20-40%. Here's how to find the right fitment and avoid costly mistakes.
content:
Wheels and tires are the most expensive routine maintenance item on any exotic car. A set of OEM wheels for a Lamborghini Huracán runs $8,000-$12,000 at the dealer. Tires for a Ferrari 488 are $2,000-$3,000 per set. And in Miami, where potholes on I-95 and construction debris downtown eat wheels for breakfast, replacements aren't a matter of if — they're a matter of when.

eBay has become the go-to source for exotic car wheels and tires, consistently undercutting Miami dealer and shop prices by 20-40%. Here's how to buy smart.

Why eBay for Exotic Wheels?

  • OEM takeoffs: Owners upgrading to aftermarket wheels sell their factory wheels on eBay — often with 90%+ tread tires still mounted. You get practically new OEM wheels at 40-60% off retail.
  • Aftermarket variety: HRE, Vossen, Forgiato, ADV.1, BBS — every major wheel brand has authorized sellers on eBay with full fitment data
  • Price competition: Multiple sellers = market pricing. No single dealer markup.
  • Returns: eBay's return policy means if fitment is wrong, you're covered

Best Wheel Deals by Car

Lamborghini Huracán / Performante

OEM Huracán wheels (Giano, Mimas, or Aesir designs) regularly sell for $3,000-$5,000 per set on eBay — compared to $8,000-$12,000 at the dealer. The Performante's forged wheels command a premium but still save 30%+ vs. new.

Browse Huracán Wheels on eBay →

Ferrari 488 / F8 / Roma

Ferrari's forged diamond-cut wheels are stunning — and insanely expensive to replace through the dealer ($3,000+ per wheel). eBay sellers regularly list complete sets of OEM Ferrari wheels for $4,000-$7,000. Just verify the finish hasn't been curbed (common in Miami with our aggressive curbs).

Browse Ferrari Wheels on eBay →

Porsche 911 (991/992)

Porsche wheels are the most liquid on eBay — massive inventory means great prices. OEM Sport Design and Turbo S wheels go for $2,000-$4,000 per set. Aftermarket options from BBS and HRE are also well-represented.

Browse 911 Wheels on eBay →

McLaren 570S / 720S

McLaren's lightweight forged wheels are the most expensive OEM wheels in this segment — $15,000+ for a set from the dealer. eBay is often the only affordable option, with used sets running $5,000-$8,000. Always check for hairline cracks on McLaren wheels — they're forged thin for weight savings.

Browse McLaren Wheels on eBay →

Aftermarket Wheels: Best Brands for Miami Exotics

Vossen

Based right here in Miami (Wynwood), Vossen is the hometown favorite. Their forged series (S17, S21) are popular on Huracáns and 911s. eBay has both new and used Vossen sets — used ones save 40-50% off retail.

Browse Vossen Wheels on eBay →

HRE Performance Wheels

The gold standard for exotic car wheels. HRE's FlowForm series offers the look at a more accessible price point, while their forged 300 and 500 series are the ultimate. eBay is one of the few places to find used HREs — they hold value extremely well.

Browse HRE Wheels on eBay →

Forgiato

If you want the Miami look — aggressive fitment, custom finishes, big lips — Forgiato is the move. They're on every other exotic in Wynwood. eBay has custom-built Forgiatos from owners who changed styles, often at 50%+ off custom order pricing.

Browse Forgiato Wheels on eBay →

Tires: eBay vs. Miami Tire Shops

Exotic car tires are a commodity — the same Michelin Pilot Sport 4S or Pirelli P Zero is the same tire regardless of where you buy it. The only variable is price and freshness.

TireSize (Example: Huracán)eBay PriceLocal Shop PriceSavings
Pirelli P Zero (Front)245/30ZR20$280-$320$380-$42025%
Pirelli P Zero (Rear)305/30ZR20$340-$380$450-$50024%
Michelin PS4S (Front)245/30ZR20$300-$340$400-$44023%
Michelin PS4S (Rear)305/30ZR20$360-$400$470-$52023%
Set of 4 savings$400-$600

Important: Check the DOT date code on any tires you buy on eBay. Tires older than 2 years from manufacture should be avoided, especially in Miami where heat accelerates rubber degradation. The DOT code is on the sidewall — the last 4 digits indicate week and year of manufacture (e.g., 2425 = week 24, 2025).

Browse Michelin Pilot Sport 4S on eBay →

Fitment Guide: Don't Get It Wrong

Exotic cars have very specific wheel fitments. Getting it wrong means the wheel doesn't fit — or worse, it fits but causes rubbing, vibration, or suspension damage. Here's what to verify:

  • Bolt pattern: Must be exact (e.g., 5x112 for Huracán, 5x130 for 911)
  • Center bore: Must match or be hubcentric-ring compatible
  • Offset (ET): Critical for exotic cars — even 5mm off can cause rubbing on wide-body cars
  • Width: Front and rear are almost always different on exotics (staggered setup)
  • TPMS sensors: Many eBay wheels don't include TPMS sensors. Budget $200-$400 for a new set and programming.

Pro Tips for Buying Wheels on eBay

  1. Ask for close-up photos of the barrel and lip. Curb rash hides in listing photos. Ask the seller for detailed shots of each wheel's outer edge.
  2. Check for refinishing. Badly refinished wheels are worse than curbed ones. Look for orange peel in the finish, uneven color, or overspray on the barrel.
  3. Buy local when possible. Search eBay with your zip code to find Florida sellers. Saves $200-$400 in shipping on heavy wheel sets.
  4. Factor in mounting and balancing. Budget $25-$40 per wheel at a local shop. Road force balancing ($40-$60/wheel) is worth it for exotics — it eliminates vibrations that standard balancing misses.
  5. Keep your OEM wheels. Even if you go aftermarket, store your factory wheels. They protect resale value significantly.

Where to Get Wheels Mounted in Miami

Once your eBay wheels arrive, you need a shop that knows how to handle exotic car wheels without damaging them:

  • RENNtech — specialty exotic shop, proper equipment for low-profile exotic tires
  • Wheels Boutique — Wynwood, specializes in aftermarket wheel mounting for exotics
  • Any authorized dealer service center — most expensive option but guaranteed proper equipment

Avoid generic tire shops for exotic car wheels. The machines need special adapters and non-marring clamps to avoid scratching expensive finishes.

title: 15 Exotic Car Parts & Accessories You Should Always Buy on eBay
excerpt: Dealer markups on exotic car parts are insane. These 15 items are consistently 30-60% cheaper on eBay — with the same OEM quality.
content:
Owning an exotic car in Miami is expensive enough without paying dealer prices for every part and accessory. The secret that experienced exotic car owners know: eBay is the single best source for OEM and aftermarket parts, consistently saving 30-60% versus dealer pricing.

Here are 15 parts and accessories you should always buy on eBay instead of at the dealer.

1. Carbon Fiber Mirror Caps

Dealer price: $800-$1,500/pair. eBay price: $200-$500/pair. Carbon fiber mirror caps are one of the most popular visual upgrades for Ferraris, Lamborghinis, and McLarens. OEM takeoffs and high-quality aftermarket options flood eBay. The fit is identical — carbon is carbon.

Browse Carbon Fiber Mirror Caps →

2. Brake Pads (OEM)

Exotic car brake pads at the dealer are criminal — $500-$1,200 for a set. The same Brembo or Pagid pads on eBay run $150-$400. These are genuine OEM supplier parts, just without the dealer markup. Front pads on a Huracán last about 15,000 miles in Miami traffic, so you'll be buying these regularly.

Browse OEM Brake Pads →

3. Air Filters

A K&N or BMC performance air filter for an exotic runs $80-$150 on eBay vs. $200-$400 at the dealer for the OEM paper filter. Performance filters are reusable — wash and re-oil every 15,000 miles. In Miami's dusty construction zones, a quality air filter matters.

Browse Performance Air Filters →

4. Floor Mats (OEM & Custom)

Ferrari and Lamborghini floor mats at the dealer: $300-$600. eBay has OEM takeoffs for $100-$200 and custom-fit luxury alternatives for even less. In Miami, where sand and rain are constant passengers, having a spare set of mats to rotate is smart ownership.

Browse Exotic Car Floor Mats →

5. Carbon Fiber Engine Covers

The engine bay is the centerpiece of any mid-engine exotic. A carbon fiber engine cover transforms the look — and on eBay, you'll find options for every major platform at 40-60% below dealer pricing. Popular for Huracán, 488, and 720S.

Browse Carbon Engine Covers →

6. LED Interior Light Kits

Swap out the dim, yellow factory interior bulbs for bright LED units. Full interior LED kits for exotics run $30-$80 on eBay vs. $200+ at the dealer (if they even offer it). Plug-and-play, no wiring modification needed. White or cool blue options available.

Browse LED Interior Kits →

7. Key Fob Cases & Covers

Exotic car key fobs are fragile and expensive to replace ($500-$2,000). A quality carbon fiber or leather key fob case protects your investment for $20-$60 on eBay. Ferrari and Lamborghini key cases are the most popular — and they look fantastic.

Browse Key Fob Cases →

8. Exhaust Tips & Valved Exhaust Components

Aftermarket exhaust tips transform the rear end of any exotic. Carbon fiber and titanium options on eBay run $200-$600 vs. $800-$2,000 from boutique shops. For those wanting more sound, valved exhaust controllers (open/close the valves on demand) are $100-$300 on eBay.

Browse Exhaust Tips →

9. Radar Detectors & Mounting Systems

Miami-Dade and Broward are aggressive with speed enforcement, especially on 836, Turnpike, and I-75. A quality radar detector is essential. The Valentine One Gen2 and Uniden R8 are the top choices — eBay often has them $50-$100 below retail. Custom exotic-car mounting brackets are also available.

Browse Radar Detectors →

10. Car Covers (Indoor & Outdoor)

A proper car cover is non-negotiable in Miami — even in a garage, dust and humidity attack your paint. Custom-fit covers for exotics run $150-$400 on eBay vs. $500-$1,200 from the dealer. Look for breathable, UV-resistant fabric with soft fleece lining.

Browse Custom Car Covers →

11. Dash Cameras

Miami drivers are... aggressive. A dash cam protects you in insurance claims and captures your spirited drives. The BlackVue DR900X Plus is the favorite among exotic owners — discreet, 4K, and cloud-connected. eBay consistently beats Amazon pricing on BlackVue units.

Browse Dash Cameras →

12. Wheel Spacers

Properly engineered hub-centric wheel spacers give your exotic a more aggressive stance without new wheels. Quality forged spacers from brands like Bonoss and H&R run $100-$250 per pair on eBay. Always buy hub-centric, always use proper torque specs.

Browse Wheel Spacers →

13. Suspension Lowering Links

Most modern exotics have adjustable ride height via electronic suspension. Lowering links let you drop the car 1-2 inches for a better stance without modifying the factory suspension system. $100-$300 on eBay vs. $500+ from specialty shops. Reversible and dealer-friendly.

Browse Lowering Links →

14. Paint Protection Film (PPF) Kits

Pre-cut PPF kits for exotics are available on eBay for $200-$500 vs. $2,000-$5,000 for professional installation. If you're handy (or know a good installer), buying the kit on eBay and paying labor only saves thousands. XPEL and 3M kits are both available.

Browse PPF Kits →

15. OEM Replacement Parts (Lights, Sensors, Trim)

This is the catch-all category — and where the biggest savings hide. OEM headlight assemblies, tail lights, parking sensors, interior trim pieces, and body clips are all massively marked up at the dealer. eBay sellers (many are dealer parts departments selling surplus) offer genuine OEM parts at 30-50% discounts.

Browse OEM Exotic Car Parts →

Shopping Tips for Exotic Parts on eBay

  • Filter by "Brand New" for safety items (brake pads, filters, sensors). Used is fine for cosmetic items.
  • Check compatibility notes carefully. Many parts are model-year specific — a 2018 Huracán Performante uses different parts than a 2015 base model.
  • Buy from US sellers to avoid 2-4 week international shipping and potential customs delays.
  • Save searches with alerts. Set up eBay alerts for specific parts you need — prices fluctuate and patience pays off.
  • Use eBay's Best Offer feature. Many sellers accept 10-20% below listing price.

The days of paying dealer prices for exotic car parts are over. eBay's inventory, buyer protection, and price competition make it the smart choice for Miami exotic car owners who want to spend their money on driving — not on parts markups.

Browse all car parts and accessories on eBay →

title: 2026 Miami Grand Prix: Complete Ticket Guide — Where to Sit, What to Pay & How to Save
excerpt: The Miami Grand Prix is one of the hottest tickets in motorsport. Here's your complete guide to every grandstand, general admission, and hospitality option — plus how to score the best deals.
content:
The 2026 Miami Grand Prix returns to the Hard Rock Stadium complex in Miami Gardens for what's become one of the most anticipated events on the F1 calendar. Whether you're a die-hard F1 fan or just want to be part of Miami's biggest party weekend, getting the right tickets at the right price is everything.

Here's your complete guide to every seating option, realistic pricing, and the smartest ways to buy.

Miami Grand Prix 2026: Key Details

DetailInfo
LocationHard Rock Stadium, Miami Gardens, FL
CircuitMiami International Autodrome (3.363 miles, 19 turns)
Race WeekendFriday Practice → Saturday Sprint/Qualifying → Sunday Race
Capacity~80,000 per day
ParkingOn-site available, rideshare recommended

Seating Options & Price Guide

General Admission (GA)

The most affordable way in. GA gives you access to the grounds and designated standing/viewing areas around the circuit. You won't have an assigned seat, but you can roam between viewing zones. The experience is more "festival" than "Formula 1" — think food trucks, live music stages, and catching the action from different vantage points throughout the day.

  • Face value: $400-$600 (3-day pass)
  • Resale market: $300-$800 depending on demand
  • Best for: First-timers, social experience seekers, budget-conscious fans

Browse Miami GP General Admission Tickets →

Turn 1 Grandstand

The premiere viewing spot. Turn 1 is where drivers brake hard from the main straight at 200+ mph into a tight right-hander — this is where overtakes happen, where mistakes happen, and where the action is most intense. The grandstand is massive and tiered, giving every seat a clear sightline.

  • Face value: $1,000-$2,500 (3-day pass)
  • Resale market: $800-$3,500
  • Best for: Serious F1 fans who want the best on-track action

Browse Turn 1 Grandstand Tickets →

Beach Grandstand

Only in Miami. The Beach Grandstand overlooks a section of the track near the artificial beach/pool area — combining racing with the signature Miami vibe. It's as much about the scene as the racing. Expect influencers, celebrities, and champagne. The views of the track are decent but not the best for pure racing action.

  • Face value: $1,200-$3,000 (3-day pass)
  • Resale market: $1,000-$4,000
  • Best for: The Miami experience, social media, being seen

Browse Beach Grandstand Tickets →

Campus Grandstands (Turns 7-11)

The mid-range sweet spot. These grandstands cover the technical section of the circuit where driver skill matters most. You'll see cars navigating a series of medium-speed corners — great for comparing driving styles between teammates and rivals. Pricing is more reasonable than Turn 1 or Beach.

  • Face value: $700-$1,500 (3-day pass)
  • Resale market: $500-$2,000
  • Best for: Best value for actual racing viewing

Browse Campus Grandstand Tickets →

Hospitality & VIP Packages

If budget isn't the primary concern, Miami's F1 hospitality is on another level. Options range from the official F1 Paddock Club to team-affiliated hospitality suites. You get premium food, open bar, pit lane walks, driver appearances, and the best seats in the house.

  • F1 Paddock Club: $5,000-$10,000+ per person
  • Team Hospitality: $3,000-$8,000 per person
  • Premium Lounges: $2,000-$5,000 per person

Browse VIP & Hospitality Packages →

Where to Buy: Best Ticket Sources

Official Race Website

The F1 Miami GP official site (f1miamigp.com) is the primary source for face-value tickets. They sell out quickly — if you can get tickets at face value, that's always the best deal. Sign up for their email list for pre-sale access.

eBay

One of the best secondary markets for F1 tickets. eBay's buyer protection covers ticket purchases, and the auction format means you can sometimes score below-market deals — especially in the week leading up to the race when sellers who can't attend need to offload quickly.

Browse all Miami Grand Prix 2026 Tickets on eBay →

StubHub & SeatGeek

The big-name resale platforms. Prices tend to be higher than eBay due to service fees (20-30% on top of ticket price), but the guarantee policies are strong. Good option if you want maximum buyer protection and don't mind paying a premium.

Avoid Scams

Miami's F1 weekend attracts scammers every year. Rules to follow:

  • Never buy from random social media accounts — Instagram and X are full of fake ticket sellers
  • Never pay via Zelle, Venmo, or wire transfer — no buyer protection
  • Always use platforms with guarantees — eBay, StubHub, SeatGeek, or official channels
  • Verify ticket transfer method — legitimate sellers transfer through the official F1 ticketing platform, not PDFs

Money-Saving Strategies

Buy Early (or Very Late)

Ticket prices follow a U-curve. They're cheapest at initial on-sale (sold out quickly), then rise steadily, then sometimes drop in the final 48 hours before the race as sellers panic-sell. If you're willing to gamble on last-minute availability, you can save 20-30%.

Go Friday Only

If full 3-day passes are out of budget, Friday practice day tickets are significantly cheaper and still give you the full F1 atmosphere. The cars are on track, the campus is fully activated, and the crowds are smaller (better experience in many ways).

GA + Strategic Positioning

General Admission with a good spot can rival lower-tier grandstand views. Arrive early, claim a spot along the fence at Turns 14-16 (back straight chicane), and you'll see cars at close range with great overtaking action — for less than half the price of a grandstand seat.

Group Deals

The official site occasionally offers group pricing for 8+ tickets. If you're going with friends, have one person coordinate the purchase. Also check corporate packages — companies often have unused tickets they sell at a discount as the race approaches.

Race Weekend Survival Guide

  • Arrive early: Gates open 3-4 hours before the first session. Parking and security lines are brutal by mid-morning.
  • Hydrate aggressively: It's May in Miami. Temperatures hit 90°F+ with full humidity. Bring a sealed water bottle (most venues allow it) and refill constantly.
  • Sunscreen is mandatory: You're sitting in direct sun for 6+ hours. SPF 50+, reapply every 2 hours. Sunburn ruins race day fast.
  • Wear comfortable shoes: The Hard Rock complex is massive. You'll walk 3-5 miles easily over the course of a day.
  • Download the F1 app: Live timing, track map, radio commentary, and real-time positions. It transforms the experience, especially from GA where you can't see the full track.
  • Rideshare, don't drive: Parking is limited and expensive ($80-$150/day). Uber/Lyft surge pricing is painful but still usually cheaper and less stressful than parking.

Beyond the Race: Miami F1 Weekend Events

The race is just the centerpiece. Miami goes all-in on F1 weekend:

  • F1 After-Race Concert: Major headliners perform inside the stadium complex after Sunday's race (included with race ticket)
  • Wynwood F1 Festival: Art, cars, and music in Wynwood throughout the weekend
  • South Beach Parties: Every major club and hotel runs F1-themed events — LIV, E11EVEN, Fontainebleau, Faena
  • Car Shows: Pop-up exotic car displays throughout Miami, often with F1-connected brands

The Miami Grand Prix isn't just a race — it's a city-wide event. And it's only getting bigger. Secure your tickets early, pick the right seats for your budget, and get ready for one of the best weekends Miami has to offer.

Find Miami Grand Prix 2026 Tickets on eBay →

title: Miami F1 Weekend 2026: The Ultimate Guide to Race Day, Parties, After-Events & Where to Be
excerpt: The Miami Grand Prix turns the entire city into a playground. Here's your insider guide to the race, the parties, the car shows, and everything happening F1 weekend.
content:
The Miami Grand Prix has transformed from a Formula 1 race into a full-blown cultural event. For one weekend, Miami becomes the center of the motorsport universe — and the action extends far beyond the Hard Rock Stadium circuit. From exclusive paddock parties to Wynwood pop-ups to South Beach nightlife takeovers, F1 weekend is Miami's Super Bowl.

Here's everything happening, where to be, and how to make the most of it.

The Race: What You Need to Know

Weekend Schedule

DaySessionsWhen to Arrive
FridayPractice 1, Practice 2Gates open ~2 PM, quietest day, best for exploring
SaturdayPractice 3, Sprint Race or QualifyingArrive by noon, energy picks up significantly
SundayRace Day (Main Event)Arrive early — gates open 4+ hours before race, lines are serious

Still Need Tickets?

The secondary market is your best bet at this point. eBay consistently has the best prices for F1 tickets — especially in the final week before the race when sellers need to move inventory.

Browse Miami Grand Prix Tickets on eBay →

Thursday: The Warm-Up

F1 Fan Zone — Bayfront Park

The official F1 Fan Zone typically opens Thursday in downtown Miami. Free entry. Live screenings of previous races, driver appearances, team merchandise, simulators, and food vendors. It's the family-friendly, wallet-friendly way to start the weekend.

Car Culture Takeover — Wynwood

Wynwood transforms during F1 week. Galleries host automotive art shows, pop-up showrooms appear (Porsche, McLaren, and luxury watch brands love this), and the restaurants fill with international racing fans. Walk the Wynwood Walls Thursday evening before the weekend crowds hit.

Welcome Parties

Thursday night kicks off the F1 party circuit. Past years have featured events at:

  • Faena Hotel Miami Beach — ultra-exclusive, invite-heavy
  • The Setai — F1 welcome reception
  • Brickell City Centre — brand activations and cocktail events

Friday: Practice Day (Best Value Day)

At the Track

Friday is the hidden gem of F1 weekend. The cars are on track for two full practice sessions, the campus is fully operational (food, merch, activations), and the crowds are a fraction of Saturday/Sunday. If you only have one day to attend, Friday gives you the most relaxed, exploratory experience.

Use Friday to:

  • Find your ideal viewing spot (especially for GA ticket holders)
  • Explore the entire campus without massive crowds
  • Hit the merchandise stores before popular sizes sell out
  • Take photos without fighting for position

Friday Night: Brickell & South Beach

After practice, the F1 crowd migrates south. Brickell's rooftop bars (Sugar, Mama Tried) fill with racing fans, while South Beach's Ocean Drive comes alive with exotic car cruising. Teams and sponsors host private dinners at Carbone, Papi Steak, and Major Food Group properties throughout Miami Beach.

Saturday: Sprint Day & Peak Energy

At the Track

Saturday features Practice 3 plus either Sprint Race or Qualifying (depending on the format). This is when the energy spikes — the racing gets serious, the grandstands fill up, and the campus activations peak. If Sunday is sold out or over budget, Saturday is the best alternative.

Saturday Night: The Main Event (Off Track)

Saturday night is THE night for F1 parties in Miami. The biggest events from past years:

LIV at Fontainebleau

The crown jewel of Miami nightlife goes full F1. Past headliners have included major DJs with driver appearances. Expect $100+ cover, bottle service tables starting at $3,000+, and a dress code. The place to see and be seen.

E11EVEN

Miami's 24-hour ultraclub runs a special F1 weekend program. This is the after-after-party — things don't peak until 3 AM. Wild energy, celebrity sightings, and no closing time.

F1 Official After-Party

The official F1 party typically happens Saturday night at the Hard Rock complex or a nearby venue. Past years have featured surprise musical performances and driver meet-and-greets. Access usually requires a wristband included with premium ticket packages.

Team & Sponsor Parties

Red Bull, Ferrari, McLaren, and Mercedes all host invite-only events throughout Miami. Getting on the list usually requires connections through sponsors, team partners, or hospitality packages. If you have access to any F1 hospitality, ask about Saturday night events.

Sunday: Race Day

Pre-Race

Arrive as early as possible. Security lines on Sunday are the longest of the weekend. The pre-race atmosphere is electric — driver parade, national anthem, grid walk (for hospitality ticket holders), and military flyover. This is Formula 1 at its most spectacular.

The Race

57 laps around the Miami International Autodrome. Lights out usually around 4 PM ET. The race runs about 90 minutes. The sunset timing means the light is incredible — golden hour racing through the final laps.

Post-Race Concert

Included with your race ticket. Past headliners have been massive (Bad Bunny, Post Malone caliber). The concert happens on the stadium grounds immediately after the race. It's the perfect transition from racing adrenaline to celebration mode.

Sunday Night: Victory Celebrations

After the race and concert, the party continues across Miami:

  • Wynwood — bars and restaurants packed with fans reliving the race
  • South Beach — every club runs an F1 celebration night
  • Brickell — more low-key but the rooftop bars have the best atmosphere

Car Shows & Automotive Events

F1 weekend brings out the best of Miami's car culture:

  • Exotic car rallies — organized by local car clubs, featuring hundreds of supercars cruising through Brickell and Miami Beach
  • Dealership open houses — The Collection, Prestige Imports, and Warren Henry all host special events
  • Pop-up showrooms — luxury brands set up temporary displays in Design District and Wynwood
  • Cars & Coffee special editions — local meets expand for F1 weekend with special guests

Where to Stay

F1 weekend hotel prices are 2-3x normal. Book early or know where to look:

AreaVibeF1 Weekend Price Range
Miami BeachParty central, beach access$400-$1,500/night
BrickellUpscale, walkable nightlife$300-$800/night
Wynwood/Design DistrictArtsy, emerging, close to track$250-$600/night
Doral/Miami LakesBudget, closest to Hard Rock$150-$400/night
Fort LauderdaleBudget alternative, 30 min away$150-$350/night

F1 Weekend Essentials: What to Bring

  • Sunscreen SPF 50+ — May in Miami is brutal
  • Portable phone charger — you'll be filming and using the F1 app all day
  • Ear protection — F1 cars are loud up close (110+ dB). Earplugs or over-ear protection recommended, especially for kids
  • Comfortable shoes — the complex is huge, expect 3-5 miles of walking
  • Clear bag — most venues enforce clear bag policy
  • Cash + cards — some vendors are cash-only, most are card-only. Bring both.

Browse F1 Merchandise & Fan Gear on eBay →

Getting Around

  • To the track: Uber/Lyft with drop-off zones. Expect $30-$60 from South Beach, $20-$40 from Brickell. Surge pricing after the race is severe — budget $80-$150 or plan to wait 30-60 minutes.
  • Between neighborhoods: Miami's public transit is limited. Metromover is free in downtown/Brickell. Otherwise, rideshare is king.
  • Rent an exotic: F1 weekend is when you pull the trigger on that Lamborghini rental. Turo and local rental companies book out weeks early.

The Bottom Line

The Miami Grand Prix isn't just a race — it's a citywide, multi-day festival that combines world-class motorsport with Miami's unmatched nightlife, car culture, and energy. Whether you're there for the racing, the parties, or the scene, there's nothing else like it in the F1 calendar.

Get your tickets, plan your weekend, and get ready for the best four days Miami has to offer.

title: Cheapest Miami Grand Prix Tickets 2026: How to Score Deals & Avoid Overpaying
excerpt: Miami GP tickets don't have to break the bank. Here's how smart buyers are getting into the race for less — plus the hidden costs nobody warns you about.
content:
Let's be honest — the Miami Grand Prix is expensive. Face-value tickets start at $400+ and grandstand seats can hit $3,000+. Add parking, food, drinks, and merch, and you're looking at a $1,000+ day before you even factor in hotel costs.

But it doesn't have to be that bad. Here are the strategies smart buyers use to get into the Miami GP without emptying their savings account.

Current Ticket Prices: What You're Working With

Ticket TypeFace ValueResale LowResale High
General Admission (3-day)$400-$600$250$800
General Admission (Sunday only)$250-$350$150$500
Campus Grandstand (3-day)$700-$1,500$500$2,000
Turn 1 Grandstand (3-day)$1,000-$2,500$800$3,500
Beach Grandstand (3-day)$1,200-$3,000$1,000$4,000

Strategy 1: Buy on eBay (Best Resale Value)

eBay consistently offers the best prices on F1 tickets because:

  • Auction format: You set the price. No-reserve auctions regularly close below market value.
  • Lower fees than StubHub/SeatGeek: Seller fees are lower on eBay, which means sellers price lower.
  • Buyer protection: eBay's Money Back Guarantee covers event tickets. If the tickets are fake or don't arrive, you get a full refund.
  • Last-minute deals: Sellers who can't attend list close to race day at steep discounts.

Browse Miami GP Tickets on eBay (Price: Low to High) →

Strategy 2: Friday-Only Tickets

This is the biggest money saver that most people overlook. Friday practice day tickets cost a fraction of Sunday race day tickets — often $100-$200 vs. $300-$600+ for GA. And here's the thing: you still get:

  • ✅ F1 cars on track at full speed
  • ✅ Full access to the campus, activations, and food
  • ✅ Merchandise shops (with better availability than Sunday)
  • ✅ The F1 atmosphere and energy
  • ✅ Smaller crowds = better experience in many ways

What you miss: the actual race result and the post-race concert. If you're going for the experience rather than seeing who wins live, Friday is the smart play.

Browse Friday Practice Day Tickets →

Strategy 3: Wait Until Race Week

Ticket prices follow a predictable pattern:

  1. On-sale day: Cheapest (face value), sells out fast
  2. 3-6 months before: Steady rise on resale market
  3. 1 month before: Peak prices (FOMO + corporate buying)
  4. Race week: Prices start dropping as sellers get nervous
  5. Day before / day of: Steepest discounts for sellers who can't attend

If you can handle the uncertainty, buying in the final 48 hours can save 20-40% vs. peak pricing. The risk: the specific section you want might sell out. But for GA tickets, there's almost always last-minute inventory.

Strategy 4: Group Buys

The official Miami GP website sometimes offers group pricing for 8+ tickets. Coordinate with friends, family, or a local car club to qualify. Group buys typically save 10-15% per ticket — and everyone gets to sit together.

Local Miami car clubs often organize group ticket purchases. Check with:

  • South Florida Car Club meetup groups
  • Reddit r/Miami and r/Formula1 local threads
  • Facebook groups: "Miami Car Enthusiasts," "F1 Miami Fans"

Strategy 5: Corporate / Unused Tickets

Companies buy blocks of F1 hospitality tickets for clients and employees. Many go unused. Check:

  • Your employer's corporate events team — you might have access you don't know about
  • LinkedIn — people occasionally post unused corporate tickets
  • Local business networks — Miami's business community is deeply connected to F1

Hidden Costs Nobody Tells You About

The ticket is just the beginning. Budget for these:

ExpenseEstimated Cost
Parking (on-site)$80-$150/day
Uber/Lyft (round trip)$60-$150 (surge pricing post-race)
Food & drinks (at venue)$50-$100/day
Merchandise (team hat, shirt)$40-$150
Sunscreen, water, basics$15-$25

True cost of a budget Miami GP day (GA + expenses): $400-$700 per person.

How to Cut These Costs

  • Skip on-site parking: Park at a nearby lot or mall and rideshare the last mile
  • Eat before you go: Have a big breakfast/lunch outside the venue. Bring sealed snacks where allowed.
  • Buy merch on eBay instead: Official F1 merchandise is 30-50% cheaper on eBay than at the track
  • Bring a sealed water bottle: Most F1 venues allow one sealed bottle per person. Refill at water stations inside.
  • Pre-arrange your ride home: Schedule a pickup 30-60 minutes after the race ends to avoid peak surge

Browse F1 Merchandise on eBay (Save vs. Track Prices) →

Free F1 Weekend Experiences

You don't need a race ticket to enjoy F1 weekend in Miami:

  • F1 Fan Zone (Bayfront Park): Free entry, live screenings, activities
  • Wynwood car culture pop-ups: Free to walk and explore
  • Exotic car spotting: F1 weekend brings the most incredible cars onto Miami streets. Post up on Ocean Drive or Brickell and watch the parade.
  • Watch parties: Every sports bar in Miami will screen the race. Many have special F1 events with giveaways.

When to Buy: The Timing Cheat Sheet

WhenWhat to DoExpected Savings
6+ months outBuy face value from official siteBest price (if available)
3-6 months outWatch resale prices, don't buy yetN/A (prices rising)
1-2 months outSet eBay alerts for your sectionMarket price
2 weeks outStart bidding on eBay auctions5-15% below peak
Race weekAggressive bidding, check daily15-30% below peak
Day beforeLast-minute grab (risky but cheapest)25-40% below peak

The Miami Grand Prix is worth every penny — but there's no reason to overpay. Buy smart, budget for the extras, and enjoy one of the best events in motorsport.

title: McLaren 750S for Sale in Miami: 2026 Pricing, Specs & Buyer's Guide
excerpt: The McLaren 750S is the sharpest, lightest supercar in its class. Here's what they cost in Miami, where to find one, and everything buyers need to know in 2026.
content:
McLaren 750S for Sale in Miami: 2026 Pricing, Specs & Buyer’s Guide

The McLaren 750S replaced the 720S in 2023 and immediately became one of the most capable supercars ever built. With 740 hp from a twin-turbo V8, a curb weight under 3,000 lbs, and McLaren’s obsessive approach to aerodynamics, the 750S does things on road and track that cars costing twice as much struggle to match. If you’re looking for a McLaren 750S for sale in Miami, the market in 2026 offers some compelling opportunities.

This guide covers both the coupe and spider variants, realistic 2026 market pricing, where to shop in South Florida, and the true costs of ownership in Miami.

McLaren 750S Specs — What Makes It Special

The 750S isn’t just a facelift of the 720S — McLaren redesigned 30% of the car’s components. The result is lighter, faster, and sharper than its predecessor in every measurable way:

SpecMcLaren 750S CoupeMcLaren 750S Spider
Engine4.0L twin-turbo V84.0L twin-turbo V8
Power740 hp / 590 lb-ft740 hp / 590 lb-ft
0-60 mph2.7 seconds2.8 seconds
0-124 mph7.2 seconds7.3 seconds
Top Speed206 mph201 mph
Curb Weight2,952 lbs3,064 lbs
Transmission7-speed SSG dual-clutch7-speed SSG dual-clutch
Drive TypeRear-wheel driveRear-wheel drive
Original MSRP$299,000$325,000

That power-to-weight ratio — roughly 5.5 lbs per horsepower — puts the 750S in hypercar territory while carrying a supercar price tag. For context, a Ferrari 296 GTB makes 819 hp but weighs 500 lbs more.

McLaren 750S for Sale — 2026 Market Pricing

The McLaren 750S price on the secondary market has settled into a predictable range now that the initial launch hype has cooled. Here’s what you’ll actually pay in Miami in 2026:

ModelYearMileage Range2026 Market Price
750S Coupe20243,000–8,000 mi$265K–$310K
750S Coupe2025500–3,000 mi$285K–$330K
750S Coupe2026Under 500 mi$300K–$345K
750S Spider20243,000–8,000 mi$290K–$340K
750S Spider2025500–3,000 mi$310K–$360K
750S Spider2026Under 500 mi$330K–$375K

The sweet spot for value is a 2024 coupe with 3,000–5,000 miles — you’re looking at roughly $270K–$290K for a car that stickered near $320K+ when optioned. That’s genuine depreciation working in your favor, which is unusual for McLaren’s top-tier models.

McLaren 750S Coupe vs. Spider — Which to Buy in Miami

This is Miami, so the Spider gets the obvious lifestyle nod. But the decision isn’t as straightforward as it seems:

  • Spider premium: Expect to pay $25K–$40K more for the Spider over an equivalent coupe. That gap has been consistent since launch.
  • Weight penalty: The Spider adds only 112 lbs — McLaren’s carbon fiber MonoCell II chassis means minimal structural reinforcement is needed. You barely notice the difference on the street.
  • Resale: Spiders traditionally hold value better in the Miami market. Buyers here overwhelmingly prefer open-top exotics.
  • Track use: If you plan to run Homestead-Miami Speedway or Sebring regularly, the coupe’s slightly lower center of gravity and stiffer structure give it the edge.

For most Miami buyers, the Spider is the right call. The ability to drop the top in 11 seconds while cruising Ocean Drive or crossing the Julia Tuttle Causeway is worth every penny of the premium.

Where to Find a McLaren 750S for Sale in Miami

Authorized McLaren Dealers

  • McLaren Miami (Coral Gables) — South Florida’s authorized McLaren retailer carries new and McLaren Qualified pre-owned 750S inventory. Buying certified gets you a factory-backed warranty extension and multi-point inspection.
  • McLaren Orlando / McLaren Palm Beach — Worth checking for broader inventory. Both dealers will ship to Miami or arrange transport.

Independent Exotic Dealers

  • RMC Miami (Wynwood) — Regularly stocks well-spec’d 750S models. Their inventory skews toward cars with unique spec and MSO options.
  • Prestige Imports (North Miami Beach) — High-volume dealer that often has competitive pricing on McLarens due to trade-in volume.
  • iLusso (Aventura) — Consignment model means you occasionally find below-market deals from motivated sellers.
  • Curated (Miami) — Specializes in modern supercars with an emphasis on documentation and provenance.

Online & Auction Platforms

  • Bring a Trailer — Several 750S models sell monthly. Full auction transparency with detailed photo sets and comment-section due diligence from the community.
  • Cars & Bids — Growing presence for modern McLarens. No-reserve auctions can yield deals.
  • duPont Registry — Usually 30+ McLaren 750S listings nationally.
  • McLaren Qualified (official) — McLaren’s own certified pre-owned program lists inventory from all US dealers.

Key Options That Affect McLaren 750S Price

McLaren’s MSO (McLaren Special Operations) personalization program means no two 750S cars are exactly alike. These options have the biggest impact on resale value:

  • MSO Defined paint colors — Unique MSO colors (Volcano Red, Paris Blue, Cerithium Violet) add $8K–$15K to resale over standard colors.
  • Carbon fiber exterior pack — Front splitter, side intakes, rear bumper, and diffuser in visible carbon fiber. Adds $12K–$18K new, holds most of that value.
  • Electrochromic roof (coupe) — Switches from tinted to transparent. A $5K option that buyers love.
  • Bowers & Wilkins audio — The $4K upgrade is worth it. McLaren’s standard system is mediocre.
  • Vehicle lift system — Raises the front axle 1.5 inches for speed bumps and driveways. Essential for Miami driving and adds $3K–$5K to resale.
  • MSO Bespoke — Fully custom MSO cars with unique interior and exterior treatments can command $30K–$50K+ premiums.

McLaren 750S vs. Competitors — Miami Buyer’s Comparison

CarPowerWeight0-602026 Used Price
McLaren 750S740 hp2,952 lbs2.7s$265K–$375K
Ferrari 296 GTB819 hp3,461 lbs2.9s$280K–$350K
Lamborghini Huracán Tecnica631 hp3,313 lbs3.0s$240K–$300K
Porsche 911 GT3 RS518 hp3,268 lbs3.0s$280K–$350K

The 750S wins on power-to-weight by a significant margin. It’s also the only car in this group with a hydraulic steering rack (reintroduced from the 720S), which gives it a level of steering feel its competitors can’t match. The Ferrari 296 GTB counters with hybrid torque and Italian cachet, the Huracán offers V10 emotion, and the GT3 RS brings Porsche’s legendary track pedigree. But for pure performance per dollar, the McLaren is hard to beat.

Cost of Owning a McLaren 750S in Miami

ExpenseAnnual Estimated Cost
Insurance$4,000–$9,000
Scheduled maintenance$1,500–$3,500
Tires (Pirelli P Zero Trofeo R)$2,400–$3,800 per set
Brakes (carbon ceramic replacement)$10,000–$16,000 (every 25K–40K miles)
Storage (climate-controlled, optional)$3,000–$10,000
Florida sales tax (at purchase)~6% of sale price

McLaren’s maintenance costs are competitive with Ferrari and Lamborghini, and in some areas genuinely lower. The 750S uses a dry-sump oil system that extends service intervals, and the carbon ceramic brakes last significantly longer than steel equivalents. The biggest ongoing cost is tires — the optional Trofeo R track tires wear fast on Miami’s hot pavement if you drive aggressively.

Common Issues to Watch For on Used McLaren 750S

The 750S is a relatively new model, so long-term reliability data is still emerging. But based on early ownership reports and inherited 720S platform knowledge:

  • Infotainment quirks — McLaren’s MIS II system has improved over the 720S but still occasionally freezes or lags. Software updates from the dealer usually resolve issues.
  • Panel alignment — McLaren’s hand-assembled body panels can have minor gaps. Check for consistent panel alignment, especially around the dihedral doors.
  • Hydraulic suspension — The proactive chassis control uses hydraulic cross-linked dampers. They’re brilliant when working but expensive to service. Listen for any unusual noises over bumps.
  • Clear bra / PPF — The 750S’s low nose and aggressive aero catch every stone. If the car doesn’t have PPF, budget $3K–$6K to have it applied immediately.

Pre-Purchase Inspection Checklist

  • Full McLaren service history — Verify all services were performed at authorized dealers or approved specialists.
  • Paint meter readings — Check all panels for respray evidence. Repainted McLarens lose 10–15% value.
  • Door mechanism test — Open and close both dihedral doors multiple times. The hydraulic struts should operate smoothly without hesitation.
  • Suspension check — Drive over speed bumps at various speeds. Any clunking or uneven behavior suggests hydraulic issues.
  • Brake rotor inspection — Carbon ceramic rotors should be free of deep cracks or delamination. Surface crazing is normal.
  • Tire date codes — Low-mile cars often sit on original tires that have flat-spotted or aged out. Check DOT dates.
  • PPI at McLaren Miami — Budget $500–$800 for a thorough pre-purchase inspection at the authorized dealer.

Bottom Line: Is the McLaren 750S Worth It in 2026?

The McLaren 750S for sale market in Miami offers one of the best performance-per-dollar propositions in the supercar world right now. A 2024 coupe in the mid-$270Ks gives you a car that embarrasses vehicles costing $500K+ on a racetrack, looks stunning on South Beach, and carries lower running costs than most Italian alternatives.

The Spider is the Miami pick for most buyers — top-down cruising with 740 hp and that characteristic McLaren turbo whistle is an experience that never gets old. And with McLaren’s strong presence in South Florida through McLaren Miami, dealer support and parts availability are solid.

Whether you’re coming from a 720S, cross-shopping a Ferrari 296, or stepping up from a Porsche 911 Turbo S, the 750S delivers. It’s the thinking person’s supercar — lighter, faster, and more engaging than nearly anything else at its price point.

title: Mercedes G-Wagon for Sale in Miami: 2026 Pricing, Models & Buyer's Guide
excerpt: The Mercedes G-Class is Miami's unofficial status symbol. Here's what every model costs in 2026, where to find one, and the insider knowledge you need before buying.
content:
Mercedes G-Wagon for Sale in Miami: 2026 Pricing, Models & Buyer’s Guide

No vehicle defines Miami’s streets quite like the Mercedes G-Wagon. Walk through Brickell, cruise down Collins Avenue, or park in Bal Harbour, and you’ll see G-Classes in every color, every trim level, and every stage of customization. If you’re searching for a Mercedes G-Wagon for sale in Miami, you’ve got options — but the market is nuanced, and overpaying is easy if you don’t know what you’re looking at.

This guide covers every current G-Class variant, realistic 2026 market pricing, the best places to shop in South Florida, and what it actually costs to own one in Miami.

Mercedes G-Wagon Model Lineup — 2026 Specs & Pricing

Mercedes currently produces three G-Class variants, plus the all-electric G 580. Here’s how they stack up:

ModelEnginePower0-60 mph2026 MSRP2026 Market Price (Used)
G 5504.0L twin-turbo V8416 hp / 450 lb-ft5.6s$145,000$110K–$155K (2020–2024)
AMG G 634.0L handcrafted twin-turbo V8577 hp / 627 lb-ft4.0s$185,000$140K–$210K (2020–2024)
AMG G 63 4x4²4.0L handcrafted twin-turbo V8577 hp / 627 lb-ft4.3s$250,000+$280K–$380K
G 580 EQQuad electric motors579 hp / 859 lb-ft4.7s$175,000$160K–$190K

The AMG G 63 accounts for the overwhelming majority of G-Wagons you’ll see in Miami. It’s the default choice for buyers who want the full G-Wagon experience — the hand-built AMG V8, the aggressive Panamericana grille, the side-exit exhaust burble, and the presence that stops traffic on every block.

Mercedes G-Wagon for Sale — What You’ll Actually Pay in Miami

Miami is one of the most expensive markets in the country for G-Wagons. High demand, year-round visibility, and a deep pool of luxury buyers mean South Florida pricing runs $5K–$15K above national averages. Here’s the breakdown by model year:

G 550 Pricing (Used)

YearMileage RangeMiami Market Price
2019–202030K–50K mi$100K–$125K
2021–202215K–30K mi$120K–$140K
2023–20245K–15K mi$135K–$155K

AMG G 63 Pricing (Used)

YearMileage RangeMiami Market Price
2019–202030K–50K mi$130K–$165K
2021–202215K–30K mi$155K–$195K
2023–20245K–15K mi$175K–$215K
2025–2026Under 5K mi$190K–$230K+

The best value play? A 2021–2022 AMG G 63 with 20K–30K miles in the $155K–$175K range. You get the refreshed infotainment (MBUX), all the same AMG V8 power, and enough depreciation to save $30K–$50K versus buying new. These years are also past the initial quality hiccups that affected some early W463A models.

G 550 vs. AMG G 63 — Which G-Wagon to Buy

This is the single biggest decision for Miami G-Wagon buyers. Here’s the honest comparison:

  • Performance: The G 63’s 577 hp vs. the G 550’s 416 hp is noticeable but not dramatic in daily driving. Both are fast enough for Miami traffic. The G 63 pulls harder on the highway and sounds significantly better.
  • Sound: The G 63’s handcrafted AMG V8 with side-exit exhausts is iconic. The G 550 sounds like a luxury SUV. If the exhaust note matters to you — and for most G-Wagon buyers, it does — the G 63 is the only choice.
  • Appearance: The G 63 gets the Panamericana vertical-slat grille, wider fender flares, and more aggressive bumpers. Most people can spot the difference. In Miami, the G 63 look is what people expect.
  • Price gap: $30K–$50K more for the G 63 at any given model year. That’s significant, but the G 63 also holds value better as a percentage of MSRP.
  • Insurance: The G 63 costs $1,500–$3,000 more per year to insure. Factor this into your total cost.

The verdict: If you’re buying a G-Wagon for the G-Wagon experience — the sound, the look, the presence — get the G 63. If you want a comfortable, capable luxury SUV and the badge is enough, the G 550 saves you serious money and is still a fantastic truck.

The AMG G 63 4x4² — Miami’s Ultimate Statement

The G 63 4x4² (pronounced “four by four squared”) is Mercedes’ most extreme G-Wagon: portal axles that raise the ride height by 3.5 inches, 22-inch wheels with all-terrain tires, carbon fiber fender flares, and a presence that makes a standard G 63 look understated.

Originally priced around $250K, used 4x4² models now trade for $280K–$380K depending on year and spec. They’re rare — Mercedes builds limited numbers each year — and Miami’s taste for over-the-top trucks keeps prices elevated. If you want the most attention-grabbing stock vehicle on the road, this is it.

The G 580 EQ — Miami’s Electric G-Wagon

Mercedes launched the all-electric G 580 in 2024, and it’s a genuinely impressive machine: four electric motors producing 579 hp and 859 lb-ft of instant torque, a 116 kWh battery offering roughly 240 miles of range, and a party trick called the G-Turn — a full 360-degree tank turn in place.

For Miami buyers, the G 580 makes sense if:

  • You rarely drive more than 200 miles in a day (covers 95% of Miami driving)
  • You have home charging capability (essential — public charging in Miami is spotty)
  • You want the newest tech and the conversation starter factor
  • You appreciate the instant torque in stop-and-go Brickell traffic

What you give up: the AMG V8 sound (obviously), the side-exit exhaust visual, and about 1,000 lbs of added weight from the battery. It drives differently than a G 63 — smoother, quieter, but less characterful. Most Miami G-Wagon buyers still prefer the V8.

Where to Find a Mercedes G-Wagon for Sale in Miami

Authorized Mercedes-Benz Dealers

  • Mercedes-Benz of Miami (Coral Gables) — One of the highest-volume Mercedes dealers in the country. Strong CPO inventory and new G-Class allocation.
  • Mercedes-Benz of Coral Gables — Adjacent to the Coral Gables auto mile. Frequently stocks CPO G 63 models.
  • Mercedes-Benz of Cutler Bay — South Dade’s authorized dealer, sometimes with less markup than the Gables locations.
  • Mercedes-Benz of Fort Lauderdale — Broward County’s main dealer, worth checking for broader inventory.

Independent Luxury Dealers

  • Prestige Imports (North Miami Beach) — Carries a wide selection of pre-owned G-Wagons, often with Brabus and aftermarket modifications.
  • South Motors (Dadeland area) — Multi-brand dealer with competitive G-Class pricing.
  • AutoNation dealers — Several AutoNation Mercedes locations in South Florida carry CPO and used G-Class inventory.

Online & Auction Platforms

  • Bring a Trailer — G-Wagons sell here regularly. Excellent for finding well-documented, enthusiast-owned examples.
  • Cars & Bids — Growing G-Class listings, especially for modified and specialty builds.
  • Mercedes-Benz CPO (official site) — Search certified pre-owned G-Class inventory from all authorized US dealers with factory-backed warranty.
  • Autotrader / Cars.com — Largest aggregate listings. Filter by Miami zip code and radius for local inventory.

G-Wagon Customization in Miami — What Adds (and Destroys) Value

Miami has a massive G-Wagon aftermarket scene. Understanding what modifications help and hurt resale is critical:

Modifications That Add Value

  • Brabus body kit and tune — Brabus-modified G-Wagons command $20K–$100K+ premiums depending on the package level (600, 700, 800, 900). Only official Brabus conversions hold value.
  • Matte/satin PPF wraps — A $5K–$8K satin PPF wrap protects the paint and gives a unique look that’s easily reversible. Buyers like this.
  • Upgraded wheels (Forgiato, HRE, Vossen) — Name-brand forged wheels in conservative designs add $3K–$8K to resale if properly fitted.
  • Interior custom leather — Professional re-upholstery in high-end materials adds value when done by reputable shops.

Modifications That Hurt Value

  • Cheap body kits — Non-Brabus aftermarket body kits (fake vents, riveted fenders) actively reduce value. Buyers see them as a red flag.
  • Excessive chrome deletion — Some blacking-out is fine, but completely murdered-out G-Wagons are harder to sell than stock examples.
  • Catback exhaust delete / straight pipes — Loud enough to fail inspection in some states and annoying for the next owner. Keep the stock exhaust.
  • Lifted suspension with oversized wheels — Unless it’s a 4x4² conversion done by a proper shop, lifted G-Wagons with 26-inch wheels are a niche market.

Cost of Owning a G-Wagon in Miami

ExpenseG 550 Annual CostAMG G 63 Annual Cost
Insurance$3,500–$6,500$4,500–$9,000
Service A (minor)$400–$700$600–$1,000
Service B (major)$800–$1,500$1,200–$2,200
Tires$1,200–$2,000/set$1,600–$2,800/set
Brakes$1,500–$3,000 (every 30K–40K mi)$2,000–$4,500 (every 25K–35K mi)
Fuel (premium, ~12 mpg city)$4,000–$6,000$4,500–$7,000
Florida sales tax (at purchase)~6%~6%

The G-Wagon’s biggest ongoing cost is fuel. At roughly 12 mpg in Miami city driving (and the G 63 is worse), you’re spending $400–$600+ per month on premium gas if you daily drive it. Factor this in — it’s the price of running a 5,800-lb V8 SUV in stop-and-go traffic.

Common Issues on Used G-Wagons (W463A / 2019+)

The current-generation G-Class is well-built, but there are recurring issues to watch for:

  • Air suspension failure — The AIRMATIC suspension can develop leaks, particularly in the rear bags. Listen for the compressor running constantly and check for uneven ride height. Repair cost: $1,500–$3,500 per corner.
  • MBUX infotainment glitches — Early 2019–2020 models had software bugs. Most have been resolved with dealer updates, but verify the system is running current firmware.
  • Sunroof drainage clogs — A known Mercedes issue across many models. Clogged drains cause water intrusion into the cabin. Easy preventive fix but expensive if left unchecked.
  • Transfer case / differential noises — Some owners report clunking at low speeds during tight turns. Often normal for the three differential lock system, but worth having inspected.
  • Door handle mechanism — The electronic door handles can stick or fail. Warranty-covered but annoying if out of warranty ($600–$1,200 per handle).

Pre-Purchase Inspection Checklist for G-Wagon

  • Full Mercedes service history — Verify Service A/B intervals were maintained at authorized dealers.
  • Air suspension test — Park the car overnight and check if it drops on any corner. Have the dealer run a diagnostic on the AIRMATIC system.
  • Underbody inspection — Miami’s salt air and occasional flooding make underbody rust checks important, even on newer models.
  • Paint meter — Check all panels for evidence of repaint. G-Wagons in Miami see a lot of parking lot damage.
  • Modification documentation — If the car has aftermarket work, verify who did it and whether it affects the factory warranty.
  • Brake wear indicators — G-Wagons are heavy and eat brakes. Check remaining pad and rotor life to avoid a $3K+ surprise shortly after purchase.
  • CPO vs. private sale — Mercedes CPO adds 1 year/unlimited miles of warranty beyond the original. For a G-Wagon, that peace of mind is worth the $2K–$5K CPO premium.

Mercedes G-Wagon vs. Competitors in Miami

VehiclePower2026 Used PriceBest For
AMG G 63577 hp$140K–$215KStatus, sound, iconic design
Range Rover SV523–606 hp$130K–$200KLuxury, comfort, refinement
Lamborghini Urus641–657 hp$180K–$250KPerformance, exotic badge
Bentley Bentayga542–740 hp$140K–$220KUltimate luxury, W12 power
Porsche Cayenne Turbo GT631 hp$150K–$200KHandling, daily performance

The G-Wagon doesn’t win on any single metric except presence. It’s not the fastest, not the most comfortable, not the most refined, and not the most fuel-efficient. What it has is identity — there’s nothing else on the road that looks like it, sounds like it, or carries the same cultural weight. In Miami, that matters more than spec sheets.

Bottom Line: Is the Mercedes G-Wagon Worth It in 2026?

The Mercedes G-Wagon for sale market in Miami is as strong as ever. These trucks hold value remarkably well — a 3-year-old G 63 retains 75–85% of its MSRP, which is better than almost any luxury SUV on the market. That means buying used doesn’t save as much as you’d expect, but it also means your investment is protected.

For Miami specifically, the G-Wagon makes more sense than almost anywhere else in the country. The year-round visibility, the valet-everywhere culture, the social currency it carries in South Beach and Brickell — these intangibles are real and part of what you’re buying.

The sweet spot remains a 2021–2022 AMG G 63 in the $155K–$175K range. You get the full G-Wagon experience, save $30K+ versus new, and own a truck that will still be turning heads — and holding value — five years from now. In a city where your car is your business card, the G-Wagon delivers.

title: Ferrari 488 for Sale in Miami: 2026 Pricing, Models & Buyer's Guide
excerpt: The Ferrari 488 is one of the best mid-engine supercars ever made — and Miami has plenty of them for sale. Here's what the 488 GTB, Spider, and Pista cost in 2026, where to find them, and what to watch out for.
content:
The Ferrari 488 is the sweet spot of modern Ferrari ownership. Produced from 2015 to 2019, the 488 brought Ferrari into the twin-turbo era with a 3.9-liter V8 that redefined what a mid-engine supercar could do. Now that the 488 has been replaced by the F8 Tributo, the used market is flooded with well-maintained examples — and if you're searching for a Ferrari 488 for sale in Miami, the timing couldn't be better.

Why the Ferrari 488 Is a Smart Buy in 2026

The 488 occupies a rare position in the Ferrari lineup: it's new enough to feel modern (Apple CarPlay, advanced traction control, turbocharged power) but old enough that prices have settled from their peak. The 488 GTB and Spider have depreciated roughly 25–35% from original MSRP, putting them within reach of serious enthusiasts who want a genuine Ferrari experience without paying new-car premiums. In Miami, where the exotic car market is deeper than almost anywhere in the U.S., you'll find dozens of Ferrari 488 models for sale at any given time.

Ferrari 488 Models, Specs & Performance

Ferrari offered the 488 in three main variants, each with the same fundamental powertrain but increasingly aggressive tuning. Here's how they compare:

Spec488 GTB488 Spider488 Pista
Engine3.9L Twin-Turbo V83.9L Twin-Turbo V83.9L Twin-Turbo V8
Horsepower661 hp661 hp711 hp
Torque561 lb-ft561 lb-ft568 lb-ft
0-60 mph3.0 seconds3.0 seconds2.85 seconds
Top Speed205 mph203 mph211 mph
Weight3,252 lbs3,350 lbs3,053 lbs
Transmission7-Speed DCT7-Speed DCT7-Speed DCT
Production Years2016–20192016–20192019–2020

The Pista (Italian for "track") is the one collectors covet. It gets 50 more horsepower from a reworked intake and exhaust, sheds nearly 200 pounds through carbon fiber body panels, and adds aerodynamic elements derived from Ferrari's 488 GTE race car. The Pista Spider — a convertible track weapon — is the rarest and most valuable of the bunch.

Ferrari 488 Pricing in Miami (2026)

Here's what you should budget for a Ferrari 488 for sale in the Miami market:

Model / VariantPrice Range (2026)Notes
488 GTB (2016–2017)$195,000 – $225,000Most affordable entry point; early models with higher miles
488 GTB (2018–2019)$225,000 – $265,000Later production with more features; lower miles
488 Spider (2016–2017)$215,000 – $250,000Convertible premium; Miami buyers strongly prefer these
488 Spider (2018–2019)$250,000 – $290,000Sweet spot for Miami — open-top V8 turbo
488 Pista$380,000 – $450,000Track-focused; appreciating in value
488 Pista Spider$500,000 – $650,000+Ultra-rare; only ~800 built worldwide

Miami's climate makes the Spider variants especially popular here. Expect to pay a 10–15% premium for open-top models compared to national averages. The Pista Spider has been appreciating steadily and may become a future collectible — production was extremely limited.

Where to Find a Ferrari 488 for Sale in Miami

South Florida has one of the densest concentrations of Ferrari inventory in the country. Here's where to start your search:

  • The Collection (Coral Gables) — Miami's authorized Ferrari dealer and the first place to look for certified pre-owned 488s. Their CPO cars come with extended warranty coverage and a thorough multi-point inspection.
  • Ferrari of Fort Lauderdale — Another authorized dealer with strong 488 inventory, especially Spiders.
  • Prestige Imports (North Miami Beach) — Multi-brand exotic dealer with competitive pricing on pre-owned Ferraris.
  • Luxury Auto Collection (Scottsdale & Miami) — High-volume exotic dealer that frequently lists 488 Pistas and Pista Spiders.
  • Bring a Trailer / Cars & Bids — Online auctions often surface well-documented, low-mile 488s with full service history. Great for buyers who know exactly what they want.
  • DuPont Registry — Still a go-to for high-end listings, especially rare specs and Pista variants.

What to Look For When Buying a Used Ferrari 488

The 488 is generally reliable by exotic car standards, but there are things every buyer should check:

  • Service history: Ferrari recommends annual service regardless of mileage. Look for a complete service book from an authorized dealer — cars with gaps sell for significantly less.
  • Sticky interior trim: Some early 488 GTBs (2016–2017) can develop a sticky or tacky coating on certain interior plastics, a known Ferrari issue. It's cosmetic but expensive to fix — budget $3,000–$5,000 if present.
  • Turbo wastegate rattle: A cold-start rattle from the turbo wastegates is common and generally harmless, but have a Ferrari tech confirm it's not something more serious.
  • Clutch wear: The 7-speed DCT is robust, but city driving (common in Miami traffic) wears clutches faster. Check clutch wear percentage on the diagnostic readout — replacement runs $8,000–$12,000.
  • Paint protection: Miami sun is brutal on Rosso Corsa. Check for paint fade and confirm whether the car has PPF (paint protection film) installed. Adding full-body PPF after purchase costs $5,000–$8,000.
  • Tire age: Even low-mile cars may have old tires. The 488 runs Michelin Pilot Sport Cup 2s or Pilot Sport 4S tires — a full set runs $2,500–$3,500 installed.

Ferrari 488 Ownership Costs in Miami

Budget beyond the purchase price. Here's what annual ownership looks like:

ExpenseEstimated Annual Cost
Annual service (authorized dealer)$2,500 – $4,000
Insurance (Miami, clean record)$5,000 – $9,000
Tires (every 8,000–12,000 miles)$2,500 – $3,500 per set
Brake pads & rotors (every 15K–20K miles)$4,000 – $7,000
Registration & property tax (FL)$1,500 – $2,500
Detailing & PPF maintenance$1,200 – $2,400

Florida's lack of state income tax and relatively low registration fees make it one of the more affordable states for exotic car ownership. That's a big part of why so many Ferraris end up in Miami.

Ferrari 488 vs. F8 Tributo: Should You Wait?

The F8 Tributo replaced the 488 in 2020 with 710 hp (vs. 661), updated aero, and a refreshed interior. But the price gap is significant — a used F8 Tributo starts around $300,000+ in Miami, while a 488 GTB can be had for under $200,000. For most drivers, the 488 delivers 90% of the experience at 60% of the cost. The 488 Pista actually outperforms the base F8 in many metrics and holds its value better.

The Bottom Line

The Ferrari 488 for sale in Miami represents one of the best values in the used exotic car market right now. The 488 GTB and Spider are depreciating into a sweet spot where they're affordable enough to actually enjoy, while the Pista variants are heading the other direction — toward collectible status. Miami's deep inventory means you can be picky about spec, color, and options. Take your time, get a pre-purchase inspection from an authorized dealer, and you'll end up with one of the best mid-engine Ferraris ever built.

title: Maserati GranTurismo for Sale in Miami: 2026 Pricing, Specs & Buyer's Guide
excerpt: The all-new Maserati GranTurismo is a genuine grand tourer with a Ferrari-derived V6 and an electric Folgore variant. Here's what they cost in Miami, where to find one, and whether the classic V8 models are worth buying instead.
content:
The Maserati GranTurismo is back — and this time it means business. After a production gap, Maserati relaunched the GranTurismo in 2024 with two powertrains: a twin-turbo V6 developed with Ferrari (the Nettuno engine) and a fully electric Folgore variant. If you're looking for a Maserati GranTurismo for sale in Miami, you now have more options than ever — from brand-new 2025 models to classic V8 versions at bargain prices.

New vs. Classic: Two Eras of Maserati GranTurismo

There are really two cars called the Maserati GranTurismo, and both are available for sale in Miami right now:

  • New GranTurismo (2024–present): Built on an all-new platform with Maserati's Nettuno twin-turbo V6 (also found in the MC20) or the electric Folgore powertrain. This is a proper modern GT car with cutting-edge tech.
  • Classic GranTurismo (2008–2019): The naturally aspirated 4.7L V8 grand tourer that sounds like nothing else on the road. These have depreciated heavily and represent tremendous value.

Both have a place in a Miami garage. Let's break down each.

New Maserati GranTurismo Specs & Performance

The new-generation GranTurismo is a serious leap forward for Maserati. Here's how the variants compare:

Horsepower483 hp542 hp751 hp

Weight4,167 lbs4,167 lbs5,225 lbs
Range (Folgore)N/AN/A~280 miles (est.)

The Trofeo is the enthusiast's pick — the Nettuno V6 is essentially the same engine in the MC20 supercar, detuned slightly for GT comfort. The Folgore is the headline-grabber: nearly 1,000 lb-ft of torque from three electric motors makes it the fastest GranTurismo ever built, though it weighs over 5,200 pounds.

Maserati GranTurismo Pricing in Miami (2026)

Here's what you'll pay for a Maserati GranTurismo for sale in the Miami market:

Model / VariantPrice Range (2026)Notes

New GranTurismo Trofeo$195,000 – $225,000Performance V6; most popular with Miami buyers
New GranTurismo Folgore$210,000 – $250,000Fully electric; limited availability
Used 2024–2025 GranTurismo$145,000 – $195,000Early models already showing some depreciation
Classic GranTurismo (2008–2014)$28,000 – $48,000Incredible value; the V8 sounds spectacular
