title: Lamborghini Temerario: Specs, Price & What Miami Buyers Need to Know in 2026
excerpt: The Lamborghini Temerario replaces the Huracán with a twin-turbo V8 hybrid making 907 hp. Here's everything about specs, pricing, delivery timelines, and what it means for Miami's supercar scene.
content:
The Lamborghini Temerario is the most important car Lamborghini has made in a decade. It replaces the Huracán — Lamborghini's best-selling model ever — with something radically different under the skin: a twin-turbocharged 4.0-liter V8 paired with three electric motors, producing a combined 907 hp. For a brand built on naturally aspirated V10s and V12s, the Temerario represents a seismic shift. And for Miami, a city where Lamborghinis are as common as palm trees, it's about to become the new default supercar on every major boulevard.

The name means "reckless" or "fearless" in Italian — fitting for a car that bets Lamborghini's future on turbos, hybrids, and a smaller displacement engine. Whether you're on the waitlist or just curious, here's everything Miami buyers need to know about the Lamborghini Temerario in 2026.

Lamborghini Temerario Specs: What's Under the Hood

The headline numbers are staggering, but the engineering details tell the real story:

SpecificationLamborghini Temerario
Engine4.0L Twin-Turbo V8 (flat-plane crank)
Electric Motors3 (1 rear axle-mounted, 2 front axle)
Combined Output907 hp (677 hp ICE + 230 hp electric)
Engine Redline10,000 RPM
Transmission8-speed dual-clutch (DCT)
DrivetrainAWD (electric front axle + mechanical rear)
0-60 MPH~2.7 seconds
0-124 MPH (0-200 km/h)Under 9 seconds
Top Speed211+ MPH
Curb Weight~3,400 lbs (estimated)
EV Range~30 miles (electric-only mode)
BatteryLithium-ion, supercapacitor-assisted
BodyCarbon fiber / aluminum hybrid chassis

The V8 alone revs to 10,000 RPM — a number that belongs in a Formula 1 car, not a road car. The flat-plane crankshaft gives it a completely different character than the cross-plane V8s in AMGs or Ferraris. Lamborghini says the sound profile is distinctly its own: higher-pitched, more frenetic, and designed to remind you that turbocharging doesn't have to mean boring.

Lamborghini Temerario Price: What Miami Dealers Are Quoting

Lamborghini has set the base MSRP for the Temerario at approximately $300,000–$320,000. But if you're shopping in Miami, base price is a starting point for negotiation — in the wrong direction.

ConfigurationEstimated Price
Temerario (Base MSRP)$300,000–$320,000
With Ad Personam options$350,000–$400,000
Dealer markup (first allocations)$50,000–$150,000+
Realistic Miami out-the-door (2026)$380,000–$500,000+

First-year Temerario allocations are going to existing Lamborghini customers — the people who bought Huracáns, Urus models, and Revueltos. If you're a new buyer walking into a Miami dealer without purchase history, expect to wait or pay a significant markup. This is standard Lamborghini practice, and Miami's demand makes it worse.

Temerario vs. Huracán: What's Actually Different

The Temerario isn't just a Huracán with a new engine. It's a fundamentally different car:

FeatureHuracán (Outgoing)Temerario (New)
Engine5.2L NA V104.0L Twin-Turbo V8 + 3 electric motors
Power602–640 hp907 hp
Torque DeliveryLinear, builds with RPMInstant (electric fill at low RPM)
0-60 MPH2.9–3.1 sec~2.7 sec
SoundIconic V10 wailHigh-revving V8 + electric whine
EV ModeNoYes (~30 miles)
Front AxleMechanical AWDElectric torque vectoring
Transmission7-speed DCT8-speed DCT

The biggest loss? That naturally aspirated V10 sound. The Huracán's engine was one of the last great automotive symphonies — no turbos, no electric assistance, just 8,500 RPM of pure mechanical fury. The Temerario will be faster in every measurable way, but it won't sound like that. Expect Huracán values to firm up as enthusiasts who want the V10 experience rush to buy the last ones.

Lamborghini Temerario Delivery Timeline for Miami

Lamborghini began taking orders in late 2024, with the first deliveries expected in mid-to-late 2025. By April 2026, the delivery situation in Miami looks like this:

  • First allocations (Q3–Q4 2025): Delivered to VIP clients and existing multi-car Lamborghini customers
  • Second wave (Q1–Q2 2026): Broader availability, but still allocation-based at most dealers
  • Open ordering (estimated late 2026): When supply begins to meet demand and markups normalize

Miami's two authorized Lamborghini dealerships — Lamborghini Miami (North Miami Beach) and Prestige Imports (also the longtime Lamborghini dealer for South Florida) — both have waitlists. If you haven't placed a deposit yet, you're looking at a 2026 or early 2027 delivery at best.

How the Temerario Fits Into Miami's Supercar Scene

Miami is one of the top three Lamborghini markets in the United States, alongside Los Angeles and New York. The Huracán was ubiquitous here — you'd see multiple on a single drive down Collins Avenue. The Temerario is going to occupy that same space, but with a few twists:

  • EV mode for Miami Beach: The 30-mile electric range means you can cruise Ocean Drive, South Beach, and the Design District silently. Late-night arrivals at restaurants and hotels without waking the neighborhood — a genuine lifestyle benefit in Miami's residential-adjacent nightlife zones.
  • Better in traffic: The electric torque fill means the Temerario won't lug or stumble at low speeds the way the Huracán sometimes could. Stop-and-go on I-95 will be more refined.
  • The rental fleet factor: Miami's exotic car rental companies will add Temerarios as soon as they can get allocations. Expect to see them on Turo and at rental agencies by late 2026 or 2027, which will make them even more visible on the streets.

Should You Wait for the Temerario or Buy a Huracán Now?

This is the question every Miami Lamborghini buyer is asking in 2026. The answer depends on what you value:

Buy a Huracán now if:

  • You want the naturally aspirated V10 — there won't be another one
  • You prefer a simpler, lighter car without hybrid complexity
  • You're buying as a collector — the STO, Tecnica, and Sterrato will appreciate
  • You want to avoid markups — used Huracáns are priced fairly right now

Wait for the Temerario if:

  • You want the latest technology and maximum performance
  • EV mode and better fuel economy matter to you
  • You plan to daily drive it — the hybrid system makes city driving easier
  • You're building a relationship with a dealer for future allocations (Lamborghini rewards loyalty)

Lamborghini Temerario Competitors in Miami

The Temerario enters a market that's more competitive than anything the Huracán faced:

CompetitorPowerBase PriceKey Advantage
Ferrari 296 GTB819 hp (V6 hybrid)$345,000Lighter, sharper handling
McLaren 750S740 hp (V8 twin-turbo)$310,000Lightest, most focused driver's car
Porsche 911 GT3 RS518 hp (NA flat-6)$230,000Track weapon, analog feel
Mercedes-AMG GT Black Series720 hp (V8 twin-turbo)$400,000+ (used)Aero monster, collector status
Aston Martin Valhalla998 hp (V8 hybrid)$800,000+Hypercar territory

The Temerario's 907 hp output puts it above all of these except the Valhalla — at a fraction of the price. Whether that translates to a better driving experience remains to be seen, but on paper, the value proposition is extraordinary.

What the Temerario Means for Lamborghini's Future

The Temerario is Lamborghini's proof that electrification doesn't have to kill the supercar. The 10,000 RPM redline, the aggressive styling, the absurd power figure — these are all designed to reassure enthusiasts that Lamborghini hasn't gone soft. And the EV mode, the improved efficiency, the electric torque vectoring — these are concessions to a world that increasingly demands them.

For Miami, the Lamborghini Temerario will quickly become as defining as the Huracán was before it. It's faster, more technologically advanced, and better suited to the city's unique combination of show-off culture and actual driving. If you can get an allocation at MSRP, it's one of the best supercar buys of 2026. If you're paying a markup, just make sure it's a markup you can stomach — because prices will normalize within 12-18 months of full production.

title: Porsche Macan for Sale in Miami: 2026 Pricing, Models & Buyer's Guide
excerpt: The Porsche Macan is the best-selling Porsche for a reason — and Miami is one of its biggest markets. Here's what you'll pay in 2026, which trims to target, and where to find one.
content:
The Porsche Macan isn't just Porsche's best-selling model — it's one of the best-selling luxury compact SUVs in America, period. And if you live in Miami, you already know why. It's everywhere: Brickell parking garages, Bal Harbour valet lines, the school pickup lane at Ransom Everglades. The Macan hits a sweet spot that almost no other SUV manages — genuinely sporty driving dynamics in a practical package that handles South Florida's daily grind without breaking a sweat. If you're looking for a Porsche Macan for sale in Miami, 2026 is a fascinating time to buy. Here's the complete breakdown.

Why the Porsche Macan Dominates Miami

Miami and the Macan are a natural fit. The compact footprint makes it easy to navigate tight parking structures downtown and on the Beach. The turbocharged engines give you enough punch to merge onto I-95 without praying. And the interior quality is leagues ahead of comparably priced competitors — you're getting genuine Porsche build quality at a price point that doesn't require selling a kidney.

There's also the image factor. The Macan carries the Porsche badge and looks the part, but it starts well under six figures. For Miami professionals who want the brand cachet without the supercar maintenance bills, it's the obvious choice. And with the all-electric Macan now in the lineup alongside the combustion models, buyers have more options than ever.

Porsche Macan Models & What They Cost in Miami (2026)

The Macan lineup has expanded significantly. Here's what you'll find at Miami-area dealers and on the pre-owned market:

ModelYear RangeNew MSRPMiami Market (Used)Key Specs
Macan (Base)2019–2024$58,600–$62,900$34,000–$52,000261 hp turbo-4, 0–60 in 5.8s
Macan S2019–2024$66,400–$71,800$39,000–$58,000375 hp turbo V6, 0–60 in 4.6s
Macan GTS2020–2024$74,800–$82,600$48,000–$68,000434 hp turbo V6, sport suspension, 0–60 in 4.1s
Macan T2023–2024$62,900–$65,500$46,000–$56,000261 hp, sport-tuned chassis, limited-slip diff
Macan Turbo2020–2024$87,900–$96,000$58,000–$78,000434 hp (early) / V6, 0–60 in 4.1s
Electric Macan2025+$79,900$72,000–$78,000Dual motor, 402 hp, 0–60 in 5.0s, 308-mi range
Electric Macan Turbo2025+$103,900$95,000–$102,000Dual motor, 630 hp, 0–60 in 3.3s, 288-mi range

Prices reflect Miami market conditions as of April 2026. Certified pre-owned (CPO) vehicles typically command a 5–10% premium over private-party pricing.

ICE vs. Electric Macan: Which One Makes Sense in Miami?

This is the big question for 2026 buyers. The combustion Macan (2024 was the final model year for the gas version in most markets) remains hugely popular on the used market. The electric Macan, built on Porsche's PPE platform, is genuinely impressive but comes with trade-offs Miami buyers should understand.

Go combustion if: You want the widest selection and best value. The used market is flooded with low-mileage 2022–2024 Macans from lease returns. You'll get a proven powertrain, no range anxiety for those random Key West trips, and significantly lower entry pricing.

Go electric if: Your daily driving is under 250 miles (which covers basically everyone in Miami-Dade), you have home charging, and you want the latest tech. The electric Macan's interior is a generational leap, the acceleration is absurd, and Florida's flat terrain is ideal for EV range. Plus, no state income tax means you keep more of the federal tax credit.

Where to Buy a Porsche Macan in Miami

Miami has one of the densest concentrations of Porsche dealers in the country. Here are your main options:

  • The Collection Porsche (Coral Gables) — The flagship Miami Porsche dealer. Massive inventory, full CPO program, and they handle everything from base Macans to GT cars. Expect premium pricing but excellent service.
  • Braman Porsche (West Palm Beach) — Worth the drive north if you want a broader selection. One of the highest-volume Porsche dealers in the Southeast.
  • Porsche Fort Lauderdale — Strong CPO selection and competitive pricing. Often has Macans that moved off Miami lots.
  • Champion Porsche (Pompano Beach) — The world's largest Porsche dealer. If the spec you want exists, they probably have it.

For used and pre-owned, also check:

  • CarGurus / Autotrader — Filter by Miami ZIP codes for the widest net
  • Porsche Finder (porsche.com/usa/find) — Official CPO search across all US dealers
  • Bring a Trailer — For rare specs or enthusiast-grade examples (GTS, Turbo with options)

Best Porsche Macan Trims to Target for Value

Not all Macans are created equal when it comes to bang-for-buck. Here's our take for Miami buyers:

Best overall value: 2022–2023 Macan S. The sweet spot. You get the 375 hp turbocharged V6, which transforms the car from "nice SUV" to "genuinely quick." These are hitting the used market from lease returns in the $42,000–$52,000 range with under 30,000 miles. That's a tremendous amount of car for the money.

Best daily driver: 2023–2024 Macan T. Porsche's "Touring" trim takes the base engine but adds sport-tuned suspension, a torque-vectoring limited-slip rear differential, and sportier aesthetics. It's the enthusiast's base model — drives noticeably better than the standard Macan without the V6 fuel costs.

Best for performance: 2022–2024 Macan GTS. The GTS has always been the driver's choice in the Macan lineup. Same 434 hp as the Turbo (in later years), standard sport suspension, and aggressive styling. If you care about how the car feels on A1A or through the Rickenbacker Causeway, this is the one.

Best future-proof pick: Electric Macan Turbo. If budget allows, the electric Macan Turbo is the most technologically advanced SUV Porsche has ever built. 630 hp, sub-3.5-second 0–60, and an interior that makes the outgoing combustion Macan look dated. Early depreciation will be steep, but for buyers planning to keep it 5+ years, it's the move.

What to Inspect Before Buying a Used Porsche Macan in Miami

The Macan is generally reliable, but Miami's climate creates specific concerns:

  • Coolant system: Check for any signs of coolant leaks around the turbo and water pump area. Florida heat stresses cooling systems harder than temperate climates.
  • Brake wear: Macan brakes are expensive to replace ($1,200–$2,500 for a full set depending on trim). Check pad thickness and rotor condition — Miami's stop-and-go traffic eats brakes.
  • Interior condition: Sun damage is real. Check the dash, steering wheel, and seat bolsters for UV fading or cracking. Cars regularly parked outside in Miami age faster inside.
  • Transfer case & differential: The Macan's AWD system uses a transfer case and rear differential that need fluid changes every 40,000 miles. Ask for service records confirming this was done.
  • Suspension bushings: On higher-mileage examples (60,000+), the front control arm bushings can wear. Listen for clunks over speed bumps during the test drive.
  • PDK transmission: The dual-clutch PDK is robust but needs a fluid change around 50,000 miles. Neglected units can develop shuddering at low speeds.

Porsche Macan Insurance & Ownership Costs in Miami

Ownership costs are where luxury SUVs separate from mainstream crossovers. Here's what to budget:

Cost CategoryAnnual Estimate (Miami)
Insurance (full coverage)$2,400–$3,800
Scheduled maintenance$800–$1,400
Fuel (15,000 mi/yr)$2,800–$3,400 (premium required)
Tires (set replacement)$1,000–$1,600 every 25k–35k mi
Registration & taxes$500–$800

Miami insurance rates for the Macan are moderate by luxury SUV standards — cheaper than a Cayenne Turbo or Urus, but more than a BMW X3. Shop around; rates vary dramatically between providers in South Florida.

Porsche Macan vs. the Competition in Miami

The Macan doesn't exist in a vacuum. Here's how it stacks up against what else you'll see on Brickell:

  • BMW X3 M40i: Comparable power, slightly more interior space, and $5,000–$8,000 cheaper on the used market. But the driving dynamics aren't as sharp, and the interior quality falls short of the Porsche.
  • Mercedes GLC AMG: Plusher ride, better infotainment (debatable with the electric Macan), but less engaging to drive. The AMG versions close the performance gap but cost more.
  • Genesis GV70: The value play — similar size, strong performance in 3.5T form, and significantly cheaper. But it lacks the badge prestige and resale value of the Porsche.
  • Alfa Romeo Stelvio Quadrifoglio: The handling champ that nobody buys. Faster and more dramatic than the Macan GTS, but reliability concerns and poor resale keep most Miami buyers away.

The Macan consistently wins on the combination of driving engagement, build quality, and resale value. In Miami's status-conscious market, the Porsche badge is also worth real money at resale time.

Final Verdict: Should You Buy a Porsche Macan in Miami?

The Porsche Macan is one of the easiest recommendations in the luxury SUV space. It drives like a sports car, functions like a practical daily, and holds its value better than nearly anything in its class. For Miami buyers, the sweet spot is a 2022–2023 Macan S in the low $40,000s — you get the turbocharged V6, a nearly new vehicle, and enough leftover budget to option it exactly how you want through aftermarket upgrades.

If you're shopping for a Porsche Macan for sale in the Miami area, start with The Collection in Coral Gables or Champion Porsche in Pompano Beach for the widest CPO selection. For private-party deals, filter CarGurus and Autotrader by Miami-Dade and Broward County ZIP codes — lease returns are flooding the market right now, and deals are there for buyers who know what to look for.

  • Porsche Panamera for Sale in Miami: 2026 Pricing, Models & Buyer's Guide
  • Lamborghini Temerario: Specs, Price & What Miami Buyers Need to Know in 2026

title: Porsche Cayenne for Sale in Miami: 2026 Pricing, Models & Buyer's Guide
excerpt: The Porsche Cayenne redefined what a luxury SUV could be — and Miami is its natural habitat. Here's what you'll pay in 2026, which models to target, and where to find the best deals.
content:
The Porsche Cayenne is the SUV that saved Porsche — and then proceeded to become the benchmark for every performance luxury SUV that followed. Two decades after its controversial debut, the Cayenne is so deeply embedded in Miami culture that it's hard to imagine the city's streets without them. From the school run in Pinecrest to weekend highway pulls on the Turnpike, the Cayenne does it all without compromise. If you're looking for a Porsche Cayenne for sale in Miami, 2026 offers a wide market with everything from bargain base models to six-figure Turbo GTs. Here's your complete guide.

Why the Porsche Cayenne Is Miami's Luxury SUV of Choice

The Cayenne succeeds in Miami for reasons beyond the badge. It's big enough to be practical for families (real cargo space, real back-seat room), powerful enough to feel exciting on empty stretches of I-75, and refined enough for the valet at Zuma or the Surf Club. The air suspension soaks up Miami's less-than-perfect road surfaces, and the cabin is a genuine luxury environment that rivals anything from Bentley at half the price.

There's also the versatility angle. The Cayenne comes as a standard SUV or a sleeker Cayenne Coupé, with powertrains ranging from a sensible turbocharged V6 to a twin-turbo V8 making over 600 hp. No matter your budget or priorities, there's a Porsche Cayenne configuration that fits.

Porsche Cayenne Models & Miami Pricing (2026)

The third-generation Cayenne (2019–present) is the one you'll find most of on the market. Here's the full breakdown:

ModelYear RangeNew MSRPMiami Market (Used)Key Specs
Cayenne (Base)2019–2026$75,300–$82,900$38,000–$62,000348 hp turbo V6, 0–60 in 5.4s
Cayenne S2020–2026$89,900–$98,600$48,000–$72,000434–474 hp turbo V6, 0–60 in 4.4s
Cayenne GTS2021–2026$112,900–$122,000$72,000–$98,000453 hp twin-turbo V8, 0–60 in 4.2s, sport exhaust
Cayenne Turbo2019–2021$130,000–$142,000$62,000–$85,000541 hp twin-turbo V8, 0–60 in 3.7s
Cayenne Turbo GT2022–2026$185,000–$198,000$138,000–$175,000631 hp twin-turbo V8, 0–60 in 3.1s
Cayenne E-Hybrid2019–2026$85,900–$94,000$42,000–$65,000456 hp combined, ~25 mi electric range
Cayenne Turbo S E-Hybrid2020–2023$162,000–$175,000$82,000–$115,000670 hp combined, 0–60 in 3.6s
Cayenne Coupé2020–2026+$4,000–$6,000 vs SUV+$2,000–$5,000 vs SUVSloped roofline, sportier stance

Miami market prices as of April 2026. CPO examples command 5–12% over private-party. Coupé variants consistently hold a premium over the standard SUV body.

Which Porsche Cayenne Should You Buy in Miami?

With this many configurations, choosing the right Cayenne comes down to priorities. Here's our recommendation for different Miami buyer profiles:

Best value: 2021–2022 Cayenne Base. Don't sleep on the base model. The 348 hp turbocharged V6 moves the Cayenne with authority — it's only "slow" compared to the V8 models above it. Used examples with 25,000–40,000 miles are landing in the $42,000–$52,000 range, which is stunning value for a full-size luxury SUV with this level of capability. The base Cayenne with the right options (air suspension, premium interior, Sport Chrono) is the smart money pick.

Best all-rounder: 2022–2024 Cayenne S. The S model received a power bump in recent years and now makes 474 hp from a single-turbo 2.9L V6. It's the Goldilocks trim — fast enough to embarrass sports sedans, comfortable enough for the family, and priced below the V8 models. This is what most Miami buyers should be cross-shopping.

Best for enthusiasts: 2022–2024 Cayenne GTS. The GTS is where the Cayenne stops pretending it's just an SUV. The twin-turbo 4.0L V8 sounds incredible (especially with the sport exhaust crackling through Brickell tunnels), the chassis tuning is noticeably sharper, and the GTS-specific interior with Alcantara touches feels special. If driving experience matters as much as practicality, this is your Cayenne.

Best flex: Cayenne Turbo GT. The 631 hp Turbo GT is one of the fastest SUVs ever built. It held the Nürburgring SUV lap record, hits 60 in 3.1 seconds, and looks absolutely menacing in person. Miami's Star Island crowd has already adopted it as the "casual" daily. If budget isn't the primary concern and you want the ultimate Cayenne, this is it — but expect to pay $140,000+ even used.

Cayenne vs. Cayenne Coupé: Which Body Style?

Porsche offers every Cayenne trim in both SUV and Coupé body styles. The Coupé sacrifices a few cubic feet of cargo space for a dramatically sloped roofline that makes the Cayenne look like a scaled-up 911 from certain angles. In Miami, the Coupé outsells the standard SUV in higher trims — the GTS Coupé and Turbo GT Coupé are especially popular with buyers who prioritize aesthetics.

Practically speaking, the standard SUV is the better family hauler. The Coupé's rear headroom is tighter, and the cargo area is slightly smaller. But if you don't regularly haul large items or tall rear passengers, the Coupé's styling advantage is significant — and it holds its value slightly better at resale.

Where to Find a Porsche Cayenne for Sale in Miami

The Cayenne is one of Porsche's highest-volume models, so inventory is plentiful across South Florida:

  • The Collection Porsche (Coral Gables) — Miami's premier Porsche dealer. Huge Cayenne inventory across all trims, strong CPO program, and they frequently have allocations for new Turbo GT and GTS models.
  • Champion Porsche (Pompano Beach) — The world's largest Porsche dealer by volume. If you want a specific spec or color combination, Champion probably has it or can source it fastest.
  • Braman Porsche (West Palm Beach) — Competitive pricing and excellent selection of both new and CPO Cayennes.
  • Porsche Miami (Doral) — Convenient for buyers in western Miami-Dade. Good CPO selection and service department.

Beyond the dealer network:

  • CarGurus / Cars.com — Search by Miami ZIP code. The 33101–33199 range covers Miami-Dade; expand to 33301+ for Broward County deals.
  • Bring a Trailer — The go-to for enthusiast-spec Cayennes (GTS, Turbo GT, rare colors, manual Cayennes from the first generation).
  • Porsche Approved CPO — Two additional years of warranty beyond the original. Worth the premium for peace of mind, especially on E-Hybrid models with complex powertrains.

What to Check Before Buying a Used Cayenne in Miami

The third-gen Cayenne is well-built, but Florida ownership patterns create specific wear areas:

  • Air suspension: If equipped (standard on GTS/Turbo, optional on lower trims), check for sagging corners or compressor noise. Replacement struts run $1,500–$2,500 each. This is the single most expensive potential repair on a used Cayenne.
  • Coolant transfer pipe (V8 models): Early 4.0L twin-turbo V8s had a plastic coolant pipe between the cylinder banks that could crack. Porsche issued a service bulletin. Verify it's been addressed on 2020–2021 GTS and Turbo models.
  • Brake condition: Cayenne brakes are massive and expensive. A full brake job (pads + rotors, all four corners) can run $3,500–$6,000 depending on whether you have steel or carbon-ceramic brakes. Check remaining pad life — it directly affects your negotiation leverage.
  • Panoramic roof drainage: Florida's afternoon downpours test drainage systems. Check the headliner for water stains and verify the sunroof drain tubes aren't clogged — a common issue on SUVs parked under trees.
  • Battery health (E-Hybrid): If shopping a PHEV model, check the hybrid battery's state of health. Vehicles that were rarely plugged in (common in Miami, oddly) may show degraded EV range.
  • Tire wear: The Cayenne is heavy and eats tires, especially on performance-spec staggered setups (GTS, Turbo). Budget $1,400–$2,200 for a full set of quality replacements.

Porsche Cayenne Ownership Costs in Miami

The Cayenne is a premium vehicle with premium running costs. Here's a realistic annual budget:

Cost CategoryAnnual Estimate (Miami)
Insurance (full coverage)$3,200–$5,400
Scheduled maintenance$1,000–$1,800
Fuel (15,000 mi/yr, premium)$3,200–$4,200
Tires (annualized)$600–$900
Registration & property tax$600–$1,100

Insurance is the biggest variable. Miami's high uninsured motorist rate and frequent accident claims push premiums higher than the national average. Get quotes from at least four providers — the spread between cheapest and most expensive can be $2,000+ annually for the same Cayenne.

Cayenne vs. the Competition in Miami

The mid-size luxury SUV segment is brutally competitive. Here's how the Cayenne stacks up against what you'll see in Miami:

  • BMW X5 M60i / X6 M: Comparable power in the V8 variants, slightly cheaper, and the X6 offers similar coupé styling. But the Cayenne's chassis dynamics and interior quality remain a step ahead. Resale favors Porsche significantly.
  • Mercedes GLE AMG / GLE Coupé: More comfortable, better ride quality in standard mode, and MBUX infotainment is excellent. But the Cayenne is sharper to drive and feels more special. The GLE depreciates faster.
  • Lamborghini Urus: The elephant in the room. Shares its platform with the Cayenne (VW Group) but adds 200+ hp, outrageous styling, and a six-figure premium. In Miami, the Urus is a statement car; the Cayenne is the one you actually live with daily.
  • Range Rover Sport: The British alternative. Better off-road (not that it matters in Miami), more opulent interior in the top trims, but Range Rover reliability concerns persist. The Cayenne is the safer long-term ownership bet.
  • Audi RS Q8: Another VW Group sibling. The RS Q8 uses a version of the Cayenne Turbo's V8 and undercuts it on price. It's a smart alternative if you care less about the Porsche badge — but the Cayenne GTS drives circles around it.

Final Verdict: Should You Buy a Porsche Cayenne in Miami?

The Porsche Cayenne remains one of the best all-around luxury SUVs you can buy, and Miami is arguably the best city in America to own one. The combination of performance, luxury, practicality, and resale value is unmatched in its segment. For most buyers, a 2022–2023 Cayenne S in the $55,000–$65,000 range represents the sweet spot — enough power to thrill, enough refinement to pamper, and enough value left on the table to make financial sense.

Start your search at The Collection in Coral Gables or Champion Porsche in Pompano Beach for CPO options with warranty coverage. For the best private-party deals on a Porsche Cayenne for sale, watch CarGurus and Autotrader filtered to South Florida ZIP codes — lease returns from 2022–2023 models are hitting the market in volume right now, and motivated sellers are pricing aggressively. If you can find a well-optioned S or GTS with air suspension, Sport Chrono, and the premium interior package, that's the Cayenne to buy.

title: Best Portable Car Lifts for Your Home Garage in Miami (2026)
excerpt: Skip the dealer markup on basic maintenance. These portable car lifts fit Miami condo garages, handle exotic car weights, and pay for themselves within a year. Here are the best options from QuickJack, BendPak, and more.
content:
If you own an exotic or performance car in Miami, you already know what dealer labor rates look like — $200 to $350 an hour at most authorized shops, and even independent specialists aren't cheap. A portable car lift for your home garage changes the equation entirely. Oil changes, brake inspections, wheel swaps, underbody detailing, even suspension work — all become doable in your own space, on your own schedule.

The problem? Most Miami garages aren't exactly spacious. Between condo parking spots, tight two-car garages in Coral Gables, and the low ceilings you'll find in plenty of older Miami homes, you need a lift that's compact, portable, and still capable of handling a 4,000+ lb exotic car. Here's what actually works.

Why a Portable Car Lift Makes Sense in Miami

Before we get into specific models, here's why a home lift is particularly smart for Miami exotic car owners:

  • Dealer labor savings: At $250/hour, a simple brake job that takes two hours saves you $500 per visit. The lift pays for itself in 3-5 service intervals.
  • Underbody protection: Miami's salt air and coastal humidity attack undercarriages relentlessly. Having easy lift access means you can regularly rinse, inspect, and treat the underbody — something most owners neglect because jacking up a car on the ground is miserable.
  • Wheel and tire work: Swapping between track wheels and street wheels before a Homestead Miami Speedway day? A lift makes a 2-hour job a 30-minute job.
  • Detailing access: Professional detailers charge $200+ for underbody ceramic coating. With a lift, you can DIY it with a $40 bottle of spray sealant.
  • Storage when not in use: Portable lifts collapse flat, meaning they don't eat your limited Miami garage real estate permanently.

What to Look for in a Portable Car Lift

Not every lift works for every situation. Here's what matters most for Miami garage use:

FeatureWhy It MattersWhat to Look For
Weight capacityExotic cars range from 3,000 lbs (Lotus Emira) to 5,500+ lbs (Urus, Cayenne Turbo GT)Minimum 5,000 lb capacity for versatility
Lift heightNeed enough clearance to work underneath comfortably18-24 inches for portable; 6+ feet for full-height
Collapsed heightMust fit under low-slung cars to positionUnder 3 inches is ideal for exotics
Garage ceiling heightMiami condos often have 8-9 ft ceilingsFull-height lifts need 11+ ft; portables work in any garage
Power sourceHydraulic vs. electric vs. air110V electric is most convenient for residential
FootprintMust fit standard parking spot dimensionsUnder 70 inches wide when deployed

Our Top Picks: Best Portable Car Lifts for Miami Garages

1. QuickJack BL-5000SLX — Best Overall Portable Lift

The QuickJack BL-5000SLX is the gold standard for portable car lifts, and for good reason. It's two independent lifting frames connected to a single hydraulic power unit, slides under most cars at just 2.9 inches collapsed, and lifts 5,000 lbs to a working height of 21.2 inches. That's enough clearance for wheel work, brake jobs, oil changes, and underbody detailing on everything from a Ferrari 296 GTB to a Mercedes G-Wagon.

What makes it perfect for Miami condos: it stores vertically against a wall, taking up virtually zero floor space when not in use. The entire system rolls on built-in wheels, so one person can position it in minutes.

2. QuickJack BL-7000SLX — Best for Heavy Exotic SUVs

If you're lifting a Lamborghini Urus (4,850 lbs), Bentley Bentayga (5,379 lbs), or Rolls-Royce Cullinan (5,644 lbs), you need the extra capacity of the BL-7000SLX. At 7,000 lbs capacity, it handles the heaviest exotic SUVs with a comfortable safety margin.

The trade-off is slightly more weight and a higher collapsed height (3.5 inches), which means very low cars like a McLaren GT or Ferrari Roma might need adapter blocks. But for the Miami buyer who owns both a performance SUV and a sports car, this is the versatile choice.

3. BendPak MD-6XP Mid-Rise Lift — Best for Serious Home Mechanics

The BendPak MD-6XP steps up from the QuickJack concept with a 6,000 lb capacity, wider frame for better vehicle compatibility, and a more rigid lifting platform. It's a proper mid-rise scissor lift rather than a portable frame system, which means better stability for heavier work — think suspension jobs, exhaust work, or anything where you need to put real force on components without the car shifting.

The downside: it's heavier and doesn't store as compactly. But if you have a dedicated garage bay (common in Miami's newer luxury townhomes and single-family homes in Pinecrest, Coconut Grove, and Coral Gables), the BendPak is the more capable long-term investment.

4. APlusLift HW-SL6600 — Best Budget Option

Not everyone needs to spend $2,000+ on a lift. The APlusLift HW-SL6600 delivers 6,600 lbs of lifting capacity at roughly half the price of a QuickJack, making it an excellent entry point for Miami car owners who want to start doing their own maintenance without a massive upfront investment.

The build quality isn't as refined as QuickJack or BendPak — the hydraulic cylinders aren't as smooth, and the safety locks require more attention — but it does the job. For oil changes, brake pad swaps, and wheel rotations on your weekend, it's more than adequate.

5. MaxJax M6K Portable Two-Post Lift — Best for Full-Height Access

If you have the ceiling height (minimum 11 feet), the MaxJax M6K is a game-changer. It's a portable two-post lift that bolts to the floor (removable) and gives you full standing-height access underneath the vehicle — the same kind of access you'd get at a professional shop. Capacity is 6,000 lbs, which covers every exotic car and SUV short of a fully armored G-Wagon.

The MaxJax is designed for residential use with 110V power, and the posts can be folded against the wall when not in use. This is the choice for Miami homeowners with a proper garage who want professional-grade capability without permanently dedicating floor space to a two-post lift.

Essential Accessories for Your Home Lift

A lift alone isn't enough. Here's what you'll want alongside it:

  • Jack pads / lift point adapters: Many exotics have specific lift points that require padded adapters. Universal rubber pads work for most, but Porsche, Ferrari, and McLaren owners should invest in OEM-spec puck adapters ($30–$80). Find jack pad adapters on Amazon →
  • LED underbody work light: You're under the car — you need light. A rechargeable LED bar that magnetically attaches to the frame is invaluable ($40–$80). Find LED work lights on Amazon →
  • Drip tray / oil drain pan: Protects your garage floor during oil changes. A low-profile drain pan with pour spout makes cleanup painless ($15–$30). Find drain pans on Amazon →
  • Torque wrench: If you're doing wheel work, a quality torque wrench is non-negotiable. Budget $80–$150 for one that covers the 80–150 ft-lb range most exotic cars require. Find torque wrenches on Amazon →

Safety Considerations

A few non-negotiable rules for home lift use:

  • Always use the safety locks. Every quality lift has mechanical safety locks that engage at various heights. Never work under a car held only by hydraulic pressure.
  • Check your garage floor. Portable lifts need a flat, solid concrete surface. Miami homes with epoxy-coated garage floors are fine. Cracked, uneven, or thin concrete can be dangerous — get an inspector's opinion if you're unsure.
  • Know your lift points. Every car has specific manufacturer-designated lift points. Using the wrong point can crush body panels, damage the frame, or cause the car to slip off the lift. Check your owner's manual or a model-specific forum.
  • Level ground only. Miami is flat (thankfully), but make sure your garage floor doesn't slope toward a drain. Even a 1-2 degree slope can cause issues under load.
  • Weight includes you. If you're working on the car while it's lifted, and you're leaning on it or placing heavy tools inside, factor your weight into the capacity calculation.

The Bottom Line

A portable car lift is one of the smartest investments a Miami car enthusiast can make. The QuickJack BL-5000SLX is our top pick for most buyers — it balances capacity, portability, and price perfectly, and it fits in every Miami garage from a Brickell condo spot to a Coral Gables estate. If you're regularly lifting heavy SUVs, step up to the BL-7000SLX. And if you have the ceiling height and floor space for a proper two-post setup, the MaxJax M6K gives you shop-level access at home.

At $250/hour dealer labor rates in South Florida, these lifts don't just make maintenance easier — they make financial sense. The average Miami exotic car owner who does even basic maintenance at home will recoup the cost of a QuickJack within the first year. Everything after that is pure savings — and the satisfaction of actually working on your own car.

title: Best Wheel Cleaners & Tire Shine Products for Exotic Cars in Miami (2026)
excerpt: Brake dust from carbon-ceramics, road salt from ocean air, and Florida's relentless humidity make wheel care a constant battle for Miami exotic car owners. These are the products that actually work — tested on the cars that need them most.
content:
Here's a truth every Miami exotic car owner discovers quickly: your wheels are the hardest-working, most abused, and most visible part of your car — and they never stay clean. Between the aggressive brake dust from carbon-ceramic brakes (looking at you, Porsche, Ferrari, and Lamborghini), the salt-laden coastal air that corrodes everything, and the road grime that Miami's construction-heavy streets coat your rims with daily, wheel care isn't optional. It's survival.

The problem is that most wheel cleaners are designed for regular cars with regular brakes. Exotic car wheels generate more heat, more brake dust (especially iron-based dust from performance pads), and are often finished with delicate coatings — forged aluminum, ceramic clear coat, diamond-cut faces — that acid-based cleaners will destroy. You need products that are both powerful enough to dissolve baked-on brake dust and safe enough for wheels that cost $2,000–$5,000 each.

We tested the best wheel cleaners and tire shine products on everything from a daily-driven Porsche 911 GT3 to a garaged Lamborghini Huracán STO. Here's what works.

Quick Picks: Best Wheel Care Products for Exotic Cars

ProductCategoryPriceBest For
Sonax Full Effect Wheel CleanerWheel cleaner$17–$22 (16.9 oz)Overall best wheel cleaner; safe on all finishes
P&S Brake BusterWheel cleaner$18–$24 (32 oz)Heavy brake dust; professional-grade
CarPro IronXIron remover$20–$28 (500ml)Embedded iron particles; color-change formula
Adam's Polishes Wheel CleanerWheel cleaner$13–$18 (16 oz)Budget-friendly; safe for coated wheels
Chemical Guys Diablo Gel Wheel CleanerWheel cleaner$12–$18 (16 oz)Gel formula that clings to vertical surfaces
AMMO Mud Tire GelTire dressing$25–$30 (8 oz)Premium satin finish; no sling
CarPro PERLTire dressing$18–$25 (500ml)Adjustable dilution for matte-to-satin finish
Gyeon Q² TireTire coating$22–$28Long-lasting ceramic tire coating

Best Wheel Cleaners — Detailed Reviews

1. Sonax Full Effect Wheel Cleaner — Best Overall

The Sonax Full Effect has been the go-to wheel cleaner for professional detailers for years, and it earns that reputation every time you spray it. The acid-free, pH-balanced formula turns purple on contact with iron brake dust particles — a satisfying visual confirmation that it's actually working — then rinses clean without any scrubbing on lightly soiled wheels.

For Miami's exotic car scene, the key feature is that it's completely safe on clear-coated, polished, chrome, anodized, and painted wheels. That means you can use the same bottle on your Porsche's satin-black GT3 wheels and your Bentley's diamond-cut alloys without worrying about etching or staining.

How to use it: Spray liberally on cool, dry wheels. Wait 2-3 minutes (you'll see the purple color change). Agitate with a soft wheel brush for baked-on areas. Rinse thoroughly with a pressure washer or strong hose spray.

Check Sonax Full Effect prices on Amazon →

2. P&S Brake Buster — Best for Heavy Brake Dust

If your exotic car runs aggressive brake pads (metallic or semi-metallic compounds on steel rotors), the brake dust situation is brutal. P&S Brake Buster was formulated specifically for this — it's a concentrated, non-acid wheel and tire cleaner that dissolves even heavily baked-on brake dust that's been cooking in Miami's heat for weeks.

Brake Buster is versatile too. It cleans wheels, tires, and wheel wells in one product, which simplifies your routine. The 1-gallon concentrate dilutes to various strengths — 4:1 for maintenance washes, full strength for neglected wheels — making it the most economical option on this list for regular use.

Pro tip for Miami owners: Keep a diluted spray bottle of Brake Buster in your trunk. After a track day at Homestead or a spirited drive through the Everglades, a quick spray-and-rinse at the nearest self-serve car wash prevents brake dust from bonding permanently in the Florida heat.

Check P&S Brake Buster prices on Amazon →

3. CarPro IronX — Best Iron Remover for Carbon-Ceramic Brake Dust

CarPro IronX is technically an iron decontamination spray rather than a traditional wheel cleaner, but for exotic car owners with carbon-ceramic brakes, it's essential. Carbon-ceramic brakes produce less dust than steel rotors, but the dust they do produce contains iron particles that embed into wheel coatings and clear coat. Regular wheel cleaners don't touch embedded iron — IronX dissolves it chemically.

The formula turns deep purple/red as it reacts with iron particles, and the smell is unmistakable (think mild sulfur). It's not pleasant, but it's effective. After a single treatment, wheels that looked perpetually dirty despite regular washing will suddenly look factory-fresh.

Use case: IronX isn't for every wash. Use it monthly as a decontamination step, followed by your regular wheel cleaner for maintenance washes. It's also brilliant for prepping wheels before applying a ceramic wheel coating.

Check CarPro IronX prices on Amazon →

4. Adam's Polishes Wheel Cleaner — Best Budget Option

Not every wheel cleaning session needs the heavy artillery. Adam's Polishes Wheel Cleaner is a pH-neutral, color-changing formula that handles weekly maintenance washes excellently at a lower price point than Sonax or IronX. It's safe on all wheel finishes, smells better than most wheel cleaners (seriously, it matters when you're working in a Miami garage with no ventilation), and comes in a range of sizes including an economical gallon jug.

For Miami owners who wash weekly (as you should, given the salt air), Adam's is the perfect maintenance cleaner to rotate with a stronger decontamination product like IronX on a monthly basis.

Check Adam's Wheel Cleaner prices on Amazon →

5. Chemical Guys Diablo Gel Wheel Cleaner — Best for Intricate Wheel Designs

Many exotic car wheels feature intricate multi-spoke or mesh designs — think Lamborghini's forged center-lock wheels or Ferrari's diamond-cut designs — where liquid cleaners run off before they can work. Chemical Guys Diablo solves this with a gel formula that clings to vertical surfaces and complex geometries, giving the active ingredients more contact time to dissolve brake dust.

The gel consistency also means less product waste. Instead of spraying and watching half your wheel cleaner drip onto the ground, Diablo stays where you put it. For Miami's multi-spoke exotic wheels, this alone justifies the purchase.

Check Chemical Guys Diablo prices on Amazon →

Best Tire Shine & Tire Dressing Products

Clean wheels without dressed tires look incomplete. But choosing the wrong tire shine in Miami is a recipe for disaster — high heat causes cheap silicone-based dressings to sling onto paint, attract dirt within hours, and leave a greasy film that looks worse than bare rubber. Here's what actually performs in South Florida conditions.

1. AMMO Mud Tire Gel — Best Premium Tire Dressing

Larry Kosilla's AMMO Mud Tire Gel is the enthusiast's choice, and it earns its premium price. The water-based gel formula applies with a foam applicator and delivers a deep, natural satin finish — not the wet, greasy look of cheap tire shines. It lasts 2-4 weeks depending on driving conditions and, critically for Miami, it doesn't sling at highway speeds.

The application process is also more controlled than spray-on products. You apply a thin layer with a foam pad, work it into the rubber, and the result is a rich, OEM-like darkness that makes your tires look freshly installed without the artificial shine.

Check AMMO Mud Tire Gel prices on Amazon →

2. CarPro PERL — Best Adjustable Tire Dressing

CarPro PERL (Protect, Enhance, Renew, Last) is uniquely versatile because it dilutes to different ratios for different finishes. At 1:1 with water, it produces a subtle matte finish. Full strength gives a deeper satin look. This means you can match the tire shine level to the car — a matte dressing on a track-focused GT3 RS, or a deeper shine on a Rolls-Royce Cullinan.

PERL also works on exterior trim, engine bay plastics, and interior surfaces, making it a multi-use product that earns its spot in your Miami detailing kit. A single 500ml bottle diluted 1:1 lasts months of regular use.

Check CarPro PERL prices on Amazon →

3. Gyeon Q² Tire — Best Long-Lasting Tire Coating

If you want a tire dressing that genuinely lasts through Miami's rain, heat, and weekly washes, Gyeon Q² Tire is the answer. It's technically a ceramic coating for tires — not a traditional dressing — that bonds to the rubber surface and provides a deep satin finish for 4-8 weeks per application.

The application requires clean, dry tires and a curing period, so it's more involved than a spray-and-go product. But the longevity in Miami's harsh conditions is unmatched. One application survives multiple washes, daily tropical rain, and the constant UV bombardment that degrades regular dressings within days.

Check Gyeon Q² Tire prices on Amazon →

Essential Wheel Care Tools

Products are only half the equation. These tools make the difference between a mediocre wheel wash and a professional result:

ToolPurposePrice RangeAmazon Link
EZ Detail Wheel BrushReach between spokes and behind the wheel face$20–$30Shop on Amazon →
Wheel Woolies (set of 3)Soft lambs wool brushes for delicate wheel finishes$35–$55Shop on Amazon →
Detail Factory Lug Nut BrushClean around lug nuts and bolt holes$8–$12Shop on Amazon →
Tire applicator foam pads (6-pack)Even application of tire dressing$8–$14Shop on Amazon →
Short-handle wheel barrel brushScrub tire sidewalls and wheel wells$10–$18Shop on Amazon →

The Complete Wheel Care Routine for Miami Exotic Cars

Here's the protocol Miami's best detailers follow — and what you should do weekly if you want your wheels to stay flawless:

Weekly Maintenance Wash

  1. Rinse wheels with water to remove loose debris. Use a pressure washer at 1,200-1,500 PSI if available — enough to blast off surface grime without damaging wheel coatings.
  2. Spray wheel cleaner (Sonax Full Effect or Adam's) on all four wheels. Work one wheel at a time to prevent the cleaner from drying.
  3. Agitate with an EZ Detail brush between spokes and behind the wheel face. Use a lug nut brush around bolt holes.
  4. Scrub tire sidewalls with a stiff barrel brush and your wheel cleaner (or a dedicated tire cleaner like P&S Brake Buster).
  5. Rinse thoroughly. Ensure no cleaner residue remains — it can leave water spots on polished aluminum.
  6. Dry with a dedicated microfiber towel. Don't use the same towel you use on paint — brake dust is abrasive.
  7. Apply tire dressing (AMMO Mud or CarPro PERL) with a foam applicator. Thin, even coat. Let it absorb for 5 minutes before driving.

Monthly Decontamination

  1. After your regular wash, spray CarPro IronX on all wheels.
  2. Wait 3-5 minutes. Watch for the purple color change indicating iron dissolution.
  3. Agitate stubborn spots with a soft brush.
  4. Rinse completely. Follow with your regular wheel cleaner if needed.
  5. Consider applying a ceramic wheel coating (like Gyeon Q² Rim) every 6-12 months for ongoing protection.

What NOT to Use on Exotic Car Wheels

Some common products can ruin expensive wheels. Avoid these:

  • Acid-based wheel cleaners: Hydrofluoric acid and phosphoric acid cleaners (common at gas station car washes) will etch clear-coated and polished aluminum wheels permanently. If a wheel cleaner says "not safe for polished or anodized wheels," it has no place near your exotic.
  • Automatic car wash brushes: The spinning brushes in drive-through washes grind brake dust and sand into your wheel finish like sandpaper. If you must use an automatic wash, choose touchless only — or better yet, skip it entirely.
  • Silicone-based tire sprays: The cheap aerosol tire shines you find at gas stations are the worst thing you can put on your tires. They create a greasy film that slings onto paint at highway speed, attracts dirt like a magnet, and actually degrades rubber over time. Use water-based gel dressings instead.
  • Steel wool or abrasive pads: Even on heavily contaminated wheels, never use steel wool. The iron particles from the steel wool will embed in the wheel surface and cause rust spots. Use chemical removers (IronX) instead of mechanical abrasion.

Budget vs. Premium: What Should You Spend?

Here's a realistic breakdown of what a complete wheel care kit costs:

Kit LevelProductsTotal Cost
BudgetAdam's Wheel Cleaner + P&S Brake Buster (gallon) + foam applicators + basic brush set$55–$75
EnthusiastSonax Full Effect + CarPro IronX + CarPro PERL + EZ Detail brush + Wheel Woolies$120–$160
ProfessionalSonax Full Effect + IronX + AMMO Mud Tire Gel + Gyeon Q² Tire + complete brush set + foam pads$200–$280

For a car with wheels worth $5,000–$15,000 per set, spending $150 on proper cleaning products is the most cost-effective maintenance you can do. One set of replacement Porsche GT3 center-lock wheels runs $8,000+. A bottle of pH-balanced wheel cleaner costs $20. The math is obvious.

The Bottom Line

Miami's combination of brake dust, salt air, road construction debris, and relentless UV makes wheel care both more important and more challenging than anywhere else in the country. The Sonax Full Effect is our top wheel cleaner pick for its effectiveness-to-safety ratio — it handles weekly maintenance washes perfectly while being gentle on every wheel finish. Pair it with monthly CarPro IronX decontamination and a quality tire dressing like AMMO Mud or CarPro PERL, and your wheels will look showroom-fresh year-round.

The real secret? Consistency beats intensity. A five-minute wheel clean every week with the right products prevents the kind of baked-on contamination that requires aggressive chemicals or professional intervention. Your exotic car deserves that five minutes. Your $8,000 wheels definitely do.

The Ghost sits below the Phantom in the Rolls-Royce lineup, but "below" is relative — this is still a 00,000+ car when new. Here's what the current Miami market looks like:

ModelYear RangeApprox. Price (Miami)Key Features
Ghost Series II (new)2024–202640,000 – 50,000+Current gen, Planar suspension, 6.75L twin-turbo V12
Ghost Series II (pre-owned)2021–202325,000 – 20,000Same generation, meaningful depreciation savings
Ghost Extended2021–202680,000 – 00,000+Long wheelbase, rear-seat focus, lounge seating
Ghost Black Badge2022–202600,000 – 20,000Dark chrome, 591 HP, sport-tuned suspension
Ghost Series I (prev gen)2010–20205,000 – 90,000Previous design, exceptional value, still a Rolls

The best value in Miami right now is a 2021–2022 Ghost Series II with under 15,000 miles. These cars originally stickered at 40,000–00,000 and can be found for 30,000–80,000. That's nearly 00,000 in savings on a car that still looks and drives like new. The Series II's "Planar" suspension system — Rolls-Royce's most advanced ever — gives it a ride quality that makes the previous generation feel like a decade older than it is.

Rolls-Royce Ghost Models: Which One to Buy in Miami

Standard Ghost vs. Ghost Extended

The standard Ghost is 5,546mm long — already enormous by any measure. The Extended adds 170mm of rear legroom, creating a limousine-like rear compartment with available rear lounge seating, a champagne fridge, and massage seats. If you're doing your own driving (and most Ghost buyers in Miami are), the standard car is the better choice. It's more nimble in South Beach parking garages and the back seat is already vast.

Ghost Black Badge: Miami's Favorite

Let's be honest — in Miami, the Ghost Black Badge is the one everyone wants. The darkened Spirit of Ecstasy, dark chrome accents, and 591-HP output give the Ghost a menacing presence that fits right in on the streets of Brickell and Wynwood. The Black Badge outsells the standard Ghost in South Florida by a significant margin, which means more inventory available — but also higher demand and less negotiating room.

Series I vs. Series II: Is the Older Ghost Worth It?

Absolutely — with caveats. The Series I Ghost (2010–2020) is a genuine bargain, with low-mileage examples available for under 20,000. That's Rolls-Royce entry for the price of a well-equipped BMW 7 Series. But be aware of a few things:

  • The Series I shared its platform with the BMW 7 Series (F01), and it shows in the infotainment system and some interior details
  • Maintenance costs are the same regardless of what you paid — budget ,000–,000/year
  • The facelift models (2015–2020) addressed many early issues and are the better buy
  • The Series II is a clean-sheet design and feels dramatically more modern

Where to Buy a Rolls-Royce Ghost in Miami

Braman Rolls-Royce Motor Cars

Braman in West Palm Beach is South Florida's authorized Rolls-Royce dealer. They typically stock 4–8 Ghost variants at any time, including new, Certified Pre-Owned, and consignment vehicles. The CPO program is worth considering — it includes a comprehensive inspection and extended warranty that can save you five figures on unexpected repairs.

Why buy here: Factory warranty, Bespoke ordering for new builds, CPO program, and a dedicated Rolls-Royce service department that actually knows these cars.

The Collection — Coral Gables

The Collection is one of Miami's most established luxury dealers and regularly stocks pre-owned Rolls-Royce models, including the Ghost. They handle everything from financing to delivery and often have competitive pricing on slightly older models. Their Coral Gables location is a one-stop shop for ultra-luxury, with Porsche, McLaren, and Aston Martin under the same roof.

Miami Motorcar Collection — Hialeah

An independent specialist that consistently has 5–10 Rolls-Royces in stock. They tend to price aggressively compared to franchise dealers and are a good option for buyers who know what they want and don't need the hand-holding of an authorized dealership. Always get a pre-purchase inspection on any independent dealer car.

Private Sales & Consignment

Bring a Trailer, Cars & Bids, and Hemmings regularly list Rolls-Royce Ghosts, particularly Series I models. Private sales can offer the best prices, but you'll need to arrange your own pre-purchase inspection (PPI) and there's no dealer warranty. Budget 00–,000 for a thorough PPI from a Rolls-Royce specialist.

Rolls-Royce Ghost Running Costs in Miami

Owning a Rolls-Royce in Miami isn't just about the purchase price. Here's what to budget annually:

Cost CategoryAnnual EstimateNotes
Insurance,000 – ,000Varies with driver history, garage, and coverage level
Maintenance,000 – ,000Annual service, brake fluid, filters, minor items
Tires,000 – ,500Specialty run-flats, replaced every 15,000–25,000 miles
Fuel,000 – ,000Premium required; 12–14 MPG combined in Miami driving
Detailing,200 – ,000Monthly professional detail recommended for Miami conditions

Total annual running cost: roughly 3,000–6,000 beyond the purchase price. That's less than a Ferrari or Lamborghini, but significantly more than a Mercedes S-Class. The Ghost's air suspension and complex electronics are the biggest wildcard — when something goes wrong, repairs can be expensive.

Rolls-Royce Ghost vs. Phantom: Which Rolls Should Miami Buyers Choose?

This is the question every Rolls-Royce shopper in Miami faces. Here's the honest breakdown:

FactorGhostPhantom
Price (new)40,000+60,000+
Best forOwner-driversBeing chauffeured
Driving feelMore connected, sportierMaximum isolation
SizeLarge but manageableEnormous — parking is a challenge
Miami vibeModern wealth, tech moneyOld money, maximum presence
DepreciationSteeper (more volume)Holds better (lower production)

For most Miami buyers who drive themselves and want a daily-usable Rolls-Royce, the Ghost is the better choice. It's easier to park in Brickell, more engaging to drive on A1A, and the Black Badge version has enough presence to hold its own against anything in a South Beach valet line.

Pre-Purchase Inspection Checklist for the Rolls-Royce Ghost

Whether you're buying from a dealer or private seller, here's what to check:

  • Air suspension: Listen for compressor cycling; test all ride height modes. Replacement struts are ,000–,000 each
  • Starlight headliner: Check that all fiber optic lights are working. Repairs require headliner removal (,000+)
  • Spirit of Ecstasy mechanism: Verify it raises and retracts smoothly. The retractable mechanism can fail
  • Infotainment system: Series I cars with iDrive can have screen failures. Series II uses a much more reliable system
  • Leather and wood: Check for warping, cracking, or discoloration — especially on Series I cars exposed to Miami sun without tint
  • Service history: Full Rolls-Royce service history is non-negotiable. Walk away from cars with gaps
  • Tire date codes: Rolls-Royce run-flat tires are expensive and should be replaced every 4–5 years regardless of tread depth

Financing a Rolls-Royce Ghost in Miami

Most Ghost buyers in Miami finance or lease rather than paying cash — even those who could write a check. Here's why:

  • Lease: New Ghost leases typically run ,800–,500/month with 5,000–5,000 down. The Black Badge and Extended command higher payments. Leasing makes sense if you plan to trade every 3 years
  • Finance: Rates for qualified buyers range from 5.9%–7.9% for 60–72 months. On a 50,000 pre-owned Ghost, expect payments around ,200–,800/month
  • Cash: No discount for paying cash at Rolls-Royce dealers (they earn backend on financing). Save your cash for investments and finance at a competitive rate

Bottom Line: Should You Buy a Rolls-Royce Ghost in Miami?

The Ghost is the most livable Rolls-Royce ever made, and Miami is arguably the best city in America to own one. The combination of year-round warm weather (no road salt), a culture that appreciates visible success, and a dense network of luxury dealers and specialists makes South Florida ideal for Rolls-Royce ownership.

If you're cross-shopping with a Mercedes-Maybach S-Class, Bentley Flying Spur, or even a high-spec BMW 7 Series — the Ghost occupies a tier above all of them. Nothing else combines this level of craftsmanship, presence, and engineering in a single sedan. And with pre-owned Series II models now available under 50,000, entry to the Rolls-Royce club has never been more accessible.

Start your search at Braman Rolls-Royce, check the pre-owned inventory at The Collection, and browse online auction sites for the best deals on Series I cars. Whatever you choose, budget for a proper PPI, factor in the running costs, and enjoy what is genuinely one of the finest automobiles money can buy.

title: Aston Martin DBX for Sale in Miami: 2026 Pricing, Models & Buyer's Guide
excerpt: The Aston Martin DBX and DBX707 are the luxury SUVs for buyers who find a Lamborghini Urus too loud and a Bentley Bentayga too subtle. Here's what the DBX costs in Miami, which version to buy, and where to find one.
content:
The Aston Martin DBX is the car that saved Aston Martin — and the one that might be the most underrated luxury SUV on the market. While the Lamborghini Urus grabs headlines and the Bentley Bentayga dominates country club parking lots, the DBX quietly delivers something neither can match: genuine Aston Martin driving dynamics in a package that actually works as a daily driver in Miami.

If you're looking for an Aston Martin DBX for sale in Miami, the timing is excellent. Depreciation on early models has been significant, the upgraded DBX707 is now well-established, and South Florida's dealer network means you won't have to look far. Here's everything you need to know.

Aston Martin DBX for Sale: 2026 Pricing in Miami

The DBX launched in 2020 as Aston Martin's first-ever SUV, and the DBX707 — the performance variant — followed in 2022 with a twin-turbo V8 making 697 HP. Here's what the Miami market looks like:

ModelYear RangeApprox. Price (Miami)Key Specs
DBX707 (new)2024–202639,000 – 10,000+697 HP, 4.0L twin-turbo V8, 0-60 in 3.1s
DBX707 (pre-owned)2022–202365,000 – 15,000Same powertrain, significant savings
DBX (standard, new)2024–202698,000 – 60,000+542 HP, refined ride, more comfort-focused
DBX (standard, pre-owned)2021–202305,000 – 55,000First-gen, heavy depreciation = great deals
DBX Straight-Six (2026)202607,000 – 70,000New 3.0L mild-hybrid inline-6, updated interior

The standout value right now is a 2022–2023 DBX707 under 00,000. These cars were 40,000+ new and the DBX707 is meaningfully better than the standard DBX in every way — more power, better brakes, tighter handling, improved transmission calibration. It's one of those rare cases where the performance model is also the better daily driver.

Aston Martin DBX vs. DBX707: Which One for Miami?

Standard DBX (542 HP)

The base DBX uses a Mercedes-AMG-sourced 4.0-liter twin-turbo V8 making 542 HP and 516 lb-ft of torque. Paired with a 9-speed automatic and all-wheel drive, it's quick (0–60 in 4.3 seconds) and composed. The ride quality is excellent — arguably the most comfortable in the luxury SUV segment — and the interior has a warmth and intimacy that the Urus completely lacks.

The downside: the standard DBX's transmission can feel indecisive, the brakes are adequate but not inspiring, and 542 HP feels merely fast in a segment where 600+ is becoming the baseline.

DBX707 (697 HP)

The DBX707 is what the DBX should have been from day one. Aston Martin bumped the V8 to 697 HP and 663 lb-ft, swapped in a wet-clutch 9-speed transmission (instead of the torque converter), added carbon-ceramic brakes as standard, stiffened the suspension, and recalibrated everything. The result is a 5,400-pound SUV that hits 60 mph in 3.1 seconds and handles like it weighs 1,000 pounds less.

For Miami buyers: the DBX707 is the one to get. The performance upgrade makes it competitive with the Urus Performante and Cayenne Turbo GT, and the Aston Martin badge carries a different kind of weight in South Beach — British elegance vs. Italian aggression.

Where to Buy an Aston Martin DBX in Miami

Aston Martin of Miami (The Collection)

The Collection in Coral Gables is Miami's authorized Aston Martin dealer and the first place to check. They typically stock 3–5 DBX and DBX707 models, both new and pre-owned, along with the full Aston Martin lineup. As an authorized dealer, they can order custom builds through Aston Martin's Q by Aston Martin personalization program.

Why buy here: Factory warranty, Q customization, Aston Martin Timeless (CPO) program, and Miami's only authorized service center for Aston Martin.

Prestige Imports — North Miami

Prestige Imports on Biscayne Boulevard regularly carries pre-owned Aston Martins alongside their Lamborghini franchise. They often price slightly below The Collection on comparable pre-owned models and are worth checking for DBX inventory.

Exotic Car Trader & iLusso

Miami's independent exotic dealers, including Exotic Car Trader in Fort Lauderdale and iLusso in Costa Mesa (they ship to Miami frequently), often have DBX inventory at competitive prices. Independent dealers can be a good option for buyers who know exactly what they want and prioritize price over the dealership experience.

Online Marketplaces

The DBX shows up regularly on Bring a Trailer, Cars & Bids, and AutoTrader. Early standard DBX models (2021–2022) are some of the most affordable exotic SUVs on the market right now, with clean examples trading under 15,000. Always get a pre-purchase inspection — budget 00–00 for a specialist to check the car before you commit.

Aston Martin DBX Running Costs in Miami

Here's what to budget beyond the purchase price:

Cost CategoryAnnual EstimateNotes
Insurance,500 – ,500Lower than Urus; depends on driver profile and coverage
Maintenance,500 – ,000AMG-sourced V8 is relatively reliable; annual service required
Tires,800 – ,00022-inch tires standard on 707; 23-inch optional
Fuel,500 – ,500Premium required; 14–16 MPG combined in Miami
Carbon-ceramic brake servicesh – 00/yearLong-lasting but expensive when replacement is needed (,000–5,000)

Total annual cost: approximately 1,000–1,000. The DBX is actually one of the more affordable exotic SUVs to maintain, primarily because the Mercedes-AMG V8 is a proven, reliable engine. The Aston Martin-specific electronics and trim pieces are where costs can escalate if something goes wrong outside of warranty.

Aston Martin DBX vs. the Competition in Miami

Every DBX buyer in Miami is cross-shopping these alternatives:

ModelStarting Price (New)HP0-60 MPHMiami Vibe
Aston Martin DBX70739,0006973.1sUnderstated power, British elegance
Lamborghini Urus Performante60,0006573.3sMaximum attention, aggressive styling
Porsche Cayenne Turbo GT95,0006313.1sTrack weapon disguised as an SUV
Bentley Bentayga Speed46,0006263.5sTraditional luxury, W12 refinement
Ferrari Purosangue00,000+7153.3sThe ultimate status play (if you can get one)

The DBX707 occupies a unique position: it's faster than the Bentley, more refined than the Urus, and more exclusive than the Porsche. In Miami, where the Urus is as common as a Honda Civic in some neighborhoods, the Aston Martin's relative rarity is a genuine selling point. You'll turn heads without screaming for attention.

Pre-Purchase Inspection Checklist for the Aston Martin DBX

Whether buying new or pre-owned, here's what to look for:

  • Transmission behavior (standard DBX): The torque-converter 9-speed in the base DBX can develop shuddering issues. Test at low speeds and during parking maneuvers. The DBX707's wet-clutch unit is significantly better
  • Infotainment system: The early DBX uses a Mercedes-derived system that can have software glitches. Ensure the latest firmware is installed and all functions work
  • Air suspension: Check for any warning lights or uneven ride height. Replacement air struts are ,500–,000 per corner
  • Paint quality: Early DBX models had some reports of thin paint in certain areas. Inspect under strong lighting for chips or touch-ups
  • Panoramic roof: If equipped, check for any rattles or seal issues. Miami's humidity can exacerbate seal degradation
  • Service history: Verify all services were performed at an authorized Aston Martin dealer. Out-of-network service can void remaining warranty
  • Carbon-ceramic brakes (DBX707): Inspect disc surfaces for cracking or glazing. Replacements are 2,000+ for a full set

Financing and Leasing a DBX in Miami

The DBX is one of the more accessible entry points into exotic SUV ownership, especially pre-owned:

  • Lease (new): DBX707 leases typically run ,800–,800/month with 0,000–0,000 down. Residual values are improving as the model matures
  • Finance (pre-owned): A 50,000 pre-owned DBX707 at 6.5% over 60 months runs approximately ,930/month. Several Miami credit unions offer competitive exotic car rates
  • Cash: On pre-owned models from independent dealers, cash can sometimes get you 2–5% off the listed price. Authorized dealers rarely discount for cash

Bottom Line: Is the Aston Martin DBX Right for Miami?

If you want a luxury SUV that drives better than a Bentley, looks more sophisticated than a Lamborghini, and won't be the third Urus in every restaurant valet line — the Aston Martin DBX is your car. The DBX707, specifically, is one of the best performance SUVs ever made, and pre-owned pricing has brought it into genuinely accessible territory.

Miami is an ideal city for the DBX. The SUV body style handles Florida's unpredictable rainstorms, the V8 sounds phenomenal on the MacArthur Causeway, and the Aston Martin badge carries a level of sophistication that resonates in a city that already has plenty of everything else. Start at The Collection in Coral Gables for new and CPO models, check Prestige Imports for competitive pre-owned pricing, and keep an eye on Bring a Trailer for the best deals on early standard DBX models.

title: McLaren Elva: Specs, Price & What Miami Buyers Need to Know in 2026
excerpt: The McLaren Elva is the most extreme open-top McLaren ever built — no windshield, no roof, just 804 horsepower and the Miami sky above you. Here's everything about the Elva's specs, pricing, production numbers, and where to find one.
content:
The McLaren Elva is the kind of car that makes people question whether McLaren's engineering team has lost its mind — in the best possible way. No windshield. No roof. No side windows. Just an 804-horsepower twin-turbo V8 sitting behind your head and an active air management system that supposedly deflects wind over the cockpit at triple-digit speeds. Only 149 were ever built (down from the originally planned 399), making the McLaren Elva one of the rarest modern McLaren models and a genuine collector's item in 2026.

For Miami buyers, the McLaren Elva represents something special: a car purpose-built for the kind of open-air, warm-weather driving that South Florida delivers year-round. But finding one is a challenge, and understanding what you're getting into — mechanically, financially, and practically — matters before you write a seven-figure check.

McLaren Elva Specs: What Makes It So Special

The McLaren Elva sits in McLaren's Ultimate Series — the same tier as the P1, Senna, and Speedtail. It's not a modified 720S or a GT with the roof removed. It's a ground-up design built on a carbon fiber monocoque chassis unique to the Elva.

SpecificationMcLaren Elva
Engine4.0L twin-turbo V8 (M840TR)
Horsepower804 hp @ 7,500 rpm
Torque590 lb-ft @ 5,500 rpm
Transmission7-speed SSG dual-clutch
0-60 mph2.8 seconds
0-124 mph6.7 seconds
Top Speed203 mph
Curb Weight2,641 lbs (dry)
DrivetrainRear-wheel drive
Body StyleOpen cockpit (no windshield standard; optional windshield available)
Production149 units worldwide
MSRP (new)$1.69 million

The Active Air Management System (AAMS) — McLaren Elva's Party Trick

Here's what makes the McLaren Elva more than just a roofless supercar: the Active Air Management System. A large intake ahead of the cockpit channels air through a duct and fires it out at high velocity over the cabin. The result is a virtual "bubble" of still air around the occupants, meaning you can theoretically drive at serious speed without being battered by wind.

Does it work? In practice, it works well enough at moderate speeds — below 100 mph, most owners report it's genuinely comfortable. Above that, helmets are recommended (and legally required in many jurisdictions anyway for cars without windshields). Some Elvas were optioned with an aftermarket windshield that McLaren offered as an accessory, which dramatically improves daily usability at the expense of the car's pure, unfiltered character.

McLaren Elva Price: What They're Worth in 2026

The McLaren Elva had an MSRP of $1.69 million when new. As of 2026, the secondary market tells a more nuanced story. Early cars that sold at slight premiums during the initial hype period have settled, while extremely low-mileage or unique-spec examples have held firm.

Condition / SpecEstimated 2026 Market Value
Standard Elva, under 1,000 miles$1.5M – $1.8M
MSO-spec / unique livery, under 500 miles$1.8M – $2.3M
Windshield-equipped variant$1.4M – $1.7M
Higher mileage (2,000+ miles)$1.2M – $1.5M

The limited production of 149 units is the Elva's strongest value proposition. For comparison, McLaren built 500 Sennas and 106 Speedtails. The Elva's uniqueness as an open-cockpit Ultimate Series car gives it a distinct place in any collection, which should support long-term value appreciation.

McLaren Elva vs. Other Open-Top Hypercars

The Elva doesn't exist in a vacuum. If you're shopping at this price point, you're likely also considering other extreme open-top machines:

ModelPowerWeight0-60ProductionApprox. Price (2026)
McLaren Elva804 hp2,641 lbs2.8s149$1.5M–$2.3M
Ferrari Monza SP2799 hp3,306 lbs2.9s499$2.5M–$4M
Aston Martin V12 Speedster690 hp3,858 lbs3.4s88$800K–$1.1M
Lamborghini SC20770 hp~3,300 lbs~2.9s1N/A (one-off)

The McLaren Elva is the lightest of the bunch by a significant margin and arguably the most extreme in concept. The Ferrari Monza SP2 commands higher prices due to Ferrari's brand premium and slightly larger production run (more collector interest at that number), while the Aston Martin V12 Speedster offers a more "usable" experience at a lower entry point.

Owning a McLaren Elva in Miami: What to Know

Miami is one of the best cities in the world for an open-cockpit car. Year-round warm weather, dramatic coastal roads, and a car culture that appreciates extreme machinery all work in the Elva's favor. But there are practical considerations:

  • Rain: Miami's afternoon thunderstorms are legendary. The Elva has zero weather protection. You either need a garage nearby at all times, obsessively check weather radar, or accept that your $1.5M car might get wet. Most owners garage-queen them, which somewhat defeats the purpose.
  • Sun exposure: The interior materials bake in direct sunlight. A high-quality car cover and climate-controlled garage are non-negotiable.
  • Registration: Florida doesn't require windshields, but you'll need eye protection (sunglasses or goggles) at minimum. The windshield-delete Elva is road-legal in Florida.
  • Insurance: Expect $15,000–$25,000 annually through a specialty insurer like Hagerty or Chubb. Standard carriers won't touch it.
  • Maintenance: McLaren Miami (The Collection) is the closest authorized service center. Annual service runs $3,000–$5,000 depending on what's needed.

Where to Find a McLaren Elva for Sale in 2026

With only 149 built, McLaren Elvas don't appear on the open market frequently. Here's where to look:

  • McLaren Qualified Pre-Owned: McLaren's certified program occasionally lists Ultimate Series cars. Check McLaren Qualified directly.
  • The Collection Miami: South Florida's authorized McLaren dealer. They handle consignments of high-value McLarens and may have access to Elvas through their collector network.
  • DuPont Registry: The go-to marketplace for seven-figure exotics. Elvas appear here periodically.
  • Bring a Trailer: Several Elvas have crossed the BaT block, typically achieving strong results with full provenance.
  • Private brokers: At this price point, many transactions happen through established exotic car brokers who connect sellers and buyers privately. Curated, Miller Motorcars, and Manhattan Motorcars are known to handle McLaren Ultimate Series cars.

Should You Buy a McLaren Elva as an Investment?

The McLaren Elva has genuine investment potential for a few reasons:

  • Limited production: 149 units is tiny, even by hypercar standards.
  • Unique concept: There's nothing else quite like it in McLaren's lineup or the broader market.
  • Ultimate Series pedigree: The P1 has appreciated significantly; the Senna has held strong. McLaren's top-tier models have a track record.

The counterargument: McLaren's brand doesn't carry the same weight as Ferrari in the collector market. The Elva's extreme nature (no windshield) limits the buyer pool. And McLaren's corporate financial history has been rocky, which creates uncertainty around long-term brand prestige.

Our take: buy it if you'll drive it and enjoy it. If it appreciates, great. If it doesn't, you still own one of the wildest road cars ever built. In Miami, that counts for something.

McLaren Elva: The Bottom Line

The McLaren Elva is a 804-horsepower, windshield-free, 149-unit fever dream that McLaren somehow made road-legal. It's not practical. It's not comfortable in the traditional sense. And in Miami — where afternoon rain can go from zero to monsoon in eight minutes — it requires a level of commitment that most car owners aren't prepared for.

But if you're the kind of buyer who wants the most extreme, most exclusive, most visceral open-top driving experience money can buy, the McLaren Elva delivers in a way that nothing else on the market can match. At $1.5M–$2.3M in 2026, it's positioned below the Ferrari Monza SP2 and above the Aston Martin V12 Speedster — and it's arguably more thrilling than both.

title: Audi R8 for Sale in Miami: 2026 Pricing, Models & Buyer's Guide
excerpt: The Audi R8 is one of the best mid-engine supercars ever built — and now that production has ended, prices are shifting. Here's what every model costs in Miami, which version to buy, and where to find the best deals in 2026.
content:
The Audi R8 is dead — long live the Audi R8. Production of Audi's mid-engine V10 supercar officially ended in 2023, and there's no direct replacement coming (the electric e-tron GT is great, but it's a completely different animal). That means every Audi R8 for sale in Miami right now is a used car, and the market is at an interesting inflection point in 2026. First-gen models have bottomed out and started climbing. Second-gen V10 Performance models are holding firm. And the final editions are already trading at premiums.

If you've been thinking about an Audi R8, this is the guide. We'll break down every generation, what each one costs in Miami, the common issues to watch for, and exactly where to find the best examples in South Florida.
