The Audi R8 spanned two generations over 17 years. Here's what you need to know about each:

Audi R8 for Sale in Miami: Which Model Should You Buy?

It depends on what you want:

  • Best daily driver: 2020–2023 R8 V10 Performance Spyder. The second-gen R8 is shockingly easy to live with — Audi's Virtual Cockpit, magnetic ride, a decent trunk, and a naturally aspirated V10 that revs to 8,700 rpm. The Spyder is the move for Miami. You'll use the top-down capability 300+ days per year.
  • Best value: 2016–2019 R8 V10 (base). You get 90% of the Performance's experience for $30K–$40K less. The base V10 still makes 540+ horsepower and sounds identical.
  • Best investment: First-gen R8 V10 with the gated manual. These are appreciating. Clean, low-mileage examples with the 6-speed will be $200K+ within five years. The manual take rate was low, making survivors rare.
  • Best collector piece: 2023 R8 GT. Only 333 built. Rear-wheel drive. The last naturally aspirated V10 Audi will ever make. Keep it under 1,000 miles and it'll be worth significantly more in a decade.
  • Budget entry: First-gen V8 with the R tronic. Starting around $55K, it's the cheapest way into R8 ownership. The R tronic transmission is jerky at low speeds, but the V8 is reliable and maintenance costs are lower than the V10.

Common Audi R8 Issues to Watch For

The R8 is one of the more reliable supercars on the market, but it's not without quirks. Here's what to inspect before buying:

First Generation (2008–2015)

  • R tronic transmission failures: The single-clutch automated manual is the R8's Achilles heel. Clutch packs wear, the hydraulic pump fails, and repairs run $5,000–$10,000. This is why manual cars command a premium.
  • Magnetic ride damper leaks: Common on higher-mileage examples. Replacement is $1,500–$2,500 per corner.
  • Carbon sigma engine (V10): The carbon-fiber intake manifold can develop cracks on earlier models. Listen for unusual intake sounds.
  • Front lift system: The nose-lift actuators can fail. Test it during inspection — you'll need it in Miami with all the parking garage ramps and driveway transitions.

Second Generation (2016–2023)

  • S tronic transmission: Far more reliable than the R tronic, but the mechatronic unit can fail on higher-mileage examples. Budget $4,000–$6,000 if it happens.
  • Carbon ceramic brake warping: If equipped with CCBs, check for pulsation. Replacement rotors are $3,000–$5,000 each.
  • Infotainment glitches: The Virtual Cockpit can develop pixel issues or lag. Software updates usually resolve it.
  • Rear diffuser damage: Miami speed bumps and the R8's low rear end are mortal enemies. Check for scraping or cracks.

Audi R8 Maintenance Costs in Miami

One of the R8's biggest advantages over Italian and British competitors: it's built on Audi's platform and shares components with the Lamborghini Huracán, meaning parts availability is strong and independent shops can work on them.

ServiceEstimated Cost (Miami)
Annual service (oil, filters, inspection)$800 – $1,500
Brake pads (iron rotors)$1,200 – $2,000
Brake pads (carbon ceramic)$2,500 – $4,000
Tire replacement (set of 4)$1,200 – $2,000
Clutch replacement (R tronic, Gen 1)$5,000 – $8,000
Major service (every 4 years / 40K)$2,500 – $4,000
Insurance (annual, clean record)$3,000 – $6,000

Compare that to a Ferrari 488 ($5,000+ annual service) or a McLaren 720S ($4,000+ annual service with potentially expensive surprises), and the R8 looks like a bargain. Several excellent independent Audi/VW specialists in Miami handle R8 work at 30–50% below dealer rates.

Where to Find an Audi R8 for Sale in Miami

Miami has one of the strongest Audi R8 markets in the country. Here's where to look:

  • Audi Coral Springs & Audi North Miami Beach: Authorized Audi dealers that regularly stock certified pre-owned R8s with warranty coverage.
  • The Collection: Coral Gables' mega-luxury dealer often has late-model R8 Performance models on consignment alongside their Ferraris and Porsches.
  • Prestige Imports (North Miami Beach): As a Lamborghini dealer, they frequently take R8s in trade (the Huracán buyer pipeline is natural R8 territory).
  • Exotic Car Trader & DuPont Registry: For higher-end examples like the R8 GT and 2023 final edition.
  • Bring a Trailer & Cars and Bids: Online auctions have become the go-to for first-gen manual R8s. Prices are transparent and provenance is well-documented.
  • AutoTrader & CarGurus: The best filters for finding specific year/mileage/color combinations within a Miami radius.

Audi R8 vs. the Competition in Miami

At the R8's price points, here's what you're cross-shopping:

ModelPower0-60Miami Price Range (2026)Key Advantage
Audi R8 V10 Performance602 hp3.1s$140K–$210KNA V10, Audi reliability, daily drivable
Porsche 911 Turbo S (992)640 hp2.6s$200K–$260KFaster, AWD, more practical
Lamborghini Huracán EVO631 hp2.9s$210K–$280KSame V10, more dramatic styling
McLaren 720S710 hp2.7s$175K–$230KMore power, lighter, exotic factor
Ferrari F8 Tributo710 hp2.9s$250K–$300KFerrari badge, twin-turbo V8

The R8's sweet spot is the buyer who wants supercar performance with luxury-car livability. It has the best interior in this group (it's still an Audi inside), the lowest running costs, and arguably the best naturally aspirated engine sound. What it gives up is outright performance to the 911 Turbo S and McLaren 720S, and brand cachet to Ferrari and Lamborghini.

Why the Audi R8 Is Perfect for Miami

A few Miami-specific reasons the R8 makes sense here:

  • The Spyder is the way to go: With 300+ days of sunshine, you'll drive top-down constantly. The R8 Spyder's folding soft top is quick, quiet, and doesn't compromise trunk space.
  • Understated enough for daily use: The R8 attracts attention without being obnoxious. You can park it at Brickell City Centre or drive to a business meeting without feeling like you're trying too hard.
  • AWD handles Florida rain: Miami's sudden downpours are no joke. The R8's quattro all-wheel drive gives you confidence that a rear-drive Ferrari or Lamborghini can't match in a surprise storm.
  • Independent shop support: Miami's large German car community means plenty of qualified independent shops for routine maintenance.
  • Salt air durability: Audi's aluminum and composite construction handles coastal environments better than some competitors' steel-heavy builds.

The Bottom Line on Buying an Audi R8 in Miami

The Audi R8 is the thinking person's supercar. It has a naturally aspirated V10 that revs to the heavens and sounds like the end of the world, all wrapped in a package you can drive to Publix on a Tuesday without drama. Now that production has ended, every R8 is a piece of automotive history — the last mid-engine Audi, and the last naturally aspirated V10 supercar from any mainstream manufacturer.

In Miami's market, you're looking at $55,000 for a first-gen V8 entry point all the way up to $350,000+ for a 2023 GT final edition. The sweet spot for most buyers is a 2020–2023 V10 Performance Spyder in the $180K–$230K range: low miles, modern tech, open-top Miami driving, and a powertrain that will never be replicated.

Whatever you choose, buy the best example you can afford, get a pre-purchase inspection from an Audi specialist, and enjoy one of the great modern supercars while the world goes electric around it.

title: Best Portable Car Canopies & Pop-Up Garages for Exotic Cars in Miami (2026)
excerpt: No garage? No problem. The best portable car canopies and pop-up shelters protect your exotic from Miami's brutal sun, afternoon monsoons, and hurricane-season debris — without a permanent structure.
content:
Here's the reality of owning an exotic car in Miami: not everyone has a garage. Between condo living, shared parking structures with zero shade, and South Florida's complete lack of covered outdoor parking, your $200K+ investment spends a lot of time baking under a sun that regularly pushes interior temps past 170°F.

A premium car cover helps, but it doesn't stop heat buildup, rain pooling, or the flying debris that rolls through every hurricane season. What you actually need is a portable car canopy or pop-up garage — a freestanding shelter that blocks UV, rain, and wind without requiring a permit or permanent installation.

We tested and researched the best options for Miami exotic car owners in 2026. Here's what's worth your money.

Why Miami Exotic Owners Need a Portable Shelter

Before we get into specific products, let's talk about what Miami's environment actually does to an unprotected car:

ThreatDamageTimelineRepair Cost
UV radiation (305 days/year)Clear coat failure, paint fade, interior cracking12–24 months$3,000–$15,000 (full paint correction + ceramic)
Afternoon rain + sun cycleWater spots etched into clear coatWeeks$500–$2,000 (compound + polish)
Salt air (within 5 miles of coast)Chrome pitting, rubber degradation, undercarriage corrosion6–18 months$1,000–$5,000+
Hurricane debrisDents, scratches, broken glassInstant$2,000–$20,000+
Bird droppings + tree sapPermanent paint etching if not removed within hoursHours$300–$1,500 per panel

A good portable canopy eliminates or dramatically reduces all five of these. At $200–$800 for a quality unit, it's one of the cheapest forms of paint insurance you can buy.

What to Look For in a Portable Car Canopy

  • UV protection rating: Look for UPF 50+ or 99%+ UV blockage. Cheap tarps block rain but not UV — useless in Miami.
  • Wind rating: Miami gets 40+ mph gusts regularly during summer storms. You need a frame rated for at least 35 mph sustained, ideally with ground anchors.
  • Size: Exotic cars are wider than you think. A Lamborghini Urus is 78.7" wide with mirrors. Budget for at least 12' × 20' for comfortable clearance.
  • Ventilation: Enclosed shelters need airflow or they become greenhouses. Look for vented panels or roll-up sides.
  • Portability: If you're in a condo with HOA restrictions, you may need something that goes up and comes down quickly.
  • Material quality: Polyethylene covers last 2–3 years in Miami sun. Polyester with UV coating lasts 5–7 years. Canvas-grade materials last 10+.

Our Top Picks

🏆 Best Overall: ShelterLogic AutoShelter 10×20

The ShelterLogic AutoShelter is the gold standard for portable car shelters, and for good reason. The 10×20 footprint fits everything from a Porsche 911 to a full-size Urus with room to open doors. The triple-layer ripstop polyethylene cover blocks 99.5% of UV and is waterproof with heat-welded seams.

SpecDetails
Dimensions10' W × 20' L × 8' H
Frame1-3/8" steel with DuPont thermoset powder coat
CoverTriple-layer ripstop polyethylene, UV-treated
Wind RatingRated for 35 mph (with anchors)
Weight~95 lbs
Setup Time~2 hours (2 people)

Why we like it for Miami: The round-top design sheds rain effectively (no pooling), the steel frame handles our gusty summer storms, and the cover material is specifically treated for UV resistance. We've seen these last 3+ years in full South Florida sun before needing a replacement cover.

→ Check price on Amazon

🥈 Best Premium: Ikuby All-Weather Car Shelter

If you want something that looks less like a construction site and more like an actual garage, the Ikuby is the answer. This semi-rigid, foldable car shelter uses a patented accordion-style frame that opens and closes in under 60 seconds — no tools, no assembly. It's essentially a retractable garage.

SpecDetails
DimensionsAvailable in Medium (sedan) and Large (SUV/truck)
FrameGalvanized steel accordion mechanism
Cover600D Oxford fabric, waterproof + UV-treated
Wind Rating40+ mph (with ground stakes)
Setup Time~60 seconds (1 person)

Why we like it for Miami: The 60-second deploy time means you can actually use this before a surprise afternoon downpour. The 600D Oxford fabric is significantly more durable than the polyethylene covers on cheaper units. It's also HOA-friendlier than a permanent carport because you can collapse it when not in use.

→ Check price on Amazon

🥉 Best Budget: Abba Patio 10×20 Heavy Duty Carport

At roughly half the price of the ShelterLogic, the Abba Patio carport delivers solid protection for the money. The 10×20 canopy-style design is open-sided, which means better ventilation (less greenhouse effect) but less protection from driving rain.

SpecDetails
Dimensions10' W × 20' L × 9.5' H (peak)
FrameHeavy-duty steel with powder coating
CoverPolyethylene with UV treatment
Wind Rating~25 mph (with anchors)
Setup Time~1.5 hours (2 people)

Why we like it for Miami: If your primary concern is UV and you park in a somewhat sheltered area (between buildings, behind a fence), this covers the basics at a price that makes it a no-brainer. The open sides also mean no moisture trapping — important in Miami's 80%+ humidity.

→ Check price on Amazon

Best for Hurricane Prep: ShelterLogic ShelterTube 12×26

When hurricane season rolls around (June through November), you need something more serious than a canopy. The ShelterTube is essentially a portable garage with a full enclosure, reinforced frame, and wind bracing designed for storm conditions.

SpecDetails
Dimensions12' W × 26' L × 8' H
Frame1-5/8" steel with ShelterLock stabilizers
CoverUltra-duty polyethylene, rip-stop, waterproof
Wind Rating50+ mph (fully anchored)
IncludesGround auger anchors, front and rear panels

Why we like it for Miami: This is the shelter you set up in May and keep up through November. The 12×26 footprint handles even wide-body exotics with room to spare, and the fully enclosed design stops wind-driven debris — the number-one cause of vehicle damage during hurricanes when you don't have a proper garage.

Best Compact: Quictent 10×20 Heavy Duty Car Canopy

The Quictent splits the difference between the budget Abba Patio and the premium ShelterLogic. It includes sidewall panels (removable), a reinforced frame with cross braces, and a decent UV-treated cover — all at a mid-range price point.

SpecDetails

FrameHeavy-duty steel with 6-leg design
CoverPE fabric with UV coating, waterproof
Wind Rating~30 mph (with all anchors)
IncludesRemovable sidewalls, ground stakes, guy ropes

Why we like it for Miami: The removable sidewalls give you flexibility — open sides for ventilation on normal days, full enclosure when storms are coming. The six-leg frame is more stable than four-leg designs in our gusty conditions.

→ Check price on Amazon

Quick Comparison

Abba Patio 10×20$150–$250Budget UV protection25 mph95%+
ShelterLogic ShelterTube 12×26$600–$900Hurricane season50+ mph99%+
Quictent 10×20$200–$350Versatile mid-range30 mph95%+

Installation Tips for Miami Conditions

  • Always anchor to the ground. Miami wind is no joke. Use concrete anchors on paved surfaces or heavy-duty auger stakes on grass. A 95-lb shelter becomes a sail in a 30 mph gust if it's not anchored.
  • Position with the opening facing away from the prevailing wind. In Miami, that typically means the opening should face west or northwest (our storms generally come from the east/southeast).
  • Add sandbag weights at each leg. Even with ground anchors, 20–30 lb sandbags at each leg add crucial stability. Canopy weight bags on Amazon →
  • Check your HOA rules first. Many Miami condo and HOA communities have rules about temporary structures. The Ikuby's collapsible design often passes where permanent carports don't.
  • Replace the cover before it fails. UV-degraded polyethylene gets brittle and can tear in a storm, sending pieces across the neighborhood. Most covers last 2–3 years in full Miami sun. Budget for replacements.

Canopy + Car Cover: The Ultimate Protection Stack

For maximum protection, pair a canopy with a breathable indoor car cover underneath. The canopy blocks UV and rain; the cover prevents dust, moisture condensation, and minor contact scratches. It's the same approach high-end storage facilities use, and it'll keep your paint looking showroom-fresh between details.

Our picks for covers to pair with a canopy: Covercraft custom-fit indoor covers →

The Bottom Line

If you're spending $3,000–$5,000 a year on detailing, ceramic coatings, and paint correction to undo Miami sun damage, a $300–$800 portable shelter pays for itself in a single season. The ShelterLogic AutoShelter is our top pick for most owners — it's proven, affordable, and handles Miami conditions. If you want quick deploy and a cleaner look, the Ikuby is worth the premium. And if hurricane season is your primary concern, the ShelterTube is the closest thing to a garage you can buy without a building permit.

Your exotic car deserves better than baking in a Brickell parking lot. Give it some shade.

title: Best Car Seat Cooling Systems & Ventilated Seat Covers for Miami's Heat (2026)
excerpt: Miami sun turns your leather seats into a griddle by noon. These aftermarket cooling seat pads and ventilated covers bring cooled-seat luxury to any car — from daily drivers to exotics without the factory option.
content:
If you've ever parked your car in a Miami surface lot between May and October, you know the drill: open the door, get hit with a wall of trapped heat, and then — the worst part — lower yourself onto leather seats that have been absorbing direct sunlight for three hours. The steering wheel is untouchable. The seatbelt buckle could brand cattle. And your back is soaked in sweat before you leave the parking lot.

Factory ventilated seats solve this problem beautifully — but not every car has them. Older exotics, base-model luxury cars, and plenty of sports cars either didn't offer cooled seats or charged an absurd premium for the option. The good news: aftermarket car seat cooling systems and ventilated seat covers have gotten genuinely good, and for Miami drivers, they're one of the best quality-of-life upgrades you can make.

Why This Matters More in Miami Than Anywhere Else

We're not being dramatic. Here's what actually happens to your car's interior in the Miami sun:

MeasurementShade / CoveredDirect Miami Sun
Dashboard surface temp90–100°F180–200°F
Leather seat surface85–95°F150–170°F
Steering wheel90–100°F160–180°F
Cabin air temp95–105°F140–160°F
Time for AC to cool cabin2–4 min8–15 min

A 150°F leather seat isn't just uncomfortable — it can cause actual skin burns on bare legs (shorts weather is 10 months a year here). And while your AC eventually cools the cabin air, the seat surface stays hot much longer because leather is a poor conductor. Ventilated seats actively pull heat away from your body, cutting that miserable first-10-minutes period down to almost nothing.

Types of Aftermarket Seat Cooling

Before we get to products, understand what you're choosing between:

TypeHow It WorksCooling PowerPrice RangeBest For
Fan-based cooling padsSmall fans blow ambient air through a mesh padModerate (evaporative)$40–$100Daily drivers, quick comfort
Thermoelectric (Peltier) seat coversTEC modules actively cool the surface below ambient tempStrong (actual cooling)$100–$300Serious heat, luxury feel
12V ventilated seat cushionsCombination of fans + breathable mesh with 12V powerGood (airflow + evaporation)$50–$150Best balance of price/performance
Professional install (aftermarket ventilation)Fans installed inside factory seat foamExcellent (OEM-equivalent)$500–$1,500 per seatPermanent upgrade, exotic cars

Our Top Picks

🏆 Best Overall: SEA TEAM 12V Cooling Car Seat Cushion

The SEA TEAM cooling cushion is the best combination of cooling performance, comfort, and price we've tested. It uses eight built-in fans with three speed settings, powers via 12V cigarette lighter, and the breathable 3D mesh fabric doesn't trap heat like some cheaper pads.

SpecDetails
Power12V (cigarette lighter / USB adapter available)
Fans8 integrated fans, 3 speed settings
Material3D breathable mesh + cool foam backing
CoverageFull seat + back
Noise LevelLow (barely audible at speed 1-2)

Why we like it for Miami: The eight-fan design covers both your back and seat bottom — most cheap pads only cool the seat, leaving your back soaked. The three speeds let you dial it in: max when you first get in a hot car, then down to low once the AC catches up. The mesh material also means no more peeling your legs off a leather seat.

→ Check price on Amazon

🥈 Best Premium: SNAILAX Cooling Seat Cushion with Massage

The SNAILAX takes the cooling pad concept and adds a massage function — which sounds gimmicky until you're stuck in I-95 traffic at 5 PM in August. The combination of active cooling and vibration massage genuinely reduces the misery of a Miami commute.

SpecDetails
Power12V with home adapter included
Cooling5 fans (2 seat, 3 back) + 2 heating zones (winter mode)
Massage6 vibration motors, 3 intensity levels
MaterialBreathable mesh with memory foam zones
ControlWired remote with independent cooling/massage/heat

Why we like it for Miami: The memory foam zones actually conform to your seat shape, which means it stays put in sports seats (a common complaint with cheaper pads that slide around). The dual-zone cooling targets both your lumbar and thighs — the two areas that get the sweatiest. And yes, the heating function is technically useless in Miami, but it's there for the three days a year it dips below 60°F.

→ Check price on Amazon

🥉 Best Budget: Big Ant Cooling Car Seat Cover

At under $50, the Big Ant is the entry point for seat cooling. It's a simple, fan-powered mesh cover that straps to your existing seat. It won't match the cooling power of the premium options, but it makes a noticeable difference — especially in the critical first few minutes after getting into a sun-baked car.

SpecDetails
Power12V cigarette lighter
Fans5 fans, 2 speed settings
MaterialBreathable spacer mesh
CoverageSeat bottom + lower back
FitUniversal with adjustable straps

Why we like it for Miami: The price. If you're not sure whether a cooling pad is worth it, spend $40 on a Big Ant and find out. Most people who try one never go back to a bare seat in summer. The universal fit works on virtually any car, and the thin profile doesn't affect your seating position much — important in sports cars where the seat is already low.

Best for Exotic Cars: Kingleting Luxury Cooling Seat Cushion

If you're putting a cooling pad in a Ferrari or Porsche, it needs to look the part. The Kingleting uses a minimalist black leather-and-mesh design that blends with premium interiors instead of looking like an aftermarket add-on. The slim profile is crucial for sports cars where every millimeter of seat height matters.

SpecDetails
Power12V / USB dual power
Cooling6 quiet fans, 3 speeds
MaterialLeather trim + breathable mesh panels
ProfileUltra-slim (< 1" thick)
AttachmentNon-slip backing + headrest hook

Why we like it for Miami exotics: The leather trim means it doesn't look out of place in a car with a $10K interior package. The ultra-slim profile doesn't raise your seating position, which is critical in low-slung sports cars where an extra inch puts your head in the roof liner. And the non-slip backing won't scratch leather seats.

→ Check price on Amazon

Best Permanent Solution: Dorman Seat Ventilation Kit (Professional Install)

If you want OEM-level cooled seats without the aftermarket pad look, the Dorman ventilation kit adds fans directly into your existing seat foam. This requires professional installation (upholstery shop or auto interior specialist), but the result is indistinguishable from factory ventilated seats.

SpecDetails
Kit Includes2 fans per seat, wiring harness, switch
InstallationProfessional required (2–4 hours per seat)
CompatibilityUniversal — works with perforated leather seats
Total Cost (kit + install)$500–$1,500 per seat in Miami
Cooling PowerOEM-equivalent

Why we like it for Miami exotics: This is the only option that's truly invisible — no pads, no wires, no accessories. If you bought an older 911 or Ferrari that didn't come with ventilated seats, this retrofit brings it up to modern standards. Several Miami upholstery shops specialize in this work, including shops in the NW 36th Street corridor.

→ Check price on Amazon

Quick Comparison

ProductPriceCooling TypeBest ForLooks Premium?
SEA TEAM 12V Cushion$50–$808-fan activeBest all-aroundDecent
SNAILAX Cooling + Massage$80–$1305-fan + massageCommuters, comfortGood
Big Ant Seat Cover$30–$505-fan basicBudget optionBasic
Kingleting Luxury$60–$1006-fan slimSports/exotic carsExcellent
Dorman Vent Kit + Install$500–$1,500OEM retrofitPermanent upgradeInvisible (OEM)

Pro Tips for Miami Drivers

  • Pair with a windshield sunshade. A cooling pad fights the symptom; a sunshade fights the cause. Used together, your cabin can be 30–40°F cooler when you return to the car. Windshield sunshades on Amazon →
  • Remote start is your best friend. If your car has remote start (or a smartphone app like Tesla, BMW, or Porsche), start the AC 5–10 minutes before you get in. The cooling pad then works with already-cool air instead of fighting 160°F cabin temps.
  • Keep the 12V plug accessible. In cars where the cigarette lighter is buried in the center console, grab a 12V splitter or USB adapter mounted somewhere convenient. 12V splitters on Amazon →
  • Don't use cooling pads on heated seats simultaneously. This seems obvious, but we've seen it. Your heated seat fights the cooling pad, both work harder, and neither wins. Turn off heated seats if your cooling pad is plugged in.
  • Clean the mesh monthly. Miami sweat + humidity + mesh fabric = smell. Most cooling pad covers are removable and machine washable. Do it once a month in summer.

The Complete Miami Heat Protection Stack

For maximum comfort in Miami's sun, here's what we recommend combining:

LayerProductCostWhat It Does
1. Block the sunCustom-fit windshield sunshade$25–$60Reduces cabin temp by 30–40°F
2. Cool the seatCooling seat cushion (any pick above)$40–$130Active cooling under your body
3. Protect the wheelSteering wheel cover or sunshade$10–$25Prevents untouchable-wheel syndrome
4. Pre-cool the cabinRemote start / app startFree (if equipped)AC running before you enter
5. Tint the windowsCeramic window tint (28% front, 15% rear)$400–$800Blocks 50–70% of solar heat

Total investment: $475–$1,015. Total improvement in quality of life: immeasurable. If you've been suffering through Miami summers with bare leather seats and a prayer, any single item on this list will make a noticeable difference. All five together? You'll wonder how you ever lived without them.

The Bottom Line

Miami's heat is relentless, and your car's interior takes the brunt of it. A cooling seat cushion won't solve everything, but it addresses the single most uncomfortable part of getting into a sun-baked car — that moment when your back and legs make contact with superheated leather. For $50–$130, you get a meaningful comfort upgrade that makes every drive between May and October significantly less miserable. The SEA TEAM is our top pick for most drivers, the Kingleting for exotic car owners who care about aesthetics, and the Dorman kit for anyone who wants a permanent, invisible solution.

Stay cool out there, Miami.

title: McLaren Artura for Sale in Miami: 2026 Pricing, Specs & Buyer's Guide
excerpt: The McLaren Artura is the brand's first series-production hybrid supercar — and Miami dealers are finally getting steady inventory. Here's what you'll pay, where to look, and what to inspect before buying.
content:
The McLaren Artura represents a genuine turning point for the Woking-based supercar maker — it's their first series-production high-performance hybrid, built on an entirely new carbon-fiber platform. For Miami buyers, it's also one of the most compelling supercars in the $250K–$350K bracket: V6 hybrid power with 671 hp combined, a sub-3-second 0–60 time, and the ability to run in pure electric mode for short bursts around Brickell or South Beach.

If you've been searching for a McLaren Artura for sale in Miami, here's what you need to know about pricing, where to find inventory, common issues, and what separates a great deal from a costly mistake.

McLaren Artura Pricing in Miami: What You'll Actually Pay

The Artura launched with an MSRP of around $237,500 for the base model, but real-world pricing in Miami has fluctuated significantly since the car's somewhat rocky 2023 debut. Here's where things stand in 2026:

Model / YearMSRP (New)Miami Market Price (2026)Notes
2023 McLaren Artura$237,500$195,000–$225,000Early production; check for software updates and recall completion
2024 McLaren Artura$242,000$210,000–$240,000Improved reliability; most software issues resolved
2025 McLaren Artura Spider$265,000$255,000–$285,000Open-top variant; strong Miami demand
2025 McLaren Artura Trophy$258,000$248,000–$275,000Track-focused with stiffer suspension
2026 McLaren Artura (current)$248,000$248,000–$270,000Full allocation pricing; some dealer markup

The 2023 models are where the value is. McLaren's early Artura production had well-documented teething issues — delayed deliveries, software glitches, and a few high-voltage battery complaints. Most of these were addressed under warranty, and a fully updated 2023 Artura is mechanically identical in reliability to later models. That 15–20% depreciation from MSRP makes early cars compelling buys if you verify the service history.

McLaren Artura Specs: What Makes It Special

The Artura isn't just a 720S with a battery bolted on. It's built on McLaren's new McLaren Carbon Lightweight Architecture (MCLA), designed from the ground up for hybrid power.

SpecificationMcLaren Artura
Engine3.0L twin-turbo V6 + electric motor
Combined Output671 hp / 531 lb-ft
V6 Only577 hp / 431 lb-ft
Electric Motor94 hp / 166 lb-ft
Battery7.4 kWh lithium-ion
EV Range~19 miles (pure electric)
0–60 mph2.9 seconds
Top Speed205 mph
Transmission8-speed dual-clutch (new design)
Weight3,303 lbs (dry)
ArchitectureMCLA carbon fiber monocoque

The 120-degree V6 is a masterpiece of packaging — the hot-vee layout (turbos nestled between the cylinder banks) keeps the engine compact and low, which matters for center-of-gravity. The electric motor fills in the low-end torque gap that plagues small-displacement turbocharged engines, so throttle response is instantaneous.

Where to Find a McLaren Artura for Sale in Miami

Miami has one authorized McLaren dealer and a robust network of exotic car specialists:

Authorized Dealer

  • McLaren Miami (The Collection) — 200 Bird Road, Coral Gables. This is your primary source for new Arturas and CPO (Qualified by McLaren) inventory. They typically have 2–4 Arturas in stock at any time, plus access to factory allocation for custom orders. Expect 4–6 months for a custom build.

Pre-Owned Specialists

  • Prestige Imports — North Miami Beach. Carries pre-owned McLarens alongside their Lamborghini franchise. Often has competitively priced Arturas that traded in against Lamborghini purchases.
  • Exotic Car Trader / Miami Motorcar — Doral area. Independent dealers who source from auctions and private sellers. Pricing is usually 5–10% below franchise dealers, but you won't get McLaren CPO warranty.
  • iLusso / Curated — Consignment platforms with Miami inventory. These are essentially brokers connecting private sellers with buyers. Inspect carefully — consignment cars skip dealer reconditioning.

Online Sources

  • Bring a Trailer (BaT) — Arturas are appearing regularly now. Auction format means potential deals, but also potential bidding wars on desirable specs.
  • Cars & Bids — Doug DeMuro's platform. Slightly younger audience, often good prices for modern exotics.
  • Autotrader / Cars.com — Filter by Miami/Fort Lauderdale area. Franchise dealers list here; pricing is usually negotiable.

McLaren Artura: What to Inspect Before Buying

The Artura is a complex machine — more so than any previous McLaren. Here's what a pre-purchase inspection should focus on:

High-Voltage Battery Health

The 7.4 kWh battery pack is the single most important thing to verify. Ask the dealer for a battery health report (McLaren's diagnostic tool can generate one). Degradation beyond 10% of capacity in the first three years is a red flag. Cars that sat for extended periods without being plugged in may have accelerated degradation.

Software Version

McLaren pushed multiple over-the-air and dealer-applied software updates through 2023 and 2024. The car should be running the latest infotainment and powertrain calibration. Outdated software can cause:

  • Phantom check-engine lights
  • Inconsistent hybrid mode switching
  • Infotainment freezes and reboots
  • Incorrect range estimates

Brake Wear

The Artura uses carbon-ceramic brakes standard. These last 30,000–50,000 miles under normal use, but track days eat them fast. Replacement cost: $8,000–$15,000 for a full set. Check pad thickness and rotor condition.

Panel Gaps and Paint

Early Arturas had some quality-control inconsistencies. Check panel alignment along the doors, front clamshell, and rear deck. Run a paint-depth gauge over every panel — Miami's used-exotic market has a lot of repainted cars from minor parking incidents.

Recall Status

Verify all open recalls have been completed. The Artura had recalls related to the high-voltage battery disconnect and a seat-belt pre-tensioner issue. Both are straightforward fixes but must be documented.

McLaren Artura vs. the Competition in Miami

The Artura sits in an interesting competitive space. Here's how it stacks up against what Miami buyers typically cross-shop:

ModelPrice (Miami)HP0–60Hybrid?Vibe
McLaren Artura$195K–$285K6712.9sYesTech-forward, lightweight, driver's car
Ferrari 296 GTB$280K–$350K8182.9sYesMore prestigious, higher power, pricier
Lamborghini Huracán Tecnica$260K–$310K6312.9sNoNaturally aspirated V10 theater
Porsche 911 GT3$210K–$280K5023.2sNoTrack-focused, reliable, holds value
Aston Martin Vantage$185K–$230K6563.4sNoGT character, gorgeous, less raw

The Artura's strongest argument is weight. At 3,303 lbs dry, it's significantly lighter than the Ferrari 296 GTB (3,395 lbs) and dramatically lighter than the Huracán Tecnica (3,390 lbs). You feel that difference in every corner. It's the most connected, most driver-focused car in this price range — which is exactly what McLaren has always done best.

Cost of Ownership: McLaren Artura in Miami

Owning a McLaren in Miami comes with specific costs you should budget for:

ExpenseAnnual Cost (Estimate)
Insurance (Miami, clean record, 30+)$4,500–$8,000
Annual Service (McLaren Miami)$2,000–$3,500
Tires (Pirelli P Zero, set)$2,000–$2,800 (every 8K–12K miles)
Registration + property tax (FL)$800–$1,200
Carbon ceramic brake replacement$8,000–$15,000 (every 30K–50K mi)
Depreciation (years 1–3)$15,000–$30,000/year

One advantage: Florida has no state income tax, so there's no additional tax on the purchase beyond sales tax (7% in Miami-Dade). And unlike some European exotics, the Artura's hybrid system qualifies for HOV lane access in some jurisdictions — check current Florida rules, as this varies.

Should You Buy a McLaren Artura in Miami?

Buy if: You want the most involving driving experience under $300K, you appreciate the engineering over the badge, and you're comfortable with McLaren's smaller dealer network. The Artura is a brilliant driver's car that happens to also be a technological showcase.

Skip if: Resale value is your top priority (Porsches and Ferraris hold value better), you want maximum social media impact (the Ferrari badge still wins at valet), or you need a grand tourer for long highway runs (the 720S/750S are better for that).

Best deal right now: A 2023 or early 2024 Artura with full service records, all software updates completed, and under 10,000 miles. You're looking at $195,000–$225,000 for a car that stickered at $250K+ — and the driving experience is genuinely world-class.

Miami's exotic car market moves fast. If you spot a well-spec'd Artura at the right price, don't sleep on it — clean, low-mile examples get snapped up within days.

title: Porsche 718 Cayman for Sale in Miami: 2026 Pricing, Models & Buyer's Guide
excerpt: The Porsche 718 Cayman is one of the best-handling sports cars you can buy — and Miami has excellent inventory across all variants. Here's your complete guide to pricing, models, and what to look for.
content:
The Porsche 718 Cayman might be the best-kept secret in the sports car world — and in Miami, it's an absolute sweet spot. Mid-engine layout, naturally aspirated flat-six in GT4 trim, everyday usability, and pricing that starts well under six figures for pre-owned examples. Whether you're looking for your first sports car or a track-day weapon that can double as a daily driver, the 718 Cayman deserves serious consideration.

If you're searching for a Porsche 718 Cayman for sale in Miami, this guide covers every variant, what they cost right now, where to find the best inventory, and the critical things to check before buying.

Porsche 718 Cayman Pricing in Miami: Every Model Ranked

The 718 Cayman spans a wide range — from turbocharged four-cylinders in the base model to the legendary flat-six in the GT4 RS. Here's what the Miami market looks like in 2026:

ModelYearsEngineHPMiami Price Range (2026)
718 Cayman (base)2017–20242.0L turbo flat-4300$42,000–$58,000
718 Cayman S2017–20242.5L turbo flat-4350$52,000–$68,000
718 Cayman T2020–20242.0L turbo flat-4300$55,000–$72,000
718 Cayman GTS 4.02020–20244.0L NA flat-6394$78,000–$98,000
718 Cayman GT42020–20244.0L NA flat-6414$95,000–$125,000
718 Cayman GT4 RS2022–20244.0L NA flat-6493$155,000–$210,000

The standout value play is the GTS 4.0. For under $100K, you get the glorious naturally aspirated flat-six engine, sport suspension, limited-slip differential, and essentially 90% of the GT4 experience without the GT4 premium. It's the variant that Porsche enthusiasts and automotive journalists consistently recommend — and for good reason.

The GT4 RS, on the other hand, has actually appreciated from its $143,000 MSRP. Low-mile examples are trading at $155K–$210K in Miami, making it one of the few modern Porsches where you won't lose money. Production was limited, and demand from collectors has kept prices firm.

Porsche 718 Cayman Specs: Base to GT4 RS

Spec718 Base718 SGTS 4.0GT4GT4 RS
Engine2.0T flat-42.5T flat-44.0 NA flat-64.0 NA flat-64.0 NA flat-6
Horsepower300350394414493
Torque280 lb-ft309 lb-ft309 lb-ft309 lb-ft331 lb-ft
0–60 mph4.9s4.4s3.9s3.8s3.2s
Top Speed170 mph177 mph182 mph188 mph196 mph
Transmission6MT / 7PDK6MT / 7PDK6MT / 7PDK6MT / 7PDK7PDK only
Weight3,034 lbs3,153 lbs3,128 lbs3,157 lbs3,227 lbs
Redline7,500 RPM7,500 RPM7,800 RPM8,000 RPM9,000 RPM

That 9,000 RPM redline in the GT4 RS deserves special mention. It uses a derivative of the 911 GT3's engine — a flat-six that revs to the stratosphere and sounds like nothing else on the road. In Miami's tunnel under the port or on the MacArthur Causeway, that intake howl is genuinely intoxicating.

Where to Find a Porsche 718 Cayman for Sale in Miami

Miami has arguably the best Porsche inventory in the Southeast. Here's where to look:

Authorized Porsche Dealers

  • The Collection Porsche — Coral Gables. The flagship dealer in South Florida. Massive CPO inventory, typically 10–20 718 Caymans at any time. Their CPO cars come with Porsche's 2-year/unlimited-mile warranty extension — invaluable for peace of mind.
  • Porsche Miami — Near Brickell. Smaller allocation but often has interesting trade-ins from customers upgrading to 911s.
  • Champion Porsche — Pompano Beach (worth the drive). One of the largest Porsche dealers in the country. Their pre-owned selection is enormous, and they're more willing to negotiate than Miami proper dealers.
  • Braman Porsche — West Palm Beach. If you can't find the right spec in Miami-Dade, Braman consistently has deep inventory.

Independent Specialists

  • Vertex Auto — Specializes in Porsche and BMW performance cars. Often has well-sorted enthusiast-owned 718s with tasteful modifications.
  • Prestige Imports — North Miami Beach. Carries pre-owned Porsches alongside their Lamborghini franchise.

Online / Auction

  • Bring a Trailer — The 718 Cayman is one of the most popular cars on BaT. GT4 and GT4 RS examples generate intense bidding. Filter by Florida for easy local pickup.
  • PCarMarket — Porsche-specific auction site. Higher-quality listings and more detailed documentation than general platforms.
  • Rennlist Classifieds — The Porsche enthusiast forum. Private-party sales from knowledgeable owners who maintained their cars properly.

718 Cayman: What to Inspect Before Buying

Turbo Four-Cylinder Models (Base, S, T)

The 2.0L and 2.5L turbocharged flat-four engines are reliable but have a few known concerns:

  • Cylinder scoring (rare but serious) — Some early 2017–2018 models experienced cylinder bore scoring. Listen for ticking or knocking at cold start. If present, walk away unless priced accordingly — repair costs are $8,000–$15,000.
  • IMS bearing — Not an issue on the 718 (that was the 986/987 era). Don't let a seller try to scare you about this.
  • Coolant leaks — Check around the turbocharger and intercooler connections. Minor seepage is common on higher-mileage cars.

Flat-Six Models (GTS 4.0, GT4, GT4 RS)

The 4.0L naturally aspirated flat-six is derived from the 911's engine and is exceptionally reliable:

  • Oil consumption — High-revving flat-sixes consume some oil by design. Up to 1 quart per 3,000 miles is normal, especially if the car is driven hard. Check oil level at inspection.
  • Clutch wear (manual cars) — Miami traffic is hard on manual transmissions. Check clutch engagement point and pedal feel. Replacement is $3,000–$5,000 at an independent shop, more at the dealer.
  • Wheel/tire damage — GT4 and GT4 RS models ride low and run staggered, expensive tires. Inspect all four wheels for curb rash (epidemic in Miami) and check tire dates — Michelin Pilot Sport Cup 2 tires degrade in heat even when not driven.

All Models

  • Service history — Porsche maintains digital service records. Ask for a Porsche Vehicle History Report. Any gaps in service are a yellow flag.
  • Paint condition — Miami rock chips are unavoidable. Check the front bumper, hood, and mirrors. Paint Protection Film (PPF) is a major plus — if a car has full-front PPF, it was likely well cared for.
  • Convertible mechanism (Boxster variants) — If cross-shopping with the 718 Boxster, check the soft-top operation and drainage channels. Florida humidity and rain can cause drain blockages and water leaks.

Porsche 718 Cayman vs. the Competition in Miami

Here's how the 718 Cayman stacks up against what Miami buyers typically cross-shop:

ModelMiami PriceHP0–60Strength
718 Cayman GTS 4.0$78K–$98K3943.9sBest handling, flat-six, value
BMW M2$55K–$72K4533.9sMore power per dollar, rear-drive
Corvette Z06$85K–$115K6702.6sInsane power, flat-plane V8
Toyota GR Supra$42K–$55K3823.9sBudget performance, BMW inline-6
Lotus Emira$82K–$100K4004.2sExotic feel, mid-engine, lighter
Audi R8 (used)$105K–$145K5623.1sV10 drama, all-wheel drive

On paper, the Corvette Z06 is the performance bargain. But the 718 Cayman offers something none of these competitors do: that mid-engine Porsche balance. The steering feel, the way the car rotates around its center of gravity, the progressive limit behavior — it's a masterclass in chassis dynamics. You don't buy a 718 Cayman for spec-sheet numbers. You buy it because it makes you a better, more confident driver.

Cost of Ownership: 718 Cayman in Miami

One of the 718 Cayman's biggest advantages over more exotic alternatives is ownership costs:

ExpenseAnnual Cost (Estimate)
Insurance (Miami, clean record, 30+)$2,000–$4,000
Annual Service (Porsche dealer)$800–$1,800
Annual Service (independent)$500–$1,200
Tires (Michelin PS4S, set)$1,200–$1,600 (every 15K–25K mi)
Registration + property tax (FL)$400–$700
Brakes (steel, standard)$1,500–$2,500 (every 25K–40K mi)
Brakes (PCCB ceramic, optional)$6,000–$12,000 (every 40K–60K mi)
Depreciation (3–5 year old car)$3,000–$8,000/year

Compare that to a Ferrari or McLaren where insurance alone runs $5K–$8K and annual service is $2K–$4K. The 718 Cayman is genuinely affordable to own by sports car standards — and Porsche's reliability reputation is earned. These engines routinely go 100,000+ miles without major issues.

Manual vs. PDK: The Miami Consideration

This is the eternal Porsche debate, and Miami adds a wrinkle. The 6-speed manual is more engaging, more connected, and more satisfying on an empty causeway at sunset. The 7-speed PDK is faster in every measurable way and turns Miami's brutal stop-and-go traffic from painful to tolerable.

Our take: If this is your only car, get the PDK. Miami traffic is genuinely awful — Brickell to the Beach at rush hour, I-95 during any hours, and the eternal construction on I-395 will make you regret a manual transmission as a daily driver. If it's a weekend car or you have a separate daily, the manual is the pure experience and will hold value better long-term.

Resale note: Manual 718 Caymans (especially GTS 4.0 and GT4) command a 10–15% premium over PDK equivalents. If you're buying to hold, the manual is the better financial play.

Best Porsche 718 Cayman Specs for Miami

If you're configuring or shopping for the ideal Miami 718, here's what we'd prioritize:

  • Color: Miami Blue, Shark Blue, or GT Silver. They photograph beautifully against the city's Art Deco backdrop and stand out at car meets. White is safe but forgettable; black is a sweat-inducing oven in Miami's sun.
  • Seats: Ventilated sport seats if available. You'll thank us in August. The lightweight bucket seats in the GT4 look amazing but have zero ventilation — bring a towel.
  • PASM (adaptive dampers): Essential for Miami roads. Our pothole-laden streets will rattle your fillings in a fixed-suspension car.
  • Sport Chrono Package: Adds launch control, dynamic engine mounts, and the drive mode dial. It's a must-have for the full experience.
  • Front axle lift: If you have a GT4 or GT4 RS, this option is non-negotiable in Miami. Speed bumps, parking garages, and steep driveways are everywhere. Cars without front-lift sell for less.

Should You Buy a Porsche 718 Cayman in Miami?

Buy if: You want the best driving experience per dollar in Miami, you appreciate handling over straight-line speed, and you want a sports car that won't drain your bank account in maintenance. The 718 Cayman is the car that reminds you why you love driving.

Skip if: You need back seats (look at the 911), you want maximum presence at valet (Lamborghini or Ferrari territory), or you need a high-riding vehicle for Miami's flood-prone streets during hurricane season.

Best deal right now: A 2021–2022 GTS 4.0 with PDK (or manual if you're a purist), under 25,000 miles, with Sport Chrono and PASM. You're looking at $80,000–$90,000 for a car that drives like a $150K exotic. It's one of the best values in the entire sports car market, and Miami has no shortage of inventory.

The 718 Cayman doesn't shout. It doesn't demand attention at every red light on Collins Avenue. But for the driver who cares about what happens between the steering wheel and the road, it's the best sports car under $100K — and one of the best at any price.

title: McLaren 720S for Sale in Miami: 2026 Pricing, Models & Buyer's Guide
excerpt: The McLaren 720S remains one of the best supercar values on the market — and Miami dealers have excellent inventory. Here's your complete guide to buying a 720S in South Florida.
content:
The McLaren 720S is, by almost any measure, the supercar that redefined what a twin-turbo mid-engine car could do. When it debuted in 2017, it embarrassed Ferraris and Lamborghinis costing twice as much — and now that it's been replaced by the 750S, prices on the used market have dropped into genuinely attainable territory. If you're searching for a McLaren 720S for sale in Miami, you're shopping at the right time and in the right city.

Miami is one of the largest McLaren markets in the country. Between McLaren Miami (The Collection), independent exotic dealers along Biscayne Boulevard and in Doral, and private sellers, inventory is strong. This guide covers every 720S variant, what they actually cost in 2026, where to find the best examples, and what to watch out for before you buy.

McLaren 720S Pricing in Miami: Every Variant Ranked

The 720S was produced from 2017 to 2024 across several configurations. Miami's warm climate means fewer weather-related issues, but it also means UV damage and overheated interiors are real concerns. Here's what the market looks like right now:

ModelYearsHP0-60 mphMiami Price Range (2026)
720S Coupe2018–20247102.7s$148,000–$215,000
720S Spider2019–20247102.8s$168,000–$245,000
720S Performance2018–20247102.7s$158,000–$225,000
720S Le Mans (Special Edition)20207102.7s$275,000–$340,000
720S GT3X (Track Only)2021–2023710+N/A$400,000–$550,000

The sweet spot for most buyers is the 720S Coupe in the $150K–$180K range. That puts you in a 2020–2022 example with reasonable miles. Spiders command a $20K–$40K premium, which makes perfect sense for Miami — you'll want that top down on Ocean Drive.

Why the McLaren 720S Is a Supercar Bargain in 2026

Here's the thing about the 720S that makes it such a compelling buy right now: depreciation has already done its worst. Early 2018 models that stickered for $290K+ are now trading in the $150K range — nearly half off. But the car itself hasn't gotten any slower. The twin-turbo 4.0-liter V8 still makes 710 horsepower, still hits 60 in 2.7 seconds, and still tops out at 212 mph.

Compared to its competitors at the same price point, nothing comes close:

CarHP0-60Miami Price (2026)
McLaren 720S7102.7s$148,000–$215,000
Ferrari F8 Tributo7102.9s$225,000–$290,000
Lamborghini Huracán EVO6312.9s$195,000–$260,000
Porsche 911 GT3 RS (992)5183.0s$260,000–$320,000

The 720S gives you more power, faster acceleration, and a lower price than all three. The catch? McLaren's reputation for reliability and build quality — which we'll address below.

McLaren 720S Specs & Performance: What Makes It Special

The 720S sits on McLaren's carbon-fiber Monocage II chassis, which weighs just 178 pounds. That obsessive weight-saving carries through the entire car:

  • Engine: 4.0L twin-turbo V8 (M840T), 710 hp / 568 lb-ft
  • Transmission: 7-speed dual-clutch (SSG)
  • Weight: 2,828 lbs (dry) — lighter than a Porsche 911 Turbo S
  • Top speed: 212 mph
  • 0-124 mph: 7.8 seconds
  • Quarter mile: 10.1 seconds
  • Braking (60-0): 95 feet

The party trick is the dihedral doors — they swing up and out in a motion that's become the McLaren signature. In Miami traffic, they're also practical: tight parking spots don't require as much side clearance as conventional doors.

Where to Find a McLaren 720S for Sale in Miami

Miami has no shortage of McLaren inventory. Here are the best places to look:

Authorized Dealers

  • McLaren Miami (The Collection) — 200 Bird Rd, Coral Gables. South Florida's official McLaren retailer. Best for certified pre-owned with warranty.
  • McLaren Orlando / Palm Beach — Worth the drive for specific specs or better pricing.

Independent Exotic Dealers

  • Prestige Imports — North Miami Beach. Huge exotic inventory, competitive pricing.
  • iLusso — Costa Mesa-based but ships nationwide; strong 720S inventory.
  • Curated — Specializes in low-mile exotics, often has cherry-picked 720S examples.
  • South Beach Exotics — Sometimes has 720S inventory from rental fleet retirements (inspect carefully).

Online Marketplaces

  • Bring a Trailer — Transparent auction history, enthusiast-vetted. Great for finding well-documented examples.
  • Cars & Bids — Doug DeMuro's platform, strong for modern supercars.
  • duPont Registry — Premium listings, often dealer inventory.
  • AutoTrader — Filter by Miami ZIP codes for local inventory.

What to Inspect Before Buying a McLaren 720S

McLarens are exotic in every sense — including maintenance complexity. Here's what to check:

Engine & Drivetrain

  • Engine mounts: Known to wear prematurely. Listen for rattling at idle.
  • Turbo wastegate actuators: Can develop issues around 20K miles. Verify service history.
  • Transmission behavior: The SSG dual-clutch should shift smoothly in both Comfort and Track modes. Any hesitation or harshness is a red flag.
  • Oil leaks: Check around the turbo housings and at the bottom of the engine bay. Minor seepage is common; active drips are not.

Suspension & Chassis

  • Hydraulic suspension: The 720S uses a linked-hydraulic suspension (Proactive Chassis Control II). It's brilliant when working, expensive when it's not. Verify all modes function and there are no warning lights.
  • Nose lift: The front-axle lift system is critical in Miami (speed bumps everywhere). Make sure it operates smoothly.
  • Carbon tub: Check for any signs of impact damage on the sills and underside.

Interior & Electronics

  • Infotainment: The IRIS system can be laggy. Make sure it boots properly and navigation works.
  • Instrument cluster: The folding instrument panel is a signature feature — verify it folds and unfolds cleanly.
  • A/C system: Critical in Miami. Run it hard during the test drive. McLarens can have A/C issues.

Exterior & Miami-Specific

  • Paint protection film (PPF): Check if it's installed. If not, budget $3,000–$6,000 for a full wrap. Miami sun and road debris are brutal.
  • Brake rotors: Carbon-ceramic brakes are standard. Replacements run $12,000–$18,000 for all four corners.
  • Tire condition: The 720S eats rear tires. Pirelli P Zero replacements cost $400–$600 per rear tire.

McLaren 720S Maintenance Costs in Miami

Let's be honest about ownership costs. The 720S isn't a Toyota:

ServiceFrequencyEstimated Cost
Annual service (oil, filters, inspection)Yearly / 10K miles$1,200–$1,800
Major service (spark plugs, brake fluid, coolant)Every 3 years / 30K miles$3,500–$5,000
Brake pads (carbon-ceramic)25K–40K miles$2,500–$4,000
Brake rotors (carbon-ceramic)50K–70K miles$12,000–$18,000
Tires (set of 4)8K–15K miles$1,600–$2,400
Hydraulic suspension serviceAs needed$3,000–$8,000

Budget $4,000–$7,000 annually for routine maintenance. The key to managing costs: buy a well-maintained example with full service records from an authorized dealer. Deferred maintenance on a McLaren gets expensive fast.

McLaren 720S Insurance in Miami

Insurance on a 720S in Miami runs $4,500–$9,000 per year depending on your driving record, age, and whether you're using it as a daily driver. Some tips to reduce costs:

  • Agreed-value policies through Hagerty or Chubb protect you better than standard carriers.
  • Bundling with your home insurance often yields the best rates.
  • Mileage caps: If you drive under 5,000 miles a year, ask about low-mileage discounts.
  • Dashcam: Some insurers offer discounts for documented driving.

McLaren 720S vs. 750S: Should You Buy New Instead?

The 750S replaced the 720S in 2024 with 30 more horsepower, revised aero, and updated interior tech. But here's the math:

Spec720S750S
HP710740
0-60 mph2.7s2.7s
Weight (dry)2,828 lbs2,795 lbs
Miami Price$148K–$215K$285K–$340K+

The performance delta is marginal. The price delta is $100K+. Unless you need the latest tech or the bragging rights, the 720S is the smarter buy.

Best McLaren 720S Configurations for Miami

If you're shopping specific specs, here's what works best in South Florida:

  • Color: Lighter colors (Glacier White, Silica White, McLaren Orange) handle Miami sun better. Dark colors show swirl marks and get scorching hot.
  • Variant: The Spider is the obvious Miami choice. Budget the premium — you'll use it.
  • Options to seek: Sports exhaust, nose lift, carbon-ceramic brakes (standard), vehicle lift, parking sensors + camera.
  • Options to skip: Track telemetry (unless you actually track it), bespoke interior trim (hard to recoup on resale).

Financing a McLaren 720S in Miami

Most McLaren purchases in this price range use financing. Here's the landscape:

  • Traditional lenders: Bank of America, Chase, and Wells Fargo all finance exotic cars. Expect 20–30% down and rates around 6.5–8.5% APR for used exotics.
  • Specialty lenders: Woodside Credit, Premier Financial Services, and JM Family Enterprises (Fort Lauderdale-based) specialize in exotic car financing with more flexible terms.
  • Lease buyout: If you find a 720S coming off a lease, the lease buyout price is sometimes below market value — a hidden arbitrage opportunity.

The Bottom Line: Is the McLaren 720S Worth Buying in Miami?

Absolutely. The McLaren 720S for sale in Miami represents one of the best performance-per-dollar propositions in the supercar market right now. You get hypercar-level acceleration, a carbon-fiber chassis, dihedral doors, and that unmistakable McLaren presence — all for less than a new Porsche 911 Turbo S.

The caveats are real: maintenance isn't cheap, reliability requires diligence, and you need to be selective about which example you buy. But if you do your homework — inspect carefully, verify service history, and budget for ownership costs — the 720S rewards you with one of the purest driving experiences money can buy.

For Miami specifically, the Spider is the move. Top down, A1A, sunset — that's what supercar ownership is about.

title: Pagani Huayra for Sale: 2026 Pricing, Specs & Where to Find One
excerpt: The Pagani Huayra is one of the rarest and most desirable hypercars ever built. Here's what they actually cost in 2026, what to look for, and how to find one — including in Miami.
content:
The Pagani Huayra isn't just a hypercar — it's a rolling work of art. Named after Huayra-tata, the Andean god of wind, Horacio Pagani's masterpiece combines a Mercedes-AMG twin-turbo V12 with obsessive craftsmanship that makes even Ferrari and Lamborghini look mass-produced. If you're searching for a Pagani Huayra for sale, you're entering one of the most exclusive markets in the automotive world — and Miami is one of the few cities where they actually appear.

With only around 100 Huayra coupes and 100 Huayra Roadsters ever built (plus limited runs of the BC, BC Roadster, and R variants), finding one requires patience, connections, and a serious budget. This guide covers every variant, what they actually sell for in 2026, where to look, and what makes each version special.

Pagani Huayra Pricing in 2026: Every Variant

The Huayra family spans over a decade of production, with each variant rarer and more extreme than the last. Here's what the market looks like:

ModelYears ProducedUnits BuiltHP2026 Market Price
Huayra Coupe2012–2018~100720$2,800,000–$4,200,000
Huayra Roadster2017–2019100754$3,500,000–$5,500,000

Huayra R2021–202330838$6,000,000–$9,000,000
Huayra Codalunga2022–20245829$7,000,000–$10,000,000+

Yes, you're reading those numbers correctly. The Huayra has appreciated dramatically since production ended, and the rarer variants have entered stratospheric territory. Even the "base" Coupe — which originally sold for around $1.4 million — has roughly tripled in value.

Pagani Huayra Specs & Engineering: Why It Commands These Prices

Every Pagani is essentially hand-built by a small team in Modena, Italy. The Huayra's construction is obsessive even by hypercar standards:

Engine & Performance

  • Engine: Mercedes-AMG M158 6.0L twin-turbo V12 (built exclusively for Pagani)
  • Power: 720 hp / 738 lb-ft (Coupe), up to 838 hp in the R
  • Transmission: 7-speed Xtrac AMT (single-clutch automated manual)
  • 0-60 mph: 2.8 seconds
  • Top speed: 238 mph
  • Weight: 2,685 lbs (dry) — extraordinary for a V12 hypercar

Materials & Construction

  • Chassis: Carbotanium monocoque — Pagani's proprietary blend of carbon fiber and titanium. Weighs just 220 lbs.
  • Body panels: Carbon fiber with exposed weave options that reveal the material's artistry.
  • Suspension: Active aero flaps on each corner that adjust independently for downforce and stability.
  • Interior: Hand-stitched leather, machined aluminum switchgear with exposed screws, and the signature exposed-gear shift mechanism.

The level of detail is staggering. Every bolt is a design element. The exhaust tips are titanium works of art. The key is machined from aluminum. Horacio Pagani's background in composite materials (he worked at Lamborghini before founding Pagani) means every structural element is designed to be both functional and beautiful.

Pagani Huayra BC vs. Standard Huayra: What's the Difference?

The "BC" stands for Benny Caiola, Pagani's first-ever customer and close friend. The BC version is the track-focused evolution:

SpecHuayra CoupeHuayra BC
Horsepower720789
Torque738 lb-ft774 lb-ft
Weight (dry)2,685 lbs2,654 lbs
AeroActive flapsMassive fixed rear wing + active flaps
Transmission7-speed AMT7-speed Xtrac sequential
Units built~10020
2026 price$2.8M–$4.2M$4.5M–$6.5M

The BC is objectively the better car to drive — the revised transmission alone is a huge improvement over the standard Huayra's sometimes-awkward automated manual. But with only 20 built, finding one for sale is the real challenge.

Where to Find a Pagani Huayra for Sale

You won't find a Huayra on AutoTrader. The market for cars at this level operates through specialized channels:

Specialist Dealers

  • Miller Motorcars (Greenwich, CT) — One of the top Pagani dealers in the US. Regularly has Huayra inventory.
  • Manhattan Motorcars (New York) — Official Pagani dealer with strong client relationships.
  • Prestige Imports Miami — Has handled Pagani sales in the past and has the clientele for this level.
  • Al Ain Class Motors (Dubai) — Global hypercar dealer that ships worldwide. Often has multiple Huayras listed.
  • Symbolic International (San Diego) — Major hypercar dealer with auction and private sale inventory.

Auction Houses

  • RM Sotheby's — Regularly features Huayras at their major sales (Monterey, Amelia Island, Paris). Achieved record results for BC and Roadster variants.
  • Bonhams — Occasionally features Huayras at their Quail Lodge and Les Grandes Marques du Monde sales.
  • Gooding & Company — Pebble Beach auction specialist that handles hypercars at this level.

Private Networks

  • Pagani Owners Group — The official owners' community sometimes facilitates private sales between members.
  • Collector car brokers — Specialists like Coco Zurita, Simon Kidston, and The Cultivated Collector operate in this space.
  • Concours events — Amelia Island, Cavallino Classic (Palm Beach), and Festivals of Speed (Miami) are where these cars appear and deals happen face-to-face.

Pagani Huayra in Miami: The Connection

Miami and Pagani have a deeper connection than most people realize. South Florida's collector car community is one of the strongest in the country, and several Huayras call Miami home. You'll occasionally spot them at:

  • Supercar Saturdays at Bal Harbour Shops
  • Festivals of Speed on the Dezer Collection campus
  • Private collection viewings in Miami Beach and Coral Gables
  • The Amelia (Amelia Island) — just 5 hours north, a major gathering point for Pagani collectors

Miami's proximity to Latin American collectors also helps — many South American Pagani owners winter their cars in Florida or maintain dual residences with garages here.

What to Inspect When Buying a Pagani Huayra

At this price level, you're working with specialists, but here's what matters:

Provenance & Documentation

  • Build sheet: Every Huayra is unique. Verify the car matches its original Pagani build specification.
  • Service history: All work should be performed by Pagani-authorized service centers (there are very few globally).
  • Ownership history: Fewer owners is better. Cars with single-owner provenance command significant premiums.
  • Certification: Pagani offers authenticity certification. Insist on it.

Mechanical Checks

  • AMG V12: The Mercedes-AMG engine is robust, but the ancillaries (turbo plumbing, sensors, ECU) are bespoke Pagani. Verify there are no fault codes.
  • Transmission: The early cars' AMT transmission is the most common complaint. Test it extensively in both automatic and manual modes.
  • Active aero: All four active flaps must operate smoothly and symmetrically.
  • Exhaust: The titanium exhaust system is fragile and incredibly expensive. Check for damage or modifications.

Cosmetic Inspection

  • Carbon fiber: Inspect all exposed carbon weave for cracks, chips, or UV fading. Repairs are extremely specialized and expensive.
  • Paint: Many Huayras feature bare carbon or tricoat metallic paints that are difficult to touch up. Document everything.
  • Interior: The leather and Alcantara are hand-dyed by Pagani. Replacements must come from the factory. Check for wear on seats, steering wheel, and the signature center console.

Pagani Huayra Ownership Costs

Owning a Huayra is not for the faint of wallet. Here's what to budget beyond the purchase price:

ItemEstimated Cost
Annual service (basic)$8,000–$15,000
Major service (engine-out)$25,000–$45,000
Insurance (agreed value)$25,000–$60,000/year
Tires (set)$3,000–$5,000
Carbon ceramic brakes (replacement)$25,000–$40,000
Climate-controlled storage$500–$2,000/month
Transport (enclosed carrier)$2,000–$5,000 per trip

Insurance alone can run $40,000+ per year in Miami. Agreed-value policies through specialists like Hagerty, Chubb, or AIG Private Client are essential. Standard carriers won't touch a car worth $3 million+.

Pagani Huayra as an Investment

The Huayra has been one of the best-performing hypercar investments of the past decade. Original buyers who paid $1.4 million for coupes are now sitting on $3–4 million in value. BC buyers who paid $2.5 million are looking at $5–6 million.

What drives this appreciation:

  • Extreme rarity: ~100 coupes and ~100 roadsters is nothing. Ferrari makes more cars in a week.
  • No dilution: Pagani doesn't mass-produce or chase volume. The brand remains exclusive.
  • Analog experience: As the industry goes electric and autonomous, the Huayra's V12, manual-ish gearbox, and hydraulic steering become more precious.
  • Artisan quality: These cars are built like watches, not appliances. That craftsmanship appreciates.
  • Successor pricing: The Pagani Utopia (Huayra's replacement) starts at $2.2 million, which retroactively makes the Huayra look like a bargain.

That said, the caveat with any collector car investment applies: buy what you love, because markets can shift. The Huayra is blue-chip, but liquidity at the $3M+ level is limited — selling quickly means accepting a discount.

Pagani Huayra R: The Track-Only Apex

For completeness, the Huayra R deserves mention. It's the ultimate expression of the Huayra platform:

  • Engine: Naturally aspirated 6.0L V12 (no turbos), developed with HWA AG
  • Power: 838 hp, revs to 9,000 RPM
  • Weight: 2,332 lbs (dry)
  • Downforce: 2,200+ lbs at speed
  • Price new: ~$3.1 million
  • 2026 value: $6–9 million

The R is track-only and not street-legal, but it might be the best-sounding car ever made. The naturally aspirated V12 screaming to 9,000 RPM without turbo muffling is an experience that's hard to describe.

The Bottom Line: Should You Buy a Pagani Huayra?

If you can afford one, the Pagani Huayra is one of the most special machines ever created. It's not the fastest hypercar (the Chiron and SF90 are quicker), it's not the most practical (obviously), and it's not the easiest to maintain. But it is, arguably, the most beautiful and most meticulously crafted car of the 21st century.

For Miami buyers specifically, the Huayra fits the city's ethos perfectly — dramatic, exotic, and unapologetically over the top. Just make sure you have the infrastructure: a trusted transporter, Pagani-authorized service access (flying a tech from Modena isn't unusual), proper storage, and the right insurance.

The Pagani Huayra for sale market is thin by design. When the right car appears at the right price, serious buyers move fast. If you've been waiting for one, have your finances and pre-purchase inspection team ready to go.

title: Best Smart Garage Door Openers for Car Collectors in Miami (2026)
excerpt: Your exotic car collection deserves a garage door that's as smart as the cars behind it. Here are the best smart garage door openers and controllers for Miami car enthusiasts — with remote monitoring, smartphone alerts, and integrations that actually matter.
content:
If you've got six figures (or more) parked in your Miami garage, it's wild that most collectors are still using a $30 clicker from Home Depot to protect it all. A smart garage door opener gives you remote monitoring, real-time alerts when the door opens, automatic closing on a schedule, and integration with your home security system — all from your phone.

For Miami car collectors specifically, smart garage access isn't just convenient — it's a security layer. Between South Florida's theft rates and the fact that garage doors are the single largest unsecured entry point in most homes, upgrading to a smart opener is one of the highest-ROI moves you can make.

Here are the best options in 2026, tested and ranked for the needs of serious car owners.

Best Smart Garage Door Openers & Controllers at a Glance

ProductTypePrice RangeBest ForSmart Home Integration
Chamberlain B6753TFull Opener$350–$400Best overall smart openermyQ, Google, Apple HomeKit (via bridge)
Chamberlain myQ Smart ControllerAdd-On Controller$30–$50Making any existing opener smartmyQ, Google, IFTTT
iSmartGate ProAdd-On Controller$120–$150Multi-door monitoring with cameraHomeKit, Google, Alexa, IFTTT
Meross Smart Garage Door OpenerAdd-On Controller$40–$50Budget-friendly smart controlHomeKit, Alexa, Google
Tailwind iQ3Add-On Controller$80–$100Auto open/close via GPSHomeKit, Alexa, Google, SmartThings
LiftMaster 87504-267Full Opener$400–$500Premium wall-mount, ultra-quietmyQ, Google, Apple HomeKit (via bridge)
Genie StealthDrive Connect 7155-TKVFull Opener$250–$300Quiet operation + Aladdin ConnectAladdin Connect, Alexa, Google

Why Miami Car Collectors Need a Smart Garage Door

This isn't a gadget pitch — it's a practical security upgrade. Here's what changes when your garage door gets smart:

  • Real-time open/close alerts: Get a push notification the second your garage door opens. If you're at Carbone and your garage opens at 11 PM, you know something's wrong immediately.
  • Auto-close scheduling: Set the door to automatically close at a specific time every night. No more lying in bed wondering if you left it open.
  • Remote monitoring: Check door status from anywhere. Heading to the Keys for the weekend? Verify it's closed from your phone.
  • Camera integration: Some controllers (like iSmartGate) include a camera feed so you can see inside your garage remotely — not just whether the door is open.
  • Guest access: Let your detailer, mechanic, or house sitter open the garage on a schedule without giving them a physical remote.
  • GPS-based auto-open: The Tailwind iQ3 detects your phone approaching and opens the door automatically. Pull up in the GT3, door's already going up.

Best Overall: Chamberlain B6753T Smart Garage Door Opener

If you're replacing your entire opener, the Chamberlain B6753T is the one to get. It's a belt-drive unit — meaning it's whisper-quiet compared to chain-drive openers — with built-in myQ smart technology, a battery backup (critical during Miami hurricane season), and enough lifting power for heavy insulated doors.

The myQ app gives you open/close control, scheduling, and real-time alerts. It also integrates with Amazon Key for in-garage delivery, which means your packages go inside the garage instead of sitting on the porch in a Miami thunderstorm.

Why it's great for collectors: The battery backup means your garage stays accessible during power outages — which happen regularly during hurricane season. The belt drive is quiet enough that you won't wake the house at 5 AM when you're sneaking the car out for a sunrise drive.

Check price on Amazon →

Best Budget Add-On: Chamberlain myQ Smart Garage Controller

Already have an opener that works fine mechanically? The myQ Smart Garage Door Controller adds smartphone control to almost any existing garage door opener for under $50. You attach a sensor to the door and a hub near the opener, download the app, and you're done in 15 minutes.

It won't give you the auto-open GPS features of the Tailwind, and HomeKit support requires an additional bridge purchase. But for basic remote monitoring and alerts, it's the cheapest path to a smart garage.

Check price on Amazon →

Best for Multi-Door Garages: iSmartGate Pro

If you've got a two or three-car garage — standard for serious Miami collectors — the iSmartGate Pro controls up to three doors from a single unit. It supports an optional wireless camera so you can visually confirm what's happening inside, and it offers native HomeKit, Google Home, and Alexa integration without needing a bridge.

The iSmartGate Pro stores all data locally (no cloud subscription), which is a privacy advantage over myQ's cloud-dependent system. Setup is slightly more involved than myQ, but the multi-door support and camera option make it worth the effort for collectors with larger garages.

Check price on Amazon →

Best Auto-Open Feature: Tailwind iQ3

The Tailwind iQ3 is the enthusiast's pick. Its standout feature is GPS-based automatic opening — the door opens as you approach your driveway and closes after you pull in, all hands-free. No button press, no phone fumbling. It uses your phone's location to trigger the action, and you can set the geofence radius to your preference.

It also supports vehicle-specific detection if you have multiple cars with different phones, so the garage only opens for authorized devices. For a Miami collector with a rotation of cars, this is incredibly useful.

HomeKit, Alexa, Google Home, and SmartThings are all natively supported. No subscription required.

Check price on Amazon →

Best Premium Wall-Mount: LiftMaster 87504-267

For collectors building out a dream garage, the LiftMaster 87504-267 is the premium choice. It's a wall-mount design that frees up ceiling space — useful if you have a car lift or high shelving. The jackshaft motor mounts on the wall beside the door rather than on the ceiling, which also eliminates the rail and trolley that obstruct overhead space.

It includes myQ smart technology, a battery backup, and an integrated deadbolt for additional security. The wall-mount design also makes it compatible with high-lift and vertical-lift garage doors, which some custom garages use.

At $400–$500, it's the most expensive option, but for a purpose-built collector garage, the space savings and security features justify the premium.

Check price on Amazon →

Best Budget Smart Control: Meross Smart Garage Door Opener

The Meross MSG100 is the value play. At around $40, it adds HomeKit, Alexa, and Google Home control to any existing opener. It's similar in concept to the myQ controller but with native HomeKit support — no bridge required. Setup takes about 10 minutes.

The trade-off is build quality and app polish. The Meross app isn't as refined as myQ or Tailwind, and the hardware feels less premium. But functionally, it does exactly what you need: remote open/close, status monitoring, and alerts.

Check price on Amazon →

Smart Garage Features That Matter for Miami

Not all smart garage features are equally useful. Here's what actually matters for South Florida car owners:

FeatureWhy It Matters in MiamiWhich Products Have It
Battery backupHurricane power outages can last days. Battery backup means you can still access your cars.Chamberlain B6753T, LiftMaster 87504
Auto-close timerMiami heat means you want the door closed ASAP to keep garage temps manageable.All listed products
Real-time alertsTheft prevention — know immediately if someone opens your garage.All listed products
Camera integrationVisual confirmation of who/what is in your garage. Pairs with existing security systems.iSmartGate Pro, LiftMaster (via myQ camera)
GPS auto-openHands-free access when you pull up — no fumbling with remotes in the rain.Tailwind iQ3
Multi-door supportMost collector garages have 2-3 doors minimum.iSmartGate Pro (3 doors), Tailwind iQ3 (3 doors)

Installation Tips for Miami Garages

  • Wi-Fi range matters: Detached garages or large properties may need a Wi-Fi extender to reach the opener. Test signal strength before installing.
  • Humidity-proof your electronics: Miami's humidity can corrode circuit boards over time. If your garage isn't climate-controlled, consider a small dehumidifier near the opener.
  • Pair with a smart lock on the interior door: A smart garage opener + a smart deadbolt on the garage-to-house door creates a two-layer security system.
  • Add a garage door sensor to your alarm system: Most smart home security systems (Ring, SimpliSafe, ADT) can integrate with myQ or HomeKit-compatible openers for monitored alerts.

Bottom Line

For most Miami car collectors, the Chamberlain B6753T is the best full replacement opener — quiet, smart, battery backup, and reliable. If you just want to add smarts to an existing opener, the Tailwind iQ3 is worth the premium for its GPS auto-open feature, or grab the myQ controller if you want the basics for under $50.

Your cars are worth protecting. A smart garage door opener is one of the simplest, most cost-effective upgrades you can make — and in Miami, where garage break-ins and power outages are facts of life, it's not a luxury. It's common sense.
