GR Supra Launch Edition (used)2020$55,000–$70,000Limited to 1,500 units, collector premium

Market insight: The manual transmission models (A91-MT and later) command a $3,000–$5,000 premium over automatic equivalents. In Miami's market, this gap is even wider because manual Supras are genuinely scarce — most Florida buyers opted for automatic. If you find a manual, especially in a desirable color, don't hesitate.

Toyota GR Supra 3.0 vs 2.0: Which Engine for Miami?

This is the biggest decision Supra buyers face, and the answer depends on what you want:

The 3.0L Turbo Inline-Six (B58): The Default Choice

The BMW-sourced B58 is one of the best engines in any sports car under $60K. It makes 382 hp and 368 lb-ft in 2026 spec, it's silky smooth at low RPM, and it responds to tuning like nothing else in its class. A simple flash tune gets you to 420+ hp; bolt-ons and a tune push 500 hp on stock internals.

  • 0-60: 3.9 seconds (auto), ~4.1 seconds (manual)
  • Miami factor: Plenty of power for highway pulls, enough torque for low-speed cruising through South Beach
  • Tuning ceiling: 700+ hp with built internals and a big turbo — the Miami tuner community has proven this repeatedly

The 2.0L Turbo Four-Cylinder (B48): The Sleeper Pick

Everyone overlooks the 2.0, and that's exactly why it's interesting. It's 200 lbs lighter than the 3.0, which transforms the car's handling balance. At $32K–$40K used, it's one of the best sports car values in Miami.

  • 0-60: 5.0 seconds (stock), mid-4s with a tune
  • Miami factor: Better fuel economy (30+ mpg highway), lighter front end = more agile in Miami's tight streets
  • Tuning ceiling: ~350 hp on stock internals — enough for 90% of drivers

Where to Buy a Toyota GR Supra in Miami

Toyota Franchise Dealers

  • South Dade Toyota (26300 S Dixie Hwy, Homestead) — Consistently has Supra inventory, including manual models
  • Earl Stewart Toyota (1215 US-1, North Palm Beach) — No-markup policy, worth the drive
  • Toyota of Hollywood (3100 N 29th Ave, Hollywood) — Good selection of CPO Supras
  • Kendall Toyota (13700 S Dixie Hwy, Pinecrest) — Large volume dealer, competitive pricing

JDM & Tuner Specialists

  • Import shops along NW 27th Ave — Miami's unofficial JDM row, some carry modified Supras
  • Tuner-focused meets (Supercar Saturdays, Ace Cafe Orlando runs) — Private sales from knowledgeable owners
  • Supra Forums & Facebook Groups — "MK5 Supra Owners Florida" group is active with 2,000+ members

Online Platforms

  • Cars & Bids — Excellent for stock and lightly modified Supras with full history
  • Bring a Trailer — Launch Editions and special specs do well here
  • Toyota Certified Used — CPO Supras include 12-month/12K-mile comprehensive warranty

GR Supra Inspection Checklist: What to Look For

The Supra is mechanically solid, but Miami introduces specific concerns:

CheckWhy It MattersCost If Missed
Differential fluid conditionHeat cycling in Miami traffic degrades fluid faster$200–$400 (service)
Coolant hose condition (3.0L)Known weak point on early 2020–2021 models$500–$1,200
Check for prior modificationsMany Supras have been tuned — check ECU flash historyWarranty void risk
Undercarriage salt corrosionCoastal Miami salt spray, especially convertible-belt carsVaries
Brake rotor conditionMiami heat + aggressive driving = faster rotor wear$1,500–$2,500 for all four
Clutch wear (manual models)Miami traffic is brutal on manual clutches$2,000–$3,000

Key tip: If buying a used Supra, always request the Toyota vehicle history report. Many Supras have been tuned and de-tuned before sale — a pre-purchase inspection by a shop with ECU scanning capability (like BimmerTech Miami, since the drivetrain is BMW) is worth every penny.

The GR Supra in Miami's Tuner Culture

The Supra isn't just a sports car in Miami — it's a cultural statement. The A90/A91 has reignited Miami's JDM scene in a way no other car has since the Nissan GT-R's heyday.

  • Monthly meets: Modified Supras are a staple at Supercar Saturdays Bal Harbour and Ace Cafe meets
  • Local tuner shops: Multiple Miami shops specialize in B58 tuning — PBD Performance, Formula Motorsports, and others offer packages from street tunes to full builds
  • Track presence: Homestead-Miami Speedway's open track days regularly feature Supras pushing 9-second quarter miles
  • Community: The Florida Supra community is tight-knit and welcoming to newcomers

GR Supra vs. the Competition in Miami

CarPrice (New)HP0-60Manual AvailableMiami Verdict
Toyota GR Supra 3.0$55,0003823.9sYesBest tuning platform, strong resale
Nissan Z Performance$50,0004004.5sYesMore power, worse transmission, less refined
BMW M2$64,0004533.9sYesMore power, same B58 platform, bigger
Porsche 718 Cayman GTS$82,0003943.9sYesBetter handling, much more expensive
Ford Mustang Dark Horse$60,0005004.0sYesV8 sound, less refined, heavier
Chevrolet Corvette Stingray$66,0004902.9sNoFaster, mid-engine, but different vibe

Owning a GR Supra in Miami: What It Actually Costs

  • Insurance: $1,800–$3,200/year (Miami rates, clean record, age 25+)
  • Maintenance: $800–$1,500/year — Toyota reliability with BMW parts pricing
  • Tires: $800–$1,200 per set (staggered, Michelin PS4S or Continental EC7)
  • Fuel: Premium required, ~$2,400–$3,000/year at 12K miles
  • Depreciation (3.0 new): ~12–15% year one, stabilizing — Supras hold value well

The Supra's running costs are notably lower than European rivals. Toyota's warranty is 3 years/36K miles bumper-to-bumper and 5 years/60K miles powertrain — competitive for the segment and dramatically better than what you'd get from a Nissan GT-R at similar money.

Bottom Line: Should You Buy a GR Supra in Miami?

The Toyota GR Supra is the rare modern sports car that's genuinely fun to drive stock, wildly tuneable for those who want more, and reliable enough to daily in Miami traffic without anxiety. The manual transmission option sealed the deal for enthusiasts, and used prices in the high-$30Ks make it one of the best sports car values in South Florida.

If you're part of Miami's tuner and JDM community — or want to be — the Supra is your entry point. If you just want a great sports car that handles everything from Brickell commutes to Keys road trips, it does that too. Miami has solid inventory on both new and used models right now, and 2026 is a buyer's market.

title: Ferrari 12Cilindri: Specs, Price & What Miami Buyers Need to Know in 2026
excerpt: Ferrari's newest front-engine V12 grand tourer replaces the 812 Superfast with 830 horsepower, a 9,500 RPM redline, and styling that splits opinion. Here's everything Miami buyers need to know about specs, pricing, allocations, and when deliveries begin.
content:
The Ferrari 12Cilindri is Ferrari's definitive statement that the naturally aspirated V12 isn't going anywhere — not yet. Unveiled in mid-2024 as the successor to the 812 Superfast and 812 Competizione, the 12Cilindri (Italian for "12 cylinders," in case the name wasn't blunt enough) is a front-engine, rear-wheel-drive grand tourer built around Ferrari's most powerful road-going naturally aspirated engine ever. For Miami buyers who've been waiting for the next chapter in Ferrari's V12 lineage, this is the car — and understanding specs, pricing, and the allocation process now will matter when deliveries hit South Florida showrooms.

This guide covers everything about the Ferrari 12Cilindri: full specifications, how it compares to the 812 it replaces, expected pricing in Miami, the allocation and ordering process, and what to watch for if you're trying to get one.

Ferrari 12Cilindri Specs: The Numbers That Matter

The 12Cilindri is built on a new platform that carries forward the front-mid-mounted V12, rear-transaxle layout Ferrari has perfected over decades. But nearly everything has been reworked.

SpecificationFerrari 12CilindriFerrari 12Cilindri Spider
Engine6.5L naturally aspirated V12 (F140HD)
Power830 hp @ 9,250 RPM
Torque678 lb-ft @ 7,250 RPM
Redline9,500 RPM
Transmission8-speed dual-clutch (rear-mounted transaxle)
DrivetrainRear-wheel drive
0-60 mph2.9 seconds2.9 seconds
0-124 mph7.9 seconds8.2 seconds
Top Speed211 mph206 mph
Weight (dry)3,450 lbs3,550 lbs
Wheelbase107.1 inches
Length184.8 inches

The headline is that 6.5-liter V12. It's an evolution of the F140 engine family that's powered every front-engine Ferrari V12 since the Enzo, but it's been extensively revised: new intake runners, redesigned combustion chambers, a higher compression ratio, and revised cam timing all contribute to the 18-horsepower bump over the 812 Superfast (and the same output as the limited-run 812 Competizione). The torque curve is broader, with 80% of peak torque available from 2,500 RPM — unusual for a high-revving naturally aspirated engine.

Ferrari 12Cilindri Design: A Departure From the 812

The 12Cilindri's design has been the most discussed aspect of the car since its reveal. Ferrari's design team, led by Flavio Manzoni, took a deliberately clean, almost minimalist approach that breaks sharply from the aggressive aero sculpting of the 812. The front end features a full-width light bar (a first for a Ferrari road car), a smooth hood with minimal vents, and a face that's more GT than supercar. The rear is equally clean — a horizontal taillight strip, a functional diffuser, and quad exhaust tips integrated into the lower bumper.

Opinions are divided. Some enthusiasts think it looks like a design study for a different brand; others see it as Ferrari maturing into a new design language that will age well. What's not debatable: it photographs beautifully from certain angles and looks substantially different from anything else on the road. In a Miami context — where standing out at Bal Harbour or on Collins Avenue matters — the 12Cilindri will turn heads precisely because it doesn't look like the "typical" Ferrari.

Ferrari 12Cilindri Interior and Technology

Inside, the 12Cilindri continues Ferrari's recent trend toward digital cockpits with minimal physical buttons. The key features:

  • Dual-screen layout: A 15.6-inch curved digital instrument cluster for the driver, plus an optional 8.8-inch passenger display that shows speed, RPM, navigation, and media controls
  • Capacitive touch controls: Climate, driving modes, and infotainment managed through haptic touch surfaces on the center bridge and steering wheel
  • New steering wheel: Smaller diameter, with integrated shift lights, turn signal controls, and driving mode selectors — no column stalks
  • Improved trunk space: 17.3 cubic feet in the coupe (nearly double the 812), making it a genuinely usable GT car for weekend trips
  • Sound system: Burmester high-end option available for the first time in a Ferrari V12 car

The passenger display is the standout feature for Miami owners who do a lot of co-pilot driving — partners and passengers can follow the route, see what gear the car is in, and control media without touching the driver's screen.

Ferrari 12Cilindri Price: What Miami Buyers Will Pay

Ferrari hasn't published official MSRP for the U.S. market as of early 2026, but based on European pricing, dealer intelligence, and Ferrari's recent pricing strategy, here's what to expect:

ModelExpected Base MSRP (USD)Typical As-Configured (Miami)
12Cilindri Coupe$425,000–$445,000$500,000–$550,000
12Cilindri Spider$470,000–$490,000$550,000–$620,000

For context, the 812 Superfast launched at $335,275 and ended production around $398,000 before options. The 12Cilindri represents a meaningful price increase — roughly 15–20% — reflecting Ferrari's ongoing strategy to move upmarket. Options will easily add $75,000–$125,000: custom paint (Tailor Made programs start at $25,000+), carbon fiber packages, special leather hides, and the passenger display are all extra.

Will There Be a Markup Over MSRP?

Almost certainly — at least initially. The 812 Competizione and SF90 XX Stradale both commanded significant markups when new, and the 12Cilindri is the only naturally aspirated V12 GT car left on the market (Aston Martin's V12 Vantage is sold out; Lamborghini has moved to hybrid). Miami's Ferrari dealership — The Collection in Coral Gables — will likely see strong demand from local collectors. Expect $50,000–$150,000 over sticker for early production slots, settling to MSRP or modest markups within 18–24 months of first deliveries.

Ferrari 12Cilindri Allocation: How to Get One in Miami

Ferrari's allocation system has become increasingly strict. Here's what matters:

  • Existing client priority: Buyers who've purchased new Ferraris from an authorized dealer (especially The Collection or other South Florida dealers) will get first access. If you've bought one or two new Ferraris in the past five years, you have a reasonable shot at an early allocation.
  • No walk-in orders: You cannot simply walk into The Collection and order a 12Cilindri. Production slots are allocated to dealers, who then offer them to their best clients.
  • Build slot timing: First U.S. deliveries are expected in late 2025 / early 2026. If you haven't already secured a slot, realistic delivery timing is late 2026 to mid-2027.
  • Spider vs. Coupe allocation: The Spider typically has a longer wait — Ferrari often prioritizes coupe production initially. Miami buyers tend to want the Spider (obviously), which means even more competition for those slots.

Ferrari 12Cilindri vs. 812 Superfast: What Changed

Feature812 Superfast12Cilindri
Power789 hp830 hp (+41)
Torque530 lb-ft678 lb-ft (+148)
Transmission7-speed DCT8-speed DCT
0-60 mph2.9 sec2.9 sec
Top Speed211 mph211 mph
Weight (dry)3,362 lbs3,450 lbs
Trunk Space~9 cu ft17.3 cu ft
Rear-Wheel SteeringYes (Virtual Short Wheelbase)Yes (evolved system)
Design LanguageAggressive, sculptedClean, minimalist

The biggest mechanical improvement is the torque increase — 148 more lb-ft makes the 12Cilindri significantly more flexible in everyday driving. The new 8-speed gearbox is smoother and allows Ferrari to keep the engine in its powerband across a wider speed range. Weight has increased slightly, but the chassis rigidity is up 15%, and the suspension geometry is entirely new with adaptive magnetorheological dampers as standard.

Ferrari 12Cilindri for Miami: Why It Makes Sense

Miami and front-engine Ferrari V12s have a long history together. The 550 Maranello, 599 GTB, F12, and 812 Superfast all became fixtures of the South Florida car scene because they offer something Lamborghinis and mid-engine Ferraris don't: genuine grand touring comfort with supercar performance. You can drive a 12Cilindri from Miami to Key West without needing a chiropractor afterward. You can load golf clubs in the trunk. You can have a normal conversation at highway speed.

The Spider variant is the obvious choice for Miami. The retractable hardtop folds in 14 seconds, the cabin is well-insulated at speed, and the V12 soundtrack — which is the real reason anyone buys this car — is spectacular with the roof down. On a warm evening on the MacArthur Causeway, with 830 naturally aspirated horsepower behind you and Biscayne Bay beside you, the 12Cilindri Spider will be hard to beat.

Should You Wait for the 12Cilindri or Buy an 812?

This depends on your priorities:

  • Buy an 812 Superfast now if: You want immediate availability, proven reliability, aggressive styling, and potentially lower total cost. Clean 812s with under 10,000 miles trade in the $350,000–$420,000 range in Miami right now — well below what a 12Cilindri will cost.
  • Buy an 812 Competizione if you can find one: The Comp is the more extreme, track-focused V12 and will almost certainly appreciate. They're trading above $800,000 and climbing.
  • Wait for the 12Cilindri if: You want the latest technology, the most powerful NA V12 Ferrari has ever made, the improved interior, and you have the dealer relationship to secure an allocation.

There's also a collector argument: the 12Cilindri may be the last naturally aspirated V12 Ferrari ever makes. EU emissions regulations are tightening, and Ferrari's next-generation models are increasingly electrified. If that turns out to be true, early 12Cilindri examples — especially Spiders in desirable specs — could become very collectible.

Where to See and Order the Ferrari 12Cilindri in Miami

Miami's authorized Ferrari dealer is The Collection in Coral Gables (200 Bird Road). They handle all new Ferrari sales, service, and allocation requests for the greater Miami area. If you're a new customer, the best approach is to contact their sales team, express interest in the 12Cilindri, and discuss what your path to an allocation looks like — which typically means purchasing a current-production Ferrari first (Roma, 296 GTB, or Purosangue).

For those who can't wait, early 12Cilindri allocations will inevitably appear on the secondary market through consignment dealers along Biscayne Boulevard and in the Design District. Expect to pay a premium of $50,000–$150,000 over sticker for the first year of production.

Ferrari 12Cilindri: The Bottom Line for Miami Buyers

The Ferrari 12Cilindri is the most powerful, most refined, and most technologically advanced front-engine V12 Ferrari has ever built. Whether its divisive styling works for you is a personal call — but the driving experience, by all early accounts, is extraordinary. The naturally aspirated V12 at 9,500 RPM is one of the last great automotive sounds, and Ferrari has wrapped it in a grand tourer that's more livable, more practical, and more comfortable than the car it replaces.

For Miami buyers, the key decisions are simple: coupe or Spider (Spider, obviously), and whether you have the dealer relationship to secure an allocation at MSRP. If you do, the 12Cilindri is one of the most compelling new Ferraris in years. If you don't, the 812 Superfast remains a spectacular alternative — and it's available right now.

title: Mercedes-AMG SL for Sale in Miami: 2026 Pricing, Models & Buyer's Guide
excerpt: The Mercedes-AMG SL is back — a twin-turbo roadster with AMG DNA, a folding soft top, and optional all-wheel drive. Here's every model, what they cost in Miami in 2026, what to inspect, and where to find the best examples.
content:
The Mercedes-AMG SL returned for 2022 as a completely new car — developed entirely by AMG for the first time in the nameplate's 70-year history. Gone is the folding hardtop; in its place is a lightweight fabric soft top. Gone is the old comfort-biased chassis; the new SL rides on AMG's modular sports car platform with standard all-wheel drive on most variants. And gone is the idea that the SL is a boulevard cruiser — this generation is a genuine performance roadster that happens to be comfortable enough for a Miami beach drive.

If you're looking for a Mercedes-AMG SL for sale in Miami, this guide covers everything: every model variant from the SL 43 to the SL 63 S E Performance, current 2026 pricing on new and used examples, what to inspect before buying, and where to find the best cars in South Florida.

Mercedes-AMG SL Models: Every Variant Explained

The R232-generation SL launched in 2022 and has expanded into a full range. Here's every version available:

ModelEnginePowerDrivetrain0-60 mphBase MSRP
AMG SL 432.0L turbo-4 + e-turbo381 hp / 354 lb-ftRWD4.8 sec$104,900
AMG SL 554.0L twin-turbo V8469 hp / 516 lb-ftAWD (4MATIC+)3.7 sec$137,400
AMG SL 634.0L twin-turbo V8577 hp / 590 lb-ftAWD (4MATIC+)3.5 sec$178,950
AMG SL 63 S E Performance4.0L TT V8 + electric motor805 hp / 1,055 lb-ftAWD (P3 hybrid)2.9 sec$252,900

The SL 43 is the entry point — and the only rear-wheel-drive model, using AMG's 2.0-liter four-cylinder with an electric exhaust-gas turbocharger (the same technology from the AMG One hypercar, scaled down). It's genuinely quick, but the V8 models are where the SL becomes special. The SL 55 is the sweet spot for most buyers: 469 horsepower, all-wheel drive, and a price that's roughly $40,000 less than the SL 63. The SL 63 adds more power, a louder exhaust, and upgraded brakes. The range-topping SL 63 S E Performance is a plug-in hybrid with 805 combined horsepower — making it the most powerful SL ever built.

Mercedes-AMG SL Price in Miami: What They Cost in 2026

The SL has been in production long enough now that used examples are plentiful, and new inventory is available at Miami dealers without the markups that plagued 2022–2023 deliveries. Here's the current market:

New 2025/2026 Models

ModelBase MSRPTypical As-Configured (Miami)
SL 43$104,900$115,000–$125,000
SL 55$137,400$150,000–$170,000
SL 63$178,950$195,000–$225,000
SL 63 S E Performance$252,900$270,000–$300,000

Used / Pre-Owned (2022–2024 Models)

Model / YearMileage RangePrice Range (Miami 2026)
2022–2023 SL 558,000–25,000 mi$105,000–$130,000
2022–2023 SL 635,000–20,000 mi$140,000–$175,000
2024 SL 553,000–12,000 mi$120,000–$145,000
2024 SL 632,000–10,000 mi$155,000–$195,000
2024 SL 63 S E PerformanceUnder 5,000 mi$220,000–$260,000

The depreciation curve on the SL 55 is favorable for used buyers — 2022 models with 15,000–20,000 miles have dropped to the low $100,000s, which is genuine performance roadster territory. The SL 63 holds value better due to stronger demand and the V8's appeal. The E Performance is too new for meaningful depreciation data, but expect it to hold well given its limited production numbers.

Mercedes-AMG SL vs. Competitors in Miami

The SL competes in a segment that's both narrow and deep. Here's how it stacks up against what Miami buyers typically cross-shop:

CarPower0-60Price RangeKey Difference
AMG SL 63577 hp3.5 sec$178K–$225K2+2 seating, folding top, luxury focus
Porsche 911 Turbo S Cabriolet640 hp2.7 sec$230K–$270KFaster, tighter, less luxurious
BMW M8 Convertible617 hp3.0 sec$140K–$160KValue play, less prestigious
Aston Martin DB12 Volante671 hp3.5 sec$260K–$300KMore exotic, less practical
Ferrari Roma Spider612 hp3.2 sec$300K+Different league entirely, more exclusive

The SL's unique advantage is that it's the only car here with genuine 2+2 seating (the rear seats are small but usable for kids or bags), a fully powered soft top that operates at up to 37 mph, and Mercedes' full suite of driver assistance technology including Level 2 semi-autonomous driving. For Miami buyers who want a performance roadster they can also use as a daily driver, the SL has no real equal.

What to Inspect Before Buying a Used AMG SL

The R232 SL is mechanically robust, but there are specific things Miami buyers should check:

Soft Top Condition

The fabric roof is acoustically insulated and well-engineered, but Miami's UV exposure and salt air can stress any soft top over time. Check for fading, ensure the mechanism operates smoothly at least three times in sequence, and inspect the rear window (heated glass) for any delamination at the edges. Replacement cost: $8,000–$12,000 installed.

Brake Wear

The SL 55 and SL 63 both offer optional carbon-ceramic brakes ($5,990 option on the SL 55, $8,950 on the SL 63). If the car has them, inspect for cracking or glazing. If it has the standard steel brakes, check pad and rotor thickness — Miami's stop-and-go traffic eats brakes. Standard brake replacement runs $3,000–$5,000; carbon-ceramic rotors are $12,000–$18,000 per set.

AMG RIDE CONTROL+ Suspension

All V8 SLs come with AMG's active suspension. Listen for any clunking over bumps, and test all driving modes (Comfort, Sport, Sport+, Race, and Individual). If a damper has failed, the car will feel noticeably unsettled on one corner. Replacement cost per damper: $2,500–$4,000.

MBUX Infotainment

The SL features a large central touchscreen that tilts automatically to reduce glare when the roof is down. Verify the tilt mechanism works, test the wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto connections, and ensure the Burmester 3D surround system (if equipped) plays through all speakers. Software bugs in early 2022 models have been addressed through OTA updates — confirm the car is running the latest software version.

Service History

Mercedes-AMG recommends service every 10,000 miles or 12 months. For a used SL, you want to see full dealer service records — ideally from an authorized Mercedes-Benz dealer. The AMG-specific items (transmission fluid, differential fluid, and brake fluid) should be documented. Miami heat is hard on transmission fluid in particular; if the car has been tracked or driven aggressively, the fluid should have been changed more frequently.

Best AMG SL Configurations for Miami

If you're ordering new or choosing between used examples, here's what works best in South Florida:

  • Best value: SL 55 with the Premium Package and AMG Night Package. The V8 soundtrack, all-wheel drive grip, and $137K starting price make it the sweet spot. Skip the SL 43 — the four-cylinder doesn't match the car's character.
  • Best daily driver: SL 55 with the Driver Assistance Package, which adds adaptive cruise with stop-and-go, lane keeping, and active steering assist. Miami traffic is brutal; let the car handle the I-95 crawl.
  • Best performance: SL 63 S E Performance. 805 horsepower, torque-fill from the electric motor that eliminates turbo lag, and the ability to run in electric-only mode for short distances (school zones, valet approaches, quiet departures at 6 AM).
  • Best color for Miami: Manufaktur Patagonia Red, OPALITH White Bright, or Spectral Blue. The AMG-specific colors stand out without being garish. Avoid black — it's brutally hot in Miami sun.

AMG SL Running Costs in Miami

Ownership costs for the SL in Miami break down as follows:

Cost CategorySL 55 (Annual Est.)SL 63 (Annual Est.)
Insurance$3,500–$5,500$4,500–$7,000
Maintenance (Service A/B)$1,200–$2,000$1,500–$2,500
Tires (per set)$1,600–$2,200$1,800–$2,600
Fuel (12K mi/yr, premium)$3,800–$4,500$4,200–$5,000
Registration (FL)$400–$600$400–$600

Total annual ownership cost (excluding depreciation) runs roughly $10,000–$14,000 for the SL 55 and $12,000–$17,000 for the SL 63. That's competitive with Porsche and less than comparable Ferrari or Aston Martin models. Mercedes-Benz also offers a prepaid maintenance plan that locks in service costs for up to four years — worth considering if you're buying new.

Where to Buy a Mercedes-AMG SL in Miami

Miami has several authorized Mercedes-Benz dealers with strong AMG inventory:

  • Mercedes-Benz of Miami (1200 NW 167th Street) — Full AMG lineup, typically the largest new SL inventory in South Florida
  • Mercedes-Benz of Coral Gables (300 Almeria Avenue) — Strong pre-owned selection, good service department
  • The Collection (200 Bird Road, Coral Gables) — Carries Mercedes-Benz alongside Ferrari, Porsche, and others; tends to have higher-spec examples
  • Mercedes-Benz of Cutler Bay — Growing AMG presence, sometimes has allocation availability that larger dealers don't

For used examples, also check the independent luxury dealers along Biscayne Boulevard in the Design District — shops like Prestige Imports and South Beach Exotic Rentals (which sells its fleet cars periodically) often have well-maintained SLs at competitive prices. Florida's no-state-income-tax status means many SLs are registered here even if driven elsewhere — which means more inventory but also more cars that may have been garaged in a different climate.

Mercedes-AMG SL: The Bottom Line for Miami Buyers

The current-generation Mercedes-AMG SL is the best SL in decades — maybe ever. It's faster, sharper, and more engaging than any SL since the original 300SL, while still being comfortable and refined enough for daily driving in Miami traffic. The SL 55 is the model most buyers should start with: it has more than enough power, all-wheel drive security for Miami's sudden rainstorms, and a price that undercuts comparable Porsche and Aston Martin convertibles.

For used buyers, 2022–2023 SL 55s in the $105,000–$130,000 range represent exceptional value — a twin-turbo V8 AMG roadster with folding top and 2+2 seating for the price of a well-equipped GLE. Whether new or used, the AMG SL is one of the best open-top performance cars you can buy in Miami right now — and one of the few that works as well on the highway to Key Largo as it does on a Saturday night in Wynwood.

title: Best Ceramic Window Tint Film for Cars in Miami — Block the Heat, Keep the Clarity (2026)
excerpt: Miami's sun is relentless and ceramic window tint is non-negotiable for exotic car owners. Here are the best ceramic tint films you can buy — from DIY rolls to professional-grade kits — with real product picks and what to know before you commit.
content:
If you own a car in Miami and haven't tinted your windows with ceramic film, you're either brand new here or you enjoy feeling like a rotisserie chicken every time you get in your car. Standard dyed tint fades, metallic tint interferes with electronics, and cheap stuff bubbles within a year of Florida sun exposure. Ceramic window tint is the only serious option — and for exotic car owners, it's as essential as insurance.

Ceramic tint uses nano-ceramic particles embedded in the film to reject infrared heat without blocking radio signals, GPS, or toll transponders. It doesn't fade, doesn't turn purple, and delivers dramatically better heat rejection than dyed or metallic alternatives. In a city where interior temperatures can hit 170°F on a parked car, that matters.

Here's what to buy, what to know, and how to make the right choice for your car in Miami.

Best Ceramic Window Tint Films for Miami Cars

ProductHeat RejectionUV BlockBest ForPrice Range
3M Ceramic IR SeriesUp to 66%99.9%Professional-grade, best overall performance$150–$350/roll
XPEL PRIME XR PlusUp to 98% IR99%Maximum heat rejection for Miami exotics$200–$400/roll
MotoShield Pro Nano CeramicUp to 99% IR99%Best DIY option, pre-cut kits available$80–$180/roll
Llumar CTX SeriesUp to 59%99%Trusted installer brand, excellent clarity$150–$300/roll
Gila Ceramic Window FilmUp to 46%99%Budget-friendly ceramic, available at retail$40–$80/roll
FormulaOne PinnacleUp to 62% TSER99%Premium clarity, color-stable for years$180–$350/roll

Why Ceramic Tint Is Non-Negotiable in Miami

Let's be specific about what Miami's climate does to your car without proper tint:

  • Interior damage: UV radiation degrades leather, Alcantara, carbon fiber trim, and dashboard surfaces. A Ferrari Roma's interior costs $15,000+ to retrim. Ceramic tint blocks 99%+ of UV rays.
  • Cabin temperature: Without tint, a parked car's interior can exceed 170°F in Miami's direct sun. Ceramic tint can reduce interior temps by 20–30°F, which means your seats are actually touchable when you get back in.
  • A/C load: Your car's air conditioning works harder without tint, which affects fuel economy and puts extra strain on the compressor — a $2,000+ repair on most exotics.
  • Glare reduction: Miami's reflective surfaces — water, white buildings, glass towers — create intense glare. Ceramic tint cuts glare significantly without making nighttime driving dangerous.
  • Privacy: In a city where car theft and break-ins are real concerns, tinted windows keep valuables out of sight.

Florida Window Tint Laws: What's Legal in Miami

Before you slap the darkest film you can find on every window, know the law. Florida tint regulations for sedans and SUVs differ:

WindowSedansSUVs/Vans
WindshieldNon-reflective tint above AS-1 line onlyNon-reflective tint above AS-1 line only
Front side windowsMust allow 28%+ light inMust allow 28%+ light in
Rear side windowsMust allow 15%+ light inAny darkness allowed
Rear windowMust allow 15%+ light inAny darkness allowed

Pro tip: Most Miami exotic car owners run 15–20% on the sides and 5% on the rear. Enforcement is inconsistent, but getting pulled over is a real hassle. The sweet spot for most owners is 20% ceramic on the front, 5–15% on the rear — dark enough to matter, legal enough to avoid tickets.

Ceramic vs. Dyed vs. Metallic vs. Carbon Tint: The Miami Breakdown

Tint TypeHeat RejectionUV ProtectionSignal InterferenceDurability in FL SunPrice
DyedLow (20–30%)ModerateNone2–4 years before fading$
MetallicGood (40–50%)GoodYes — GPS, phone, toll tags5–8 years$$
CarbonGood (40–55%)GoodNone6–10 years$$
CeramicExcellent (50–98%)99%+None10+ years, no fading$$$

For exotic cars, the signal interference issue alone disqualifies metallic tint. Modern supercars rely on GPS, Bluetooth, radar detectors, toll transponders, and sometimes cellular connections for telemetry. Metallic tint can degrade all of these. Ceramic is the only tint technology that delivers premium heat rejection without touching your electronics.

Product Deep Dives: Our Top Picks

Best Overall: XPEL PRIME XR Plus

The XPEL PRIME XR Plus is what most high-end Miami tint shops install on Ferraris, Lamborghinis, and Rolls-Royces. It rejects up to 98% of infrared heat — that's not marketing fluff, it's measurably the best heat rejection available in a window film. The clarity is exceptional (no haze, no color shift), and XPEL's warranty is industry-leading.

The downside? Price. A full professional installation on an exotic car runs $800–$1,500 in Miami. But if you're driving a $300K car in 95°F heat, this isn't where you cut corners.

Best Value Professional: 3M Ceramic IR Series

The 3M Ceramic IR is the workhorse of Miami tint shops. Slightly lower heat rejection than the XPEL XR Plus (66% vs. 98% IR), but significantly more affordable and still dramatically better than any non-ceramic option. 3M's manufacturing consistency is excellent — you won't get batch-to-batch color variations like with some cheaper brands.

Professional installation in Miami: $500–$900 for a full car. The film itself is available on Amazon for DIYers, though we'd recommend professional installation for exotic cars (more on that below).

Best for DIY Installation: MotoShield Pro Nano Ceramic

If you're handy with a squeegee and have patience, MotoShield Pro offers excellent ceramic performance at a fraction of the professional install price. They sell pre-cut kits for most popular vehicles, which eliminates the hardest part of DIY tinting — cutting the film to fit. Heat rejection specs are genuinely impressive (up to 99% IR claimed), and the film handles Miami sun without degrading.

The catch: DIY tint installation on curved exotic car glass (like a Lamborghini Huracán's aggressive rear window) is genuinely difficult. For a daily driver or second car, MotoShield Pro is a fantastic choice. For your six-figure exotic, pay a professional.

Best Budget Ceramic: Gila Ceramic Window Film

Gila's ceramic film is available at major retailers and Amazon, making it the most accessible ceramic option. It won't match the heat rejection of XPEL or 3M, but it's a massive upgrade over dyed film and costs a fraction of the premium options. For a second car, a daily driver, or anyone who wants ceramic performance without the premium price, Gila delivers.

Essential Installation Tools & Accessories

Whether you're DIYing or just want to understand what your installer should be using:

ToolWhat It DoesPrice Range

Wagner Furno Heat GunShrinks film to curved glass without bubbles$30–$80
Tint Application SolutionSlip solution for positioning film before squeegeeing$8–$15
Olfa Precision KnifeClean, precise cuts around gaskets and edges$10–$20

Professional vs. DIY Installation in Miami: The Real Cost

ApproachCost (Full Car)TimeQualityWarranty
DIY with MotoShield Pro$80–$1804–8 hoursDepends on skill levelProduct warranty only
Professional with 3M Ceramic IR$500–$9002–4 hoursExcellentProduct + labor warranty
Professional with XPEL XR Plus$800–$1,5002–4 hoursPremiumFull manufacturer + shop warranty

For exotic cars, we strongly recommend professional installation. The curved, complex glass on modern supercars (McLarens, Ferraris, Lamborghinis) requires experienced hands and proper heat-shrinking technique. A bad tint job on a $250K car looks terrible and can damage window defroster elements. Most reputable Miami tint shops offer lifetime warranties on their work.

Top Miami Tint Shops for Exotic Cars

  • Tint World (Multiple Miami Locations): National chain with consistent quality. They carry 3M and Llumar ceramic lines. Good for daily drivers and luxury SUVs.
  • Advanced Window Tinting (Doral): Specializes in exotic cars. They stock XPEL PRIME XR Plus and have experience with complex glass shapes. Popular with Ferrari and Lamborghini owners.
  • Prestige Auto Spa (Coral Gables): Full detailing and PPF shop that also does ceramic tint. Convenient if you're getting PPF and tint done together — and you should be.

Ceramic Tint + PPF + Ceramic Coating: The Miami Triple Protection Stack

Smart exotic car owners in Miami don't do just one protective treatment — they do all three:

  1. Ceramic window tint: Heat rejection, UV protection, privacy
  2. Paint protection film (PPF): Rock chip and scratch protection for exterior paint
  3. Ceramic coating: Hydrophobic surface protection and gloss enhancement

Done together, this "triple stack" typically costs $3,000–$8,000 depending on the car and products used. It's a real investment, but it preserves resale value, reduces maintenance time, and keeps your car looking factory-fresh in a climate that actively tries to destroy automotive paint and interiors every single day.

Should You Buy Ceramic Window Tint for Your Miami Car?

Absolutely, unequivocally, yes. It's not a luxury in Miami — it's maintenance. The sun here will fade your interior, crack your dashboard, and make your car feel like the inside of a pizza oven from April through October. Ceramic tint solves all of that while preserving your electronics, your visibility, and your sanity.

For exotic car owners: go with XPEL PRIME XR Plus installed professionally. For daily drivers and second cars: MotoShield Pro DIY kits deliver 90% of the performance at 20% of the cost. Either way, don't drive another Miami summer without ceramic tint on your glass. Your leather — and your skin — will thank you.

title: Best Car Vinyl Wrap Film & Color Change Wraps for Exotic Cars in Miami (2026)
excerpt: Miami's wrap culture is as big as its car culture. Here are the best vinyl wrap films for color changes, accents, and full-body transformations — from 3M and Avery Dennison to budget-friendly alternatives that actually hold up in Florida heat.
content:
Walk around any valet stand in Brickell, Design District, or South Beach and you'll see it: matte black Lamborghinis, satin chrome McLarens, color-shifting Ferraris that look nothing like they did when they left the factory. Miami has become the vinyl wrap capital of the Southeast, and for good reason. A quality wrap lets you completely transform your car's appearance — sometimes radically — without touching the factory paint underneath.

For exotic car owners, wrapping isn't just cosmetic. It's paint protection with personality. A full vinyl wrap shields your $15,000+ paint job from rock chips, UV damage, bird droppings, and Miami's corrosive salt air. When you're ready to sell, peel it off and reveal the pristine factory paint underneath. It's reversible, customizable, and in many cases cheaper than a high-end respray.

But not all wrap film is created equal — especially in Miami's heat and humidity. Here's what to buy, what to avoid, and how to get the best results.

Best Vinyl Wrap Films for Exotic Cars in Miami

FilmFinish OptionsDurabilityBest ForPrice (per 5ft × 60ft roll)
3M 2080 Series100+ colors, gloss/matte/satin/carbon5–7 yearsBest overall, industry standard for exotics$500–$800
Avery Dennison SW90080+ colors, specialty finishes5–7 yearsBest conformability on complex curves$450–$750
KPMF K75400 SeriesUnique colors (Matte Iced Blue, Midnight Purple)4–6 yearsStandout colors you can't find elsewhere$400–$650
Hexis Skintac HX20000Wide range, good specialty finishes5–8 yearsEuropean quality, excellent for European exotics$400–$700
VViViD+ XPO PremiumGloss, matte, satin, chrome delete3–5 yearsBest budget option that actually works$150–$350
Inozetek Super GlossUltra-high-gloss, paint-like finish5–7 yearsBest gloss finish — rivals actual paint$500–$900

Why Miami Is Different: What Heat & Humidity Do to Vinyl Wrap

Miami's climate is uniquely challenging for vinyl wrap film. Here's what you're dealing with:

  • UV degradation: Miami gets ~3,150 hours of sunshine per year. Cheap vinyl will fade, discolor, or become brittle within 12–18 months. Premium films from 3M and Avery are formulated with UV inhibitors that maintain color stability for 5+ years.
  • Heat expansion: When ambient temps hit 95°F and surface temps on a dark car exceed 160°F, vinyl expands. Low-quality adhesive can fail, causing lifting at edges and seams. Premium films use pressure-sensitive adhesive that strengthens with heat rather than weakening.
  • Humidity under the film: If the surface isn't properly prepped (decontaminated, stripped of wax/sealant), Miami's humidity can get trapped under the vinyl and cause bubbles or adhesive failure months later. This isn't a film problem — it's a prep problem.
  • Salt air corrosion: For cars parked outdoors near the coast, salt particles can work under wrap edges and corrode paint underneath. A properly installed wrap with sealed edges prevents this.

Product Deep Dives: Our Top Picks for Miami

Best Overall: 3M 2080 Series

The 3M 2080 is the film most professional Miami wrap shops reach for when a client pulls up in a Ferrari or Lamborghini. It features 3M's Controltac adhesive with Comply air-release channels, which means faster installation with fewer bubbles. The color range is massive — over 100 options including Gloss Black, Satin Dark Gray, Matte Metallic, and specialty finishes.

For Miami specifically, the 3M 2080's UV resistance is the headline feature. 3M guarantees 5–7 years of outdoor durability without fading or cracking. That's five years of Miami sun, salt, and summer storms. The film removes cleanly when you're ready for a change, leaving factory paint untouched.

Best for Complex Curves: Avery Dennison SW900

If you're wrapping a car with aggressive body lines — a McLaren 720S, Lamborghini Aventador, or Pagani Huayra — the Avery Dennison SW900 is the installer's choice. Its Easy Apply RS adhesive allows repositioning during installation, which is critical on cars with compound curves, deep recesses, and aggressive fender flares.

Avery's color palette includes some stunning specialty finishes — Satin Pearl White, Gloss Dark Grey, and a line of color-shift "ColorFlow" films that change hue depending on viewing angle. In Miami's sunlight, those color-shift wraps are absolutely stunning and guarantee you'll be the only car at the valet that looks like that.

Best Unique Colors: KPMF K75400

KPMF is the enthusiast's brand — they produce colors that nobody else offers. Their Matte Iced Blue Titanium, Midnight Purple, and Matte Aurora Green are colors that make people stop and pull out their phones. If you're in Miami to be noticed (and let's be honest, you are), KPMF gives you color options that are genuinely unique.

The film quality is excellent, though durability is slightly shorter than 3M or Avery (4–6 years vs. 5–7). For a car that gets wrapped every 2–3 years anyway — which is common in Miami's trend-driven car culture — that's perfectly fine.

Best Budget Option: VViViD+ XPO Premium

Not every wrap needs to be a $5,000 investment. VViViD+ XPO Premium delivers genuine automotive-grade vinyl at roughly half the price of 3M or Avery. It's available in a wide range of colors and finishes, ships quickly from Amazon, and has built a loyal following among DIY wrappers.

The trade-offs: slightly shorter outdoor durability (3–5 years), less forgiving during installation on complex curves, and the adhesive isn't quite as repositionable as the premium brands. For chrome deletes, accent wraps, interior trim, and full wraps on daily drivers, VViViD+ is excellent value.

Best Gloss Finish: Inozetek Super Gloss

Inozetek has become the go-to for owners who want their wrap to look like fresh paint — not "wrapped." Their Super Gloss line delivers a mirror-like finish that's nearly indistinguishable from automotive clear coat. Colors like Midnight Purple, Racing Green, and Pearl White have become Instagram-famous on Miami exotics.

Inozetek films are premium-priced but deliver a finish quality that justifies the cost. If your goal is a color change that looks factory-applied, this is the film to use.

Full Wrap vs. Partial Wrap: What Miami Owners Actually Do

Wrap TypeTypical Cost (Professional)Film NeededBest For
Full color change wrap$3,000–$7,00060–75 ft of filmComplete transformation, maximum paint protection
Chrome delete (trim only)$500–$1,20015–25 ft of filmBlacking out chrome on luxury sedans/SUVs
Accent wrap (roof, mirrors, hood)$800–$2,00020–35 ft of filmTwo-tone look, contrast styling
Protective clear wrap (satin/gloss)$3,500–$6,00060–75 ft of filmPaint protection without color change

The most popular wrap jobs in Miami right now: matte or satin finishes on supercars (matte black Huracán, satin gray 911 GT3), chrome deletes on luxury SUVs (blacked-out Cullinan, murdered-out G-Wagon), and color-shift wraps on attention-seeking exotics (iridescent Aventador, anyone?).

How Much Vinyl Wrap Film Do You Actually Need?

Vehicle TypeFilm Needed (Full Wrap)Approximate Film Cost
Compact sports car (Boxster, Supra)50–60 ft$350–$700
Mid-size exotic (488, Huracán, 911)60–70 ft$450–$800
Full-size exotic (Aventador, 812)65–75 ft$500–$900
Luxury SUV (Urus, Cullinan, G-Wagon)70–85 ft$550–$1,000
Hypercar (Chiron, Senna, Huayra)65–80 ft$500–$950

Always buy 10–15% more than you think you'll need. Waste happens during installation — especially on complex curves where film needs to be stretched, heated, and sometimes reapplied. Running out of film mid-wrap with a color from a different lot is a nightmare (slight batch color variations are real).

DIY Wrapping: Can You Do It Yourself?

Short answer: yes, but not on your first try, and probably not on your exotic.

Vinyl wrapping is a genuine skill. Flat panels (hood, roof, trunk) are manageable for beginners. Complex curves (bumpers, fenders, mirror caps) require experience, the right tools, and patience. Professional installers spend years mastering the craft.

If you want to DIY, here's what you need beyond the film itself:

ToolWhy You Need ItPrice
Vinyl Wrap Tool KitSqueegees, tucking tools, magnets, cutting tape$25–$60
Wagner Furno 750 Heat GunEssential for stretching film around curves and post-heating edges$40–$80
3M Knifeless TapeClean cuts without blade contact on paint$15–$30
Yellotools Wrap Cutting SetPrecision cutting tools designed for vinyl$30–$50
Isopropyl Alcohol (70%)Surface prep — removes wax, sealant, oils before wrapping$8–$15
Clay Bar KitDecontaminates paint surface for clean adhesion$15–$30

Our recommendation for Miami exotic car owners: Pay a professional for the full wrap. Use DIY for accent work, interior trim, chrome deletes, and practice vehicles. The risk of damaging paint or getting a mediocre result on a $200K+ car isn't worth the savings.

Top Miami Wrap Shops for Exotic Cars

  • MetroWrapz (Opa-locka): Miami's most well-known exotic wrap shop. They've wrapped everything from Bugatti Chirons to Brabus G-Wagons. Their Instagram alone is worth following. They use 3M, Avery, and Inozetek films.
  • Wrapped World (Hialeah): Specializes in color-change wraps and chrome finishes on exotic cars. Competitive pricing and fast turnaround.
  • Xclusive Autosports (South Miami): Full customization shop that does wraps alongside wheels, suspension, and audio. Good for a complete build.
  • SunTek/XPEL Certified Shops: Several Miami locations offer certified installations with manufacturer-backed warranties.

Vinyl Wrap Care & Maintenance in Miami

A wrapped car in Miami needs slightly different care than a painted one:

  • Hand wash only: Automatic car washes with brushes will damage vinyl. Touchless washes are acceptable but hand washing is ideal.
  • No wax: Traditional carnauba or synthetic wax can stain matte and satin wraps. Use a ceramic spray specifically designed for vinyl wraps instead.
  • Immediate contaminant removal: Bird droppings, tree sap, and bug splatter should be removed ASAP. Florida's acidic bug residue and bird droppings can stain vinyl permanently if left more than a day or two.
  • Garage when possible: Even the best vinyl degrades faster in direct sun. If you're parking outdoors daily in Miami, expect 30–40% shorter wrap life compared to garage-parked cars.
  • Edge sealing: Have your installer apply edge sealant (or use 3M Edge Sealer 94) on all wrap edges. This prevents lifting from Miami's humidity and car wash water intrusion.

Wrap vs. Respray vs. PPF: Which Is Right for You?

OptionCostDurabilityReversible?Best For
Vinyl wrap$3,000–$7,0003–7 yearsYes — peel and reveal original paintColor change, customization, paint protection
Professional respray$5,000–$20,000+PermanentNo — original paint is gonePermanent color change, damage repair
PPF (clear film)$4,000–$8,0005–10 yearsYesInvisible paint protection, no color change

For Miami exotic car owners who like to change things up every few years, vinyl wrap is the clear winner. It's less expensive than a respray, fully reversible, and protects your factory paint in the process. PPF is better if you want invisible protection without changing the color. A respray only makes sense if the original paint is damaged beyond correction or you're committed to a permanent change.

Should You Wrap Your Exotic Car in Miami?

If you drive an exotic or luxury car in Miami and you're even considering a wrap, just do it. The combination of paint protection, style customization, and resale value preservation makes wrapping one of the smartest investments you can make for your car. Miami's UV, salt air, and road debris are constantly attacking your paint — a wrap takes that punishment instead.

Start with 3M 2080 or Avery Dennison SW900 if you want the safest choice. Go with Inozetek or KPMF if you want to stand out even at Miami's most exotic valets. And if you're on a budget, VViViD+ XPO proves you don't need to spend a fortune to get a quality wrap.

Your car's paint will thank you. Your Instagram followers will too.
